launches.title: Hebbian Robotics - APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale
launches.tagline: We enable evaluation of data quality without training a robotics model
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TLDR;**

* **Hebbian Robotics builds APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale**
* Our APIs enable data providers to get **on-demand signals and metrics** on the quality of their data, without managing infrastructure
* We help our customers evaluate data quality without training a robotics model

<https://youtu.be/ffvFNs3bjbs>

**Our Ask**

* Buyers want data they can trust. If you're selling egocentric or robot data, **Let’s Chat ([https://calendly.com/brandon-hebbianrobotics/30min](https://calendly.com/brandon-hebbianrobotics/30min)**) and we'll show you how quality signals and metrics help you sell more at higher prices
* **Check out Pareto ([https://pareto.hebbianrobotics.com/](https://pareto.hebbianrobotics.com/)),** an example of how our APIs can be used

### **Who We Are**

* We’re Brandon and Kingston, we've trained AI models for industrial cleaning robots and built production systems for camera fleets across the globe
* [**Brandon Ong**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/388120)'s previous AI startup was backed by Sequoia. He did research on AI for low resource languages that topped Stanford’s LLM benchmark, SEA-HELM, and dropped out of his joint PhD in Robotics at Columbia and NTU
* [**Kingston Kuan**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/968709) spent years at Jane Street building systems that scaled to millions of messages per second. At Verkada, he worked on their core video surveillance platform that processed large scale multimodal data

### **The Problem**

* **High quality data is the bottleneck for unlocking the next frontier of intelligence in robotics**
* Buyers want **data they can trust** 
* Data providers don’t have the bandwidth to provide signals and metrics about the quality of their data when they are **focused on** **operational excellence**  
* This means that **model developers are forgoing model improvements due to a lack of high quality data**, impeding progress in robotics

### **Our Solution**

* APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale that enables providers to get **on-demand signals and metrics on data quality**
* Buyers demanding per-collector hour limits? **Prove compliance while we stay ahead of the workarounds**
* Changed standard operating procedures for collection? **Monitor for quality drift and regression**
* Suspect duplicate samples? **Verify quickly with a single API call**
* Our APIs enable **evaluation of data quality without training a robotics model, fast iteration cycles for** high quality data collection, and unlock **model improvements** 

### **How to reach us**

* We want to support data providers who believe in collecting high quality data in an ethical way
* To get started, email [**brandon.ong@hebbianrobotics.com**](mailto:brandon.ong@hebbianrobotics.com)

launches.title: GUILD - New Generation of Defense Contractor
launches.tagline: Making aerospace and naval parts faster and cheaper for defense
launches.body:
# ****

Hey everyone 🙂 - we’re [\@Kaya Celebi](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3161464) and [\@Erim Gurlemis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3163115) , co-founders of [\@GUILD](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/32194) .

**TL;DR**

[\@GUILD](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/32194) **is an AI-native defense contractor making aerospace parts faster and cheaper than today’s supply chain**. We win government contracts, turn technical requirements into production-ready workflows, and execute through factory integrations that eliminate the weeks normally lost between RFQ and factory floor. <https://guildai.co>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109739&key=user_uploads/3161464/3cf82073-c0e0-4c42-8d2b-d4fab3e159ca)

We’re building GUILD in two connected motions:

- First, we win and execute government manufacturing contracts directly.
- Second, we help defense hardware companies turn designs, technical packages, and supply-chain requirements into executable procurement and production workflows.

In both cases, the goal is the same: move from technical requirements to manufactured parts faster, with less cost and less operational drag.

**THE PROBLEM**

Government contracting is fragmented, overcomplicated, and inaccessible. That makes defense manufacturing slower and more expensive than it should be.

The government waits too long and pays too much for parts the country already knows how to make. Meanwhile, the supplier base is shrinking: DoW’s reported in 2023 that small-business participation in the defense industrial base has fallen by over 40% in the last decade.

**Less competition means fewer options, higher prices, weaker supply chains, and more critical work stuck before it ever reaches a production floor.** 

**THE CAUSE**

The defense supply chain is not wired together. Government demand, technical requirements, manufacturer capability, financial markets, and execution data all live in different places, so every contract becomes a manual search problem - stuck in PDFs, portals, spreadsheets, and domain knowledge.

The hard part is not finding government opportunities. Anyone can have Claude build a scrape-bot for [SAM.gov](http://SAM.gov) and call it a pipeline. **The hard part is turning messy technical requirements into a manufacturing decision, then executing the work.**

This favors large incumbents who can throw teams of people at the problem. Smaller manufacturers usually cannot. They either spend weeks decoding the package, price in too much risk, miss the timing, or never enter the market at all.

**OUR APPROACH**

**GUILD is the prime contractor**, not a marketplace or lead-gen layer for manufacturers. We win government work directly. We break the technical package into the operational steps required to produce and deliver the part. Then we execute.

**The core of this is our company brain: a structural ontology of defense manufacturing.**

AI-native, to us, means the company documents and learns from its own execution. Every artifact around a contract - requirements, quotes, supplier interactions, decisions, awards, workflows, and deliveries - becomes structured memory. Our agents traverse that graph to understand what a part is, how it can be made, what it should cost, and what needs to happen next.

The company brain compounds. Every bid makes the next bid smarter. Every factory handoff improves the next handoff. Every delivery teaches the system what actually happened, not just what the plan said. That is what lets us move from document parsing to execution as the contractor responsible for the work.

**WHAT WE’VE BUILT**

We’ve built the company brain that turns technical packages into executable manufacturing workflows. It ingests messy contract packages, understands the requirements, prices work against known factory capability, generates the production path, and keeps improving as new parts, factories, and outcomes enter the system.

This is not a hard-coded set of workflows. The system helps us build and refine new workflows as it observes more of the defense manufacturing knowledge space. GUILD Forge is the interface for this: a procurement and production planning system for defense companies that need to move from technical design to supply-chain execution.

**WHAT WE MAKE**

Our current focus is aerospace precision metals. That includes jet and engine components, structural and wing-adjacent parts, housings, brackets, fittings, retainers, and the simple but critical hardware that sits inside larger aerospace systems.

These parts are not always glamorous, but they are everywhere. When their supply chain is slow, expensive, or opaque, the larger programs above them slow down too.

**THE TEAM**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109739&key=user_uploads/3161464/9f3944e0-0a34-426b-a920-033542ce928f)

Kaya has an MS in Computer Science from Columbia and studied CS + Statistics at Duke. His background is in ML research, AI modernization, and quant work: he worked on AI modernization and quantitative systems at Morgan Stanley, and later led an AI team at hedge fund Hartree Partners. Coming into defense from the outside forced him to learn the industry from first principles and turn that learning into GUILD's technical architecture.

Erim studied Biological Sciences at Rutgers University, where he conducted research on metabolism before working in pharma consulting supporting oncology research. He then pivoted into finance at Morgan Stanley. There, he led full-scale AI implementation for Wealth Management & Advisory. At GUILD, he turns the messy reality of defense manufacturing, supplier coordination, pricing and execution into operating requirements our system can handle.

**THE ASK**

We’d love intros to defense companies that need better access to procurement, people with government or program connections, and teams dealing with supply-chain pain around technical packages, suppliers, compliance, packaging, or delivery.

We’re especially interested in meeting defense hardware companies, aerospace manufacturers, primes, and manufacturers with end-to-end automation capability - the kind of partners where GUILD can integrate directly into the factory operating layer, not just send PDFs back and forth.

Email us at [founders\@guildai.co](mailto:founder@guildai.co) or visit <https://guildai.co>.

\-  Kaya + Erim 🧿

launches.title: Dawn Industries - Automatic Diagnosis & Fix for Industrial Automation
launches.tagline: AI that understands the entire industrial cell and stages the fix in minutes.
launches.body:
Hey BF 👋 We are [@Joohyun (CJ) Cha](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1720857) and [@Robin Lee](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2574843), cofounders of [@Dawn Industries](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/33344). We’re building **VIM**, Automatic Diagnosis & Fix for Industrial Automation Cells.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109744&key=user_uploads/2574843/10398df4-83d1-4d24-860a-5ede83b91f9c)

# **TL;DR:**

**VIM is Sentry for industrial automation cells. When a cell faults, VIM reads the error code and the live machine signals, digs the root cause out of the OEM manuals and the cell's own history, and stages one safe fix for the operator to approve. When a CNC drifts, VIM catches it with the machine's own probe seconds after the cut and stages the offset correction. Downtime goes from hours to about a minute; scrap gets caught at part one instead of final inspection.**

Watch how **VIM** works:

Robot Cell Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JfGQjorNS2U>

CNC Machine Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fgNPOtBLku8>

# WHAT WE BUILT

VIM sits on the cell and closes the loop from fault to recovery:

1. **Connect**. Reads **PLC**, **HMI**, **robot**, **CNC**, **sensor**, and **driver state** without touching the controls you already trust.
2. **Understand**. Matches the fault to live signals, the right page of the right manual, and this cell's own prior recoveries or trends the probe touches and traces drift to tool wear, thermal growth, a bumped fixture.
3. **Recover**. Stages one bounded, validated action: a restart, a parameter change, an offset correction. The operator approves it like a pull request.

Before anything moves, the safety chain is verified: interlocks, light curtain, area scanner. VIM cannot bypass it; that's a precondition in the action policy, not a feature. And when the fault is genuinely hardware, VIM routes the incident to the right person with the exact diagnosis and repair steps attached, instead of a generic alarm and a prayer.

**Autonomy is earned, not assumed**: VIM ships read-only, then one-click approval, then unattended recovery only on fault classes where it has earned trust. And it's mixed-vendor by design (FANUC robots and CNC controls, Universal Robots, Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Cognex, Keyence, Renishaw probes), because a cell is multi-vendor by definition and a copilot that speaks one vendor's language can't close the loop.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109744&key=user_uploads/2574843/83b531fe-5737-4f94-8b70-cd37330dae7c)

# TEAM

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109744&key=user_uploads/2574843/df76af6e-3516-4d76-9081-145424822ef3)

We're four people covering both halves of the problem.

[Robin Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/robinlee02/) and [Joohyun (CJ) Cha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joohyun-cha), cofounders, Robin was the founding AI engineer at an aviation AI startup, and built the production AI systems behind its $10M Series A and a 1st-place Minister's Award from Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT. CJ cofounded Zipper as CTO (acquired by MetaZone), did ML on genomic data at Avalo. We spent the past years in plants and machine shops learning all the faults and error that happen during manufacturing processes.

Our founding engineers, come from Tesla and robotics research labs. They spent years building and fixing automation cells and various robot cases.

# OUR ASK

* **Intros to plant managers, manufacturing engineers, and controls engineers** at plants running robot cells (palletizing, case packing, welding, machine tending, inspection). If a stopped line ruins their week, we want to meet them.
* **Intros to machining and quality leaders at plants and shops (primarily aerospace & defense) running CNCs**, anywhere scrap gets discovered at final inspection instead of at the machine.
* **War stories.** Tell us about the cell that keeps stopping or the machine that keeps drifting. Best case, we make it your most reliable one.

Reach us at [joohyun_cha@dawnxr.com](mailto:joohyun_cha@dawnxr.com) or 401-226-3503, or book a demo at <https://dawnxr.com>.

launches.title: Cognitio Labs -  the AI Back Office for Product Quality Teams
launches.tagline: CoAsync by Cognitio Labs, the AI back office for product quality teams.
launches.body:
CoAsync by Cognitio Labs, the AI back office for product quality teams.

<https://youtu.be/IvQ1RtQ3280?si=oq-kHI5nO5iWeoji>

Certificates of Analysis are one of the sources of documentation clogging food and consumer product shipments today. Every day, millions of dollars of product sit waiting to ship because paperwork isn't ready to certify it is safe.

Before food can leave a facility, quality teams review supplier documents, lab reports, product specs, and regulatory requirements to produce a COA, the document certifying a product is safe, meets quality standards, and complies with destination-country rules. That still happens across PDFs, emails, spreadsheets, and disconnected ERPs, and a single COA can take hours.

CoAsync ingests supplier documents, extracts lab data, validates specifications, applies country-specific compliance requirements, and drafts audit-ready COAs, keeping quality teams in control at every step.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109669&key=user_uploads/339188/d089cbb5-ccba-49ee-a89b-29f4ad88253f)


Results: A Fresno-based dry fruit manufacturer cut COA processing from 8 hrs/week to under 1 hr in a six-week deployment, an 85% drop in QA admin work. A California fig grower now processes 4x more COAs per shift, saving 1 to 2 hours per document, and onboarded in under a day.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109669&key=user_uploads/339188/c9de609b-22b8-4634-a6d0-47768cd58e52)


We're starting with food, one of the most document-intensive, regulated supply chains in the world, building toward an AI operating system for safety and quality across consumer products adoption.

Our founder @[Diva Avaya Sharma](https://www.linkedin.com/in/diva-sharma/) presented on critical supply chains adopting artificial intelligence tools at the World Economic Forum's SmartStart Manufacturing Initiative Initiative and the AI for Good Global Summit (International Telecommunications x United Nations).

If you know a food, consumer products, or ingredients manufacturer buried in paperwork overload, we welcome an introduction: <https://www.cognitioiq.com/contact>.

launches.title: OpenRelay: The Inference Delivery Network
launches.tagline: One API for inference across every chip.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** OpenRelay is building an Inference Delivery Network (IDN) on top of its CDN for GPUs. We provide one entrypoint for inference across every chip. 

Send us a workload and we’ll cut your costs up to 20% by running it through our network, balancing the best available accelerator (NVIDIA, TPU, Trainium, AMD) across clouds and handing back a single endpoint. You never pick the hardware, chase quotas, or rebuild your stack per provider. And if you run GPUs or other AI accelerators (an NVIDIA cluster, TPUs, a reserved fleet), you can plug your capacity into our rails and we'll bring the inference demand. Get started [here](https://openrelay.inc/).

P.S. sign up for our Luma page to be notified of our Launch Party!

<https://luma.com/s6x8cx5x>

\
<https://youtu.be/7uNhqcjBXJg>

## The Team

Hey guys! We're **Jaden and Prashant**, the founders of OpenRelay. We came at the same problem from opposite sides.

* Jaden built a half-megawatt data center at 20 from a warehouse shell, then joined Voltage Park early, where he ran virtualization and helped stand up HPC.
* Prashant built accelerator infra at AWS, where he ran custom model deployments and wrote custom kernels to squeeze out Trainium performance.

 

We kept seeing the same thing: there's more AI compute than ever, and you still can't reach it. We left our jobs to fix that.

## The Problem

Compute is everywhere; liquidity is nowhere. Accelerators are scattered across dozens of clouds, chip vendors, and operators, each behind its own quotas, drivers, contracts, and console. Teams that want to run inference can't reach the capacity, and the capacity can't reach them.

Running inference naively is easy; running it at scale is hard. Any operator can spin up a model on a box. Turning idle GPUs into a production endpoint (load balancing, isolation, autoscaling, failover, metering, billing) is a software platform most individual operators won't build. So capacity sits stranded behind their own front door, and developers either overpay for scarce reserved GPUs or hand-stitch a fragile multi-provider stack.

## Solution

We built one set of rails across all of it.

Send a workload (any container or model) and we schedule it onto the best-fit accelerator, attach a production endpoint, and scale it. We route to the cheapest accelerator that meets your latency and throughput targets, and we benchmark continuously. If the market can't beat renting yourself, we backstop with our own inference demand, so you’re never on the hook. 

You never pick the chip, cloud, or region; we handle routing, isolation, failover, metering, and billing across 4+ clouds and every major chip family. We're language- and framework-agnostic (no SDK lock-in), and you can drive everything from our CLI and REST API.

It's two-sided: if you run GPUs or other accelerators (a neocloud, a data center, a pay for an underutilized reserved fleet), you can connect that capacity to our rails and we'll bring the inference demand, turning hardware into a revenue-generating endpoint without building a platform yourself.

## Traction

We're **live in production**, generating 100 billion tokens a week across 22 physical locations across Europe, APAC, North America, and the Middle East running on 8 different accelerator SKUs.  

## Asks

We'd love to hear from you!

* **Run GPUs, or know someone who does?** This is who we most want to talk to: companies running their own nodes for inference, data centers, reserved fleets, even a crypto or mining cluster looking to move into AI. Plug your capacity into our rails and we'll bring the demand. Reach us at [founders@openrelay.inc](https://mailto:founders@openrelay.inc).
* **Shipping inference and tired of picking chips?** Bring a workload and we'll get you on the best available hardware today.
* **Feedback, intros, or just want to chat?** Book a call with us, or email [founders@openrelay.inc](mailto:founders@openrelay.inc) for anything else.

launches.title: Maingen: Simulations of real industrial operations, so agents can run the physical world
launches.tagline: Long horizon RL environments for the $5 trillion industrial economy
launches.body:
Hello everyone!

Phillip and David here, founders of Maingen (YC S26).

**TLDR: AI is moving to the industrial world. Maingen builds RL environments for industrials (a $5 trillion slice of the US economy) so frontier labs can train models that actually run factories.**

**Problem**:

We believe the next capabilities frontier is the physical world: operating factories, power plants, and industrial infrastructure. But that data doesn't exist on the internet, but rather as tacit knowledge inside enterprises, on operations desks, and in CMMS systems and vendor portals.

**What we do:**

<https://youtu.be/jE5HtSiAqxE>

We embed with operators in these industries and translate their decision making process into RL environments labs can train.

**Our first public benchmark evaluates whether agents can run a solar portfolio [solarbench.maingen.ai](http://solarbench.maingen.ai).** We’re continuing in other areas like factories, and we’re already working with frontier labs.

**Who we are**

The founders Phillip Yan and David Yang have previously built RL environments, worked in the energy industry, shipped software powering 150 million+ TPV, and have been cited by Anthropic.

**Get Involved**

Maingen is looking for researchers and industrial operators to help shape its next environments. We’d love to hear from you if you:

1. Work on research on long-horizon **agents, RL environments, or physical-world capabilities**.
2. Run operations at an industrial site or can introduce the team to someone who does

Reach out at [founders@maingen.ai](mailto:founders@maingen.ai)! We're always down for a coffee!

Thanks,

Phillip and David

launches.title: Sidekick: AI agent that handles frontline operations over text
launches.tagline: Sidekick gives frontline workers an AI assistant they can text, with no app, login, or training.
launches.body:
**Hey everyone 👋**

I'm Justin, founder of Sidekick.

**TL;DR** Sidekick is an AI assistant that frontline manufacturing workers use over text message. They text a number and it answers from the company's own documents, creates and routes work orders, and syncs with the software the company already uses. No app, no login, no training. I built Sidekick for my dad's manufacturing shop. It’s now live at facilities across the globe.

**_Ask:_** Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility? I'd love an intro! Email [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick).

Check out our launch video:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yxwq5ZAojXg>

## ❌ The Problem

I grew up in my dad's manufacturing plants and spent summers working on the factory floor at EDS Manufacturing.

Here's what I watched happen repeatedly. A machine goes down, everyone's waiting, and the person who can help is in a meeting or on another line. Half the time the answer already existed. Nobody could get to it.

Why it keeps happening:

* **No computer access.** Nobody on that floor has a company login or an email address, so none of the plant's software reaches them.
* **The answers are scattered.** An SOP in a binder, a manual on a shared drive few have permissions to, a safety procedure someone printed and taped to a wall in 2019.
* **The best answers were never written down.** Thirty years of tribal knowledge lives in one guy's head, and when he retires it leaves with him.
* **So the same questions get asked over and over.** Shift after shift, and every one of them costs somebody their afternoon.

There are 239,000 manufacturing plants in the US, and only 29% of the people working in them have advanced digital skills. Any tool that requires a download, a login, and training makes adoption difficult.

## ✅ Our Solution

Workers text the Sidekick phone number. Problems, photos, voice memos, in any language. No app to download, no account to create, nothing to learn. Every worker on the floor already knows how to send a text, which is why adoption isn't a fight.

* **Answers from your own documents.** SOPs, manuals, safety procedures, tribal knowledge. Sidekick responds in the worker's language, in seconds.
* **Creates and routes the work order.** The issue gets logged and sent to the right person, without anyone needing a laptop.
* **Syncs with the software you already run.** Sidekick pulls from and writes to your existing systems instead of replacing them, and integrates directly through PLC and SCADA systems so the floor and the software finally see the same thing.
* **Captures tribal knowledge.** Every exchange builds a searchable knowledge base the company owns, so the know-how stays when the veteran leaves.

Here's a full walkthrough:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a5zBRSXi-90>

## 👤 The Team

I'm Justin, founder and CEO. I'm the third generation in a manufacturing family, and I've been around plant floors since I was a kid. I studied Computer Science at the University of Pennsylvania, worked in finance at Arm, and left both to build Sidekick after watching the same problem play out on every floor I'd been on.

## 🙏 Our Ask

If you answer "yes" to any of these, I'd love your help:

* **Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility?** Even a name and a "you two should talk" goes a long way.
* **Have you sold software into manufacturing?** I'd love to hear what actually worked and what didn't.

Contact me at [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo here**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick)**.**

launches.title: Praxis AI - Training Data for Robotics
launches.tagline: Praxis offers labs the most diverse environments, SOTA hardware, and rigorous post processing to train their models
launches.body:
**Hey YC!**

We're Rohan, Dev, and Tommy, and we're building Praxis.

**Praxis turns real-world work into training data for robots.**

<https://youtu.be/xri7vyzxW-I?si=L6ZBgLO24OrvYuuH>

**What we do**

Robots learn to act in the physical world by watching humans do the work. We partner with businesses to capture egocentric human demonstration data, the first-person video of how tasks actually get done in factories, warehouses, homes, and other physical work environments, then supply it to the labs and humanoid teams training the next generation of robots. Robotics data is our focus, but since our collection infrastructure overlaps, we're happy to explore other multimodal data too.

**The problem**

Robotics is missing its internet-scale training corpus. LLMs learned from the web, books, code, and the accumulated record of human thought. Robots need the equivalent record of human action: how people pick, pack, clean, assemble, inspect, cook, use tools, recover from mistakes, and move through messy physical environments.

Collecting some of this data is easy. Collecting enough of the right kind is brutally hard, for two reasons.

First, diversity is capped by access. Models only generalise if they've seen the full range of real environments and operators, from a one-person shop to a national-scale industrial operation. Getting in the door across that entire spectrum, and across continents, is a physical-world access problem that most teams can't solve.

Second, it takes two rare skills at once. You have to know what frontier labs need at a technical level, and be able to run demanding physical operations across thousands of real sites, standardising capture and turning fragmented workflows into model-ready data. Few teams have both halves.

**Our solution**

We already run collections across 150 environment types on 5 continents, with diversity from mom-and-pop stores to conglomerates accounting for 3% of a nation's GDP, and a reachable network of 60,000 workers. Depending on the task, we capture egocentric video, stereo-RGB, IMU, wrist-camera views, glove kinematics, haptics, and dense annotations. Everything is delivered calibrated, synced, pose-tracked, QA'd, and PII-scrubbed. We build and deploy custom capture hardware quickly because part of the team operates out of Shenzhen.

**Why us**

Praxis is built to do both hard things at once. We pair robotics research depth (IEEE, NASA JPL) with the ability to actually run demanding operations in the real world, from Fortune 500 supply chains to Parliaments, plus a Shenzhen hardware team. That combination- technical understanding of what labs need plus real physical-world access at scale- is what lets us deliver diverse, model-ready data at a cost and breadth that is irreplaceable.

**Our asks**

1. Intros to anyone working on robotics, embodied AI, or world-models, especially data and research leads. If you need other forms of multimodal data, we're happy to explore that too.
2. If you run a business with interesting physical work (logistics, manufacturing, food, retail, or lab work) and would like to monetize it, we'd love to talk.

You can reach us at [founders@praxisrobotics.io](mailto:founders@praxisrobotics.io) and [rohan@praxisrobotics.io](mailto:rohan@praxisrobotics.io)[ https://www.praxisrobotics.io](https://www.praxisrobotics.io)

launches.title: Experiential Labs - Turn your AI spend into a cheaper + better model you own
launches.tagline: Train a model your company owns, guaranteed to match or beat frontier quality at 50% lower cost.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Companies are spending more on AI every month, but almost none of that spending becomes an asset they own. We train a small language model for your company's use cases. You fully own it, and we guarantee the same or better quality as the frontier models you use today at 50% lower cost.**

<https://youtu.be/YRkN_-6rl3Y>

Companies are spending more on AI every month, but almost none of that spending becomes an asset they own.

The prompts, traces, and use cases are yours, _but the model stays rented._

So you keep paying frontier prices for repetitive work a smaller, specialized model could do faster, cheaper, and often better

We built Experiential Labs to change that.

**Here's how it works**

Keep using GPT, Claude, or whatever models are already in your stack.

Experiential Labs uses your traffic to build a simulation of the tasks, failures, and edge cases your agent encounters. You can also upload existing traces to bootstrap the process.

The platform trains you a model against that simulation, so it gets better at your specific use cases over time.

As your model improves, it earns more traffic. Hard requests can still go to the frontier. Everything else moves to your faster, cheaper model.

You own the weights, can run them wherever you want, and keep the profits they create. When a stronger base model comes out, we transfer what your model has learned instead of making you start over.

On some tasks we've seen up to 97% lower cost and +50% higher quality. Across a full deployment, we guarantee at least 50% lower cost at the same or better quality, backed by an SLA.

**The team**

We are both AI researchers. Kion built simulation systems for autonomous vehicles at Waabi after earning his ML PhD at Georgia Tech. Silen built and grew AutoGPT to 160,000 GitHub stars and has worked across continual learning, evaluations, interpretability, and AI for science.

## Our ask

**The problem**

This is one of the largest, fastest-growing markets in the country. 11,000 Americans turn 65 every day, and 70% want to age at home. 53 million people are already unpaid family caregivers, over $1 trillion in economic value every year that the system doesn’t capture.

But getting someone into home care is brutal. The application and paperwork alone take weeks of back-and-forth across a caregiver, a patient and their family, a doctor, and a state caseworker, with paper forms bouncing between all of them. Most of that time isn't care; it's coordination. Most families give up before care ever starts, and caregivers wait unpaid.

When care finally begins, caregivers suffer from missed payments and poor coordination, affecting patients downstream. All of this because existing agencies aren’t built to handle care at scale.

**What Cova does**

We own the full stack: Cova is its own home care agency serving Medicaid, LTCI, and private-pay patients, and AI agents run it end to end.

* **Weeks → days.** AI agents handle the applications and paperwork that normally drags on for weeks in just a few days.

launches.title: Vestris: Al native title processing service
launches.tagline: We allow title shops to close more deals
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Title insurance is the thorn in the side of every single residential real estate transaction in America. With the home market bleeding, you'll find attorneys processing documents by hand with outdated software at title agencies. Vestris automates the back office and supplements processors the way software should — _letting shops give the same care to closing the biggest purchase of a buyer's life._

<https://youtu.be/u2do97AOvQY?si=JB78OAx5hDp80PXT>

### The Problem

Imagine you're shopping the market and you just found your dream home. You're ready to purchase, the contract is signed, everything is in place.

And you're recommended a settlement company, and told to buy title insurance.

Most homeowners couldn't tell you what title insurance actually buys them. In a nutshell: **you're paying for the peace of mind that the property you're buying has no open claims against it** — payments a title company makes on your behalf.

But it's also a process that takes weeks. Behind the phone, you've got lawyers processing files, manually checking emails, and scanning two seemingly identical documents for changes.

Meanwhile, the incumbent software is a decade-old, per-file database whose premium plans put it out of reach for the small and mid-size shops that make up most of the market.

### The Solution

Vestris runs the file end to end:

**Reads everything on arrival** — every document that hits a processor's inbox is routed to the right order, new contracts spin up new files, and the routine back-and-forth is handled, so the first 30% of a file is done before a human even looks.

**Does the math** — logs into county tax and land portals to pull up-to-date figures, then prorates taxes, utilities, HOA dues, and special assessments to the settlement date on that county's convention, every figure traced back to its source.

**Drafts the commitment** — building Schedule A from the vesting and legal description and Schedule B from the exceptions in the record, the work a small shop waits a week and pays an abstractor hundreds for.

**Closes it out** — reconciling the closing disclosure against the settlement statement, handling the lender back-and-forth, and showing the processor exactly what changed, so no one's squinting at two seemingly identical PDFs.

Every step still goes through human approval. What changes is bandwidth: **a mom-and-pop shop never has to turn down an order because they're swamped**, and they get to spend their time on the in-person care that made buyers seek them out in the first place.

### The Team

We're Aahil and Josh, best friends and UMich roommates.

Aahil previously built SafeKids and holds three USPTO patents. He spent the summer closing files at a title shop, seeing the processor's grind firsthand.

Josh previously built live-telemetry and communication systems for Michigan's Formula SAE team. He worked the same title desk, and stole the cubicle with the monitor 😠

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109429&key=user_uploads/3411947/af48be0b-23b2-4cb5-9c1c-4eb5c7b45e50)

## **The problem**

Real user feedback is the gold standard for deciding what to build and almost nobody gets it, because it's slow and expensive. So teams substitute: survey panels, ICP interviews, and lately AI personas prompted with a demographic sketch. All of them share the same flaw — they don't know _your_ users. The result is confident feedback with no context, and ideas that ship blind anyway.

Connect your product analytics tools. Promi builds behavioral profiles of your actual user segments, not personas, not survey panels, and turns them into simulated users. Describe a proposed change: a flow, copy, pricing, onboarding, and they react the way your real segments tend to: where they'd hesitate, what they'd skip, and why.

I spent 5 years as a PM at Uber, where real user feedback was the gold standard nobody had time or budget for — so most ideas shipped blind. When we did get feedback, 9 times out of 10 we preferred existing customers over a generic ICP, because real users knew _why_ they used the product. AI feedback needs that same context, so we built Promi to have it: simulated users trained on your customers' actual behavior.

Every product decision deserves real user feedback. We're making that the default instead of the luxury.

launches.title: SpaceFlow: The managed runtime for enterprise AI agents
launches.tagline: AI employees that do supply chain work and prove every task.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** $400M in annual supplier spend already runs through SpaceFlow. We give large enterprises AI employees that do supply chain and purchasing work, prove every task they complete, and run wherever the data must live, including the company's own datacenter. Hundreds of users are in production daily, one customer cut off-contract spending by 42%, and already canceled three planned hires.

<https://youtu.be/lS9pBj_LeV8>

### **The work the ERP never sees**

SAP runs most of the world's largest companies. The majority still run it on-premise, customized over twenty years, and that whole ecosystem got skipped by the AI wave.

Here is what that looks like on the ground. The real work of procurement and planning happens where the ERP cannot see it: inboxes, spreadsheets, and phone calls. A buyer opens 47 unread supplier emails, reads quotes in five incompatible formats, re-types the numbers into Excel, builds the comparison by hand, chases delivery dates, and finally records the outcome in SAP. Hours per request, every day. We interviewed 200 companies and shadowed procurement & SAP teams for weeks watching this happen. Nobody was exaggerating.

### **What the AI employees do**

SpaceFlow agents do that work end to end and stage every action for a human to approve:

* **Sourcing.** A purchase request comes in. The agent qualifies it, picks suppliers from the company's own purchase history, and sends the RFQs. Supplier replies land as messy human emails; the agent reads them the way a buyer does and extracts price, lead time, and minimum order. It compares bids, flags risk (a supplier that shipped late three times last quarter), and sends the counter-offer. The buyer sees one card with a recommendation and a confidence score. One click approves it.
* **Planning.** The agents keep supply plans in line with real demand and prepare the orders and the numbers behind every planning meeting, daily instead of once a month.
* **Spend control.** They match invoices against contracts and catch price drift and off-contract buying before it compounds.

Humans stay in control. Every agent has per-action autonomy limits; everything above a threshold waits in an approval queue, and every step is logged and auditable. The ERP stays the system of record, SAP or otherwise. Every feature in the product is exposed over MCP as well as REST, so the whole system is agent-operable by design.

### **What it is worth**

Work that takes a buyer hours happens in minutes. Across our customers: 3x faster RFQ cycles, $120K saved per year at one company, off-contract spending cut 42% at another, and one customer canceled three planned hires it no longer needed. A shared company brain learns how each company buys and decides, so the agents get better with every cycle.

### **Why on-premise, and what we had to build for it**

The largest enterprises keep SAP in their own datacenters because their data cannot leave. The same rule kept AI out: they will never send twenty years of operating history to someone else's cloud.

So we bring the models to the data. SpaceFlow is a managed runtime for enterprise AI agents: we operate the models, the agents, and the compute wherever the customer's data must live. Our cloud, their private cloud, or their own hardware inside their own walls. Same product in every deployment; data never leaves the perimeter. No migration, nothing to rip out, live in days.

### **The deeper bet: enterprise work that can be checked**

AI got good at code because every answer could be checked. SpaceFlow brings the same loop to enterprise work. Each time a person approves or corrects a task, that verdict is saved, and the verdicts become evals, the tests the AI is measured against. The AI improves at each company's specific way of working, and finance sees exactly what it did and what it saved. Our bet is that enterprise AI becomes real when its work can be checked.

### **Where we are**

* $400M in annual supplier spend runs through the product, and it is growing.
* Our first enterprise contract is signed with a national restaurant brand. That customer's Chief Supply Chain Officer went on to invest personally upon seeing Spaceflow’s capabilities.
* Before YC, we built an autonomous procurement engine with a medical manufacturer and saw both gaps firsthand: the work lives outside the ERP, and nobody could tell whether the AI did it right.

### **What's in it for you?**

1. **Run SAP, especially on-premise?** Your team can have AI employees without waiting for a migration. Book a demo at [spaceflow.tech](http://spaceflow.tech) or write to [emre@spaceflow.tech](mailto:emre@spaceflow.tech).
2. **Know a supply chain, procurement, or IT leader at a manufacturer?** An intro helps more than anything else at this stage. We will make you look good.
3. **Building agents for the enterprise?** We are happy to compare notes on evals, on-prem model serving, and MCP-first product design.

### **About the team:**

**Emre Isik (CEO)**  studied computer engineering at the University of Cambridge and dropped the master's to build SpaceFlow full time. Before that he researched embedded AI for motor control at UCLA's Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics, published a machine-learning paper on reasoning with small data, and trained with Turkey's international informatics olympiad reserve team at 15. 

**Ali Eren Aytekin (co-founder)** left engineering at Istanbul Technical University to build SpaceFlow.  He was Microsoft Imagine Cup EMEA runner-up for a genetic-signal classifier that hit 98.3% accuracy, and co-authored the published paper on low-data reasoning. [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ali-eren-aytekin-6305a41aa/) . He talked his way into an invite-only AI showcase in Istanbul, came out with a procurement problem from the CEO of a UK medical manufacturer, and shipped the solution with the team in two weeks. That deal became the learning SpaceFlow grew from.

**Hakan Enes Aksu (co-founder)** left information engineering at Boğaziçi University to build SpaceFlow. He has been shipping commercial software since 16, when his Reddit ad-automation service earned $40K in revenue, and he later built a tender-matching engine that reads public tenders against a company's product catalog and sold it to a corporate customer for five figures. He scored in the top 500 out of roughly 3 million students in Turkey's national university entrance exam. [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hakan-enes-aksu/)

launches.title: Florin: A full-stack insurance company with 0 underwriters
launches.tagline: Autonomously places hard-to-price risks in seconds
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Florin is a full-stack insurance company with 0 underwriters. Software takes a submission from a raw intake form to a bindable quote in seconds. Instead of matching a business to a class code, it verifies what the business actually does using satellite imagery, permits, public records and social media, then prices it by simulating tens of thousands of ways its next few years could go.

<https://youtu.be/BaXtkdP6_nc>

**What we do and why**

Insurance prices risk with class codes. An underwriter receives an application PDF, matches the business to a row in a rate table, and quotes off that row. This breaks in two ways. Applications are incomplete or wrong, so the price is built on bad inputs. And when a business does not fit any row, either because it is genuinely new (robotics, AI, autonomy) or because the table says the whole class or state is unprofitable, the answer is a declination. That is why carriers are exiting entire states and why a three-year-old industry can barely buy coverage at any price.

Florin replaces the table with evidence. It ingests the submission directly, no intake team. It builds its own picture of the business from the outside: aerial imagery of the actual premises, permits and public records, even the insured's social media, where it has caught operations that were never disclosed on the application. From that verified picture it runs simulations of the business's possible futures and produces a quote you can bind in seconds. No human touches the file.

launches.tagline: Unlocking remote, harsh, and hard-to-reach places with robotics. Starting with solar.

Libra Robotics builds collaborative robot squads for solar installation.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1fmbWSY7337l1Pe6quT0TALhC8Ua0Y5_q](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1fmbWSY7337l1Pe6quT0TALhC8Ua0Y5_q/view?usp=sharing)

Libra is building robots to unlock places once considered too difficult to develop. Unlike solutions that automate only one task, or even part of one, Libra covers the workflow after PV module pallets arrive on-site: transportation, installation, and fastening. Each robot has a specific role, and fleets can be configured based on each project’s cost and schedule requirements.

Libra Robotics works directly with EPCs through a Robotics-as-a-Service model, requiring no robot purchase or large upfront capital investment, and it also works with racking and PV module manufacturers to certify compatibility and give customers confidence in deployment.

Purpose-built hardware, intelligent software, and multimodal sensing help Libra’s robots handle real-world construction uncertainty. These patent-pending innovations form a core part of its moat.

Jermaine Zhao brings a Stanford background in ME, EE, and CS, plus experience building and deploying agricultural robots from scratch. launches.title: Can you beat frontier LLMs at social strategy games? | Multi-Agent Arena by Olam Labs, evaluating through multi-agent simulations
launches.tagline: Play games like Risk, Poker, or Codenames against frontier AIs. We're running public long-horizon games to do evaluations on social behavior and agentic performance.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** As many researchers and labs will say, there is a massive shortage of genuinely good AI evaluations. Multi-agent environments are an underdeveloped way of evaluating models that we think will help address our increasingly worse shortage of evals. We're starting with **Multi-Agent Arena**, where anyone can come compete against frontier AI models in social multiplayer games, as we build towards the full stack for multi-agent environments. Try Multi-Agent Arena for free at <https://olamlabs.ai/> :) \
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/186GgmnOLz4Yc1BpFk6AxHd3aqUdFYCQy](https://drive.google.com/file/d/186GgmnOLz4Yc1BpFk6AxHd3aqUdFYCQy/view?usp=sharing)

---

## **Overview**

Multi-agent environments provide an essential, underutilized framework for benchmarking autonomous AI models. Multi-Agent Arena is an interactive platform where human participants compete against frontier AI models in multiplayer games, serving as an experimental foundation to evaluate complex agent interactions. Multi-Agent Arena is the first of many stepping stones to building the entire stack and ecosystem for multi-agent environments.\
\
**The Evaluation Gap** \
Current AI evaluations primarily focus on single-agent, task-oriented capabilities. While benchmarks such as SWE-bench measure functional task execution, they do not assess the dynamic social behaviors required for autonomous real-world deployment: negotiation, coalition stability, long-horizon planning against adaptive opponents, and spontaneous deception.

Simulated multi-agent environments induce these complex interactions while preserving complete experimental control. Unlike unstructured real-world deployment, these environments offer full data legibility, enabling researchers to inspect every reasoning trace, state transition, and stochastic variable behind model decisions.

**Our Preliminary Evaluations**\
The platform runs deterministic, replayable environments hosting human players alongside anonymized frontier models. Structured as accessible multiplayer games, the infrastructure captures interaction data to score models across two primary axes in our first evaluated game, Poker:

* **Competitive Capability:** One of our preliminary methods is using a Bradley-Terry model to yield Elo ratings with bootstrapped confidence intervals, supplemented by domain-specific metrics such as big blinds per 100 hands in poker. Top-quartile human participants currently outperform all benchmarked models in Poker.
* **Behavioral Diagnostics:** Model reasoning traces are evaluated against ground-truth game states using expert-curated rubrics and variance-checked grader panels to ensure inter-annotator agreement.

**Initial Metric: Deception Index** \
The benchmark's initial diagnostic metric, the Deception Index, quantifies deliberate misrepresentation per 10,000 turns. A deceptive event is logged only when an agent's private chain-of-thought confirms awareness of a true state while its external communication directly contradicts it. In baseline tests with no explicit instructions or prompts to deceive, frontier models demonstrated performance variance spanning nearly two orders of magnitude across identical environments.

Complete evaluations, research methodology and technical documentation are available at [olamlabs.ai/research/social-arena](https://olamlabs.ai/evaluations)\
\
**Launch**\
\
We already passed a thousand matches a day in our early access, are nearing a billion tokens used per day, ranking on the OpenRouter leaderboards, and have thousands of users that are paying to play in the arena while we work with researchers on use cases they have for our work and environments. We’re hoping this is just a stepping stone and want to scale towards our roadmap and ambitions of what we believe multi-agent environments, when properly developed with the right stakeholders in the training/eval ecosystem, can achieve for AI progress.\
\
\
**What’s in it for you?**

1. **Play.** It's free, and every match directly informs the evals. Bring friends, try to beat the models, it’s harder than you'd think. 🃏
2. **Speak with researchers.** We love speaking with researchers interested in this space and it’s all that we think about; if that’s you please feel free to reach out to us at [founders@olamlabs.ai](mailto:founders@olamlabs.ai) or on <https://olamlabs.ai/about> \
   \
   🫡

---

## About the team

**Om Buddhdev (CEO)** — Previously a Product Engineer then promoted to Staff Engineer at AI Dungeon / Latitude working on AI infra, agents, and consumer platform work, left for Olam Labs. Before that he was among the best Valorant players in the world (top 25, 8x radiant), at 17 a large content creator on TikTok with 195k followers, and as a young teenager made Roblox games played millions of times, among other things in his past. More on Om at <https://www.sensho.xyz/>

**Shreshth Sharma (CTO)** — Background in production data engineering: was a Data Scientist at RBC while doing a double degree at the University of Waterloo in CS and Math, dropped out of both for Olam Labs. He has a background in many data and statistics projects, alongside briefly being a top 50 Fifa player. More on Shreshth at <https://shresh.ca/>\
\
Om and Shreshth have been friends since middle school, and Olam Labs was born out of their personal interest and desire to build out the entire stack for multi-agent environments to be the default way we evaluate models in the future.

Hello!

Yahia here, founder of [Context.dev](https://link.context.dev/yc) (YC S26).

**TL;DR:** [Context.dev](https://link.context.dev/yc) turns the live web into structured data for AI agents and applications. Trusted by Mintlify, Passionfroot, Rho, and more than 400 customers.

The web was built for humans to browse, not agents to understand.

Once an AI product needs live internet data, its team often ends up maintaining browsers, proxies, crawlers, parsers, queues, retries, caches, and multiple data vendors.

We built Context.dev so that entire workflow starts with one API.

<https://youtu.be/c2mVWBJmBtQ>

**How it works**

Give Context.dev the sources your product cares about and tell us what context you need. We collect it, structure it, and keep it current without your team building the infrastructure underneath.

* Send URLs, domains, companies, websites, sitemaps, or files.
* Get back clean Markdown, screenshots, company data, or structured JSON matching your schema.
* Use Batches to process large workloads and Monitors to keep information current.
* We handle the browsers, proxies, rendering, extraction, caching, retries, and queues underneath.

Here’s what customers are already using it for:

* **Soria** monitors hundreds of healthcare and financial sources.
* **Murph** structures data on 2M+ foods, supplements, and tests.
* **Mintlify** turns GitHub repositories into custom branded documentation.

* **Dench** monitors social platforms for leads, generating $3M+ in pipeline.

Your team builds the product. Context.dev keeps it connected to the live web.

**The team**

I’m Yahia Bakour, founder of[ Context.dev](https://link.context.dev/yc). Before this, I led engineering at Sunrun, worked at Amazon, and built and sold two startups.

I started [Context.dev ](https://link.context.dev/yc)after watching teams repeatedly rebuild, and get stuck maintaining, the same web data infrastructure.

Models are no longer the main bottleneck for intelligent knowledge work. Context is.

launches.title: Ultrasonium: A new way to make complex metal parts, 15x faster and 75% cheaper
launches.tagline: Ultrasonium makes the most difficult metal parts for the world's most important systems 15x faster and 75% cheaper.
launches.body:
**The problem**

The technologies that define this century - data centers, rockets, satellites, robots, etc. - are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and hazardous.

**What we built**

Ultrasonium has invented a new method to make these critical parts. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part safely comes out, controlled by a physical AI layer and novel control processes. We produce near-net-shape complex metal parts 15x faster and 75% cheaper than the methods they replace, in the U.S. and at scale.

 <https://youtu.be/M9T49n6WuV8>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109239&key=user_uploads/2875171/55d1e111-fc43-450d-a83c-2c191d88d909)


**Why now / why us**

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, defense, energy, and compute are demanding metal geometries that can’t be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with the incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has built and innovated some of the most complex engineering systems known to man - quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and novel aerospace alloy processing methods. Jack Qiu (CEO) completed his PhD in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at MIT and has published pioneering quantum computing work in Nature Physics. Chris Carter (CSO) dropped out during the 5th year of his PhD program at MIT and has over a half dozen years of experience researching state of the art metallurgy and materials processing systems. Alexander Urbanski (Chief Research Officer) previously founded a DOE-funded nuclear startup and was the first hire at Phase3D where he built and commercialized metals manufacturing monitoring technology. Hunter Brown (VP, Engineering) began working at national labs when he was 15, graduated from UC Berkeley Physics, and contributed to the ITER fusion reactor.

launches.title: Dailybot CLI: Your AI agents now report to the team
launches.tagline: An open-source CLI and skill that turns private agent work into team updates, approvals, and workflows in chat
launches.body:
Hey everyone! we’re Mauricio and Sergio, co-founders of Dailybot (YC S21).

**What Dailybot is**: a place for team updates, check-ins, and coordination inside Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, and Google Chat. For people and AI agents.

**TL;DR**: we built an open-source CLI so people, scripts, and AI agents can drive Dailybot from the terminal. Updates, check-ins, chat messages, forms, and more land where the team already works: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, or Google Chat. **Ask:** ask your agent to try our skill ([**www.dailybot.com/skill.md**](http://www.dailybot.com/skill.md)), run one workflow that matches how your team actually works, and tell us which one helped you move forward today.

Dailybot skill: [**https://www.dailybot.com/skills/agent-skill/#install**](https://www.dailybot.com/skills/agent-skill/#install)

**Demo**

[**Dailybot CLI + Agent Skill: Connect your AI coding agent to your team**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rwopfsPzgSQ)

\
**The problem**

Teams are getting real work done with coding agents and scripts. A lot of that work still finishes in a private session. The rest of the team only hears about it if someone rewrites it into Slack or a standup.

So you get the usual mess: invisible agent work, stale status during a release, approvals bouncing between tools, and check-ins that someone rebuilds by hand for every new project.

**What we shipped**

Dailybot CLI. Same Dailybot account and team feed you already use, now from the command line. A few workflows we’re highlighting:

1. Agent update to team chat — done / next / blockers show up in the feed, without a human rewrite
2. One status message that stays current — one release/status message you keep updating, instead of a pile of outdated posts
3. Simple approvals in chat — approve/reject in Slack or Teams; your system gets the result and work continues

There’s more under the hood (forms, check-in creation, agent inbox, activity into reports, kudos, teams, workflows). We’re leading with the ones that produce a visible team result fast.

**Installing the CLI**

Easiest path: pass the skill to your agent and ask it in plain language, e.g. “post a team update that we finished the CLI install path” – [**https://www.dailybot.com/skill.md**](https://www.dailybot.com/skill.md)

**How we got here**

We’ve been building Dailybot for hybrid teams for a while: async check-ins, reports, and coordination inside chat. As our own team (and customers) started running agents all day, the gap got obvious: agents ship work, humans still retype the update.

The CLI is our answer to that gap. A bridge into the place the team already coordinates.

**Our ask**

1. Install and try one workflow: [**https://www.dailybot.com/skills/agent-skill/#install**](https://www.dailybot.com/skills/agent-skill/#install)
2. Reply with the workflow you’d want documented/explored next
3. If useful, intros to eng teams already running agents in production (contact our founders)

Thanks,\
Mauricio & Sergio

launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋

We're [Aniket](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anideshp/) & [Mugdhaa](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mugdhaa-patankar/), co-founders of [Agent FM](https://www.agentfm.ai/).

**TL;DR:** Agent FM is a desktop app that gives engineers one group chat to hear and steer their coding agents. Instead of manually bouncing between different claude code and codex sessions, and combing through walls of text to monitor agents, engineers just tune in to Agent FM. Agents share important progress updates, blockers, assumptions, and decisions in the group chat. Engineers get live text and audio updates and respond right from the chat.

**Launch video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bVGLQwclkYI> 

#### The Problem:

**Babysitting agents is exhausting.** Engineers running claude code and codex agents spend all day bouncing between multiple sessions, combing through walls of text to keep track of the work. In long horizon tasks, agents often go down the wrong paths, add unnecessary complexity or make bad assumptions that waste time and tokens. Agents can also sometimes misinterpret instructions, make poor decisions, or perform destructive actions due to lack of context and context compaction. To avoid this, engineers continuously keep tabs on their agents, read agent trajectories realtime for anything substantial worth intercepting. This gets really exhausting with more agents and time. We lack the tooling that automatically does this for engineers.

#### Our Solution:

* **One interface to rule them all:** Computer use + live audio updates + group chat with your agents. One command center to interact with your coding agents without babysitting and manually polling different Claude Code and Codex sessions.
* **Actionable metrics and insights into agent activity across model providers:** Deep insights and metrics about token spend across providers, cost distribution, skills and mcp token performance, and recurring patterns.
* **Works with the tools engineers already use:** No setup needed. Agent FM automatically works across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other coding tools. Local and remote workspaces supported.

launches.title: Understudy: The self-optimizing inference cloud
launches.tagline: We distill your production usage into cheaper, specialized models your company owns
launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re Luis and Aamir, founders of Understudy.

### TL;DR

We help you cut your company’s Anthropic bill by 80% with no loss of performance.

Understudy is an inference cloud. We capture your employee’s AI work traces, train smaller models, and automatically deploy them (only when they outperform the expensive model you are currently paying for).

Instead of renting the same frontier model forever, your AI infrastructure gets cheaper and better every time it runs.

See more: <https://youtu.be/YhfoOchpYaw>

### The problem

Last week, we met with a company spending $40M/year on Anthropic. And it’s only going in one direction.

To them, it feels totally out of control.

They’re not alone - every company we meet is spending record amounts on models from frontier labs.

But almost none of that spending compounds.

I.e. You send a prompt, pay for the answer, and throw away the experience. Six months later, you are still renting the same general-purpose model at roughly the same price.

Meanwhile, training custom models requires an entire ML team to collect and clean traces, build evals, choose training data, fine-tune and reinforce models, test serving configurations, compare cost, latency, and quality, safely deploy or roll back the winner.

For most companies, it’s just too much to bother with.

### What Understudy does

Point Understudy at an AI workload.

We capture how your existing agent performs, turn those traces into evals, and start training smaller models that can do the same job better.

Understudy handles the entire loop:

**Observe → evaluate → train → test → deploy → repeat**

A new model is promoted only when it beats the incumbent on the metrics you care about, such as:

* task success
* inference cost
* latency
* privacy
* deployment size

Your customized models are owned by you, and can run in our cloud, your cloud, or on-premise.

### An example

Suppose your product uses Claude for a repetitive legal workflow.

Understudy observes successful production runs, learns the specific tools and judgment required for that workflow, and trains a specialized open-weight model.

Once that model matches or beats Claude on a held-out evaluation, Understudy starts routing production traffic to it.

As more work is completed, the model keeps improving.

### Why us

Aamir and I met building Instacart’s optimization and experimentation systems, growing multiple business lines to more than $1B in annual revenue.

We started Understudy because we believe every company using AI should be accumulating intelligence, not accumulating API bills.

### Our ask

Spending too much on repetitive model workloads? Ready to own your own models? We want to meet you - come to [understudylabs.com](http://understudylabs.com) today.

launches.title: Salem Robotics - Autonomous robots for hazardous spaces
launches.tagline: We deploy robots to perform autonomous inspections and surveys in hazardous spaces, like nuclear.
launches.body:
We're [Caleb](https://www.linkedin.com/in/caleb-horan) and [Janak](https://www.linkedin.com/in/janak-panthi), PhD roboticists from UT Austin. We've spent a combined 15 years in nuclear, 10 of which deploying autonomous robots at Los Alamos National Lab, and we're building Salem Robotics.\
**TLDR:** Our software turns robots into independent survey and inspection workers at your facility.

[Launch Video](https://youtu.be/7xObOE6knZM)

## **Life and death pain worth $Millions/year**

At every nuclear facility, highly trained radiation-protection teams spend hours each day walking the site, filling out hand-drawn maps, and searching for something life-threatening: radiation. IN THE BEST CASE they find nothing, and still have to return to their posts to transcribe the data into a computer before doing the actual high-value work they were assigned. These surveys are time-consuming, dangerous, expensive, and prone to data inconsistencies that carry direct regulatory consequences.

The same pain exists well beyond nuclear. Whether it's gas-leak inspection or ammonia surveys, similar workflows run across oil, gas, chemical, biological, space, and other hazardous facilities.

## **What we do**

An operator defines the work from a simple dashboard; the robot then navigates the site, handles instruments, opens doors, turns valves, collects measurements, and generates structured, auditable, compliance-ready reports. We're hardware-agnostic, so plants run our software on robots they already own, many of which sit in a closet today as "$200k paperweights, " or we can provide the right robot for the job. Our stack is designed for safety-critical infrastructure and comes with theoretical safety guarantees, exactly what regulators and plant leadership require. Our core manipulation framework was not possible before and is based on **breakthrough founder research** published and presented at the most prestigious IEEE journals and conferences in the world. 

We're already in active contract-scoping conversations across the nuclear industry and oil & gas.

**Our asks**

* Intros to operations or innovation leaders in nuclear or similar hazardous sites (oil, gas, chem, bio, space).
* Advice from founders who've sold into safety-critical industrial environments.
* Sites where routine surveys are frequent, hard to staff, or particularly painful? We'd love to hear about them.

launches.title: Caution: Hosting platform for software you can't afford to have hacked
launches.tagline: Deploy to secure enclaves in minutes, isolate sensitive workloads, cryptographically prove what code is running.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We're [Anton Livaja](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alivaja/), [Lance Vick](https://lance.dev), and [Ksenia Lesko](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ksenialesko/) from [Caution](https://caution.co).

**TL;DR:** Caution is a hosting platform for software you can't afford to have hacked. Your software and data Istay protected even if your CI/CD pipeline, host infrastructure, or a developer laptop gets compromised. You go from source to a verifiable deployment in three commands. 

**Built for:** payment processors, PHI processors, AI agents, policy and fraud engines, secrets management, and other sensitive workloads.

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1u-l2TSBQO2t5dbhBsatCkZf5earCTyDD](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1u-l2TSBQO2t5dbhBsatCkZf5earCTyDD/view?usp=sharing)

### **Why we built this**

On February 21, 2025, attackers stole **$1.5 billion** worth of Ethereum from Bybit, the largest digital heist in history. They never breached Bybit's own infrastructure: North Korea's Lazarus Group compromised a single developer machine at Safe{Wallet}, Bybit's multisig provider, and injected malicious JavaScript into the signing interface. Bybit's team approved what looked like a routine transfer and handed over a cold wallet to the attackers. The code everyone trusted was not the code that was running.

This keeps happening because nearly all software runs on blind trust:

* trust in the cloud host
* trust in production admins
* trust in CI/CD
* trust that the code you reviewed is the code actually running

If any part of that chain is compromised, an attacker can read your secrets, tamper with your business logic, or quietly run code your team never reviewed. It's the same failure behind SolarWinds and Codecov: tampered code arriving through a trusted channel, passing every check. Caution exists to shrink that attack surface and make the most sensitive systems verifiable.

### **Caution proves exactly what's running on your server**

Cryptographically, and in real time. Deploying into secure enclaves normally takes a specialist team and months of integration. Caution automates the entire flow: source to verifiable deployment in minutes, with three commands:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108800&key=user_uploads/3654857/f3161435-2a97-4207-915a-96375a72be82)

**🎥** [Watch Anton walk through the platform](https://caution.co/platform-tour.html)

Under the hood, **Caution is a verifiable confidential compute platform:** hardware-backed cryptography isolates your workloads, preserves data privacy, and proves what software is running on a server in real time. The entire platform is open source, so verification never requires trusting us. In practice, this eliminates entire classes of attacks out of the box:

* **Build & CI/CD tampering**: reproducible, multi-party signed builds mean injected code can't pass as a legitimate release.
* **Infrastructure & insider compromise**: a compromised cloud account, admin, or laptop can't silently swap what's running.
* **Runtime data theft**: data is processed in hardware-isolated enclaves, unreadable even to the host, the cloud provider, or us.

Caution guards against everything but first- or third-party code bugs: if the release you approve has a flaw, that's what runs. Nothing can be added, no fix can be stripped out, and every patch is provably live.

### **Why now**

With advances in AI, attacks that used to require rare, expensive expertise are now cheap and scalable, and the gap between a vulnerability existing and being exploited is collapsing toward zero. Reactive patching was already losing. It can't win a race against automated attackers.

In the post-Mythos world, the security model has to flip. Infrastructure can no longer assume it won't be compromised. It has to be built to stay secure even when the host, the pipeline, or individuals with privileged access are compromised, and to prove, cryptographically, that it has. That's what Caution does.

Caution is a general-purpose platform: if it runs on CPU or GPU, it can run verifiably on Caution. We're starting where trust failures cost the most, but we believe verifiable compute will become the default way software runs, the same way HTTPS became the default way it's served.

### **Why us**

[Anton](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alivaja/) and [Lance](https://lance.dev) have spent their careers securing some of the most security-critical systems in the world: BitGo, Ledn, Turnkey, OpenZeppelin, and Unit 410 (later acquired by Coinbase). Across hundreds of engagements, from hedge funds to critical grid operators, the systems we've helped secure hold more than **$600B** in digital assets. [Ksenia](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ksenialesko/) spent years helping enterprises adopt new technology, and now leads go-to-market, customer education, and operations at Caution, turning deep security engineering into a product companies can understand, buy, and use.

We've been the people companies call in when this class of attack hits. Teams needed stronger guarantees against supply chain and runtime attacks, but existing solutions were too hard, too bespoke, or too expensive. So we built the platform we kept wishing existed.

### **Traction**

Caution is in production and onboarding customers spanning crypto infrastructure, blockchain labs, digital asset lending, consumer hardware, post-quantum security, and private AI inference.

We support AWS Nitro Enclaves today. Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP, TPM 2.0, NVIDIA Confidential Computing, and broader cloud support is in active development and coming soon.

### **Our ask**

If you're running software where sensitive data must stay private or business logic can't be tampered with, we'd love to help you level up your security. [Book 20 minutes with us](https://caution.co/contact.html) or email us at [founders@caution.co](mailto:founders@caution.co).

We'd especially love to hear from you if you're a:

* security team that wants proof, not promises, from your infrastructure
* fintech running payments, policy, or fraud engines
* crypto custodian, exchange, or wallet team that can't afford another Bybit
* healthcare or AI company processing PHI or other regulated data
* team giving AI agents production credentials and losing sleep over it
* company using AI inference with sensitive data

You can also learn more on our [blog](https://caution.co/blog.html), and follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/cautionco/) and [X](https://x.com/CautionHosting) for updates.

launches.title: Executor — One place to connect your agents to everything
launches.tagline: Connect your tools once and every agent has them, with permissions you control
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Executor is your tool gateway. Connect every service and every account once, set per-tool permissions, and any MCP-compatible agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, whatever ships next) reaches all of it through one endpoint. Try it at [executor.sh](https://executor.sh).

https://youtu.be/NWYFpDW02Dw

## The problem

You don't have one agent anymore. You have Claude Code, a ChatGPT account, Cursor, maybe a box in the corner running jobs overnight. Three problems follow:

1. **Every agent wants its own OAuth into everything.** You connect your calendar to the tenth harness in a slightly different way, tokens expire, connectors deprecate, and each agent is missing something when you need it.
2. **Most connectors stop at one account per service.** One Google login means your agent sees your work calendar or your personal one, never both. Your flights land in one inbox, your meetings in the other, and no agent can reason over your actual day.
3. **Permissions are an afterthought.** Once an agent holds a token, it can do anything that token allows. Giving an agent your email shouldn't mean trusting it to never hit delete.

## What Executor does

Connect once in Executor, and sever all the one-off connections.

Each integration gets credentials plus a per-tool policy: **always allowed**, **needs approval**, or **blocked**. Point any MCP-compatible agent at Executor and it has everything.

- **All your accounts, not just one.** Accounts are connections: work and personal Gmail, two calendars, a staging and a production Stripe, side by side. Every agent sees all of them.
- **One tool shape.** MCP, OpenAPI, and GraphQL integrations all normalize into a consistent name + schema. 1,600+ tools collapse into a single ~1k-token surface instead of ~280k tokens of tool definitions.
- **Safe by default.** Executor preserves operation semantics (GET vs DELETE, destructive hints, GraphQL mutations), so agents auto-run safe operations and ask before risky ones.
- **Sandboxed execution.** Tool calls run in an isolated JavaScript sandbox; secrets are injected host-side, so the model never sees a raw token.
- **Team-ready.** Per-user and shared credentials. Onboard the team once, not per agent per person.

Because enforcement lives in Executor rather than in any agent framework, you can adopt whatever new agent ships next week without re-thinking data access. You keep everything first-party connectors offer and gain what they don't: multiple accounts per service, per-tool policies, and one place to see and revoke access.

## How to use it

- **Local:** open-source (MIT) desktop app and CLI, everything stays on your machine
- **Self-hosted:** a Dockerfile that lets your team own all its data
- **Executor Cloud:** hosted, nothing to manage

## Traction

- 2,800+ GitHub stars, ~14k npm downloads/week, ~3,000 users on the local version

## Background

Solo technical founder, previously at Vercel. Before Executor I built [answeroverflow.com](https://www.answeroverflow.com) and grew it to 1.5M monthly users as a solo dev, bootstrapped.

## Asks

1. **Try it and tell me where it breaks.** [executor.sh](https://executor.sh) has a "Copy prompt" setup you can paste into your agent to get started.
2. **Intros:** if your team (or one you know) is drowning in per-agent integration setup, I'd love an intro: rhys@executor.sh
3. **Star the repo:** [github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor](https://github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor)
4. **Want a walkthrough?** Grab a time: [cal.com/rhys-sullivan/executor-chat](https://cal.com/rhys-sullivan/executor-chat)
