launches.title: TareBio: Vaccines for any cancer or infection in weeks
launches.tagline: We make personalized or population-level vaccines reverse-engineered from the immune system. We have already cured cancer in mice and are vaccinating our first patient within the year.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Our platform develops **personalized** or **population-level** vaccines for **_any_ disease** in weeks by **changing _only one input_**: the immune imprint. Instead of trying to predict which antigens might work, we read out immune cells already fighting the disease in the body and reverse-engineer antigens that activate them. We've already run our platform end-to-end and created a vaccine that cured cancer in mice. We will be vaccinating our first patient within the year.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108804&key=user_uploads/431020/46cdbd4d-72d9-4231-a781-01a886dd82a4)

View our launch video here: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ty7jA8ecY2o>

**The vaccine bottleneck**

For 200+ years, vaccines have been designed using the same workflow: study a pathogen or tumor, _predict_ which antigens might trigger protection, vaccinate, and hopefully generate a good immune response. This works for simpler infections. It has struggled for decades on complex diseases like HIV, TB, Hep C, and nearly _every cancer_. Currently, vaccine design is treated as a prediction problem.

**What we do differently**

Instead, we treat it as a readout problem. The **immune system has _already solved_** antigen selection in the body, it knows what it's responding to and the best immune cells for the job. So, we flip the whole process around:

1. Capture the immune cells already responding to a cancer or infection, the "**immune imprint**"
2. Use this imprint to directly identify, or “**reverse engineer**”, activating antigens
3. Build a **vaccine** from those antigens

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108804&key=user_uploads/431020/31744f0e-4a44-4aa9-aa2e-29d174a8d30a)

The same platform works for **_any_ disease** by changing one input: the immune imprint. Function over prediction, no constrained search space, and the output is a vaccine that can generate durable immunity in the body, not a transient antibody conjugate or cellular therapy.

**Proof**

We built the full platform in mice and ran it end-to-end: identified antigens from the immune imprint of the cancer, designed a vaccine from them, and **cured lymphoma in mice.** Nothing about the technology is specific to lymphoma, it generalizes to any cancer or infection. We are using our technology to create both personalized (n=1) and population-level vaccines.

**Why us**

I'm Eta Atolia, founder and CEO. I built this platform over the last 8 years as part of my MD-PhD at UCLA-Caltech with funding from The Gates Foundation. Before this, I did my undergrad at MIT with most of my time dedicated to cancer immunotherapy and infectious disease research at the Koch and HMS. Our scientific advisory board includes Darrell Irvine, PhD (Vice Chair of Immunology at Scripps, Former MIT Professor of 22 years, world-renowned vaccine engineer) and Manish Butte, MD, PhD (Chief of Immunology at UCLA and expert rare disease clinician).

**Our ask**

We are actively working with organizations and individuals to create both population-level vaccines and personalized treatments.

Helpful things as we build:

* If you have **patient tumor** **or** **blood samples**, please reach out.
* Intros to **biotech + pharma** and **vaccine teams** for partnerships.
* **Immunologists, oncologists, infectious disease specialists,** and **ML engineers** who want to build this with us.

If any of this resonates, reach out at [contact@tarebio.com](mailto:contact@tarebio.com).

launches.title: Omanta: A personal research lab dedicated to each patient.
launches.tagline: A research lab, for one.
launches.body:
Hey YC! We're Alfredo and Ranad, the founders of Omanta.

**TL;DR: Omanta creates a personalized research lab around a single patient. We integrate a patient’s complete medical record, personal genomics, and use AI to take on the most complex cancer cases. Our researchers tackled GitLab co-founder Sid Sijbrandij’s case, helping bring him into complete remission.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AwMthrNP7Bs>

\
**Why this matters**\
If you're a cancer patient, you'd think the hardest cases have entire teams dedicated to solving them. The reality: most doctors have about 20 minutes per patient, while the science never stops moving. New discoveries emerge every day, yet reaching standard clinical care can take over a decade (\~17 years on average). Physicians make high-stakes decisions with limited time, and even the most difficult cases rarely have anyone whose full-time job is to interrogate every layer of that one patient's disease and push the newest science toward their treatment.

That's the gap we built Omanta to close.\
\
**What we do**\
We meet patients wherever they are in their journey. We integrate their complete medical record and personal genomics with AI and clinical evidence to understand the molecular drivers of their disease. Then we map every existing therapy against their biology, and if the right therapy doesn't exist, we build it, from cancer vaccines and immunotherapies to highly targeted radioligand therapies.\
\
We've worked on some of the most complex cancer cases in the world. Most notably, **Alfredo was the genomics lead for the personalized therapeutic campaign behind GitLab founder Sid Sijbrandij's complete remission**, partnering with leading institutions to pursue personalized mRNA/DNA vaccines, CAR-T programs, drug repurposing, expanded-access therapies, and continuous molecular monitoring. We've seen what becomes possible when the full force of modern science is organized around a single person, and Omanta brings that depth of investigation to every case.\
\
**Why us**\
We met eight years ago working on early CRISPR cancer research and have been building toward this ever since.

* **Alfredo Gonzalez, PhD (CEO)** — translational genomics. Led the year-long investigation of 25TB of sequencing and molecular data for Sid Sijbrandij, key missing information in existing genomic reports, and uncovered actionable findings that reshaped his therapeutic strategy, including personalized mRNA/DNA vaccines, CAR-T, expanded access, drug repurposing, and continuous monitoring. PhD at UCLA, where he built one of the world's largest centralized multi-omic datasets for rare tumors. Previously at the Broad Institute (Cancer Dependency Map, validating targets from large-scale CRISPR screens) and Harvard's Wagers Lab.
* **Ranad Humeidi, PhD (CSO)** — chemical biologist. Earned her PhD in Chemical Biology from Harvard in three years, where she identified a druggable mechanism in ulcerative colitis that became the basis of a multimillion-dollar GSK collaboration. Built and directed a multimillion-dollar scientific program centered on a single rare-cancer patient, then went on to direct scientific strategy for 12+ medically complex patients after standard options were exhausted. At the Broad, she co-created and co-led a fellowship turning scientific discoveries into companies.

\
**Our ask**

* Intros. If you or someone you love is facing a difficult cancer diagnosis, we want to hear from you.
* We're also looking to connect with physicians who want a dedicated research team behind their most complex cases.
* Reach us here on Bookface or at [alfredo@omanta.com](mailto:alfredo@omanta.com) & [ranad@omanta.com](mailto:ranad@omanta.com).

History’s greatest ages are named after materials (Stone Age, Bronze Age, Iron Age, Silicon Age, etc.). The next great age is ours to make together.\
\
<https://youtu.be/ysIdrc7mowM>
\
**TL;DR:** We are a team of Stanford, MIT, and Harvard researchers discovering breakthrough materials by training frontier models on decades of unpublished experimental data. **We've already discovered a novel material and drafted a manuscript for publication.**

Industrial R&D teams use us to find scalable application-specific materials that frontier models can't predict. Academic labs turn decades of unpublished data into new papers, citations, and commercialization revenue with us.

**What we do**

We are uncovering novel materials that help industry improve performance at scale and stay top of new regulations. launches.title: Amorphic Labs - Agentic, Personalized Product Demo Videos for Sales
launches.tagline: AI agents that create personalized demos at scale for outbound, inbound, and call follow-ups without your team recording a thing.
launches.body:
**tl;dr: We build AI agents that create personalized product demo videos for outbound, inbound qualification, and post-call follow-ups. Just give us a demo account for your app and a list of prospects, and our agent researches each prospect, uses its own computer to record a tailored workflow in your app with seeded personalized data, then edits and narrates the video so it is ready to send as a link to each prospect.**

**Launch Video:**

<https://youtu.be/uq9LyHYYyOU>

**Our Ask:**

* If you’re a founder or part of a startup that sells software, we can help you give every prospect a tailored product experience while saving your team hours of recording time. Book a demo at [amorphiclabs.com](http://amorphiclabs.com)!
* If you know any sales or RevOps leaders, we would love introductions or referrals to them.

**The Problem:**

Recording a personalized product demo is one of the clearest ways to communicate your value and show someone how your product solves their problems, but preparing a demo environment, seeding data, and recording a high-quality video for every prospect takes too long. As a result, teams skip personalized demos in situations where they could be highly effective, such as outbound, and spend hours every week creating them for inbound requests and post-call follow-ups. This means teams miss opportunities to show prospects exactly how their product fits their needs, while wasting hours that could have been spent talking to and selling to prospects.

**The Solution:**

We use AI agents to create personalized product demo videos at scale, bringing tailored demos to parts of the sales process where they were previously too time-consuming to produce. All you need to provide is a demo account for your app and a list of prospects.

Our agent then:

* Learns and interacts with your app on its own computer like a real sales engineer.
* Researches each prospect to determine which workflow and data best fit their needs.
* Seeds personalized data in your app.
* Records itself completing the relevant workflow.
* Edits the video to remove long waits and adds effects such as zooms.
* Narrates the video with a script tailored to the prospect.
* Gives you a finished video link ready to send.

You remain fully in control of how the videos are created: you can clone your own voice, define the workflows the agent can choose from, control the narration style and how each video begins and ends, and regenerate videos by giving the agent feedback.

**Sample video our agent generated:**

<https://youtu.be/QONd3u3NoGo>

**Where you can use it:**

Tailored Outbound: You can import a list of leads you want to reach out to and ask our agent to create personalized demos for each one, showing prospects exactly how your product fits their needs through data, workflows, and narration tailored directly to them.

Qualifying Inbound: Add a request-a-demo form to your landing page so prospects who are not yet convinced enough to spend 30 minutes on a discovery call can spend 20 seconds requesting a personalized demo video and receive an email showing exactly how your product solves their problems.

Call Follow-ups: After understanding a prospect’s key use cases and pain points during a discovery call, you can create multiple personalized demo videos showing how you address their needs. You can even create additional videos tailored to different stakeholders that your champion can use to sell your product internally.

We are initially focused on sales, but the same technology can also create walkthrough videos for onboarding, customer support, and documentation.

**Our team:**

We have been best friends for close to a decade, have competed together in competitions spanning math, debate, pitching, business, and hackathons, built countless projects, and are now building Amorphic Labs together.

Frank worked as a software engineer for three years while graduating from UW. He was a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI and previously interned at Two Sigma, NVIDIA, and Amazon.

Dylan was a quantitative trading intern at UBS and recently graduated from Georgia Tech. He represented Team China twice at WSDC, was a grand finalist and the eighth-best speaker in the world in 2022, and co-authored a paper published at NeurIPS.

**If you sell software and want to see what our agent could create for one of your prospects, book a demo at [amorphiclabs.com](http://amorphiclabs.com).**

launches.title: Buildbox: Agent analytics for real user outcomes
launches.tagline: Find the user-facing agent failures hidden behind successful traces and evals.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** An agent can pass its evals and look healthy in traces while still failing to help users complete important tasks. Buildbox identifies those failed user journeys, ties them to business outcomes, and tests better agent behaviors and interaction patterns. Product teams get evidence-backed fixes they can review and ship.

**Ask:** If you’re building a customer-facing AI agent, we’ll help you find the agent failures you haven’t seen yet. Book 20 minutes with us:[ ](https://cal.com/marknour/20min)[cal.com/team/buildbox/discovery](http://cal.com/team/buildbox/discovery)

[www.youtube.com/watch?v=Er_CW5WS6Lw](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Er_CW5WS6Lw)

**The problem:** the most expensive agent failures rarely look like errors.

Your agent can return an answer, produce a normal-looking trace, and pass its evals while still failing to help the user. If someone has to ask the same question three times, repeatedly redirect the agent, and eventually abandon the task, was the agent actually successful?

Today, teams uncover these failures by manually reading conversations, watching sessions, checking product analytics, and comparing what they find against their most important business metrics. By the time a pattern becomes obvious, many more customers have already experienced it.

**Our solution:** Buildbox is agent analytics built around user outcomes.

Buildbox analyzes the full user journey to find where agents create friction, fail to complete a task, or leave users without the outcome they came for. It turns these breakdowns into recurring, measurable patterns, showing product teams how often they occur, who they affect, and what they cost the business in terms of activation, conversion, and retention.

For the failures that matter most, Buildbox tests better agent behaviors and interaction patterns. Teams get the underlying evidence and a validated fix they can review and ship.

If you’re shipping a new agent feature before it has real traffic, Buildbox can test it against realistic user tasks and find failure points before users encounter them.

**Who we are** 

We’re [Mark](http://www.linkedin.com/in/marknour) and [Trishala](http://www.linkedin.com/in/trishalajain7), the founders of Buildbox (YC S26). We met as undergrads at UC Berkeley and have been building together for three years. 

Before this, we worked at Netflix, Google, Amazon, and MongoDB. Across different engineering & product teams, we saw the same pattern: companies had plenty of signals & observability, but finding the issues that actually mattered and turning it into a fix still took a lot of manual detective work.

We think agents make that gap more consequential.

launches.title: Rasyn: One place to run any Chemistry task
launches.tagline: Towards a General Intelligence for Chemistry

**Hey! Ansh, Ayush and Daood here.**

We're **Rasyn**, and we built a platform called **Marigold**. \
**Here's the team:** \
**Ansh** studies Physics at Caltech, worked at NASA JPL, and researched with scientists from Nvidia and Deepmind. **Ayush** has worked on softwares serving 50 million users, and his research was used by frontier AI labs including OpenAI and Meta. **Daood** studies Computational Chemistry at Caltech, has done Total Synthesis for 4+ years, and researched alongside Nobel Laureates, so he has faced these problems firsthand. He'd lose hours deciding which tool to call next, moving outputs between disconnected tools, and running a single program at a time.

**Problem:** \
Chemistry has countless software. There's one for predicting a structure, another for proposing a route, another for reading a spectrum. None of them talk to each other, so you're stuck feeding outputs between them; this clerical work is where the time goes, none of which is science.

**Solution:**\
We tried coding agents first. They're built to write software, so a chemistry task gets handled as a scripting problem and the chemistry goes unverified. Marigold checks between steps and stops when something doesn't hold.

It runs on its own machine, so it installs and executes what it needs. It works with the tools chemists already use, submits jobs to your cluster, and runs on whatever model endpoint you have, so your data can stay in the building. In the demo we hand it four thousand compounds and ask which are worth screening. It does the whole thing itself.

Longer term we're building toward a general intelligence for chemistry. Marigold today reasons over existing tools, and that's where we start.

**The Ask:**

This is only the first version; it will break. And we'd like it to break in front of chemists, so if you run any sort of chemistry, please try it and tell us where it falls over. 

We'd also love intros to any lab doing chemistry, computational or wet, since we want to sit down and work through a real problem with people. 

Happy to answer any questions!

launches.title: Molagri: Resistance-free pesticides 🪲
launches.tagline: Species-specific biopesticides built from engineered insect viruses, updatable the moment pests develop resistance.
launches.body:
**TLDR:** We build next-generation pesticides from engineered insect virus-like particles. They target a single pest species, stay safe for humans, pollinators, and the environment, and can be reprogrammed over time as pests evolve resistance.

Pesticides underpin modern agriculture and food security, accounting for $80B in annual spend. Without effective pesticides, we can't grow enough food.

**The Problem 🌱**

Pests are developing resistance faster than new pesticides can be invented to replace the failing ones. At the same time, regulators are banning core active ingredients over environmental and human toxicity. Farmers are losing tools from both ends at once.

**Our Solution 🪲**

We build pesticides out of insect virus-like particles. We start with a virus that only infects insects and is harmless to humans. We strip out its genome so it can't infect or replicate, and we keep the empty protein shell as a delivery vehicle.

We engineer that shell with two parts:

* A **targeting element** that recognizes a single pest species (or a set of species). This is what keeps the product species-specific and invisible to humans, pollinators, and beneficial insects.
* A **payload** that kills the pest.

Both parts are swappable. Changing the targeting element will modify which pest it kills. Changing the payload will result in a new kill mechanism for the same pest, which is how we update the product when resistance appears.

Designing for true pollinator safety is hard, so we did the underlying science ourselves. We solved a cryo-EM structure of a key receptor in honey bees, which lets us deliberately engineer our targeting elements so they do not bind pollinators.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108796&key=user_uploads/2273508/62f4362a-1938-4843-ab26-c9a62c742a84)

**Why Us? 🧑🏽‍🔬**

We are Zaky and Min, viral structural biology PhD candidates and lab mates at the University of Toronto, where we have worked together for the past 6 years studying how viruses interact with their hosts. We have published in Nature Microbiology and Nature Communications, and Min holds the world record for the highest-resolution structure of a coronavirus spike protein.

**Traction 📈**

We have signed our first grower LOI, have more in the pipeline, and produced our first set of viruses for testing. During the batch we also solved a cryo-EM structure of a honey-bee receptor that directly informs our pollinator-safe design.

**Connect with us!**

* **Growers and producers**: if you are fighting resistant pests or losing tools to bans, we would love to talk about your crops and target pests. Reach us at [molagri.com](http://molagri.com) 
* **Everyone else:** intros to ag and crop-science operators, or anyone who has built regulated biological products, are always welcome.

launches.title: Lamb Labs: Custom Chips for AI Inference
launches.tagline: Co-designed models and silicon: we hardcode the model architecture into chips targeting 20,000+ tokens per second and 63x higher intelligence per watt.
launches.body:
**Hi Everyone!** 

**We’re Niki and Thomas - cofounders of Lamb Labs.**  

**TL;DR: We build custom AI inference chips that run inference at 20,000+ tok/s and 63x higher intelligence per watt than a traditional GPU. Fully local and private by construction, no subscriptions, no API costs.** 

**Our mission: the world’s fastest LLM at the lowest power.** 

<https://youtu.be/MhhY1Dy9ltE?feature=shared>

**Our hot take: AI models are finally getting good enough to hardcode them directly into silicon.** Once you stop treating the chip as a general-purpose GPU and burn a specific model into hardware, inference gets radically faster and cheaper per watt. Most of the industry is still building flexible, general chips. We think that flexibility is exactly what's wasting your energy. So we’re on a mission to reduce the energy footprint of AI. 

**The Problem**

AI is taking power on two fronts: concentrating control of data and intelligence, and consuming ever more electricity to grow. That future scares us, so we're building against it.

Here's the technical root of the waste: **GPUs burn most of their energy during inference moving data, not computing.** LLM/VLM inference is memory-bound, fetching a weight from memory costs \~100–1000x the energy of the arithmetic you do with it. So you underutilize the GPU you paid for: some GPUs only hit 20–40% compute utilization during LLM inference while the rest idles waiting on memory.

Cloud hosting adds its own tax: expensive per-token bills, latency you can't control, network dependencies, and your data leaving your control.

**Our Solution**

We build the model and the chip together. 

The Hardware Layer

* **Custom architecture, RL-tuned.** We built an RL environment that co-designs the chip architecture for a given model, optimizing directly for speed and energy per token.
* **Aggressive quantization.** Removes complex math, which shrinks the size and cost of the chip.
* **Weights on-chip.** The model weights live where the compute is overcoming the memory-bandwidth bottleneck

 

Because everything is hardcoded, it's fully local and secure by construction. No connectivity dependency, nothing leaves the device.

The Software Layer 

Designing the chip led us to solving a fundamental flaw in LLMs so we are now open-sourcing a new model next week, converted from another open source model, to run 2x faster on any hardware. Come back next week for part 2 of our launch to find out more….

**Our Ask**

If you answer "yes" to any of these, we'd love your help:

* **Are you paying for inference in watts, not just dollars?** Neocloud or private DC operators who are power- or hardware-cost-bound rather than demand-bound, talk to us.
* **Do you need inference where the cloud isn't an option?** Private AI deployments, regulated, air-gapped, sovereign, or bandwidth-starved deployments.
* **Do you want to deploy the fastest AI models in your stack?** High frequency trading, agentic workflows 
* **Are you stuck on a thermal or battery budget?** Robotics, wearables, consumer AI hardware where a Jetson-class part is over-provisioned and runs too hot.
* **Can you introduce us to anyone above?** Warm intros are the single most useful thing.

Contact us at [contact@lamb-labs.com](mailto:contact@lamb-labs.com)

launches.title: Slashy - start saving 2 hours a day on email
launches.tagline: Slashy drafts replies in your voice, schedules meetings, and handles follow ups, so you spend less time managing email, and more time on what matters
launches.body:
Hey everyone we’re Harsha and Dhruv from Slashy. Our goal is to define the next generation of email, by building an email platform that actually works for you, and learns over time. \
\
**TLDR:** Slashy is the next big email platform after Superhuman, the first with an assistant built in. Slashy can do everything from writing drafts in your tone, texting you when an important email comes in, prepping you for calls, to the things you expect from a true email client like keyboard shortcuts, open tracking, a mobile app and more. All while continuously learning about you and your preferences, so it only gets better over time. The average user takes 5 minutes to get set up and saves an extra hour a day. Read an independent review from Tom’s guide (1m+ subscribers) [here](https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/slashy-is-the-ai-email-app-replacing-notion-mail-heres-why).

You can get started for free at [slashy.com](http://slashy.com), and use our YC deal for a long-term discount.

**Launch Video:** <https://youtu.be/o2TN-wwCYm8>

## **Problem**

Most founders we speak to, have one of two problems (sometimes both)

1. They spend too much time manually handling email, and not enough building their company.
2. They don’t spend enough time on email, and lose important deals/hires due to things slipping.

## **Solution**

That’s why we built Slashy, the first email platform that reliably gets work done for you, whether it be drafting emails, notifying you when a prospect replies, schedule meetings, or more. Slashy works wherever you work best, so onboarding is seamless (just ask some of our users). It takes 10 minutes to set up, and saves the average email power user an extra one hour a day. It does this by:

1. **Doing all the basic things right:** Stuff like keyboard shortcuts, open tracking, unified inbox, team comments, availability links, all come part of Slashy. So you don’t lose anything transitioning from Gmail, Superhuman, Front and more. ([@Jayme Hoffman](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/60463) actually switched to Slashy being surprised just that a new email client could match the speed, shortcuts of something like Superhuman)
2. **Writing drafts that sound like you:** Claude drafts sound like slop because they just look at the thread. Slashy does a lot more, it looks at the linkedin/web of recipients, past emails you’ve sent, past changes you’ve made to prior drafts, and more including using our own custom-built memory system for email. (Fun fact we have a special tool for handling suggesting times/scheduling as base llms are very bad at this). ([@Michelle Marcelline](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/379052) pretty much just hits send on all her Slashy drafts with minimal edits)
3. **A powerful sidebar:** Slashy comes with a cursor-like sidebar. That lets you do things like search, draft, schedule and more. So you no longer need to keep flipping between ChatGPT and your email. ([@Yahia Bakour](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2538368) loves this to power thorugh drafts and replies)
4. **Integrations:** Slashy connects to not just your email, but your meeting notes (Granola, Fathom, Circleback, etc.), crm (Attio, Hubspot, Salesforce, etc.), Notion and more since the context to handle email isn’t just in email. ([@Pavlos Markesinis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2511438) loves how Slashy connects to his Attio and makes life simple)
5. **Automations:** The best assistants also know when to handle things in the background. So Slashy can also automatically do things like prep you for calls, text you when an important email comes in, and more. ([@Owen Botkin](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2579867) relies on Slashy to prep him from calls, and [@Pranav Madhukar](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1531197) doesn’t even check his email anymore unless Slashy alerts him an email comes in)
6. **iMessage/Slack Bot:** One of the worst parts of traditional clients? You need to open them to see if something important comes in. Slashy can ping you on text/slack so you don’t even need to context switch. (@devansh is one of our bigger Slack fans, while [@Abhinav Gopal](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/979064) for iMessage).
7. **Voice:** Sometimes it’s easier to speak your mind than write (or you’re driving and just can’t haha). So Slashy lets you dictate your thoughts, and our AI will make it sound like a much better version of you. Or you can talk with our voice to voice agent when you’re commuting (@vishruth is one of our power users for our voice drafts).
8. **Personalized Memory:** Slashy gets better the more you use it. It keeps notes on how you write, who you talk to, when you schedule, and also it learns from every edit you made before hitting send. It even once a week goes back and rewrites its notes to better match you. After all you'd expect a human assistant to be smarter after a few months, why not your ai one. ([@Devraj Gopal](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2057015) loves how Slashy has grown to know him more and more).
9. **Natural Language Labels:** A common complaint we hear is the rise of the AI SDR, and how everyone’s inbox is inundated with emails. The problem with traditional labelling systems is they don’t adjust over time, leading to important emails getting missed. Slashy’s labelling system does, leading to a much better filtering rate, and fewer dropped balls. ([@Nazli Danis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/520906) was drowning in spam before Slashy)

## Security and Privacy

We take security/privacy as an email client very seriously.  We’ve already gotten CASA, and SOC II. We also get monthly pen-tests done by [@Casco](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/30477) to ensure our users' data is safe. None of our AI providers train on your data as well.

## Getting Started

Now if you want to get started just go to[ slashy.com](http://slashy.com), or you can book a time here if you’d like me to demo the product/ask any questions just shoot an email to [founders+ea@slashy.com](mailto:founders+ea@slashy.com), and Slashy will schedule a time that works for both of us :)

launches.title: Tracer: Fable-level AI at 1/3 the cost using open-weight models
launches.tagline: Adaptive AI systems that combine open-weight models for better answers at lower cost.
launches.body:
Hi! I’m Adam, founder of Tracer.

We built **Echo**, an adaptive AI system built entirely from open-weight models. Instead of making you choose between models, Echo decides how much compute each request needs, which models should work on it, and how their answers should be combined.

**Across our current eval mix, Echo reaches Fable-level performance at roughly 1/3 the inference cost.**

Today, Echo is strongest on math, science, and the coding benchmarks we currently cover. Multilingual and broader knowledge performance still has room to improve, while longer-horizon coding and agentic evaluations are underway.

Echo is continuously updated as we expand the model pool and improve ensembling and cross-model coordination.

<https://youtu.be/hM0NypILdgw>

## **Why we built Echo**

There are now dozens of strong models, each with different strengths, weaknesses, and prices.

We started with a simple experiment: what if you had a perfect oracle that always knew which model would perform best for each request?

The oracle was substantially stronger than any individual model in the pool.

Echo is our attempt to recover that advantage without knowing the answer beforehand.

Instead of picking one model for everything, Echo goes beyond routing and dynamically allocates compute across a pool of open-weight models behind a single interface.

## **The result**

We evaluate Echo against frontier models across reasoning, math, coding, multilingual and other benchmarks.

We measure both **quality and the actual model inference cost used to produce the answers.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108361&key=user_uploads/1217984/867cc6aa-16b8-4330-b497-c33d78e62b24)

On MATH-500, Echo reached **98.6% at $4.58**, compared with Claude Fable at **99.8% at $12.64**.

On LiveCodeBench, Echo reached **92.8% at $5.35**, compared with Claude Fable at **92.0% at $8.71**.

These results show where Echo is already strongest. LiveCodeBench is encouraging, but it does not capture the full difficulty of repository-level and agentic coding. We are currently running longer-horizon evaluations where Echo must plan, use tools, modify code, and recover from errors across multiple steps.

Those results are visible in the Eval Observatory and are active areas of improvement.

We publish the underlying evaluations, including individual answers, costs, wins, and losses:

**→[ Explore the Echo Eval Observatory](https://echo.tracerml.ai/eval?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**

## **From open source to Echo**

We first explored this idea through Tracer's open-source work: learning from real AI workloads where expensive model calls are actually necessary and where cheaper paths are enough.

The project has now crossed **1,000 GitHub stars**, with developers using and experimenting with the approach in their own AI pipelines.

Echo is the next step. Instead of optimizing individual calls with a routing layer, we're building one adaptive system that decides how intelligence should be allocated end to end.

**→ [GitHub](http://github.com/adrida/tracer)**

## **Every company’s AI traffic has a shape**

Our public evaluations test Echo across a broad mix of general tasks. Production workloads are different.

Every company has its own traffic distribution and quality requirements. Some requests genuinely need expensive frontier-level intelligence. Many don’t.

For teams that work with us, Echo can be configured to learn the structure of their workload and identify where expensive intelligence is useful and where cheaper paths are enough.

**Public Echo does not train on users’ private traces. Workload-specific learning is enabled only for teams that explicitly work with Tracer to configure it.**

We set up this optimization with each team around its workload, quality bar, and data requirements.

The goal is simple: **an AI system that continuously learns how to spend the minimum amount of inference required to maintain the quality you need.**

That means **\~3x cheaper is not necessarily the ceiling for a real production workload.**

## **Try Echo now**

Echo is publicly available through a chat UI and an **OpenAI-compatible API**.

You can try it directly, connect an existing application by changing the base URL, or plug Echo into OpenCode and other agent harnesses.

Echo is continuously updated as we improve model selection and ensembling.

**→[ Try Echo now](https://echo.tracerml.ai)**

## **We’re looking for teams with large inference workloads**

If your company is running meaningful LLM inference in production, we’d like to test Echo against your workload.

We’ll map the quality-cost frontier on your traffic and determine how much of your inference actually requires expensive intelligence.

Teams can then work with us to activate private, workload-specific optimization.

→ [**Optimize Echo for your workload**](https://cal.com/adam-rida-tracer/tracer-first-call)

## **About Tracer**

I’m **Adam Rida**, founder of Tracer. I was previously a PhD candidate at **Sorbonne University/CNRS**, where I conducted and published research in ML interpretability. Before founding Tracer, I built applied ML systems across finance, insurance, and supply chain, then grew [DeepRecall](http://deeprecall.io/) to \~**€100k ARR as a solo founder in less than 3 months**.

I’ve spent most of my career studying how models make decisions and turning that research into production systems.

**TLDR;** OpenVector turns existing cameras into an automated 24/7 workforce. Describe a task in plain English, and it auto-builds a custom vision model that takes real-time actions on a computer when it spots an event.

**Ask;** If you or someone you know runs physical operations (manufacturing, logistics, retail, security) and wants to automate visual tasks without buying new hardware, we’d love to connect!

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=36OaIJ4FPZ8>

OpenVector was founded by a team of builders and engineers obsessed with bringing self-improving visual intelligence to the physical world.

* [Andrey Gizdov](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andreygizdov/), CEO, dropped a fully-funded **PhD** scholarship from Fulbright, worth **$170,000**, with invitations at **Harvard and MIT**, where he worked on real-time vision models.

**We’ve Already Started:**

launches.title: Blaze - AI CFO for Businesses
launches.tagline: An AI CFO that pays your bills, collects your invoices, and forecasts your cash.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Blaze is an agent that runs the entire finance function for your business: pay bills, accept payments, forecast your cash flow, and keep your books current. Install it with **npx @blaze-money/cli**. Use it with your favorite agentic harness or at blaze.money/agentic-finance. ChatGPT, Claude apps, and OpenClaw plugin coming soon.\
\
Our launch video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ulOQ2cVK9Ds>

## ❌ The problem

You're a lean team busy doing more than you can handle already, and finances feel like a perpetual weight on your shoulders. You know there are bills to pay, invoices to collect on, questions you want answered. But a real finance team costs $10,000 to $20,000 a month, and you could always "do it yourself," so the problem goes on dangling, half solved, half annoyance, always taking up RAM.

What ends up happening is bills get paid late, you spend money on some $300/month marketing software your interns bought months ago without you knowing, and real problems with your vendors, payroll, and runway sneak up on you at 2am on Sunday.

We've lived this personally. As a 3 year old, super lean fintech team running all our own finances, we know what it's like trying to keep the finances afloat while doing everything else it takes to make it big. It's not like the work is rocket science. It's just constant, manual, nagging, and spread across 18 different tools that need sense making.

Until recently, you had to pay $10,000 a month to hire a finance function. We'd like to change that.

## 🛠 What we built

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108616&key=user_uploads/85958/4ef6fa06-6115-4df5-bacf-cc481a437e15)

\
Chat with Blaze from your favorite agentic harness and watch it get real things done for your finances:

* **Pay bills and contractors.** Tell it to pay the AWS bill and it finds the invoice, shows you the amount, and pays on your approval. "Send Maria $3,000 for the design work" works the same way, domestic or international.
* **Collect payments and send invoices.** "Send Acme a payment link for $12,500." Blaze creates the link, sends it, and updates you when it's paid. Draft a real invoice the same way, from a one-line request. If a client drags their feet, it follows up automatically.
* **Forecast cash.** Connects to your bank through Plaid, finds the recurring patterns, and projects your balance so you know your runway.
* **Handle the pre-accounting.** Categorizes transactions and matches them to the bills and invoices they belong to as they happen, so your actual accounting is easier when you get to it.
* **Move stablecoins.** On and off-ramps USDC across 80+ currencies, with support for cards and various local payment methods around the world.
* **Flag problems early.** Tells you about a low balance, an overdue invoice, or unusual spend before it becomes an issue.

It installs with one command:

```
npx @blaze-money/cli
```

You can use it anywhere you use AI agents. Our favorites are in Hermes on Telegram and on the dashboard at dashboard.blaze.money. There's a REST API and SDK if you want to connect it to your own systems.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108616&key=user_uploads/85958/492a039d-5aeb-4cab-bc85-33fe8f82f1c0)

## 🙏 Ask

If you are, or you know, any of the following, we'd love to hear from you.

**Founders running lean**

You're doing your own bills, invoicing, and cash flow because a real finance team costs $10,000 to $20,000 a month. Try it and tell us what breaks: **npx @blaze-money/cli** or <https://blaze.money/agentic-finance>.

**Early customers**

We're onboarding our first businesses now, and want people who'll help us decide what the agent should handle next. Especially focused on handyman and trades businesses (HVAC, repair, remodeling) and property managers, especially in the Airbnb space.

**Anyone with an intro**

To founders and small teams who'd rather not open their bank again. You can reach us at [founders@blaze.money](mailto:founders@blaze.money).

## 👥 Team

Faiyam is a full-stack engineer who dropped out of med school to build startups instead. As a founding engineer at Luc's previous startup, he helped it scale to $1m in ARR. He manages finances for Blaze, and is personally relieved he no longer needs to stay up on Sunday nights to do so.

Luc is a two-time founder. His first startup hit #1 on the App Store. Before that, he was a tech lead at Spotify and Artsy. Luc built Blaze's cross-border payment rails after living the problem firsthand, moving money in and out of Latin America.

Fun fact: Luc and Faiyam met after Faiyam "coincidentally" sat down next to him at a coffee shop in Williamsburg, New York, seven years ago. The rest is history (in the making).

Hey everyone, Pulkit and Agnay here!

**TLDR:**

Tsenta **matches** you with jobs, **rewrites** your **resume**, and **applies** for you. We built this because we applied to over 3,000 jobs as international students, and no other tool worked for us. 45,000+ people use it now, and over 70% of our paid users have landed interviews.

launches.title: machine0: Cloud Computers for Agents
launches.tagline: One command spins up a persistent VM. Your agent drives it via CLI or MCP, building its own fleet from 1 vCPU up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB and 8×H100s.
launches.body:
TLDR: machine0 is a CLI for agent compute: “machine0 new mybox” gives your agent a full cloud VM, billed by the minute, from $0.013/hr up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB and 8×H100s. Agents drive it themselves via CLI or MCP.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gyllkZ0M04E>

## The Pain

Agent workloads are moving from ephemeral to always-on. A coding agent working on a hard feature runs 6-8 hours. Auto-research agents run for days. OpenClaw & Hermes run 24/7. As you run more in parallel:

* **Resources**: a few agents on a big codebase saturate your RAM and CPU. Auto-research needs GPUs you don't have.
* **Security**: “—yolo” on your personal machine is one prompt injection away from exfiltrated credentials.
* **Availability**: close your laptop and the agent dies mid-task.
* **Isolation**: there's no clean line between everything on your laptop and the minimum this agent actually needs.

## The Solution

machine0 gives every agent its own computer. It's a CLI that both humans and agents can use without reading docs:

* “machine0 new mybox” creates an SSH-ready VM with a static IP and HTTPS endpoint. Always on (99.99% uptime) until you switch it off.
* **Billed by the minute.** 1 vCPU / 1 GB at $0.013/hr up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB, plus GPUs from RTX 4000 Ada to 8×H100s.
* **Profiles.** Bundles of MCP connections, credentials, prompts, and env vars, injected at VM creation. Each agent gets exactly the capabilities (or personality) you choose, and nothing else.
* **Agents self-serve.** Hand the CLI or MCP server to Claude, Codex, or OpenCode and it manages its own fleet: spin up a box for a build, snapshot it, tear it down.
* **Suspend & resume.** Pause an idle machine, stop paying for compute, resume exactly where it left off.
* **Snapshot & clone.** Configure one machine perfectly, then stamp out ten identical agents from it.
* **NixOS is first-class.** Declarative, reproducible machines.

## How people use it

* **Compute for your agent**: give it the CLI and it spins up its own VMs for builds, tests, and long jobs instead of grinding your laptop.
* **Hosting the agent itself**: run Claude, Codex or Hermes 24/7. Snapshot once, then clone as many as you want.
* **Swarms of agents**: an orchestrator agent spawns worker machines, farms out subtasks, and tears them down when the work is done.
* **Auto-Research on GPUs**: drop an agent on an H100 with a goal and let it run for days.

## About me

I'm a solo, second-time YC founder. I was CTO of Upflow (YC W20), where I scaled EPD post series A and personally owned DevOps, infra, and security for years because they were too high-stakes to delegate. Upflow handles sensitive accounting data for companies like Postman, ProductBoard, and Lattice, and is doing many millions in ARR.

Before that I built consumer payments at Hike Messenger (100M+ users) in India. Working with sensitive data and infra for years is what got me deep into the problems machine0 solves, security especially.

## Asks 🙏

* Try it: <https://machine0.io>
* Let's talk about your agent fleets, software factory or auto-research: [hello@machine0.io](mailto:hello@machine0.io)

launches.title: Zaplar - Replacing PMS and the Hotel Tech Stack.

launches.body:
Hi everyone, we're Axel, Oscar, Jon, and Douglas, founders of Zaplar.

**TL;DR:** Zaplar as an agentic hotel OS that replaces the fragmented hotel tech stack (PMS, booking engine, channel manager, POS, revenue management, housekeeping, and more) with one system built from the ground up for AI. We're eight people with backgrounds in hotel operations, engineering, AI research, and cybersecurity.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107463&key=user_uploads/3037509/c7720ef9-5a08-43eb-9631-4fefb2d239b6)

**Ask:** Intros to hotel owners and operators who are unhappy with their PMS, and to executives and C-suite at hotel groups planning their next core system replacement. Details at the bottom. Reach us at [founders@zaplar.com](mailto:founders@zaplar.com).

[Launch Video!](https://youtu.be/bpfJATRnYQM)

## The problem

Incumbents are bolting AI onto systems built for a different era. They provide a layer of AI to the end user, but the automations beneath it stay constrained. Their claim to use AI is correct. They just can't reason across the operation or automate work end to end.

No existing PMS or bolt-on solution gives hotels the architecture AI actually requires. And even if one did, a PMS alone still wouldn't automate hotel operations. It's one of as many as 15 systems a hotel runs, each built on a different architecture, each focused on one part of the operation, none able to act beyond its own boundaries.

AI can't run a hotel if it can't understand the hotel.

To unlock the full potential of AI, a hotel has to run on a single system with a unified architecture: one that lets AI reason across the entire property, free of the boundaries integrations create and the context each one isolates behind them. Incumbents can't build this without replacing the foundation their business depends on, and they won't.

We arrived at this the slow way. Douglas's family has spent their careers running hotels, and we first built Zaplar to solve event bookings for them. In demo after demo, hotels were already evaluating another PMS, including ones that had just switched. Even leading vendors did not make a product hotels wanted to use.

## The solution

Zaplar was built on this thesis from the start: the first truly AI-native operating system for hotels. It’s the path of most resistance, but the only way to do it right.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107463&key=user_uploads/3037509/5a0f8f2c-bcb0-4ebc-a3e1-e2c30c80baec)

Zaplar spatially maps out the entire property and its resources so that AI agents can reason across the hotel and understand how everything connects. On top of this architecture sit a PMS, POS, channel manager, booking engine, guest portal, housekeeping system, and more, with no boundaries between them. The result is an autonomous system that works in the background and completes work on its own. The system surfaces suggestions for staff to review, edit, and approve.

Our goal is to be vertically integrated. Beyond deeper automation and richer context, the greatest benefit is that we can put all our effort into staying at the forefront, because we're not constrained by what anyone else is doing. Major hotel groups are starting to replace their aging systems, and we intend to be the only option on the table designed for what comes after.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107463&key=user_uploads/3037509/ad3b8b01-9f05-41f1-877e-952a35dc8e8a)

## Our ask

**Hotel owners and operators.** If you own or operate a hotel that is unhappy with its PMS, we would love to talk directly.

**Executives and C-suite at hotel groups.** This is the intro we want most. Anyone at the VP level or above at a group, especially COOs, CIOs, CTOs, and heads of operations or commercial, and above all anyone whose group is planning a core system replacement in the next 18 months.

**Everyone else.** You do not need to know their software situation to make the intro useful. We are focused on independents, small and mid-size groups, and boutique and luxury properties. If you have stayed somewhere you loved, send us the name and we will take it from there.

Reach us at [founders@zaplar.com](mailto:founders@zaplar.com) or learn more at [zaplar.com](http://zaplar.com).

launches.tagline: An open API, IRS-authorized e-file tax engine for CPA firms and Fintechs
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: We're building a modern tax engine for accountants and fintechs building on tax: a deterministic tax calculation and e-filing core behind a single API, built on the IRS's official e-file infrastructure (MeF).**

## A tax return is math. It should be a function call.

We're Angelo and Akash, and we built Luca IQ, a new tax engine for accounting firms. One set of inputs in, a completed, filed return out in minutes. Not bolted onto decades out desktop software.

For CPA firms, that means more returns per preparer, less spend on labor, and a clean path off 30-year-old desktop software. For the PE groups acquiring and scaling firms, it means real operating leverage on the single most labor-intensive part of the business.

<https://youtu.be/IV5nl7grMxI>

**The problem.** \~95% of US firms file their returns through just four companies, and all of them were built decades ago, for the desktop, and are closed. Firms are stuck running tax season on software that can't scale with them. Every modern AI tax tool just pushes data into that same closed software it can't control. Everyone rebuilt the interface.

**What we built.** A new one, and we're opening it. A key principle: AI never does the tax math. AI and human judgment set the inputs, and a deterministic engine computes the return, with a full audit trail on every number. It's either 100% correct or it's wrong, and only a deterministic engine can promise the former. For firms, that means throughput without giving up accuracy or defensibility.

Our core leverage: we're an **IRS-authorized e-file provider as a Software Developer, Transmitter, and Intermediate Service Provider**, so Luca IQ doesn't just compute the return, it e-files straight to the IRS. That full path, calculation through filing, is what firms can't get from a closed engine today.

**Why now.** The profession is running out of people. 300,000+ accountants have left since 2019, and \~70% of CPAs are near retirement. At the same time, private equity is rolling up firms and pushing hard on margin. The work isn't going away. The people are, and the pressure to do more with fewer preparers has never been higher.

**Who we are.** Angelo (CEO) is a CPA who worked in forensic accounting with the FBI, Wall Street, EY and spent years working at tax firms using the legacy softwares we are now replacing. Akash (CTO) was employee #1 at a fintech data-infrastructure startup and leads engineering.

**What we need:**

* **CPA firms who dread tax season**, We'd love 20 minutes to show you what Luca IQ does for throughput and margin. This is who we build for.
* **PE firms rolling up accounting practices.** If tax prep labor is your biggest cost line, let's talk.
* **Developers and fintechs** who need 1040 calculations or e-filing. The engine is one API call, and you can build on it early.

Reach us at [founders@lucaiq.com](mailto:founders@lucaiq.com).

launches.title: Stoa: The market behind AI hardware
launches.tagline: GPU marketplace where vetted dealers bid blind with firm quotes. $300M+ in RFQs in our first month.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** AI hardware trades over phone calls and forwarded spreadsheets. No venue, no price to mark against: lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals. We're building Stoa, an RFQ marketplace where buyers and sellers get firm quotes within 48 hours, and settled trades build the prices the market can mark, finance, and hedge against.

<https://youtu.be/zbD21BgAo88>

GPU deals close in group chats. We know because we've been in them.

A price arrives as a voice note. Someone forwards an inventory list, then it gets forwarded again, and soon three brokers are offering the same machines. Nobody knows who actually owns what or whether any quote is firm.

The market behind those chats is worth hundreds of billions of dollars a year. Lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals, not trades.

We're Berat, Eren, and Kaan. We're building Stoa.

AI hardware is becoming an asset class, but its market is missing the basics: a venue where hardware can trade, prices that buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against, and eventually financing and hedging built on those prices. We're starting with the venue: an RFQ marketplace for GPUs. It gets buyers and sellers firm quotes, and every bid and settlement builds the history the rest needs.

**Here's how it works**

Post what you want to buy or sell: B300s, H200s, H100s, a bare card or a full cluster, new or secondary.

Vetted dealers bid blind with firm quotes. Instead of spending weeks calling around, you get through the RFQ in 48 hours.

We handle the unglamorous parts too: KYB and counterparty checks, contracts, shipping, and settlement.

In our first month, $300M+ in RFQs ran through the book.

**Why the marketplace comes first**

Ask what an H100 is worth and everyone you call gives you a different answer.

On Stoa, dealers quote against the same RFQ without seeing each other's bids. Because every RFQ, firm quote, award, and settlement runs through us, we see what the hardware actually trades for.

A quote is an opinion. A settled trade is a receipt.

That transaction history becomes prices buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against. Once marks are grounded in settled trades, financing and hedging can follow.

Platts started printing oil prices in a magazine. Kelley Blue Book began as one dealer's published list of what he'd pay for cars. GPU inventory is still being passed around in forwarded spreadsheets, and Blackwell upgrades are now pushing H100 fleets into the secondary market.

Someone is going to be the price.

**The team**

We've known each other for more than ten years. We have founded companies, traded interest rate derivatives, and built trading and pricing infrastructure for oil and gas. Now we're building it for AI hardware.

**Buying or selling?**

If you're buying GPUs or compute, or you're sitting on hardware, sign up at [stoaexchange.com](http://stoaexchange.com).

Hey YC! 👋

We’re [Luca](https://www.linkedin.com/in/luca-hadife/) and [Hosny](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohamed-hosny-hussein/), founders of [Kebra](https://kebra.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=launch&utm_campaign=yc_launch_2026).

Kebra makes field service companies AI-native.

We capture what happens in the field and put the back office on autopilot. Before the truck leaves the driveway, Kebra turns every job into complete notes, filed warranty claims, ordered parts, and follow-up sales opportunities.

We’re working with field service companies across Florida, Pennsylvania and California.

<https://youtu.be/VIwv5iVm8Ok>

## The problem

**Field service runs like it’s 2015.**

Field technicians are bad at documenting their jobs, which paralyzes the back office.

Companies juggle their Field Service Management software, CRM, calls, texts, and incomplete job reports. The office has to chase technicians for missing serial numbers and photos, reconstruct what happened, then manually file warranty claims, order parts, update customers, and prepare invoices.

Everyone is trying to automate this top-down, but it breaks. If the job is not documented correctly, AI employees are executing on an alternate reality that never happened in the field.

After working alongside technicians in the field, inside back offices, and climbing into a few 140° attics taught us one thing:

**You can’t automate what wasn’t documented.**

## Our Solution

Kebra is one platform that puts the entire field service operation on autopilot.

**Field Capture:** captures each job as it happens and collects the exact information the back office needs.

* Collects equipment details, photos, serial numbers, diagnoses, work completed, and parts used
* Catches what’s missing and calls or texts the technician to get it
* Spots potential sales opportunities

**Back Office AI Employees:** integrate with the company’s existing software and use computer-use and voice agents to complete the work that follows.

* Write complete job notes
* File warranty claims
* Automate parts ordering
* Prepare and send invoices
* Follow up on sales opportunities and open estimates

**Company Brain:** makes the field queryable.

* Remembers equipment history, past repairs, and technician decisions
* Captures the expertise of the company’s best technicians
* Connects information across existing field service systems
* Helps every future workflow run with better context

launches.body:
Cloud coding agents are painful to set up, lacking ergonomics, and don't allow you to move as fast as possible. We let you bring your local set up to the cloud.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/28db62de-d65b-4498-84ac-12e2683c65f2)

**The Problem** 

In the next 10 years the best software startups will be those who can effectively deploy tokens. 

Right now that's significantly harder than it needs to be. If you’ve ever ran multiple agents locally you immediately know this pain.

Laptop crashes, wrangling gitwork trees, juggling ports, and more headaches.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/6f320e85-ccbb-4fb4-a5e9-6ec3cb0206c7)

So cloud is the obvious answer right? 

But setting up with these existing providers is quite a hassle, and oftentimes they miss some key feature that your local config has.

**What we do**

We deploy software factories into businesses that want to **tokenmaxx** but don't have the time or the resources to set up the infrastructure.

During onboarding, we transfer all of your local sessions and MCP servers to Hoplite, meaning you can pick up right from where you left off. We also configure all the required dependencies and CLIs that your projects require, letting you see instant previews of what your agent is doing.

Our bet is that as models improve, we’re going to start caring less about the code that they output (we’ll implicitly trust it), and shift our focus towards the product itself. Hence, a platform that prioritizes iteration on product rather than code will ultimately win. 

We also have an iMessage integration so you can prompt on the go.

We installed in our first business last week and we saw an immediate result, from sentry logs going from largely ignored to fully proactive PRs when something breaks. 

They have significantly faster iteration cycles and lower priority tickets have been continuously getting merged. 

They wanted faster iterations but didn't have the infrastructure to support a software factory, so we went in and built it.

launches.tagline: Marble uses computer vision and voice AI to count inventory in minutes and a collection of AI agents that run inventory and labor management on autopilot.
launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re Arjun and Aakar, and we’re launching Marble (previously Truffle), the first AI-native operating system for the restaurant back-of-house.

**TL;DR:** We help restaurants control their two biggest costs, inventory and labor—saving them thousands of dollars per month in food waste, stockouts, and labor overage. We replace today's patchwork of disconnected point solutions, spreadsheets and clipboards with a single, easy to use system that actually does the work. We use computer vision and voice AI to count inventory 90% faster than manual counts, ML models to forecast item-level demand with 97% accuracy, and AI agents that run dozens of end-to-end workflows autonomously, including ordering, invoice reconciliation, scheduling, food prep, menu engineering, and more.

**The result**: We're live and scaling rapidly across multi-unit operations in the US and Canada. You can find us today in A&W Restaurants, The Kati Roll Company, Sophie’s Cuban, Kokomo NYC, HolyShred, Dead Letter No. 9 and many more. We’ve driven a 40% reduction in food waste, eliminated stockouts, and saved managers 30+ labor hours per week.

Check us out here:[ www.joinmarble.ai](http://www.joinmarble.ai)

**Our ask:** If you run or know someone who runs a restaurant, café, bar, or hospitality group, we'd love to talk. You can reach us at [founders@joinmarble.com](mailto:founders@joinmarble.com).

**Everyone knows someone who runs a restaurant, bar, or cafe - we’re also giving away $500 (or an Oura Ring) per referral!** [www.joinmarble.com/refer](http://www.joinmarble.com/refer) 

<https://youtu.be/Sbib-QYUH_Y> 

**The Problem**

Restaurant operators face an uphill battle. Ultra-competitive markets, rising food and labor costs, unforgiving hours, and after all of it, they take home 5% in net profit (if they're lucky).

A restaurant can be full all day and night, but it's the back office operations that determine whether that money hits the bottom line. Today that back office still runs on clipboards, spreadsheets, and guesswork. Inventory gets counted by hand, if at all, so no one has a real-time picture of what's actually on the shelf. Orders get placed from memory, so operators either over-buy (contributing to $150B+ in annual food waste) or under-buy and stock out on the exact items guests came for. Food prep and schedules are built on best-effort guesses, and invoices go unchecked while suppliers quietly raise prices line by line.

Every one of these is a margin decision, and every one is being made blind, leading to errors that compound every day, across every location.

**The Solution**

Marble runs the entire back office for restaurants. This centers around managing the two biggest cost centers (inventory and labor) and works in 4 phases:

* **Capture:** Computer vision + voice AI through our mobile app allow operators to count inventory 90% faster than manual counts, with 99% accuracy. No more hours spent counting items in a walk-in freezer with a clipboard (IYKYK). Invoices and deliveries are captured the same way.
* **Forecast:** ML models predict item-level demand for the weeks ahead at 97% accuracy. In addition to that, LLM-powered agents scan the signals a spreadsheet never sees - local events, weather, news, reservations, holidays - and adjust the forecast for what's actually happening around each location.
* **Act:** A set of AI agents run the workflows that actually move the needle on profitability: placing optimized orders, building demand-informed prep sheets, drafting schedules, proactively tracking and flagging waste, reconciling invoices, engineering menus, and more.
* **Learn:** This industry runs on tribal knowledge. We have built the product as a closed-loop system from day one: every count, correction, and order flows back into the platform as context that our agents carry forward, so Marble learns how each location actually runs, adapts to its patterns automatically, and gets sharper every day.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108273&key=user_uploads/1278164/1dd8a396-a754-4277-ad3b-1613bf1d4212)

**Team**

We’ve been close friends for nearly 10 years, since our freshman year at Michigan, and we're having a blast taking on this industry.

Aakar grew up managing the back office for his family's multi-unit quick service restaurants, where he saw the problem up close. He later covered the restaurant sector as an investment banker at Goldman Sachs before leaving to lead growth at an applied-AI startup in healthcare.

Arjun is a second-time founder and was previously a Senior Software Engineer at Bloomberg, where he led AI/ML initiatives on the Electronic Trading team. At Bloomberg, he built out complex trading systems that processed tens of millions of dollars daily.

launches.title: Gutgutgoose: Personalised probiotics
launches.tagline: AI training infrastructure for the gut microbiome via personalized probiotics.
launches.body:
# TL;DR: We’ve created the last probiotic you’ll ever need - personalised, constantly improving, while also generating valuable data.

### 

# What we do and why

Your gut is the most unique part of your body, different enough that the same probiotic can work for one person and do nothing for another. Most probiotics disappoint because they’re one formula for everyone, and in any gut most of their strains never establish. GutGutGoose makes a probiotic that won’t work for any gut but yours: we sequence your microbiome, find which strains can establish in the microbes you already have, compound those into your formula, and re-sequence you weeks later to confirm they took hold.

It’s for people who’ve tried things for IBS, bloating, digestion, mood, weight or GLP-1 symptoms without luck. If it doesn’t work you get your money back, and retesting shows how your gut changed, so you know it’s not a placebo.\
\
<https://youtu.be/Cn6oGduZosc>

The innovation is accurately predicting which bacteria will live in a gut, which is extremely hard. It’s built on two peer-reviewed models, MICOM and AGORA2, and more than 7,000 metabolic reconstructions of gut bacteria, and it finds the strains that can hold in your gut’s community. On two published human cohorts, its predictions matched what actually established 84.7% and 76.7% of the time, and we reproduced the first at 78.1% ourselves. Off-the-shelf products manage under 5%. Once we can control which bacteria live where, we can run precision interventions in the gut and engineer it.

We’re a supplement today and can’t treat disease, but each cycle produces a record of one gut, one intervention, and the result. That record makes each customer’s next formula better, and across thousands of people it becomes the first longitudinal dataset of the human gut responding to known, controlled changes. Our vision is to use changes in metabolic pathways over time to predict Alzheimer’s, dementia and Parkinson’s a decade before symptoms appear.

We gave a talk at an endometriosis event, and 20 of the 50 people joined our waitlist. The first night we opened paid deposits, we called five people from that list at 7:30pm. Three picked up, and we managed to get seven sign ups, they were so excited they referred and paid for their families that night. Five of the 20 referred someone else, and our traction has only grown since.

# Team

The GutGutGoose founders winning the YC product pitch

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2iEHRvcKN8g>

## **The Problem**

Most of the built world is opaque.

Pipes, cables, and structural elements hide behind walls until they're discovered mid-project, driving $20B+ a year in avoidable rework.

Defects remain hidden inside composites until parts break.

Entry teams are missing critical information before they breach a barrier.

An imaging platform that uses radio waves to see behind walls. It works just like a camera, requiring no training and producing high-resolution images that are instantly understandable. The resulting point cloud is natively to scale, accurate down to 1mm.

## **The Team**

Four engineers who've worked together for 8+ years, shipped multiple zero-to-one hardware products, and hold 250+ patents.

**Bilgehan** — PhD in electromagnetics; led antenna technologies on four iPhone generations, shipping the first phones with UWB and 5G mmWave; inventor of the zirconia dielectric resonator antenna.

Hi! We are Lucas and Paul, cofounders of Tire Swing: the AI compliance platform for Affordable Housing.

<https://youtu.be/x4qyhXXz38I>

## **The Problem**

Every Affordable Housing move-in and recertification requires applicant income verification and a strict eligibility review. In addition to the high labor costs and regulatory burden, delays in reviewing applications and thoroughly screening applicants can cause weeks of lost rental revenue.

Lost revenue on a single move-in can accumulate to thousands of dollars, and penalties for non-compliance can cost millions in credit recaptures and fines.

## **The Solution**

Tire Swing uses AI to bring compliance expertise to the point of leasing. It turns weeks of reviews and approvals into a minutes-long process. The platform:

* **Reviews evidence as it is collected.** Tire Swing processes documentation in minutes, allowing problems to be addressed before the applicant leaves the office.
* **Performs the eligibility analysis.** It calculates household income, applies all applicable property, state, and program eligibility rules, and links every finding to its supporting evidence.
* **Automates certification compliance.** Tire Swing flags missing, inconsistent, or incorrect information with steps to resolve the problem from a library of thousands of deterministic and AI driven compliance checks.

**Tire Swing means faster move-ins and recertifications, reduced consulting budget, and more consistent, audit-ready files.** 

## **Looking ahead**

We believe Affordable Housing is the first application of a much larger needs-based eligibility opportunity. Federal, state, and local governments distribute more than $1.5 trillion annually through needs-based programs including Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, utility assistance, and tax credits.

These programs share a common underlying workflow: collect documents, convert them into structured facts, apply eligibility rules, and resolve missing or contradictory information.  The administration costs for these services are approximately $20B annually.

## **The Team**

Tire Swing is founded by Paul and Lucas, college friends and Princeton computer science graduates. Prior to founding Tire Swing, Lucas worked as a software engineer at Instacart and Capital One, and Paul worked as a cybersecurity consultant at Stroz Friedberg.

launches.title: Tandem: Office broker on steroids
launches.tagline: Tandem is an AI-native office leasing brokerage.
launches.body:
**Tl;dr:** Our agents have seen every office building in the city — they know exactly what’s available, what it’s going to cost you, and how to negotiate the best possible deal. You get human support backed by the best real estate AI anywhere. And it’s all done at no cost to you. Start your search at [tandemspace.com](http://tandemspace.com)

## Why office leasing is broken

**There are thousands of office spaces in a city and no single view of them.** **What exists instead is memory.** A few hundred people, each carrying their own map of the city, built by walking it.

Those maps are good. Brokers who have been doing this for twenty years know their buildings cold, know the landlords, know what a deal should actually cost. **But it's one person's map of a market that changes every week, and there is no version of this job where one person keeps up with all of it.**

So the process runs on relays. You spend an hour explaining what you need. Your broker spends the week calling the brokers they know, who call the landlords they represent. Eight options come back. You like one. The calls start over. Nobody is doing anything wrong. It just takes days to move a question through a chain of people, and you are one of a dozen searches your broker is running at the same time.

The economics of this market were built for bigger deals. Commercial leasing grew up around full floors and ten year terms, and everything in it is sized for that. A 3,000 square foot suite on a two year term takes nearly the same work and returns a fraction of it, so smaller spaces get less attention across the board. It's why so many of them go unphotographed, unlisted, and unmentioned. That's most of the market by count.

The people in this industry are not the problem. This is just what a market looks like when it runs on memory:

**You're seeing only what your broker chooses to show you, prioritized only as much as your deal size warrants, with no way to verify you're getting a fair shake.**

## How Tandem works

On paper, Tandem is an office leasing brokerage like any other. Same license, same tenant rep fee, same person meeting you in the lobby. **The difference is what that person knows, and how quickly they can act on it.**

Every Tandem agent works with an agentic brain behind them\*\*. It's watching the market constantly: what came available this morning, what a similar unit actually leased for last month, which landlords are flexible on term, what's about to come back online.\*\* Knowing the market stops being one person's job, so it doesn't stop when they go home, and it isn't limited to the buildings they've personally walked.

What that means for you:

* **You see the whole market on day one**, not on the third callback. Your agent already knows what fits before you finish describing it.
* **Answers in minutes**, over email, text, or phone, on anything from zoning to what the freight elevator situation is.
* **You know what it should cost.** Your agent can see what comparable units actually went for, so you go into a negotiation knowing where the number should land.
* **You don't have to talk to anyone if you don't want to.** The same market is browsable at [tandemspace.com](http://tandemspace.com). Compare asking rents, book a tour for tomorrow, bring your agent in whenever you want them.
* **A 3,000 square foot requirement gets the same attention as a 30,000 one**, because your agent isn’t paid more for a bigger deal.

**The result: clients who search with Tandem see 30%+ more spaces than in a traditional search, and finish about 6x faster. At no cost to you.**

## Start your search with Tandem

We’re proud to have placed more than 500 companies into offices, including Cursor, Upwork, Apollo GraphQL. But, we’re even prouder that our average time from first tour to signed lease is 27 days, versus an industry average of \~180.

If you’re in the market for an office now or anytime in the future, get started for free at [tandemspace.com](http://tandemspace.com), or email [team@tandem.space](mailto:team@tandem.space).

launches.title: Stratum Industries - clearing the entire U.S. Government backlog
launches.tagline: AI agents that review government applications end-to-end, so backlogs that took years clear in minutes.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Stratum builds AI agents that clear the U.S. government's backlog. A reviewer drops in an application, picks the rubric to check it against, and an agent plans, executes, and reviews the file end to end. Hundreds run in parallel with a human approving every decision, so a backlog that used to take months clears in the time it took to review one file.

**The Problem**

Every permit, license, patent, drug approval, grants and benefits claim in America has to be reviewed by a government adjudicator, on software built decades before AI. The result is millions of applications stuck in queues, and real people waiting months or years: veterans on disability ratings, families on pensions, builders on permits. The approval isn't the problem. The software it runs on is.

**How Stratum Works**

1. A reviewer drops in an application and selects the rubric it needs to be checked against.
2. An agent reads every page and checks the file against that rubric.
3. Every step routes to the model that reviews it most accurately for the least cost.
4. Anything missing goes back to the applicant as one specific request.
5. The officer gets the whole file summarized, with every citation behind it, and approves or denies it.

Hundreds of these run in parallel in the cloud, with full auditability at every step, and a person always makes the final call.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108348&key=user_uploads/1648613/15e81a7e-32ca-4280-9822-bc49caed3028)

**The Vision**

In a couple of years, dealing with the government should feel as frictionless as booking an Uber or paying with Apple Pay. You tell your Stratum agent what you need, a permit, a license, a claim, and it fills out the application and submits it. On the other side, the government's Stratum agents review it, ask your agent for anything missing, and settle it between themselves. The decision comes back the same day, in minutes. No waiting weeks or months. Clearing today's backlog is only the beginning.

**Team**

We're Vihaan and Raj, brothers. Vihaan was founding engineer #3 at Cadastral (acquired by Legora) and dropped out of Waterloo to build Stratum. Raj led GTM at Deel, averaging 220% of quota over two years and ranking top 5 of 1,000+ reps globally, and dropped out of grad school at Bath to build Stratum.

launches.title: hiloop: we run thousands of experiments to improve your models
