launches.body:
We're Karan and Thomas, and we're building hiloop: **infrastructure for automated research**.

**TL;DR: we gave two stock coding agents 50 B200s and our infra. They ran 4,188 experiments in two days and beat the published state of the art on [Karpathy's autoresearch benchmark](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch). The same machinery found a [NanoGPT speedrun](https://app.primeintellect.ai/speedrun/nanogpt) candidate that beats the best known result. [See](https://hiloop.ai/blog/search-is-enough/) full writeup.**

Now we want to point it at your hardest problems.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108337&key=user_uploads/1714115/63396f7f-3e21-41ea-83ea-54cbaaa9f63f)

**The results**

On Karpathy’s autoresearch benchmark, our final recipe reached **0.9016 val_bpb**. The previous best published result was [Recursive’s 0.9109](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/first-steps-toward-automated-ai-research-recursive-si-kybtc) on B200 hardware. For NanoGPT, our implementation had **12.54% lower runtime** than upstream.

There was no bespoke research agent or elaborate scaffold. We used Claude and GPT-5.5 out of the box. What changed was the system around them.

**What hiloop does**

Give us a hard task, your current agent or model, and an evaluation criteria. Hiloop runs an autoresearch campaign across training, data, prompts, tools, harnesses, and systems, then returns the best verified improvement. It runs in your cloud or hosted by us.

We’re starting with agent and model training: SFT, post-training, continual learning, and optimization.

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Rv8HttSHZ-yvSJk6hsWQsqCXWTHJQogK](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Rv8HttSHZ-yvSJk6hsWQsqCXWTHJQogK/view?usp=sharing)

**Who we are**

We met at Reducto, where we built its ML, post-training, and platform systems. Karan previously led ML infrastructure at DynamoAI . Thomas was a founding engineer at Crosswise and an MLE at Discord and SoFi.

**Two asks**

1. **Want your models or agents better, faster, or cheaper?** If you have a hard objective in post-training, continual learning, inference optimization, or classic ML, send us the task, your baseline, and the eval. We’ll personally run a campaign with you through verified improvement.
2. **Building autoresearch or RSI loops?** Reach out to give our system a try! We’d love to compare notes.

Email [**founders@hiloop.ai**](mailto:founders@hiloop.ai) to get in touch with us!

launches.title: Speko: OpenRouter for Voice
launches.tagline: Every speech model, benchmarked language by language, wired into one API.
launches.body:
Speko is a router for voice models. One API key, and your agent runs on the speech-to-text, LLM and text-to-speech models we measured as best for your language and use case.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108267&key=user_uploads/451241/2038963f-c769-47a9-8fd9-c59f3966027b)

### I picked voice stacks by trial and error for four years

A voice agent is three models in a row: speech-to-text, then an LLM, then text-to-speech. Three vendors, a dozen credible options each. You run a bake-off, you argue about whose numbers are real, and you ship the combination that felt best that month.

Then next week another model drops. And another. Nobody has time to re-run the bake-off, so the stack you picked under deadline quietly becomes the stack you are stuck with for a year.

That is how most voice agents are running today. Not on the best models. On the models that were best whenever someone last had a free week.

Public leaderboards do not settle it either. They are averages over somebody else's audio, in somebody else's conditions.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AjC8WVA96kUBdD09RJMUgFfvxGfxPvL-/](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AjC8WVA96kUBdD09RJMUgFfvxGfxPvL-/view?usp=sharing)

### We measure, then we route

We benchmark the speech models people actually ship on, language by language, and publish everything at [benchmarks.speko.ai](http://benchmarks.speko.ai): word error rate, finalize latency, time to first token, cost per minute. When a vendor ships a new model we test it the same day and the board updates.

Point your agent at Speko and that measurement becomes routing. One API key across every provider we support. Tell us the language and the conditions, and your traffic runs on the stack our numbers say wins. When the numbers change, the routing changes and you rewrite nothing.

If a provider fails when we open the connection, the router drops to the next ranked model on its own.

### Or build the agent with us

You do not need an existing agent to start. A few lines gets a working voice agent live on Speko, and it inherits the same routing from day one.

If you are picking a voice stack right now, start with the numbers at [benchmarks.speko.ai](http://benchmarks.speko.ai), then build on them at [speko.ai](http://speko.ai).

launches.title: Medley: Give Claude Code missions, not just tasks
launches.tagline: Medley is a free Claude Code plugin for work bigger than one session. Type /mission to turn an outcome into a live dependency graph, coordinate Claude Code and Codex workers, review the assembled result, and keep going.
launches.body:
Hey YC! 👋 We're Akshay and Ashwin, and we're building Medley.

You type **_/mission_** and give it the outcome, the budget, and the constraints. Medley builds a live dependency graph, coordinates Claude Code and Codex workers, reviews what comes back, and keeps going when execution reveals more work. It's free and runs on the subscriptions and API access you already have.

<https://youtu.be/xe7bj3b5Aw0>

## **❌ The Problem**

Coding agents got good at bounded tasks. Once a job outgrows one session, you become the harness. You break the work into prompts, move context between agents, review outputs, and decide what happens next. There's no shared definition of done, so "finished" just means "looks finished."

## **🛠 Our Solution**

/mission takes on that orchestration. Three things sit between your outcome and the models:

* **A contract.** Before any work starts, Medley sets the objective, the acceptance criteria, the constraints and budget, and the conditions that should make it hold or stop. That's what "done" gets measured against later.
* **A live graph.** Medley doesn't write one giant plan upfront or spawn a swarm by default. It plans the next useful set of steps, runs them, reviews what came back, and updates what should happen next. Each node carries a brief, its dependencies, and a verification target. Sometimes one worker should carry a tightly coupled job end to end; when work is genuinely independent, Medley runs it in parallel. Work is routed across Claude Code and Codex workers - and with your own OpenRouter key, Codex workers can run models like Kimi and GLM.
* **An acceptance stage.** When a batch lands, a separate reviewer role inspects the outputs and changed files, runs the contract's verify commands, and decides whether the evidence satisfies the contract - not whether the work merely looks finished. If it doesn't, the mission replans.

You can watch and steer the mission in your browser. Anything that needs your judgment or approval - publishing, sending outbound, spending, contacting people - lands in the attention queue. Everything else keeps moving. 

## **📊 Why This Works**

The model is only the local capability. The harness decides where to apply it - the contract fixes the target, the graph splits the work, routing matches each task to a worker, and an independent acceptance stage runs the real verify commands and replans when the contract isn't met.

Before launch, we pressure-tested a benchmark-specialized version of the same architecture on four complete public benchmarks: 93.25% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 71.37 on HealthBench Professional, 93.24% on ViBench, and 60.98% on DrugDiscoveryBench. Those are the highest reported results on each, and they span coding, healthcare, and drug discovery.

No new foundation model. The gains came from how the work was decomposed, routed, carried across contexts, and reviewed.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108332&key=user_uploads/1362282/3af52f57-057a-475d-8bc4-ec0b1531a504)

Full methodology and results are[ on our blog](https://www.medley.sh/blog/the-harness-is-the-capability-multiplier).

## **🙏 Our Ask**

**Try it.** Medley is free on Mac. Install it from Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Spine-AI/medley
/plugin install medley
/reload-plugins
```

Then run /mission.[ ](http://medley.sh/)[medley.sh](http://medley.sh)

**Tell us what you think.** We're shaping the product around how people actually use it. Email [support@getspine.ai](mailto:support@getspine.ai) with what you tried, where it worked, and where it broke - and where you'd want Medley to keep going versus stop and ask.

### TL;DR

**Atlia is the AI-native short-term rental property management company.**

**You give us your Airbnbs to manage, and you’ll take home 10-20% more while both you and your guests have a better experience.**

Launch Video:\
<https://youtu.be/gvvV5zLIPV4>

Short-term rentals were sold as passive income. But in reality, every Airbnb is a tiny hotel and a nightmare of operations. Every reservation restarts the operational clock: prices must be adjusted, guests screened, messages answered, cleaners scheduled, access coordinated, supplies restocked, and maintenance handled, often overnight or between back-to-back stays.

And in traditional short-term property management companies, operational failures are common, and they can quickly become very costly:

* A missed cleaning becomes a bad review
* A poorly screened guest becomes property damage
* A neglected maintenance issue becomes an issued refund or lost booking

On top of these operational failures, the average management company takes 15–30% of rental revenue, often alongside cleaning, maintenance, and other fees.

We’ve been property managers for the past year and ran into the same lose-lose choice every owner faces: manage a 24/7 hospitality business yourself, or hand over a quarter of your revenue to a management company whose costs increase with every property it adds.

We are building a new type of property management company, with infrastructure built for agents and human-computer-interaction from the ground up. By replacing the layers of coordination and operational overhead built into traditional management companies, we provide a much better service at a much lower fee.

We center around a simple premise: owners shouldn’t have to choose between good service and reasonable fees. With our model, **owners take home 10–20% more and guests have a more premium experience.**

We’re Shaan and Edmond, longtime friends, Duke roommates, and property managers.

Edmond previously built AI voice agents at Rilla, LLM agents at S&P Global, and data pipelines at Vanguard. He has been managing rentals for a year, experiencing the owner’s dilemma firsthand.

launches.title: Datoric | Trustworthy data for the next generation of models
launches.tagline: Collecting the human experience AI needs, securely.
launches.body:
Datoric provides custom, security-first training data for voice models, robotics, and world models. Our private, project-specific contributor systems have led to a dramatic improvement in quality for customers and helped us generate nearly seven figures in revenue over the last 30 days.

## **Our background**

In 2023, we built large-scale automations that completed paid LLM training tasks across major crowd-work platforms by bypassing QA testers. We earned six figures in three months, and even helped fix some of the vulnerabilities that we found. From this experience, we learned just how easily training data can be compromised, and how it can lead to unsafe model behavior.

<https://youtu.be/GXuyd2PfsAY>

## **The problem**

Labs are searching for the high-quality, authentic human data their models need, but quality and provenance become harder to control at scale, especially when relying on outside data providers. Poor-quality or compromised data can distort model behavior, while unqualified contributors, automated submissions, unclear instructions, and weak consent records can still slip through QA. At the same time, data providers hold concentrated stores of customer data, contributor identities, and payments that attract fraud and security threats.

## **What we built**

Datoric manages the full collection process for multilingual speech, egocentric video, and action-conditioned data. We collect this data through more than 300,000 active contributors who record conversations, everyday tasks, and other project-specific activities through our private apps. Because Datoric has no public marketplace or open upload system, every collection can run inside its own isolated environment, keeping customer projects separate and limiting unauthorized access. Each recording also remains linked to the verified contributor who created it and the consent they provided. This blocks automated or manipulated submissions and protects quality throughout the collection process rather than leaving it to final QA.

## **Traction**

We’ve seen a major uptick in quality compared to other providers, and in the last 30 days, Datoric has generated nearly seven figures in revenue.

## **Our ask**

We would love introductions to teams building voice models, robots, or world models that need difficult, custom human-generated data.

Send us your hardest collection specification at [**founders@datoric.com**](mailto:founders@datoric.com), or visit [**datoric.com**](http://datoric.com).

launches.title: Avoca Systems: AI-powered radiology scheduling and communications
launches.tagline: Automating radiology scheduling and patient communications
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re Max Shand and Campbell Mercer, co-founders of Avoca Systems.

TL;DR: Avoca automates patient scheduling and communications for radiology groups. Our radiology-specific AI handles calls, online scheduling, faxes and e-referrals, guiding patients from referral and booking through to results and follow-up. We’re already live across more than 250 clinics, including networks operating 150+ locations.

<https://youtu.be/ZU3Ebvs5Mk0>

**What it does**

Radiology scheduling is unusually complex. A valid appointment can depend on the modality, body region, contrast requirements, patient history, preparation instructions, equipment availability, staff qualifications and referring-provider details.

These rules are fragmented across legacy systems, spreadsheets and the tacit knowledge of experienced receptionists. Generic voice and scheduling tools struggle to bring them together.

Avoca integrates with a radiology network’s existing systems and turns its workflows and operational knowledge into one automation layer:

* **AI calls:** Answers inbound calls and runs outbound campaigns for bookings, rescheduling, cancellations, preparation questions and general enquiries.
* **Online scheduling:** Lets patients upload their referral, complete the necessary clinical and safety questions, and find an appropriate appointment in real time.
* **Fax and e-referral automation:** Ingests and interprets referrals, identifies missing information and contacts patients to complete their booking.
* **Operational intelligence:** Encodes each network’s booking rules, rosters, staff capabilities, preferences and tacit knowledge so Avoca can safely fill available scanner capacity.
* **Patient communications:** Guides patients through preparation, intake, reminders, results and follow-up using voice, text and email.

**Why this matters**

Up to 30% of calls into radiology centres go unanswered as patients wait on hold. Referrals arrive through phones, websites, faxes and electronic systems, leaving staff to manually interpret documents, contact patients and coordinate appointments across multiple systems.

At the same time, radiology providers face staff shortages, rising operating costs and reimbursement pressure. Missed calls and unprocessed referrals mean patients wait longer while valuable scanner capacity goes unfilled.

Avoca helps networks capture more patient demand, reduce administrative work and complete more scans using their existing clinics, equipment and clinical systems.

**Traction**

* Partnered with 250+ clinics, including several of Australia’s largest radiology networks
* Reduced call abandonment from approximately 30% to 2%
* Patient satisfaction averaging 4.6/5
* More than 80% booking conversion for eligible patient calls in major deployments
* Integrated with leading radiology and healthcare systems, including Visage, Karisma, Comrad, Epic, Oracle Health and eClinicalWorks
* Now expanding into the United States

**Why we’re building this**

I (Max) was the first employee at Afterpay and later founded and sold Serenade. Cam was previously a principal engineer at Honey Insurance and Macquarie. Across those experiences, we saw how much better an industry can operate when complex workflows are turned into simple, intuitive products.

Healthcare is a chaotic mess of work that falls between systems: calls that go unanswered, referrals that sit in fax queues and operational knowledge that exists only in the heads of experienced staff.

We started with radiology because the scheduling complexity is exceptionally high and the consolidation of radiology clinics into large groups allowed us to focus our GTM efforts on just a few influential stakeholders who acutely feel the pain we’re solving for.

**Our big** **ask**

* Any introduction to a radiology network or health system chief executive (CEO, CIO, COO, CDO, CRO - even the new brand of CAIO - Chief AI Officer) would be hugely appreciated. We’re new to the US and eager to meet leaders tackling the patient access and scheduling challenges we’re solving.

Finally, if you operate a radiology network - or know someone who does - we’d love to hear from you. Please reply here or reach us at [hello@avocasystems.com](mailto:hello@avocasystems.com).

launches.title: Bizmark – Transforming physical industries
launches.tagline: The operating system for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods
launches.body:
[Bizmark Launch](https://youtu.be/-5g3wv2OE2g)

Hey everyone, we're Rodrigo and Oscar, founders of Bizmark (S26).

**TL;DR:** Bizmark is the operating system for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods. It connects the systems, spreadsheets, and knowledge a company already has, and turns them into optimized decisions and automated workflows: quotes priced in seconds, schedules that reflow when a machine goes down, inventory balanced between service levels and cash. Bizmark adapts to how each company operates, not the other way around. Working product in weeks, not years. Some of the most innovative American companies use Bizmark to transform their operations. Ask: intros to decision makers at manufacturers, distributors, and retailers.

**The problem**

> _“Quotes take too long, so I lose revenue. Or I quote too fast and give away margin.”_

> _“Days of inventory are critical for my business, but I’m not sure I’m buying the right quantities at the right time, or getting the best supplier terms.”_

> _“An urgent order comes in and I do not know what to run next. I’m hitting max capacity constantly, but I’m not sure I’m using my equipment and labor in the most efficient way.”_

After 150 of these conversations, we've realized these problems share the same cause. Legacy ERPs force operators into templates that don’t reflect how the business runs, while custom implementations often run to years and seven-figure budgets. As a result, decisions that directly affect revenue, margins, and service levels are made from spreadsheets, delayed reports, and fragmented tools, with less information than the company has, often by whoever is closest, not whoever knows best.

**What we built**

Bizmark is the operating system for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods. It connects the systems, spreadsheets, and knowledge a company already has, and turns them into optimized decisions and automated workflows. Bizmark adapts to how each company operates, not the other way around. And customers get a working product in weeks, not years.

**Here’s how some of the most innovative American companies use Bizmark to transform their operations:**

A spec-heavy RFQ lands in the inbox. Bizmark reads it, and a quoting engine prices it against inventory, capacity, and customer history. It returns a customer-ready quote in seconds. The team approves it, it goes out, and when the customer says yes, the order enters the system without any retyping.

Then the order runs. Bizmark schedules it into your machines and crews against your objectives, using the same estimates the quote was priced on. When a machine goes down or a rush order lands, the plan reflows and the new sequence reaches the queues that run the operation. The job runs, passes quality, and ships.

The order drew down inventory. Bizmark forecasts what you will sell next, holds your days of inventory in balance – enough for minimum service levels while protecting cash – and decides what to buy, when, and from whom. It sends RFQs to qualified suppliers and compares what comes back. The team chooses, and the PO books straight into the system.

**Who we are**

We’re cousins who love seeing how things get built in the real world.

Rodrigo grew one of the largest e-commerce logistics startups in Brazil from zero to $60M in revenue running 100k orders/month across 10k SKUs as the first employee. Prev. CS at UChicago, MBA from Chicago Booth.

Oscar led process optimization at Intel, Amazon, and J&J, and deployed AI for the U.S. government. Prev. Operations Research at Stanford and Georgia Tech.

**Ask**

Intros to decision makers at manufacturers, distributors, and retailers.

launches.title: Hanji - Turn your hardest documents into reliable data
launches.tagline: We turn scanned, faxed, and handwritten documents into structured data with a pipeline tuned for the accuracy, speed, and cost you need.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋, we’re David, Soami, and Achyut from [Hanji](https://hanji.dev/). \
\
At YouLearn, we processed **70M pages for 2.5M users.** To handle 500 page textbooks, handwritten notes, and scanned documents with broken tables, we built our own document parser. We launched it as an API and didn’t expect healthcare, government, and insurance teams to be the first to reach out. But after talking with them, **we realized they still couldn’t find a pipeline they could rely on in production.** 

<https://youtu.be/S5OVXZVv61A>

### **Problem**

As companies process more documents with hard formats, **they either build in-house and take on the cost of maintaining it, or use a provider and accept tradeoffs they cannot control.**

* **Build:** It can work at a certain scale, but as volume increases and harder formats come in, your team has to keep fixing the pipeline. Over time, you end up maintaining something that was never your product.
* **Buy:** Providers can work too, but you have to accept tradeoffs you cannot change. They may cost too much, take too long at higher volumes, or miss important cases that your team then has to fix.

In both scenarios, your team pays for these tradeoffs through more engineering time, slower workflows, or lower margins.

### **Our Solution**

**Hanji tunes the document pipeline to your workflow,** so you don’t have to maintain it yourself or accept fixed tradeoffs.

Send us your hardest docs, and we’ll take care of the rest by tuning your pipeline **to the accuracy, speed, and cost you need.** And when human review is still necessary in your document workflow, we’ll improve that process too, such as by adding field-level confidence scores and review flags.

### **Benchmark**

Even before tuning, **Hanji holds the highest text accuracy across five providers** on our benchmark: 400 human-verified pages spanning seven document types.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108085&key=user_uploads/1378551/eb2e7fbd-b541-4b77-93fe-e29fb3af7948)

_Text accuracy, 400 human-verified pages, 95% CIs. Full methodology [here](https://hanji.dev/bench)._

### **Results**

After tuning Hanji to each customer’s document workflow, one YC healthcare company improved their text accuracy from **71% on our first pass to 96.5% within a few days.** Another reduced its end-to-end latency from **1.5 minutes to under 1 minute** with Hanji extracting **78/78 fields** containing payer to member ID associations across 53 packets. And another company **reduced its projected processing costs by 75%** after we implemented a routing step that found the relevant forms in every packet.

In each case, we started with their own documents, tuned the pipeline around what matters for their workflow, and kept improving it as new failures appeared.

### **Our Ask**

**Try your hardest docs in the playground [here](https://hanji.dev/dashboard/playground),** then [book a call](https://cal.com/team/youlearnai/hanji-intro) to see how we can improve your accuracy, speed, or review process.

Processing regulated documents? [Book a call](https://cal.com/team/youlearnai/hanji-intro). For PHI documents, we can sign a BAA and enable access the same day.

For any other questions or feedback, email us directly at [founders@hanji.dev](mailto:founders@hanji.dev).

# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR:** AI agents are quietly pulling secrets off your employees' laptops — and your security gateway can't see it. Traceforce installs in under 5 minutes and gives you a full inventory of every AI app, MCP, and skill running on every device, then lets you block the dangerous stuff in real time. Built by the ex-Clumio engineering team. Already deployed at a 500+ person company and in PoCs with Fortune 500s. Try it free at [www.traceforce.ai](http://www.traceforce.ai).\
\
**The incident that started this**\
At our last company, an AI coding agent running on a developer's laptop scraped what looked like database credentials and pushed them straight into a public GitHub repo. It took us _weeks_ to investigate, rotate credentials, and clean up the fallout. We got lucky — they were dev-environment creds, so no customer was affected. Next time, nobody will be that lucky.\
\
That's the whole problem with AI at work now: ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and Claude Code are everywhere on employee devices, wired into your data through MCPs and skills that no one is tracking. The tools your security team already owns — gateways, proxies, enterprise APIs — never see any of it, because the risky action happens _on the device_, before it ever hits the network.\
\
**Why us**\
We're Xia and Varun. We ran engineering at Clumio, a cyber-resilience company acquired by Commvault in 2024, where Xia was Director of Engineering and Varun was tech lead. We've spent our careers building security infrastructure — and we validated this problem with 50+ CISOs and CIOs before writing a line of code. Every one of them said the same thing: \_I need to see and control this without slowing my engineers down.\_\
\
**Why on-device — and why gateways can't do this**\
Competitors sit at the gateway or plug into enterprise APIs. That misses the self-adopted AI tools employees install themselves, and it can't see how an agent is actually connected to your data via MCPs. Traceforce runs on the endpoint, so we see the full picture — which AI apps are running, what MCPs and skills they're wired to, what data they can reach — and we can _warn or block_ an unsafe action the moment it happens, not after it's already on the network.\
\
**What you get**

* Install in <5 min. Full inventory of every AI app, MCP, and skill across your devices within 30 minutes.
* Discover shadow AI and see exactly how each agent connects to your data sources.

Today we're sharing Agency Tool Company and our first product, ATC Deploy: a faster, more reliable way to ship software to robots wherever they are. It moves updates up to 20 times faster than docker pull or scp and works with any software stack already in use.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jx0rLRVa06s>

## The updates that took until 2 a.m.

Davis and I spent eight years building Scythe Robotics and putting hundreds of autonomous mowers to work across the country. For years, we deployed software with a tool I'd cobbled together for our first few robots. As the fleet grew, deployment became an ordeal: engineers stayed up until 2 a.m., we coordinated with customers to move robots out of sheds and into LTE coverage at set times, and failed transfers restarted from zero. Shipping a fix could take more coordination than building it. We had models to train and customers to serve, so the tooling limped along with incremental bandaids.

We've since heard the same story from robotics teams across industries. That deployment becomes a hidden bottleneck: teams become release-averse, feedback loops slow and improvements stall. Stitched-together web and IoT tools barely work if you know which scripts to run and who to call, so they survive, even if it means every update is distracting from improving the product.

## What we built

ATC Deploy ships whatever you already run: OS images, Docker images, or any file tree. Run “atc ota push user@robot”, and it sends only the changed bytes, then restarts your software through hooks you define—way faster than a docker push.

Install takes one “curl | sh” command and a config file so you can get back to work fast. Interrupted transfers resume where they stopped, and an offline robot can receive updates by USB if you need. There's no new runtime, packaging format, or operating system to adopt.

## Shipping to robots today

ATC Deploy already ships software to robots at Burro, which has deployed more than 750 machines worldwide, Tempo, polishing concrete across several US states and Canada, and Gather, who is scaling their 99.9% accurate inventory drones nationwide. Their teams spend less time managing delivery and more time improving the robot.

Hey everyone, we're the team behind [**mcp-use**](https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use), the open-source MCP framework with **10k GitHub stars** and **\~10M+ downloads**.

[**Manufact**](https://manufact.com/) is the cloud platform that gets your product onto the **Claude Connectors marketplace** and the **ChatGPT (Codex) Plugin Store** via MCP.

<https://youtu.be/Pyh_3tKDXuU>

## The problem

Paul Graham recently tweeted: "_AI apps are the new browsers_". \
Your customers now do most of their work inside Claude and ChatGPT, and the connector marketplaces are a new distribution channel: someone installs your product in one click and uses it inside the chat they already live in.

We listed Manufact on Claude and saw a **surge of signups** that is still going on now.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107462&key=user_uploads/859771/65a0b3fd-75cf-4eea-a2ee-02590e3256ba)

But shipping a production-ready MCP server is its own project:

* MCP is a protocol evolving fast .
* Auth is easy to get [wrong](https://manufact.com/blog/authentication).
* Every client behaves differently.
* The stores have their own conformance requirements, and review can block you for weeks.

## How Manufact works

Manufact is the cloud built specifically for MCP:

* **Push to deploy.** Connect the GitHub App once and [every commit ships a new version of your MCP server](https://manufact.com/platform/hosting), with a preview deployment for each PR.
* **Test every MCP tool and MCP-UI widget** in the [cloud inspector](https://manufact.com/platform/cloud-inspector).
* **Know the moment your MCP breaks** in ChatGPT or Claude with [automatic cross-client testing](https://manufact.com/platform/cross-client-testing).
* [**Publishing checklists**](https://manufact.com/platform/publishing-checks) so your MCP app doesn't get stuck in marketplace review.
* **Auto-generated submission assets** (logo, copy, screenshots).
* **Analytics, session replay, and traces** built in for MCP, so you can see [how it's used and why tools fail](https://manufact.com/platform/analytics).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107462&key=user_uploads/859771/ee30e016-9fb5-4958-890f-74febc54de3c)

## Your product's UI inside the chat

A plain MCP server lets the agent read and write your data. \
An **MCP App** goes further: it's an MCP server that can return a UI as the result of a tool call, so your actual product interface renders inside Claude or ChatGPT. The user sees your charts and forms instead of a wall of text.

Ferruccio Balestreri (Amplitude) [put it well](https://x.com/0xferruccio/status/2028966278971670979):

> since mcp ui was released in claude we got a 2x boost in retention.

With the [mcp-use SDK](https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use) you write a normal React component, drop it in, and it registers as an MCP UI resource automatically.

## Backstory

We've been building on MCP since the protocol shipped. It started with the mcp-use SDK, the full-stack framework for MCP servers and apps. We kept watching companies struggle to take those servers to production, so we built the cloud for it (mcp-use is to Manufact what Next.js is to Vercel).

Manufact is now the **#1 recommended deployment option in OpenAI's docs.** 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107462&key=user_uploads/859771/ddba2350-67c4-43d5-8150-30847d4375a2)

We've helped startups from recent YC batches like **AgentMail** and **Item** get onto the Claude Connectors marketplace, and larger companies in finance, insurance, and marketplaces run their MCP apps on Manufact in production.

## Our asks

1. Have an MCP server? **Deploy it on [Manufact](https://manufact.com/)**.
2. Thinking about building an MCP App? [Copy our prompt for agents](https://manufact.com/prompt.md) and your coding agent will guide you.
3. Trying to get listed on the marketplaces? [Book a call with us](https://cal.com/team/manufact/chat). We have publishing checks and direct contacts on the MCP teams at Anthropic and OpenAI.

Hope to see your MCP on [manufact.com](http://manufact.com), or that you at least learned something new. 🙂

launches.title: Hop Aero 🚀 Rocket Cargo
launches.tagline: Rockets that deliver cargo anywhere on Earth in minutes, including battlefields
launches.body:
**TLDR: We’re building rockets that deliver cargo faster than anything else on earth. We already have a $1.25M contract with the US Air Force for delivery to contest environments, and we’ve completed a tethered flight of our small-scale prototype.** 🚀🌎\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dI3bRpiuqdShHQ2xHMhqOhPluYQMGS2B](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dI3bRpiuqdShHQ2xHMhqOhPluYQMGS2B/view?usp=sharing)

❌ **Problem**

While Jacob was serving in the U.S. Marine Corps, Typhoon Haiyan had just swept through the Philippines. Jacob and his unit were given a clear order: deliver life-saving supplies of medicine and food as soon as possible. Despite working around the clock, the effort was regularly blocked due to aircraft breaking down, flight-critical parts being out of inventory, and pilot fatigue.

Similarly, when building his previous startup, Matija’s team were given 24 hours’ notice to deliver a satellite propulsion system to the mission integrator. FedEx and UPS could not guarantee on-time delivery, forcing Matija to make a 23-hour trip to hand-deliver the flight hardware. He spent the flight back thinking that there has to be a better way.

It turned out that it wasn’t just us. Everyone from startups to the U.S. military, needs faster delivery. We saw an opportunity to create the fastest form of transportation in the world.

🚀 **Rockets are the answer**

We are building Rook, an autonomous rocket that delivers 250 kg of cargo up to 750 km away. That’s Okinawa to Taiwan in 15 minutes.

Rook launches from a standard 40-ft shipping container, flies through space, re-enters at hypersonic speeds and lands on unprepared surfaces, allowing it to launch and land anywhere on the planet. This opens up completely new commercial markets and military capabilities.

Rook can deliver swarms of autonomous unmanned systems to the battlefield, delivering a fully-autonomous 21st century D-Day effect for the U.S. and allies. The same Rook can deliver time-critical goods for manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, offshore oil and pharma, preventing downtime costs of up to $2M/hour.

🏆 **Traction**

* **Won a $1.25M DoW contract** from the US Air Force.
* **Completed our first tethered test** at the Oklahoma spaceport on a small-scale prototype
* **Successfully hot-fired our engine and igniter** built using hopOS, our AI-augmented secret sauce.

🥷 **Team**

**Matija (CEO):** Previously founded porkchop (electric propulsion for small satellites) - launched on SpaceX Transporter-3, built a $400M+ sales pipeline, sold the IP. Led a 20+ person supersonic UAV team at Destinus and scaled Ukrainian loitering-munition production from 10 to 100+ units/month.

**Jacob (CTO):** US Marine Corps (MV-22 avionics) → SpaceX (Falcon 9/Heavy; built the OG booster refurb program) → Virgin Orbit (LauncherOne) → Masten (led systems integration & test on NASA's CLPS lunar lander) → SpinLaunch. A decade of making rockets fly on schedule.

launches.title: Scispot Smart Actions
launches.tagline: We stopped connecting instruments and started letting them make decisions
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107928&key=user_uploads/697526/3baf4e61-60db-413e-a024-a596c1cf70d1)

At 11:40pm, an analyst at a biotech we work with was staring at a plate of 96 ELISpot wells, trying to figure out why three "positive" results didn't match the raw counts. She'd already re-typed the spot counts into a spreadsheet once. She was about to do it again, by hand, to double-check herself because the instrument doesn't know what a "positive" is. It just counts spots. Someone has to turn that count into a decision, and that someone was her, at midnight, for the fourth night that week.

That's not a story about one analyst. That's the entire industry's relationship with lab data, and it hasn't meaningfully changed in a decade.

## **The part everyone stops short of**

Most labs eventually solve the easy problem: getting a file off an instrument and into some kind of system of record. That's plumbing, and plumbing gets built. What almost nobody automates is the step after deciding whether a result is even valid.

Does it clear the CV threshold?

Is this well too confluent to trust (TNTC)?

What's the right baseline to compare against? Is this a Positive, a Negative, or a QC Fail?

That judgment still lives in someone's head and someone's spreadsheet, redone by hand, every single run.

We think that's the real bottleneck in lab data - not moving files around, but making trustworthy calls on what's inside them, fast enough to keep up with how fast science actually moves.

## **The infrastructure that makes this possible: GLUE**

None of this works without a real connectivity layer underneath it, so we built one. [Scispot GLUE](https://www.scispot.com/glue) is our API-first integration backbone with hundreds of connectors, native HL7/ASTM support, and webhooks — that plugs into instruments, LIMS-like entities, and external systems without custom code for every new device.

GLUE is the nervous system; Smart Actions are the brain sitting on top of it, deciding what every signal actually means.

That distinction matters. A lot of "lab automation" stops at GLUE's job: get the file, map the fields, store the record. We built Smart Actions specifically because moving the data was never the finish line — it was the prerequisite.

## **What we actually built**

[Smart Actions](https://www.scispot.com/smart-actions) are AI-agent workflows inside Scispot that don't stop at moving data - they interpret it.

A Smart Action parses a raw instrument export, maps every well to the right sample and treatment condition, applies your lab's QC rules automatically (CV thresholds, LLOQ cutoffs, TNTC handling), computes the real statistics — averages, fold change against baseline — and writes the _decision_, not just the number, straight into your Labsheets.

The ELISpot plate our analyst stayed up for?

Today that run finishes, and by the time she opens her laptop, the QC-gated summary is already sitting in the [Scispot Labsheet](https://www.scispot.com/labsheets) - Positive, Negative, Indeterminate, or QC Fail, each one traceable back to exactly why. Not a spreadsheet she has to trust blindly. A decision she can audit in one click.

## **Why this is a bigger bet than "faster data transport"**

Moving data fast, which is what GLUE gives you, is table stakes. The hard, valuable problem is the judgment layer on top of it is this result real, does it pass QC, what does it mean for the next experiment. That's what Smart Actions own, permanently, for every run, not just the one someone remembered to check carefully.

Smart Actions are composable, build one for ELISpot, reuse the same pattern for a plate-reader screen routing hits into follow-up assays, chain them together across protocols, all running on top of GLUE's connectivity. And they're callable by [Scibot Omega](https://www.scispot.com/product-releases/scibot-omega), our AI orchestrator, so a scientist can just say "clean this run, QC it, summarize it for the sponsor" and the right Smart Actions execute end to end.

## **Why we're telling you this now**

We've launched Scispot on YC before as a platform, and GLUE as our connectivity layer.

This time we wanted to talk about the layer built on top of it that our customers actually thank us for - the layer that means their best analyst stops being a human QC script running at midnight, and starts being a scientist again.

If you've ever stared at a spreadsheet at 11pm trying to figure out why a result doesn't add up, we built this for you.

👉 **scispot.com/demo**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_BFoFo_0zHk>

launches.title: Beluga - Creator Marketing on Autopilot
launches.tagline: Run creator marketing like paid ads
launches.body:
**TL;DR**: We run creator marketing end-to-end so companies can test and scale the channel without needing to hire.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107925&key=user_uploads/2204818/717d980b-6271-4c94-a779-1c60e4277af9)

Marketers do not need to be convinced that distribution matters.

The harder question is whether a channel can become repeatable before it consumes the whole team.

Creator marketing is one of those channels. It oftentimes performs 3-5x better than traditional digital ads. When it works, it can drive real awareness, clicks, and signups from audiences that are hard to reach through paid ads. But running it well still tends to mean spreadsheets, inboxes, rate negotiations, contracts, draft reviews, tracking links, payment follow-up, and a lot of manual judgment.

That is what we built Beluga to fix.

---

## Why this problem got under our skin

One of the largest spenders in creator marketing made the labor problem concrete for us. They are spending in the high six figures each month, and told us they employ 30+ people to run their creator partnerships. Even then, each rep can only manage around 18 creators.

They also told us that if they had $2M ready to put into the channel tomorrow, they wouldn’t be able to do it. They would need to hire even more people.

That is a wild ceiling for a marketing channel that should scale with spend.

We got pulled into this from both sides.

Fernando saw the brand side up close at Dare Drop, helping gaming publishers run creator campaigns. The demand was real, but the operating model still looked like a traditional agency: lots of coordination, lots of manual work, and a hard ceiling on how much the team could scale.

We also spent time on the creator side while trying to build a Rippling for the self-employed. Working with creators on taxes showed us the other half of the problem: even when a brand deal is a good fit, the process around it is painful. Creators have to find deals that match their audience and content style, align expectations with the brand, actually run the campaign, and then hope they get paid on time.

We kept seeing the same thing from both sides: brands wanted creator marketing to work, creators wanted better deals and less chaos, and everyone was somehow stuck in spreadsheets, email threads, and manual follow-up.

---

## What Beluga does

The problem is not that creator marketing is mysterious. It works when you find the right creators, give them enough room to make authentic content, track the results properly, and run enough shots on goal.

The hard part is doing all of that consistently without making it a headcount problem.

Beluga is our attempt to make creator marketing feel more like running a paid acquisition channel: set the target, set the budget, see what is happening, and double down on what works.

We run campaigns ed-to-end, including:

* Creator sourcing and vetting
* Pricing and negotiation
* Contracting
* Deliverable management
* Creator payments
* Performance tracking
* Post-campaign analysis

The goal is that a founder or growth team can test creator marketing without building the internal machine. If the results are there, we help them scale the channel without turning it into a hiring plan.

Since starting in March, we have generated over 3M views for clients ranging from YC companies to Series F hyperscalers, and saved over $100k in negotiations.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107925&key=user_uploads/2204818/2dd9d0b8-f197-41aa-aa36-621c473b6569)

_Beluga helped take Freebuff, Codebuff's free coding agent, from roughly 50 to 1,200 daily active users at peak._

For another Series F company, we drove 3,500+ signups in two weeks.

---

## Who Beluga is for

We are most useful when you already believe creator marketing could fit your market, but you do not want the channel to require a whole internal team before it can scale.

Our bet is that the traditional operating model is the problem: most of the sourcing, negotiation, coordination, payments, and reporting should not require dedicated headcount inside every company.

That also changes what is possible. When the work gets cheaper and easier to coordinate, you can test more creators, go after smaller but better-matched channels, and deploy more capital without being bottlenecked by how many deals an internal team can manually manage.

The signal we look for is simple: can we name a real content audience where your users spend time?

"Developers who watch AI coding tool reviews on YouTube" is a clean audience shape. So is a consumer category with obvious creator communities. A niche B2B buyer can still work, but if the buyer is hard to describe in creator and audience terms, or the product only moves through a long enterprise committee, the test usually has less conversion signal.

The other important thing is seriousness about the experiment. Creator marketing is not one magic post. It takes enough well-matched attempts to learn which creators, formats, and messages work. If distribution is a real priority and you want to test the channel properly, that is the conversation we are best suited for.

---

## Why us

The reason we think we can make this work is that we have lived the messy parts.

Fernando ran millions in ad spend at Meta and then sold creator campaigns at Dare Drop. Zan, our Head of Account Management, led outreach across tens of thousands of creators and is a content creator himself. [@Jack Swisher](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2210281) spent years building AI systems at Bubble and now works on building the infrastructure needed to make our vision a reality.

Between us, we have seen the agency side, the creator side, the paid acquisition side, and the automation side.

Our mission is simple: make creator marketing as measurable and easy to run as paid ads.

---

## The ask

If creator marketing is on your roadmap and you do not want the channel to become an internal ops burden, we would love to chat.

And if you know another founder or growth lead who already believes distribution matters and is thinking about creator marketing this year, an intro would be hugely helpful.

[Learn more here](https://www.trybeluga.ai/)

launches.title: Rex: Turn enterprise order-to-cash into an autonomous operation
launches.tagline: AI Operations Partner for Enterprise Order to Cash
launches.body:
Rex is an AI service that runs order-to-cash and accounts receivable operations for enterprises. Founders [Merlin Kafka](https://www.linkedin.com/in/merlinkafka/) and [Lewis Blackwood](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisblackwood) spent 4 years at an a16z-backed startup helping finance teams at startups like Cognition, Legora and Bridge automate revenue collection. The problem is 100x bigger in the enterprise, so they built Rex: agents that do the work end-to-end. Live in production with Synthesia.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BKS7qaZS8Is>

**Revenue ≠ cash**

Enterprises invoice customers, then spend months chasing the money through email chains, PDFs and ancient web portals. A $1M invoice sits unpaid because one PO number didn't match.

Multiply that across thousands of customers and you get 100+ person teams, often offshore, doing this by hand: collections, invoice submission, dispute resolution, deduction management, cash application. Order-to-cash is the most outsourced process in finance because the work needs judgment. Reading a customer's email and deciding whether their dispute is valid. Working out which of 14 open invoices a lump-sum payment covers. Knowing that this account always pays late but always pays, and that one needs escalating now.

AR automation software has existed for 20 years and the teams never got smaller, because the tools organise the work while people still do it. Businesses invoice each other tens of trillions of dollars a year; the labour and outsourcing spend on collecting it is over $100B. Until now the only way to scale was headcount or a BPO contract.

**What Rex does**

Rex connects to the ERP (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle), CRM (Salesforce), billing system and shared AR inbox, and learns how the team runs the process today. That knowledge becomes editable agent operating procedures: how to chase a Fortune 500 buyer vs a startup, which deductions get investigated vs written off, when a dispute goes to a human.

Then agents run those procedures across thousands of accounts in parallel:

* Collections and payment follow-ups, including the long tail no team gets to
* Invoice submission and status tracking inside procurement portals (SAP Ariba, Coupa, Tungsten and hundreds of others)
* Dispute and deduction investigation
* Remittance processing and cash application
* Responding to customer finance emails
* Updating ERP, CRM and billing records
* Routing exceptions to the team for approval

Portals deserve a special mention: an increasing share of enterprise invoices must be submitted and tracked inside the buyer's procurement system. It's the work AR teams hate most and the work software vendors ignore. Rex treats it as core.

**Is Rex a managed service or software?**

Enterprises can partner with Rex as a managed service provider or let their team operate Rex. AR software (dunning tools, collections worklists, AR dashboards) organises work for a team to do. Rex agents do the work, and the finance team approves exceptions. With Rex, the team stops drowning in routine chasing and handles the judgment calls. Customers compare Rex to their next AR hire, their offshore team, or their BPO contract.

**Can finance teams trust AI agents with collections?**

Autonomy is earned, not switched on. Each procedure starts supervised: Rex proposes, the team approves. Once a procedure hits its accuracy bar for the account, it graduates and runs autonomously. Safe, high-volume work goes first; judgment-heavy edges stay gated as long as the team wants. Every action is logged with its full reasoning, so finance audits the system instead of babysitting it.

**Traction**

[Rex is live in production with enterprises like Synthesia](https://www.rex.inc/customers/synthesia), running collections, portal submissions, inbox triage and cash application. Cases that used to take weeks of back and forth resolve in minutes.

**Get in touch**

If invoice volume is outgrowing the finance team, or order-to-cash runs on offshore headcount or a BPO contract, get in touch: [rex.inc](http://rex.inc)

launches.title: Waddle Labs - Agents that control robots
launches.tagline: Claude Code for robotics - prompt your robot to do physical tasks
launches.body:
Waddle is the Claude Code for robotics. Connect our API to your robot and type a prompt, then our agents write code to achieve the task in \~20 minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107821&key=user_uploads/2132817/afc74f28-33c6-450c-80c3-7f2d263f213d)

### **Our Hypothesis**

Robot intelligence today depends either on large end-to-end VLAs or classical approaches.

\- VLAs are difficult to customise and steer, require huge amounts of data to train, and don’t yet generalise across embodiments and environment. They face limited deployment.

\- Meanwhile, classical approaches are widely deployed for their reliability and explicit control, but are often brittle and costly to redevelop in new setups.

_Does this tradeoff have to be inevitable?_

**Our hypothesis:** By using agents to control robots, we combine the generalisation of VLAs with the speed and reliability of classical approaches. 

### **Our Solution**

Our agents decomposes a goal into subtasks, and completes each subtask by viewing camera feeds, writing control code, and calling models like VLAs. The agent outputs a program that you can run and iterate on by talking to our agents. 

**Where we've been using Waddle internally:**

\- **Create a working policy in 20 minutes** ("Write a program to package the box")

\- **Generate data for model training** ("Pick and place lego bricks at random positions 1000 times")

\- **Facilitate robotics auto-research** ("I am tuning a policy overnight. Reset the scene after each trial”)\
\
Because our agents are LLMs, they inherit properties of the underlying models. Agents and the code they write are inherently generalist, so they work with any robot and any environment without additional data. Moreover, agents excel at long-horizon planning and can decompose a physical goal into subtasks, verify each stage, and re-plan on failure.

**Interested in trying our agents via our preview API?** Sign up at \[our website\](<https://www.waddlelabs.ai/>) or email [founders@waddlelabs.ai](mailto:founders@waddlelabs.ai)

### **Our Research**

Waddle's agents enable new forms of scaling that we are very excited about:

\- **Scaling compositional generalization:** Our agent first wrote the “fold_grasp” skill while flipping a package; another agent later used it to fold a t-shirt. Over time, agents accumulate a library of skills, enabling future agents to compose them and achieve harder tasks.

\- **Scaling multi-robot cooperation:** Imagine an entire fleet of robots collaborating to achieve a task. For VLAs, this is a nightmare. For Waddle, simply hook up more agents. A master agent spawns subagents, coordinating multiple robots working concurrently.

\- **Scaling from scale:** We evaluated Opus 4.8, Fable 5, and GPT 5.6 Sol on a suite of manipulation tasks: larger models with larger thinking budgets consistently produce better policies. As foundation models improve, so do our robots.

### **The Team**

We are @Yiding Song (Vincent) and @Hanming Ye. We met at MIT’s Research Science Institute, where Vincent was working on multimodal astrophysics models and Hanming was researching topology in the math department. Since then, we’ve become roommates at Harvard where we are either doing ML research or breaking robots - usually both.

There will be millions of robots in the future. Our mission is to enable everyone to take part in building them.

launches.title: hardware intelligence: AI tools for the chips your AI runs on
launches.tagline: Bringing the $20B chip tooling industry into this decade
launches.body:
We’re Athreya and Rishov - the founders of [@hardware intelligence](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/33573). We’re here to pick a fight with the $20B industry whose debuggers suck and won’t open until an ancient license server gives it permission.

**TL;DR: Our first product, Wave, is a SOTA waveform debugger that lives completely in the terminal, built for the agentic era.** An agent can jump you to the moment a design breaks, drag in waveforms and manipulate them, trace bad signals to its source and even prove its fix against the simulation - all visual. We allow teams to build better chips in less time.

**The quick ask:** If you or anyone you know builds or verifies chips (ASICs/FPGAs), please email us! We would love to talk :)\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5nXvicwWONQ>

❌ **The Problem**

The AI boom is a chip boom - more companies and teams than ever are designing silicon. However, the reality is hardware is not software: you can’t patch a chip after it ships. A bug that reaches manufacturing can be a nine-figure mistake. That’s why **companies spend 70% of the entire chip design process just on verification**.

Hardware verification engineers run thousands of simulated tests first on their code (simulation) which typically can take **hours to days**. If one of these tests fail, debugging means reading a waveform - a log of every signal, millions of ticks long, hiding the tick where a value went wrong. It’s literally a needle in a haystack… a big haystack. It’s common for these waveform files to be several gigabytes large. **Finding this needle is the single largest activity in verification.**

**The current tools are dinosaurs.** 20-year-old GUIs behind license servers whose seats run six figures a year sold by our favorite incumbents: Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens. Free tools are even worse.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/fd100b13-f0dd-45f0-8ee4-395edf96fcae)

Yes. This is from 2026.

Software engineers got coding agents. Chip engineers got a queue for a license and whatever this is.

👋 **What Wave actually does**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/a75818b0-b001-466b-9586-705d26deb5f9)

Wave is the first of its kind! **A fully terminal-native waveform debugger with a verification agent built in.** Wave opens files before Verdi, the industry-standard viewer, finishes its license check. Let’s do a quick dive!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/ac7e5c75-8abb-4a6d-881f-a2a9b883a8b3)

**Why the terminal?** Surprisingly, most hardware engineers are terminal power users - typically doing all their coding in Vim. We wanted to meet them where they are and make our product extremely intuitive to use - we even employ Vim bindings across the interface.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/d4063fbc-2f57-4b5c-a421-bfaa697433d6)

**Ask in plain english.** _Why is a wave x at 12.4us?_ The agent will pull in signals, act on them and trace the root cause. Everything happens in front of your eyes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/8f37dd5c-22f0-4271-b665-a096c5dbfbd2)

**Pick your fix and see it.** Wave will propose different approaches with tradeoffs. The definition of “best” in hardware design depends on the use case. Maybe you want to optimize for performance? Maybe for power? Pick the one for you! Wave re-simulates and re-reads the new waveform. See a diff of how the waveform changed and a visual indication of where the fix was implemented.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/b0875bc9-fb55-4275-8c7e-11f926bc597d)

Now watch it fix a bug end to end with Rishov!

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eTycCILW6Jk>

🙏 **Asks & Offers**

If you design chips or lead a team, email us! We’d love to work with you and speed up your RTL development.

Know someone who does? Email us!

Just want to chat about hardware? **EMAIL US!!**

👬 **The Team**

We met in our freshman dorm at Georgia Tech nearly a decade ago! We became best friends and roommates for all four years of college - after, Athreya went to NYC to work at Google and Rishov stayed to do his PhD. We promised each other that once we’re free, that we’ll go all-in and work on something we’re passionate about together. Turns out, Rishov’s deep PhD thesis on chip simulation and compilers was the perfect spark.

Today we announce our company and are roommates once again ❤️

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/eef30a82-c606-494a-a093-3649920c7857)

—

Say hi 👋 [hi@hardwareintelligence.ai](mailto:hi@hardwareintelligence.ai) · [hardwareintelligence.ai](http://hardwareintelligence.ai)

[@Athreya Anand](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/551607) · [athreya@hardwareintelligence.ai](mailto:athreya@hardwareintelligence.ai)

[@Rishov Sarkar](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2565323) · [rishov@hardwareintelligence.ai](mailto:rishov@hardwareintelligence.ai)

launches.title: Synapse Semiconductor: We put a neural network inside the camera pixel.
launches.tagline: Semiconductors to push machines where humans cant go.
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/oHKXAeiH79Y>

**TLDR:** Synapse Semiconductor builds image sensors that process **AI on the sensor** itself. Each pixel captures light and runs neural-network computation in the same device, replacing the need for a GPU while cutting the power and latency of edge vision.\
\
\
A camera has no use by itself. Its value is only when its information gets evaluated. How can a camera that only has value when combined with a GPU support local intelligence? GPUs will get better, yet the fundamental problem is the separation of the camera and the GPU. Solving that separation will unlock bountiful innovation in machine perception. 

**RETINA: a chip designed like the human retina which runs neural network operations in the camera pixel.** 

\
We have compressed the whole edge AI vision hardware stack into **one wafer**. CNNS, VLMS, etc can run on just one chip that senses light. Our compute transistors are also the same photosensors that see light. There is no longer separation between compute (Nvidia Jetson Nano) and a camera (RealSense Depth Camera). \
\
If you are building robotic perception, drones, and vision systems for physical AI —> [book.synapsesemi.org](http://book.synapsesemi.org)

launches.title: Atlas Discovery - Foundation models that predict patient outcomes
launches.tagline: SOTA results on drug response and clinical trial success prediction
launches.body:
TL;DR: Nine out of ten drugs fail in clinical trials because we can’t predict how a patient will respond. We backtested our model on multiple clinical trials in Cancer and Autoimmune diseases and separated responders vs non-responders successfully 70-90% of the time. We’ve presented our research at 3 conferences so far.

Hey everyone! We ([Sanjukta Bhattacharya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sanjukta-b-82b541198/), [Christian Gensbigler](https://www.linkedin.com/in/christian-g-a2594029a/), and I) started Atlas Discovery to get treatments to patients who need them most.

**The problem:** We don’t have the tools to predict how a patient will respond to a given drug because our predictive tools are limited to testing drugs on cells in a dish, in animals, or directly in human clinical trials. Cells in a dish and animal models offer some biological information, but the translation to human response is fundamentally limited. Clinical trials, on the other hand, can cost hundreds of millions of dollars and take nearly 15 years end-to-end. 

**Our solution** is to train foundation models on both pre-clinical and clinical data. Our model learns the underlying biology from abundant pre-clinical data and then relates it to human response with the scarce clinical data that exists from hospitals and clinical trials. 

**Progress**: 0.7-0.9 AUROC across different clinical trials when using our foundation models to predict whether a patient will respond to a drug in a clinical trial. When we run interpretability on our model, we find that the model attends to genes relevant to drug response. We validated this with disease-area experts; find more in our blog linked below.

We've also shown that models trained on in vitro cell data (Latin for "in glass") and mouse data can translate to gains in predicting patient response to drugs in human clinical trials.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/6813bfeb-e5c9-47ec-9b9e-89362cf8eb15)

We’ve presented our research in 3 top conferences (ICLR, CSHL, ICML) and shown that new AI architectures like discrete diffusion can learn these gene expression patterns and predict response to treatments with over 10x improvement in accuracy while training on 50x less data.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/fa2a6593-751d-448b-a67b-e232e3e07ffb)

When benchmarked on an out-of-distribution task of ranking targets for atherosclerosis, a heart disease condition, our model outperforms traditional methods as well as other AI models. The task was to use the latent space to rank genes that, when knocked out, would reverse a cell from a diseased inflammatory state to a non-inflammatory state. Notably, our model achieved this without ever being trained on the relevant cell type, suggesting a capacity for generalization that extends well beyond its training distribution.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/784a4ce4-2933-49eb-81a9-32649bbf60cc)

Our value is in informing trial success, whether a given trial will succeed, whether a failed drug will work in a particular subset, or whether a drug could be repurposed for another indication. 

**Our ask** is intros to:

1. People at hospitals and healthcare systems for data and research partnerships
2. People in biopharma who work on clinical trials or broadly on drug discovery and development
3. Friends who would be interested in our work.

Reach us at [founders@atlasdiscovery.bio](mailto:founders@atlasdiscovery.bio)

Website: <https://atlasdiscovery.bio/>

Preprint: <https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.15.732063v1.full>

Clinical trial case study: <https://atlasdiscovery.bio/clinical-trial-response-prediction>

**Your users are telling your agent exactly why they churn! You’re not listening.**

Hey YC! We’re Shubham and Parth, childhood friends, founders of **Agnost AI**.

**TL;DR: Agnost AI reads every conversation your chat or voice agent has with your users. We show you what your users want, where they get frustrated, and why they leave.**

**The feedback hiding in your logs becomes discoveries, evals, and fixes ready to ship. We’re already processing over 1 million events every day and growing.**

Try us out at[ agnost.ai](http://agnost.ai)

### <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gKyhf6rUELg>

### **The problem**

Traditional product analytics were built for clicks.\
Observability was built for token costs, latencies, and deterministic errors.

But every product is rapidly moving from UI to conversation, and agent failures don’t look like traditional failures. The LLM returns 200 OK and says “sorry, I can’t do that.” The real failures are hiding in your conversations:

* “can it remember this for next time?” → feature request
* “you said it’s done, but nothing happened” → bug
* “i’ve told you this three times already” → frustration
* “nvm i’ll just do it myself” → churn

Today teams throw more evals at this. But evals only tell you whether you fixed something, not what to fix. You can’t write a test for a problem you haven’t discovered yet.

### **How it works**

1. **Install our skill:** 3 lines of code, or point your OpenTelemetry exporter at us. Any LLM, any framework. Add any custom metadata like user tier, model versions, etc. We’re at:[ docs.agnost.ai](http://docs.agnost.ai)
2. **Every conversation becomes a signal:** feature requests, bugs, frustration, churn risk, failed upgrades. Detected for your product, with the exact users & conversations behind each.
3. **The insight becomes action:** when hundreds of users rageprompt at your agent due to a specific bug, Agnost AI hands you the insight with the exact conversations behind it: 
   * create an eval from it
   * debug it,
   * or let Agnost fix it itself: our GitHub app opens a PR, tested against your past conversations, so you know it works before it ships.

   Your agent gets better every week.

### **Who we are**

Childhood friends, 8 years and counting.

launches.title: HERA: catches thousand-dollar drawing mistakes before the shop floor.
launches.tagline: Hera reviews every drawing against your factory's own standards and the ASME code, catching expensive mistakes and preventing rework 10x faster than manual review.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Every custom metal part starts as a drawing, and every drawing gets checked by hand before anyone builds it. Hera does that check in minutes instead of a full day, and catches the mistakes that turn into scrapped parts.**

[**https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y**](https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y)

**The Problem**

Custom mechanical parts run on 2D drawings. Whether you're an OEM releasing drawings to suppliers, or an aerospace supplier answering to source inspection, every drawing has to be checked against ASME/ISO standards and GD&T requirements before it goes anywhere near a machine.

Right now, that review is done by hand, and usually by the most senior engineer in the building. And a single missed tolerance callout or an ambiguous datum reference can mean a scrapped part, a blown schedule, or a shipment that fails inspection.

We heard the same story from a pressure vessel fabricator, a semiconductor tooling shop, and a medical device manufacturer: reviews take days. This isn't because the work is hard. There's simply no good way to do it faster without cutting corners, and nobody cuts corners on a drawing that could scrap a $40,000 part.

**Our Solution**

Hera is a brain for manufacturing. Any real advance in manufacturing has to be grounded in two things: the standards parts are held to and the reality of the shop floor. So that's what we built Hera on.

Upload a drawing and Hera checks GD&T callouts, tolerance stack ups, and title block requirements against ASME Y14.5, relevant ISO standards, and your own design intent. The result is a drawing your shop can build right the first time, without the delays and rework that eat margins. Every review also makes Hera more valuable, creating a system of record for drawing errors that helps teams build better models for engineering processes.

**While the current review takes days, Hera takes minutes… and gets better by the drawing.**

**Us**

**Noelle** grew up in an industrial park her family runs in the Philippines and has been on factory floors her whole life. At 19, she built a water-treatment facility that added 40 L/s of capacity to the park. 

**Meera** has spent years around manufacturing: at her family's plants, and on projects at Pfizer and TE Connectivity, where she built a SOTA discrete-event simulation. She taught herself PLC programming and C++, and has published ML research at UW.

We actually met on a bus to a factory tour, and have been best friends ever since!

tl;dr: Why can't e-commerce companies scale like tech companies? And how we might be able to change that.

We spent 12 months embedded in the operations of 30 e-commerce brands\! Here’s what we learnt:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107204&key=user_uploads/3288698/1a3cc8c3-db71-4d81-b2ad-9679b77f9451)

Most companies couldn't even automate a basic return processing, let alone offer exchanging items or build an AI agent to approve returns or send shipping label to the customer.

Expansion made it worse: more countries and/or SKUs = exponentially more problems.

**What we built:** We have built an agentic OS for e-commerce: You connect your shop stack, then describe how you want to handle shipments, returns, refunds, or claims → Pango builds the return portal, fixes the delivery options, and builds a customer service process and agent for you.

launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: [Daqstra](https://www.daqstra.com/) is the AI-native test orchestration platform for physical R&D. We connect fragmented test hardware, capture every run, and give engineers an API to operate their test setup, helping aerospace, energy, and robotics teams spend less time rebuilding infrastructure.**

Hey! We’re [Anchit Kumar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anchitk/) and [Darell Chua](https://www.linkedin.com/in/darell-chua/), the founders of [Daqstra](https://www.daqstra.com/).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106987&key=user_uploads/2547322/7ed7475e-d673-4796-9462-d40f72da12ad)

We met while testing liquid rocket engines in the Mojave Desert.

The engines were difficult, but much of the friction came from the infrastructure around them. Before each test, we connected sensors, custom electronics, NI hardware, PLCs, and controllers that were never designed to work together. After each run, the data was scattered across machines, file formats, scripts, and people’s heads.

Before we could learn from one test, we often had to reconstruct what had happened.

After talking with teams building rockets, energy systems, robots, and drones, we kept hearing the same story: **their hardware was advancing faster than the infrastructure used to test it.**

## What We Built

[Watch the demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ykvD67omalI) or visit [daqstra.com](http://daqstra.com).

launches.title: Cosmic Robotics: Autonomous construction on Earth and beyond
launches.tagline: Robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars. We’re proving the technology by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth — utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re [James](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamesemerick/) and [Lewis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewis-c-jones/) - co-founders of [Cosmic Robotics](https://www.cosmicrobotics.com). 

**TL;DR**

**We build robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars**. We’re proving the technology today by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth – utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers. Our first machine, Cosmic-1, has already installed tens of thousands of solar panels in the field and more than doubled the productivity of traditional crews.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Dl00xlJbcI> 

**❌ The problem**

After working at NASA JPL, SpaceX, and Relativity Space, we believe rockets are no longer the limiting factor to space exploration and that the first humans will land on Mars by 2034. **The new bottleneck is construction**. We won't be sending thousands of construction workers to Mars to build the energy, compute, and housing needed to sustain even a small city. **It has to be built by robots that don't exist yet**.

On Earth we have a similar problem - **we’ve lost the ability to build**. Construction productivity has declined for 50 years while manufacturing and agriculture became 10-15x more productive through automation. **The missing technology is robotic manipulation for the tasks still done by hand**: lifting, placing, fastening.

Meanwhile, there is a generational infrastructure buildout happening right now. **$7 trillion** is going into AI data centers, power, and compute over the next six years, **more than the Apollo Program, Manhattan Project, and Interstate Highway System combined**. 40% of US data center projects are running behind schedule, and the skilled labor shortage is the #1 cause. 

**🤖 What we've built**

Cosmic-1 is a 10,000 lb autonomous robot capable of heavy-lift manipulation. In solar, it picks up 90 lb panels and places them onto racking with millimeter precision in any environment: 100-degree heat, freezing rain, snow, and dust. It seamlessly integrates into existing construction processes. Across tens of thousands of cycles it has more than doubled the labor productivity of solar installation, on some of the largest solar projects in the US.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/bb5f86ec-a23b-4ffd-a173-87f36ce6fb1c)

**👬 The Team**

We come at this problem from two angles. James (CEO) grew up on construction sites, then spent his career bringing robots to the field with Built Robotics and Autodesk Research. He learned you don't change the oldest industry in the world by disrupting it; you earn your way in by giving crews better tools.

Lewis' (CTO) life ambition is to build a city on Mars. His work at NASA, SpaceX, and Relativity Space spans rocket engines, launch vehicles, satellites, space stations, and, yes, Martian robots. When it became clear the space industry was well on its way to Mars, he went looking for the construction robots. When he didn't find them, we started Cosmic.

We’ve brought together a team of industry experts with experience building robots, rockets, drones, self-driving cars, humanoids, and nuclear reactor operations. We know what it takes to get a machine to show up day-in-day-out on the jobsite.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/87f30a8e-6f83-490e-8bef-04225d1a525e)

**🚀 What's next**

We're scaling in solar, taking Cosmic-1 into data center construction, and working with NASA on lunar construction robotics. Revenue and data from deployments on Earth train the systems we'll deploy on Mars.

**🙏 Our asks**

1. **Know a hyperscaler or neocloud construction team?** Please connect us.
2. **Share this post** and [follow our journey](https://www.linkedin.com/company/cosmic-robotics/).
