Hi Launch YC,

I'm the founder and CEO of OneSignal. Today, we're announcing our new AI vision, and I'm excited to share it with the Launch YC community.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r7ccDbGVJ5U>

**The problem**

OneSignal first went through YC as a mobile gaming company called Hiptic Games.

After pivoting away from mobile games, we used our experience to uncover an opportunity to truly "Make something people want," and began working toward a mission to Democratize Customer Engagement for B2C companies.

For years, most B2C marketing automation products have had lengthy implementation processes, dated interfaces, and a learning curve steep enough that many teams hire a full-time expert. Many of them were also built in a world where email was the dominant channel, and have zero or weak support campaigns that span across Email, Mobile Push, SMS/RCS, and other channels.

In contrast, we made OneSignal incredibly easy to use from the start: customers can get going for free with an intuitive product experience, a powerful suite of tools for omni-channel messaging, and the performance to support some of the largest brands in the world. Today, OneSignal sends billions of daily messages for hundreds of thousands of active apps.

But no matter how easy and powerful we made the product, marketers still needed to bring a lot of their own time and expertise to get the best results from their campaigns.

**The solution**

Today, I'm excited to announce our vision and the products that will make lifecycle marketing autonomous. Our mission is still to Democratize Customer Engagement, but with AI we can achieve it in ways that were never possible before. This AI vision enables us to empower under-resourced marketing teams with the time and expertise that has seemed always out of reach.

We've broken this mission into phases, which we think of as an autonomy ladder. Most marketers don't want to hand the keys to an autonomous system on day one, so we'll roll out features that build the systems and trust needed at each step.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105807&key=user_uploads/5571/09a43a18-3ca8-4268-bd70-ab1798220546)

**Level 0 — Manual.** The dashboard. A marketer drives every click, and the team scales by hiring. This is where the entire category has lived.

**Level 1 — Assistance.** AI drafts copy, suggests audiences, and explains your analytics in plain language. You review and ship. This is live today.

**Level 2 — Expert Assist.** AI becomes proactive. It recommends campaigns to fill lifecycle gaps, flags mistakes, and checks your work. Your input is still required.

**Level 3 — Agentic Autopilot.** You delegate bounded work, and AI does it within the scope and rules you've defined. You approve work in batches.

**Level 4 — Full Operator.** You set the goals and the guardrails. AI plans, sends, tests, and improves campaigns against them, reaching out only when it needs you.

**What we're launching today**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105807&key=user_uploads/5571/da0aff66-9335-4ac3-87bf-d61aaa95b014)

**OneSignal AI** — An in-product agent that can do everything a person can: generate message copy, design emails, analyze message performance, and recommend next steps to maximize user engagement. Best of all, it can create and analyze complex multi-step Journeys, saving hours of work.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105807&key=user_uploads/5571/f96522b2-51f9-404c-83fe-5b8bcbf4618a)

**Brand Kit** — Define your audience, voice and tone, industry, and visual assets on a centralized configuration page or pull them automatically from your website. Set guardrails for language to avoid. OneSignal AI uses your Brand Kit when generating copy, email designs, and in-app messages.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105807&key=user_uploads/5571/b4c791bc-66cd-4849-afbf-d6921338d492)

**OneSignal MCP** — Brings OneSignal's capabilities to the AI tools and agents you already use. The MCP is available now on the ChatGPT and Cursor marketplaces, coming soon to the Claude marketplace, and available through Smithery for any other AI client. Together, the MCP and the OneSignal API make it possible to use the platform in a fully headless way.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105807&key=user_uploads/5571/16f8ec08-92f4-4612-b342-555017d5082b)

Soon, we'll also release a OneSignal Slack Agent, bringing the capabilities of OneSignal AI and the OneSignal MCP to where your team already spends its time. And we'll be rolling out an API to create, edit, and analyze Journeys, so your team can set up complex campaigns without ever logging into the OneSignal dashboard.

**Try it today**

All of these features are available on OneSignal's free plan. Small companies can send unlimited push notifications and up to 10,000 emails per month for free. Paid plans start at $19/mo plus affordable usage-based pricing. Installing OneSignal is as simple as copying a prompt into Claude Code. You can get started at https://onesignal.com

launches.title: Screenpipe: Record how you work and turn that into agents
launches.tagline: Record how you work and turn that into agents
launches.body:
screenpipe records what you do, see and hear on your computer, makes it searchable, and gives agents the context to understand how you actually work. The project has 20K+ GitHub stars.

<https://youtu.be/c1jV6E9pyug>

Most AI agents start every task with partial context.

They can read the prompt and apps you connect. They do not remember the meeting where a decision was made, the tab you opened last Tuesday, the exact steps you took to fix a problem, or the edge case you discovered while doing the work.

screenpipe runs quietly in the background and captures screen and audio context on your machine. Then you can ask:

* maintain a second brain for every person, projects, tasks, meetings


* turn the workday into a daily recap and time breakdown for standups or client billing
* maintain a personal CRM from the people, conversations, and follow-ups seen during the day
* find commitments mentioned in meetings or messages that never made it into a task list
* analyze repeated work and produce a list of workflows worth automating
* save prompts and context from Claude, Codex, and ChatGPT into a searchable journal

Agents can use screenpipe as long-term memory, so they work from what actually happened instead of only what you remembered to paste into a prompt.

The same foundation also works across team machines. Teams can map repeated workflows, generate SOPs, find bottlenecks, and identify automation opportunities across the tools where work actually happens.

screenpipe is open source and local-first. You control what gets recorded, can exclude apps, windows, and URLs, and choose where your data lives.

I’ve been building my own AI second brain since 2020, but it could only remember what I explicitly saved. I built screenpipe so my AI could understand what I was actually doing across my screen and conversations. Other people began using it for the same reason. Today, we’re turning that foundation into context for personal and team agents.

**Our ask**

Try screenpipe and comment with the agent you would build if it could remember everything you’ve worked on.

Try screenpipe: <https://screenpipe.com>

launches.title: Prized: Lovable for internal tools
launches.tagline: The fastest way for non-engineers to ship secure internal tools.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Marinos and Hudson, co-founders of Prized.

**TL;DR:** Prized lets anyone at your company build and ship secure internal tools with AI. Company data comes pre-connected and scoped to what each person should see, every access is audited, and finished tools deploy behind your company's sign-in.

**Launch video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WILimoqemD4>

**The problem**

Building software has never been easier. And the people who need internal tools most, in ops, support, and finance, are done waiting on engineering.

So they build it themselves. They rip Claude Code or Cursor, pull straight from company data, and ship a working tool in an afternoon. No permissions. No audit trail. No one watching where the data goes.

Security is assumed to be fine because the tool is "just internal."

it's not…

**The solution**

People aren't going to stop building with AI. So we built them a place where it's safe.

With Prized, anyone can spin up a sandbox that comes with company data already attached, scoped to what they should see, with an audit trail on every access. 

From there it's whatever building style they like: describe the tool in our app builder and watch it take shape, or bring a coding agent like Claude Code and build it themselves. Shipping is one click, and the finished tool sits behind your company's sign-in.

The person who runs the workflow finally gets to build the tool for it. Safely, this time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105647&key=user_uploads/2485896/e426b427-8a79-4ca5-b462-b26b98db43e0)

**Secure by default**

Security is enforced in the infrastructure, not left to the person building the tool:

* **Least privilege per tool.** Every tool gets its own database role and integration scopes; it can read and write only what it was granted.
* **Credentials stay out of reach.** Secrets live in a broker and never touch the tool's code or the agent's context, so they can't leak or cross workspace boundaries.
* **Outbound traffic proxy.** External calls only go to explicitly allowed hosts, and integrations are read-only until someone turns writes on.

launches.title: Instance: Automated evaluation for robot policies, starting with the success detector
launches.tagline: Today, evaluating a robot policy means humans have to watch the robot roll out, mark success, and reset the scene – we're automating that.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We’re **automating robot evaluation**– the loop where you wait for your robot to roll out, judge its success, and then reset the scene. Today, we’re launching step one: a **success detector** that automatically tells you whether your robot actually completed its task. Book a demo with [founders@instancelabs.ai](mailto:founders@instancelabs.ai) and we’ll visit your office to show you how it works!

<https://youtu.be/EqxkPffnUKk>

**The problem**

In Lucy’s robotics research this past year, she **spent way too much time being a babysitter for her robot**. Her project was to get a humanoid to find objects around a room, so her days went like this: start a rollout, watch the robot open all the drawers in the room for 30 minutes, mark success/fail in a spreadsheet, then get up, close all the drawers, and put the objects back where they started. Then do it again, and again, and again. Some days ended with back pain, and for weeks she couldn’t work on anything else because she was stuck doing exactly this.

That was one robot, in one lab, running a single policy. Industry teams run fleets of robots across dozens of policies, with **multiple people assigned to sit and watch each one**. Every robotics team we’ve talked to has some version of this– and it will only grow as robot foundation models scale.

**Our solution**

Instance is building the **autonomous evaluation rig for robot learning**: your robot rolls out, we judge success, a second robot resets the scene, and the next rollout starts– with no humans in the loop at all.

Today, we’re starting with the success judge. Point us at a task description and your video rollouts, and we return a verdict with detailed subtask captions. We benchmarked our verifier against 10,000+ held-out, human-labeled episodes across 7 robot platforms, and it resulted in **higher accuracy than Claude Opus 4.8, at a fraction of the latency.**

**Try it**

Try it at [demo.instancelabs.ai](http://demo.instancelabs.ai) – drop in a video, or record one from your phone and watch it get verified live.

**Team**

We’re Claire and Lucy, MIT grads and friends since middle school! 

Claire studied math and CS at MIT. At NASA JPL, she built software to simulate planetary atmospheres, and at the MIT Media Lab, she researched sustainable propulsion for spaceflight. She loves working where software meets the physical world.

Lucy studied CS at MIT and completed her MEng in MIT's Learning and Intelligent Systems lab. She’s an experienced robotics researcher, and has in the past worked on satellite software at SpaceX, LLM unit testing at Amazon, and brain computer interfaces at Blackrock Neurotech.

* deploying robots in the real world

On major projects, the record keeps losing: 80% of megaprojects blow their budget or schedule, and sums in dispute average a third of contract budgets. We think the root cause is hiding in plain sight — in the paperwork.

The documents aren't a pile, they're a web: the safety plan leans on procedures; procedures lean on templates, registers and licences; and the tender made promises all of them have to keep true. launches.title: Freesolo: Post-Training Built for your Agent
launches.tagline: Small models, frontier performance
launches.body:
Not every AI interaction is best served with a large frontier model. There is a long tail of trillion-token use cases, from tagging to search, best served by a sub-10B-parameter model that runs in milliseconds and costs many orders of magnitude less than the frontier. However, engineers historically had to choose between model size and quality; as models got smaller, performance, adherence, and recall dropped linearly. Post-training on production data closes that gap. We built Freesolo Flash to make training loops like SFT and RL easy and end-to-end completable through your coding agent.

We accomplish this in a few different ways

* Upfront pricing: instead of billing by GPU hours or tokens spent while training, we quote the cost of the entire run upfront, so your agent can accurately tweak the dataset, model size, and algorithms it uses while staying in your budget before it starts the run.
* Our GPU infrastructure is optimized to make your specific run as in-expensive and fast as possible. This optimization means training with flash is 8x less expensive for SFT and 5.5x less expensive for GRPO (RL) when compared to Tinker.

Flash is built out of our own frustrations with current managed post-training solutions, especially for SLMs. We believe that unlocking frontier capability for a narrow task into a small model will prove to be the best improvement for all agentic product UX. Flash is our first step towards solving this. Just grab a Freesolo API Key, point your agent at the training package, and watch it push your lightweight model beyond the frontier.

Flash is publicly available today at  <https://freesolo.co>[ ](https://freesolo.co/). Train on!

launches.title: PathPilot - AI Platform for Lenders
launches.tagline: AI agents that help lenders grow without scaling operational headcount.
launches.body:
Today, we’re launching PathPilot Agents for Lending: specialized AI agents that help consumer lenders automate origination, servicing, collections, and quality on their operations.

## The problem

Consumer lenders need to grow, but lending operations are still expensive, manual, and dependent on large internal teams and external vendors.

Borrowers are often asked to submit the same information multiple times, wait for manual reviews, and navigate disconnected processes across origination, servicing, and collections.

For lenders, this means higher operating costs, slower decisions, inconsistent customer experiences, and difficulty scaling without adding more headcount.

Current AI solutions are not enough. Without specialization, guardrails, and the right operational context, agent quality breaks down—especially in regulated, customer-facing workflows.

## What we built

PathPilot builds specialized AI agents for lending operations, powered by a proprietary harness that connects AI models directly to each lender’s workflows, systems, policies, and data.

It starts with the **Origination Agent**, which guides borrowers through WhatsApp or web forms, collects the right information, pre-verifies documents, and connects with underwriting, identity, and fraud systems to support faster decisions.

Once the loan is active, the **Servicing Agent** helps customers with payments, balances, questions, and account updates across voice, WhatsApp, chat, and email.

When a payment is missed, the **Collections Agent** follows up compliantly, keeps full conversation and account context, connects with call center and CRM systems, and negotiates next steps to drive resolution.

Behind every workflow, the **Audit and Quality Agent** reviews every interaction and action, identifies quality or compliance risks, and provides actionable feedback that helps both human teams and AI agents improve continuously.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aAQ1mLB-qPo>

## One agent or a coordinated workforce

Lenders can start with a single agent for one workflow or deploy a coordinated workforce of agents that work together and share context.

For example, the Origination Agent can pass a customer’s application history to the Servicing Agent. If the account later becomes delinquent, the Collections Agent can use the same operational context rather than starting the relationship from zero.

The Audit and Quality Agent works across the entire system, creating a continuous feedback loop that improves accuracy, customer experience, and compliance.

Because PathPilot is built on a modular framework, internal AI and engineering teams can extend, customize, and ultimately own the system as their capabilities grow.

We do not want lenders to become permanently dependent on another black-box vendor. We want to give them a reliable foundation for building and operating their own AI workforce.

## Why we built this

The problem became personal when I tried to finance my first car after moving to the U.S.

I had no local credit history and very little understanding of how the process worked. I went through a long and frustrating process in which multiple lenders manually reviewed my application, repeatedly requested information, and ultimately offered me a loan with very high fees.

Today, as a real estate investor, I still experience many of the same problems when applying for a mortgage or refinancing a property. The process remains slow, repetitive, and difficult to navigate—even when you understand how lending works.

There needs to be a better way.

Before PathPilot, David and I spent years building and operating AI first products at Meta. We learned that making AI work reliably in production requires much more than choosing a model. It requires integrations, evaluations, guardrails, feedback loops, and deep operational context.

We started PathPilot to bring that infrastructure to lending—so lenders can operate more efficiently and borrowers can receive a faster, clearer, and more responsive experience.

## Where we are today

PathPilot agents are already supporting fintech lenders, BNPLs, embedded lending platforms, and collections organizations across the U.S. and Latin America.

Our customers use PathPilot for workflows including conversational origination, document validation, servicing, collections, and quality assurance.

## Our ask

We would love to speak with:

* Consumer lenders, BNPLs, neobanks, and embedded lending companies
* Operations, servicing, collections, risk, and compliance leaders
* Lending platforms interested in offering specialized AI agents to their customers
* Internal AI teams looking for a framework they can customize and eventually own

Book a demo at [getpathpilot.com](http://getpathpilot.com).

launches.tagline: The smarter way to offer great benefits — without overpaying for coverage employees don't need
launches.body:
**TLDR**

Hey all, I run Every, the all-in-one HR and Finance platform. We are currently serving 2100 customers, including over 300+ YC startups.

Today we are launching Every Health Benefits. We combined our HR and Fintech stack to build a new way of funding health benefits that **saves the average startup $1,200 per employee per year** - while keeping the same carriers, networks, and employee experience.

Launch video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T59_0OouTEU&feature=youtu.be>

**Problem**

Healthcare is the second largest cost for many startups behind payroll, and every year costs are increasing while insurance coverage is staying the same or decreasing. Costs have climbed 24% over the last five years, according to[ KFF's Employer Health Benefits Survey.](https://www.kff.org/health-costs/2024-employer-health-benefits-survey/)

I have been the CEO at a startup for 10+ years now. The first few times I renewed benefits (at my previous startup) I thought my HR vendor was ripping me off. I don’t love being taken advantage of, so I got pretty upset and immediately started looking for a new vendor. When I did, I realized prices went up everywhere, and I was stuck paying thousands of dollars more for a product that wasn’t even improving.

The math is broken, and I was paying a lot of money is for benefits I knew my team was barely using.

Most startup teams skew young and healthy. The average startup employee never comes close to hitting their deductible, but given the war for talent, startups have to offer expensive Gold and Platinum level plans.

**Solution**

Every Benefits flips the model. Instead of paying higher premiums upfront to cover employee healthcare costs, employers choose a lower-premium plan and pair it with an employer-funded reimbursement arrangement. **Employees are reimbursed for eligible expenses as they're incurred**—so you are paying for benefits as costs are incurred, instead of before.

The result? Silver plan that feels like Gold. A Gold plan that feels like Platinum. Same carriers. Same networks. A $0 effective deductible experience for employees—at a meaningfully lower cost for employers.

**Savings**

launches.title: Keystroke - open sourcing our internal agents & automations platform
launches.tagline: An all-in-one platform for building internal agents & workflows.
launches.body:
**_tl;dr:_** Keystroke is an all-in-one platform for building internal agents and workflows. It's built from the ground up with coding agents in mind. Build agents and workflows as TypeScript in your own repo, then deploy them to a web app where your whole team can use them.

Try it free: <https://keystroke.ai/> \
GitHub: <https://github.com/keystrokehq/keystroke>

### why we built keystroke (our pivot story)

Hey everyone, we’re [Blake](https://x.com/cblakerouse) and [Dallin](https://x.com/dalbentley) from [Keystroke](https://keystroke.ai/home). Keystroke is a recent pivot from Buster, our original YC W24 idea.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105225&key=user_uploads/699099/e5ee8874-7b36-45d5-b9cd-f0f96cd14846)

At Buster, we spent a lot of time building internal agents and automations. We used visual platforms like n8n and Gumloop, as well as code-first tools like Trigger.dev, Mastra, and several of Vercel’s open frameworks. We genuinely liked many of them, but kept encountering two different problems:

1. Visual tools gave us integrations, credentials, hosting, and an application the rest of the team could use. They were fast initially, but became difficult to maintain as the systems grew. Tests and typechecks were limited, JSON blobs were hard to review, and debugging failures was painful.
2. Code-first tools gave us ordinary TypeScript, tests, npm packages, and a codebase that coding agents could work with directly. But after building something, we were deploying it to infrastructure rather than an application people could use. We still needed to configure the chat UI, streaming, credentials, integrations, run history, permissions, and sharing ourselves.

So, we started building the thing we wish existed: a code-first framework that made it stupid easy to build complex agents and AI systems, with a web app for teams to collaborate on top.

We liked it so much that we decided to pivot away from Buster and focus on building Keystroke full time.

## keystroke rebuilt our W24 idea in 5 minutes

With Keystroke, I was able to rebuild our original startup’s product (an AI data analyst) in \~5 minutes.

I pointed Cursor at our old Buster repo and it was able to:

* spin up a local Keystroke project
* rebuild the OG Buster agent w/ memory, its own file system, etc
* connect our Postgres DB, PostHog, Metabase, and Slack
* build skills for using each of the data sources
* explore our DB and add schema docs to the file system
* build a workflow to keep schema docs synced
* name the agent "Delbert"
* then pushed him up to the Keystroke app

Since then, Delbert has been answering ad-hoc questions for me in Slack on a regular bases. He builds me metabase dashboards when I need them. He sets his own triggers, reviews key metrics periodically, and pings me in Slack if anything looks off.

## how keystroke works

In Keystroke, workflows are ordinary async TypeScript: a ‘for’ loop is an actual ‘for’ loop, inputs use Zod schemas, and everything you build can be tested with Vitest. Our managed runtime makes workflows durable across errors, sleeps, approval steps, and process restarts.

Agents wrap Vercel’s AI SDK and can use workflows, actions, other agents, MCP servers, and integrations as tools. They also include memory, a persistent filesystem, web search, triggers, and optional VM sandboxes.

Deployed agents and workflows instantly appear in the web app with a chat UI, workflow visualizations, input forms, sharing, credential management, integrations, and logs.

**The entire platform was built from the ground of with coding agents in mind**. Your coding agent can use the CLI to scaffold a local directory with a Keystroke project and an [AGENTS.md](http://AGENTS.md). Then, it can build whatever agent or AI system you want, search our docs, run tests, and push what you build up to the Keystroke platform.

##

launches.title: Coasty: The computer-use agent that doesn't break on real software
launches.tagline: Coasty helps developers kill RPA.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Coasty gives developers a computer-use agent that reliably automates back-office work in legacy desktop software where RPA scripts and other CUAs fail. It’s achieved 82.81% on OSWorld and it’s great at automating workflows where quiet mistakes cost the most: regulatory filings, patient records, payments, and gives developers precise control and observability over its work.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3EwLfqlgDEM>\
(_The portals and the data in it, are mockups_)

**Replayable audit trail (real run):** <https://coasty.ai/share/5b3320fc-0e64-4f1b-b684-9fd6e8cd8960> 

**OSWorld submission (Coasty scored 82.81% on OSWorld Verified, confirmed by the OSWorld team, with our latest internal run at 85.60%.):**[ https://github.com/coasty-ai/coasty-osworld](https://github.com/coasty-ai/coasty-osworld)\
\
**The Problem**

Most back-office work doesn't happen in clean web apps. It happens in legacy desktop software, full of surprise pop-ups, wandering menus, and impenetrable UIs.

Today, developers automating this back-office “real” work are stuck choosing between brittle RPA scripts and CUAs that demo beautifully and score high but break on contact.

The problem isn't getting an agent to click. It's trusting it when a silent mistake gets someone fired.

### **Why Coasty is reliable where others aren't**

**It recovers mid-task.** Coasty catches its errors and fixes them mid-run. If it’s crunching on a 20-step workflow and makes a misclick at step 3, it will recover and start from the error. First-pass accuracy is vanity. Recovery keeps a run alive.

**It survives messy software.** Pop-ups, modals that steal focus, legacy desktop apps. Coasty doesn’t record clicks, it reads the screen. So when the UI changes overnight and every RPA script breaks, Coasty looks at the new screen and keeps going.

**It knows when it's done.** An agent that thinks it finished but didn't is worse than one that fails loudly. Coasty verifies its own output and leaves a timestamped audit trail you can replay.

**It swarms.** One task across forty state portals, each with its own ancient interface, all at once. Forty agents, one verified result set. What takes a team a week, is done overnight.

### **Traction**

Coasty has been verified by the OSWorld team and will be published soon, but also another internal benchmark we published (85.60%): <<https://github.com/coasty-ai/coasty-osworld> >.

We have paying customers on four continents, a few thousand active users, and we have actually grown 24x since Claude Cowork came out.

### **Why us**

We started working on this idea when models weren’t good enough for computer use (last summer), so we’ve built frameworks to test and run the perfect combination of models and harnesses to see what works in practice. Prateek worked as an ML engineer at multiple startups and dropped his Stanford admit while I did CS at Columbia and built my previous company’s entire agentic sales automation. We’ve grown with this field and have been working on it even before it got much attention, so we understand where CUAs mess up and how to deal with these messes realistically.

### **The ask**

Send us one workflow your team runs by hand. We’ll tell you straight whether Coasty can run it reliably today. If it looks automatable, we’ll build a working proof of concept on your real software before a long sales process.

We’re especially looking for intros to operators and executives in accounting, tax, insurance, healthcare, compliance, and data privacy - anywhere teams are still babysitting RPAs, clicking through legacy portals, reconciling records, filing forms, or moving data across old desktop software.

Here's our Calendly:[ https://cal.com/coasty/15min](https://cal.com/coasty/15min)

launches.title: Rindler - Turn Any Website Into An API For AI Agents
launches.tagline: Reliable web actions for AI agents, without integrations or scripts
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Rindler turns websites into deterministic APIs for AI agents. We map a site once into screens, actions, and structured outputs, so agents can read data and take actions quickly and reliably.

**Ask:** If you’re building an agent that needs to browse the web, compare products, fill forms, search listings, use authenticated portals, or act on third-party websites without an API, we’d love to help.

<https://youtu.be/V_nCIxYD-so>

## Problem

More products are starting to depend on AI agents that can do real work on the web: shop across retailers, pull housing listings, use job boards, submit forms, monitor prices, update back-office systems, and operate inside customer portals.

But most browser agents still treat every website visit like a new puzzle. On every run, they need to decipher the page, infer what matters, decide what to click, and recover when the page behaves differently.

That works for demos, but it breaks down in production. Real websites have pop-ups, login gates, cookie banners, bot defenses, slow-loading forms, dynamic filters, fragile dropdowns, layout changes, and pages that look similar but behave differently.

The result is slow execution, high token cost, and workflows that are hard to trust.

## Solution

Rindler maps websites into deterministic APIs for agents.

Instead of forcing an agent to re-explore a site every time, Rindler captures the site as structured screens, available actions, and typed outputs. Agents can then call actions like **search,** **add_to_cart**, or **download_records,** depending on the mapped site.

At runtime, Rindler handles the browser work through a remote MCP endpoint:

* Returning structured data
* Applying dynamic filters
* Managing popups, bot defenses, and layout changes
* Supporting authenticated flows

## Background

We started Rindler because “AI agent uses a browser” is compelling, but the current browser-agent loop is too brittle for teams building real products.

If an agent needs to use the same third-party site hundreds or thousands of times, it should not have to rediscover that site from scratch on every run.

Rindler is still a work in progress. Some sites map cleanly, others require more in-depth mappings, and bot-defended or logged-in sites may need a one-time credential or cookie capture.

We’re looking for feedback from founders building products where reliable web actions are part of the core workflow.

If there’s a website you wish your agent could use reliably, send it to us!

launches.title: Elements by Unlayer - Open-source React components for emails, pages, and PDFs
launches.tagline: Elements lets developers and AI agents create emails, web pages, and PDFs from the same React codebase.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We’re launching Unlayer Elements, an open-source React content layer that lets developers and AI agents create emails, web pages, and PDFs from the same codebase. Write once in React, render everywhere.

Today, we’re launching something new and open source:

# Unlayer Elements

An open-source React content layer for developers and AI agents to create emails, web pages, and PDFs from the same codebase.

GitHub: <https://github.com/unlayer/elements>\
Docs: <https://docs.unlayer.com/elements>\
Demo: <https://youtu.be/-ZoMlPYUbtk>

## **The Problem**

Every SaaS product eventually needs content creation.

At first, it’s just one transactional email.

Then it becomes welcome emails, password resets, receipts, invoices, reports, landing pages, PDFs, internal templates, previews, exports, and visual editing.

Most teams end up maintaining separate systems for each output:

* one system for email templates
* one system for web pages
* one system for PDFs
* one system for visual editing
* one system for exports

The content is often similar, but the implementation is different.

This becomes even more important now that AI agents are generating more code and content. Agents can create fast, but teams still need the output to be structured, reusable, version-controlled, and production-ready.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105004&key=user_uploads/105300/5911c2cd-ca33-48e8-86ff-72e1ce4fcfe7)

## **What We Built**

We built Unlayer Elements: open-source React components for creating emails, web pages, and PDFs from the same codebase.

Developers can use familiar components like:

* <Email>
* <Page>
* <Document>
* <Row>
* <Column>
* <Heading>
* <Paragraph>
* <Button>
* <Image>
* <Custom>

Each output mode is tuned for where the content will live:

* <Email> renders email-safe table HTML
* <Page> renders responsive web HTML
* <Document> renders print-ready HTML for PDFs and documents

Same component system. Different surfaces.

A few examples of what you can build:

* Transactional emails
* Landing pages
* Web versions of emails
* Invoices
* Receipts
* Reports
* Internal template galleries
* PDF documents
* AI-generated content flows

Hey everyone! We're [Matthew](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mdchow/) and [Victor](https://www.linkedin.com/in/victor-vannara/) - cofounders of [Trope](https://trope.ai/). We’re building the AI-native platform for ERP services.

**TLDR**

* After buying an ERP, companies spend over $50B a year on consulting services to get the software implemented

* Trope deploys agents to help ERP implementation teams deliver projects on time and on budget from one AI-native platform

**Launch Video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mhDiw0nKB34>

\
**❌ Problem**

Companies buy an ERP expecting it to become the most powerful software in their stack. It runs finance, inventory, procurement, operations, reporting, and the workflows the business depends on.

Buying an ERP is easy. Implementing it is hard and requires labour heavy consultant work where:

* Requirements get missed
* Workflows get configured differently than agreed
* Data issues get discovered too late
* Testing reveals the system does not match how the business actually works
* End-user adoption suffers

For implementation teams, the challenge is managing hundreds of stakeholders across concurrent projects, with thousands of documents, decisions, and system dependencies to track.

That is why so many ERP projects miss their budget, timeline, and targets, and why companies spend billions on implementation services.

Trope is the AI-native platform that deploys agents to deliver successful implementations faster.

Using Trope is like having a project manager, consultant, and developer working 24/7, so you can spend more time on the design and decisions.

Trope connects to the systems where project work already lives. It compares what was promised with what is actually being built, then flags gaps across scope, configuration, data, testing, training, and documentation before they become expensive.

We grew up in Vancouver and met at the University of British Columbia. We built operations and AI software at Tesla, Amazon, Zipline, and Schneider Electric.

launches.title: Energent.ai: Audit — The Fact-Checker for Every AI-Generated Result
launches.tagline: A fresh, independent AI agent that re-verifies every number in your AI results and shows its work — so trusting AI stops being a leap of faith.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We're [Rachel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rachelsonghu/) and [Kimi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/0xlingjiekong/), founders of [Energent.ai](https://www.energent.ai). We're excited (and honestly, a little proud) to introduce our newest feature: **Energent Audit**.

## 🚀 TL;DR

Energent Audit is a built-in, independent second opinion for your for every AI-generated results, especially numbers. Ask Energent to "prove it," "double-check that," or "show me where this number came from," and Audit spins up a completely fresh sub-agent — one with zero stake in the original answer — to retrace every number back to its source and hand you a clean HTML report on whether it holds up.

## ❌ The Problem

AI hallucination hasn't gone away — it's just gotten quieter. It shows up in the reports people care about most: financial analysis, health recommendations, board decks, the numbers real decisions get built on.

We interviewed 150+ users doing serious work with AI, and hallucination came back as their second-biggest concern overall — right after data security and privacy, and ahead of cost, speed, and everything else. The message was clear: people don't just want AI that's fast. They want AI they can stand behind.

## 🛠️ Our Solution

Meet **Energent Audit** — an independent audit layer for anything Energent builds for you.

Here's the insight at the heart of it: the agent that wrote an answer is the worst-positioned agent to grade it. So instead of asking Energent to mark its own homework, Audit calls in a brand-new AI sub-agent with no memory of how the analysis was built and no attachment to the outcome. Its only job is to verify.

**Independent, every time**

A fresh sub-agent re-checks the work with zero investment in the original answer, so nothing gets rubber-stamped.

_"The agent that built it doesn't get to grade itself."_

**Number-by-number validation**

Every figure is traced back to its source and re-derived — not glanced at, actually re-verified, one by one.

_"Trust, but verify, down to the decimal."_

**Visual data lineage**

A clear map of exactly which file, row, and transformation produced each number — so "where did this come from?" always has an answer.

_"Show your work, automatically."_

**A report you can actually hand someone**

Every audit ends in a clean, shareable HTML report you can send to a stakeholder, a boss, or an auditor — or just keep for your own peace of mind.

_"Confidence you can forward."_

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104955&key=user_uploads/315284/d0fb4f45-98f2-4687-b4a7-b777d6700ed6)

Audit is purpose-built to check work Energent has already done in your conversation — it's not a general web fact-checker, and it won't review a plan before it's run. It's laser-focused on one question: does this answer, and every number in it, actually hold up?

## 📖 Why We Built This

The same story came up again and again in our interviews: people loved what AI could do for their analysis, right up until they had to defend a number in a meeting. That gap — between "the AI said so" and "I can prove it" — is exactly what Audit closes. We believe trust in AI shouldn't be something you hope for. It should be one click away.

## 🎯 Our Ask

👉 Try Energent Audit today at [app.energent.ai](http://app.energent.ai) — run an analysis, then ask us to prove it.

👉 Reach out directly at [admin@energent.ai](mailto:admin@energent.ai) to see it live.

Cheers, The [Energent.ai](http://Energent.ai) Team ❤️

launches.title: Inkbox: Give your AI agents email, phone, iMessage, and an internet address
launches.tagline: The identity and communication layer for AI agents
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Inkbox is the identity and communication layer for AI agents: giving agents their own email, phone, iMessage, and internet address. Inkbox pulls together what your agent sees across email, calls, iMessage, and more, so your agent can act on the full context.

Hey YC! We're Ray, Alex, and Dima building Inkbox.

**How we got here**

A few months ago we were building web-automation agents. Every time an agent needed to log into a portal, it had to receive a confirmation email or get a 2FA code. And when we were away from our desks, we wanted to seamlessly contact the agents themselves: text them, check in, get a reply. We ended up stitching together services like Gmail, Twilio, and ngrok: separate services, each built for humans, none of them sharing any identity or context. 

That's the problem we set out to fix. We didn't need another email or voice API. We needed one service to tie its identity together with rich context. So we built it.

[**Launch video**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oJKl6tPHxRA)

**What Inkbox does**

Our API gives every agent:

* A unique email inbox (+ custom domain)
* A phone number that can call and text
* iMessage
* A persistent internet address (HTTPS tunnel) to receive internet traffic, like webhooks
* An encrypted credential vault with TOTP/2FA

**Who we are**

* Ray (CEO): CS PhD from MIT; previously cofounded Empallo, an AI virtual clinic for cardiovascular patients.
* Alex (CTO): MS in CS @ Northeastern. Previously ML engineering and computer networking research.
* Dima (CAIO): built ML pipelines on gigapixel pathology images at Harvard Medical School; co-author on 6+ peer-reviewed publications.

[**Quick demo with Claude**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTVkW_EG-Y4): Watch Claude Code provision an email, phone, and iMessage in a Minute.

**Our ask**

* **Try it**. Drop Inkbox into your preferred agent harness: we have plugins for[ Hermes](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/hermes-agent-plugin),[ OpenClaw](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/openclaw-plugin),[ Claude Code](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/claude-code-plugin), and[ Codex](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/codex-plugin). Each one runs a wizard that provisions Inkbox resources for your agent.
* **Ask your agent to self signup**. _Sign up for an Inkbox email account by following the guide at[ https://inkbox.ai/docs/get-started/agent-signup.md](https://inkbox.ai/docs/get-started/agent-signup.md) and refer to[ https://inkbox.ai/llms.txt](https://inkbox.ai/llms.txt) for full documentation._
* **Intros**. We'd love intros to teams running fleets of agents that each need their own identity to act in the real world: reaching out to people and businesses (email/phone/iMessage), holding their own accounts, and authenticating with a built-in credential vault.

Contact Ray at [ray@inkbox.ai](mailto:ray@inkbox.ai). Would love your feedback.

launches.title: Stillwind Builder — Zero to BOM in minutes instead of days
launches.tagline: AI agent that turns your PCB design intent into a complete, verified bill of materials.
launches.body:
❌ **The problem**

Every PCB design is a constraint problem: you need components that are electrically and functionally compatible with each other. Solving it by hand means hours — often days — of tracking down parts, reading datasheets, adding a component, discovering a conflict, and backtracking. Pick an MCU and the cascade begins: it needs a specific crystal, external flash on the QSPI bus, a regulator that can source its peak current. Every choice ripples through the whole design.

✅ **The solution**

Stillwind Builder formalizes your design constraints as an explicit system of equations and solves for matching components.

* **Verified specs.** Before we show you a part, a second model independently re-reads its datasheet and verifies the specs match — so the numbers you design against are what the datasheet actually says, not extraction artifacts.
* **Dependency-aware.** When you lock in a component, the agent reads its datasheet for the supporting parts it requires — voltage regulators, crystals, external flash — and updates the constraint system. The ripple effects of each choice are handled instead of discovered later.
* **You stay in control.** You set the direction and make the calls that matter; the agent handles the combinatorial grind.

At the end, you download your BOM and start wiring.

🚀 **Try it**

The public beta is live and free during launch week: [**https://stillwind.ai**](https://stillwind.ai)

Building hardware and want to tell us what's broken? We'd genuinely love that — grab time with us: <https://calendar.app.google/Bd7KQEAYLgt6SmHZ6>

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** 

Verdant is building the modern tech infrastructure for local government, and we’re starting with end-to-end permitting software that dramatically cuts local government permit review time. 

We help applicants file complete, compliant applications upfront, then help staff review them - our AI reads documents, plans, and diagrams, then flags issues and drafts the final report. 

**Launch Video**
[ ](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e5VeQc-NIrlNqIHZP-ASPhuE9DwUzouM/view?usp=sharing)
**Our story**

While studying international politics at Georgetown, I spent three years in and around government (Capitol Hill, then DOJ and Deloitte) and kept hitting the same wall: policy sets direction, but execution is throttled by legacy software. My co-founder Jason has worked in govtech for the past four years researching public benefits automation at Georgetown and building govtech products at Holly and Aidy (YC W24) for local governments.

Jason and I connected over our passion for improving local government processes. The people who keep cities running are stretched thin across understaffed offices, and we want to give them the capacity to do more of what they signed up for. After interviewing 200+ local government staff, we learned that permitting is one of their most painful processes and their software has not done enough to help.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104860&key=user_uploads/3242750/71ea38cf-11ee-427f-8a30-f9381d983c70)

**What we’ve heard**

Permit and entitlement review takes too long, and local government staff are overwhelmed. Applicants often apply with incorrect information, triggering rounds of back-and-forth with the government. And once complete materials are finally in, understaffed departments can’t review everything quickly enough. 

Pandemic-era incumbent contracts are churning because staff are frustrated with expensive legacy systems that only intake and track permits – no automation involved. Our end-to-end solution picks up where those systems stop, automating the review itself to fix permitting where it's most broken.

**What we’re building**

Say a homeowner wants to renovate their house. Before anything else, they have to figure out which permits and entitlements they need. Verdant starts here: applications chat with an AI agent trained on the city ordinances to determine what to apply for. From there, we route applications to a Turbo Tax-style permitting intake portal that guides them through the application, answers their questions, and flags gaps before submission, so what lands on the staff's desk is correct and compliant.

After submission, our AI helps building officials and planners run completeness checks on applications, flagging errors in site plans and drawings. When the application is approved, Verdant uses the context already gathered to draft the next deliverable, whether that's a staff report for the planning commission or a memo for city council.

Beyond the permit lifecycle, Verdant also supports long-range planning: our ordinance research tools let local governments compare how other jurisdictions have written their codes so they have reference points when updating their own.

**Our asks**

* Reach out! If you work in local government (planners, building officials, community developers, city managers, etc.) we’d love to chat.
* Spread the word! If you know anyone in the permitting or planning space, we’d love to connect with them.

launches.title: Nitrode - Advancing AI for Game Development
launches.tagline: Advancing game development through frontier AI research.
launches.body:
Hey YC,

We’re Ben, Brian, and Sejoon from **Nitrode.**

Nitrode is a research company focused on improving game development with AI. 

**The Problem - How do we advance game development with AI?**

We started by building an AI game engine. It got to [**#3 on Product Hunt**,](https://www.producthunt.com/products/nitrode-ai-game-engine) and we gained several useful insights:  despite recent progress in agentic coding, game development remains uniquely difficult for AI models because it requires **(1) strong spatial reasoning**, **(2) reliable tool use/tool-calling**, **(3) strong agentic coding capabilities** and the **(4) ability to operate in real-time environments for complex games**.

**The Solution** 

To advance game development, we believe AI models firstly need to be judged against robust evaluation frameworks that reflect the **actual complexity of the field.** Over the coming months, Nitrode will open-source a suite of benchmarks designed to measure where AI models truly stand in game development. Our first benchmark, [**GameEngineBench**,](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03525) evaluates agentic coding performance on C++ game engine tasks in real runtime environments.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104921&key=user_uploads/1654263/a084ce2c-86d5-431b-97a1-d2ccf07b3f04)

Our results are clear: model class and reasoning effort are strong predictors of performance, while model rankings align more closely with spatial reasoning benchmarks than with traditional agentic coding benchmarks. **This suggests that game development is fundamentally different from pure coding.** Success requires not only writing correct code, but also understanding space, tools, runtime behavior, and the interaction between systems.

We also observe significant complementarity across frontier models, indicating that different models exhibit distinct strengths within the game development task space. Mythos/Fable-class models point toward a potential step change in AI game development capability, where improved spatial understanding and stronger tool use combine to produce emergent behaviors that older model generations struggle to match.

Our benchmark has revealed clear model-specific performance gaps across game development tasks, with outcomes that diverge meaningfully from standard agentic coding benchmarks.

We are also building [Mint](http://mint.nitrode.com), a platform that onboards game development experts to work on custom datasets. Think engine programmers, technical artists, and developers with years of enterprise/indie game development experience. We already have hundreds of contributors across game development and creative software. Whenever you need a certain type of data, we construct and lead a team to produce:

* Post-training /SFT data captured from real workflows: how developers actually build, debug, test, and iterate inside engines and creative tools.
* RL environments and executable tasks where models learn through execution and feedback.
* Custom benchmarks and post-training for gaming enterprises: we pinpoint where models fail on real game development tasks, then post-train a custom model to close those gaps.

**Team** 

Ben and Brian studied Information Science and Computer Science at Cornell, while Sejoon studied Computer Science and Product Design at Stanford. The trio has been building things together for the last six years, from a sports team analytics tool to Nitrode, and are, unsurprisingly, massive gaming nerds. Sejoon is top 400 in the world at moving GeoGuessr and a certified Civ sweat, Brian is ranked in Tetris, and Ben used to be ranked in Minecraft speedrunning.

**Our Ask:**

1. If you need custom datasets or evals, let us know! Email us [research@nitrode.com](mailto:research@nitrode.com)
2. Are there any creative or gaming companies you could introduce us to?

**Thank you!**

Our bet is on proactive background systems that augment how people work, without forcing change to habits they've already built. This compounds, as teams share automations with each other and we learn to create a system where everyone benefits.

launches.title: Baud - AI Chips for Accelerated Training and Inference
launches.tagline: Novel AI hardware and developer platform, co-designed from first principles to let companies train, fine-tune, and deploy frontier models with orders of magnitude better performance than incumbents
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Baud is building a new chip for training and inference of large AI models

We have developed a new arithmetic representation of neural networks that does not contain multiplications. Our silicon is architected specifically for this representation and doing this lets us train and serve AI faster and more efficiently than incumbents.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104577&key=user_uploads/1348413/43bfbd38-2274-4963-b225-3714d18f7c65)

\
\
**Our Team** 

* **Sarang Zambare**, multi-time founder with 4 patents and 7+ years in deep learning and AI hardware. ML lead for Peloton Guide from concept to 100,000+ devices shipped and founding engineer at Caper (acquired by Instacart) building edge deep learning models.
* **Eric Taylor**, ex-NVIDIA chip design veteran with a decade of experience including 4 tape-outs on leading process nodes, two major IP releases, multiple patents and publications, prior roles at NVIDIA, Freescale/NXP, Arteris IP, and Enfabrica.

\
\
**The Problem**

We are living in exciting times where humanity has figured out a way to turn sand and sunlight into machines of scientific discovery.

But creating and serving these machines aka frontier AI models, is extremely capital intensive.

NVIDIA’s publicly documented training recipe of the Nemotron model took **6144 H100 GPUs**, going on for around 3 months, drawing around **4.3 megawatts** of electricity.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104577&key=user_uploads/1348413/eddfed11-11fd-41b3-bbc2-8bb950078002)

That's **$44M in rentals or $245M in capex** plus an ungodly number of developer hours standing up distributed training. Models like Claude Opus 4.6 surprised the world, and that's just the beginning. But at these numbers, **only a handful of teams on Earth control the frontier in AI** and have a shot at a new opus-level moment in other domains like robotics, world models, drug discovery, material science, physics, simulation, the list goes on.\
\
Current attempts at solving this such as Cerebras, Groq, Etched, D-Matrix and 50 other chip startups are only attacking the silicon side and leaving the fundamental math side of the problem untouched, because they are focused on inference and hence have to run existing model weights.

When we looked deeper, we found that if you let go of the constraint of running existing model weights, a radically different silicon architecture becomes possible, with an order of magnitude better performance.

We think we're just scratching the surface of what's possible when you co-design the hardware with the model architecture.

And that’s what we are betting the farm on.

**Solution**

We have developed a new way to represent neural network architectures that eliminates multiplications from both the forward and backward passes, and also compresses the weights by more than 10x without any loss in intelligence. The catch is that you need to train the model in this representation, or start with a base model that is also in this representation.

Both during training and inference, our chip does not need multiplier circuits.

This makes our individual cores drastically smaller and simpler than say GPU’s tensor cores or the PEs in TPU’s systolic arrays.

Which means we can pack way more compute and SRAM on the die and move way more weights for the same memory bandwidth.

This makes our chip faster, less power hungry and simpler to build - letting us use cheap off the shelf server hardware, commodity DRAM, standard chip to chip interconnects and air cooling equipment.\
\
We provide a developer platform based on our hardware that makes creation of frontier AI frictionless and economical to serve, so businesses of all sizes can start owning their intelligence.\
\
**We are live already**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104577&key=user_uploads/1348413/fb27985c-5941-4f2b-aac1-a81378047b7c)

Our first chip is validated on the Global Foundries 12nm process and on schedule for tape-out by the end of this year.\
\
Our training and inference service is already live on a cluster of FPGAs running the chip architecture in emulation.\
\
Using FPGA emulation, we've developed a compiler and a distributed training stack that converts any PyTorch exportable model to our format with bit exact results in most cases, including popular opensource architectures such as GLM, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek, Flux, Wan and others.\
\
You can checkout a small demo of our chip running in emulation on a single FPGA here: <https://baudlabs.ai/demo>

**Our partner program**\
\
Baud is now working with design partners who can test our systems and help smooth out the developer experience, in exchange for reserved capacity on our first cluster for training and inference.\
\
Capacity is limited. Contact us if you are training something new or are tired of paying through the nose for intelligence that you do not own.\
\
<https://baudlabs.ai/partner>

launches.title: 6thSense — Giving Robots Touch
launches.tagline: Giving Robots Touch
launches.body:
6thSense builds wearable tactile sensing rigs that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and pose — across touch, vision, depth, force, and 3D hand pose, all in real environments. We sell that multimodal data to the companies training the next generation of dexterous robots.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gXx53tcIv5U>

Robots are getting good at seeing. They're still terrible at touching. That's because there's almost no data capturing what a hand actually feels while doing real tasks in real homes. Lab data doesn't cut it. We go anywhere and capture the missing layer that manipulation models need to learn fine motor control.

What makes our data different is the hardware we built to collect it. Our tactile sensing devices are designed and manufactured in-house, purpose-built to capture the richest touch signal in the industry — with scale in mind from the very beginning, enabling us to actually solve the tactile data problem. Every sensor maps directly to how robotic skin needs to work: a 1-to-1 analog for the tactile arrays going into the next generation of robot hands. That means the data we collect today doesn't just train better policies. It transfers directly to the hardware it's meant to run on. The team comes from Tesla, Mecka, Samsung, DoorDash, and Amazon, with expertise across hardware, sensors, ML, robotics, and software at scale. If you're training a manipulation policy or need custom tactile data, reach out.

launches.title: Simi: The Fastest AI Whiteboard Explainer Video Generator

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Simi is the fastest, easiest, and most cost-effective way to create whiteboard explainer videos. You give it a prompt or a document. It writes the script, draws the illustrations, animates them, adds narration, and hands you a finished video in seconds. Anything from a one minute short to a full hour, in one shot, in 80+ languages. Built by Lamina Labs (YC P26). Use it through the app or the API for training, onboarding, product walkthroughs, sales, marketing, and education at <https://laminalabs.ai>.

Here is an explainer video about Lamina Labs: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RLuOCdamcHE>

## Why we built this

AI video right now is built to look like a movie, not to explain something.

But most of the video people actually need at work is the boring kind. A training module. An onboarding flow. A walkthrough of the feature you shipped last week. And making one of those is absurdly slow. You either pay an agency thousands of dollars and wait weeks, or you sit in a template editor dragging boxes around for an afternoon and it still looks like you dragged boxes around.

That is fine if you need one video. It falls apart the moment you need a hundred. A course. Every feature documented. Onboarding in every language your customers speak. Anyone who has priced that out knows the math does not work.

## How it works

You type what you want. Simi writes the script, draws and animates it, and gives you a properly narrated video in seconds.

That is the whole thing. No storyboard, no timeline, no boxes to drag. Type "explain how photosynthesis works," or hand it a long compliance doc, and you get a finished video, not a draft. And it does not choke on length. One minute to a full hour, generated in a single shot.

If your team makes videos, you should be using this.

## What people make with it

Training and onboarding videos from the docs you already have. Product walkthroughs, one per feature, updated as fast as the product changes. Sales and marketing explainers, in every market you sell into. Course and lecture videos in the Khan Academy style. Faceless YouTube channels and localized social video at volume. Agencies run it through the API to produce explainer videos for their clients.

## What makes it different

An agency gives you a video in weeks for thousands of dollars. Simi gives you the same video in seconds for a fraction of that. That is the whole pitch, and it is enough.

A few things worth knowing beyond speed. It generates anything from a minute to an hour in one shot. It speaks 80+ languages, so you write once and localize everywhere. And it is built to plug in. Use the app, call the API from your own product, or run it inside agent frameworks like OpenClaw and Nous Research's Hermes.

## Who we are

We are Sudip and Kartikesh, the founders of Lamina Labs, and Simi is the first thing we have built. We are both from Nepal. We met at MIT and started building together there. We are the first Nepalese founding team to go through YC.

Simi is named after Simikot, the Himalayan village where Sudip grew up. We started with education because that is where this problem hurt us personally. But it is everywhere. Any time someone needs to turn an idea into a clear picture, that is us.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104668&key=user_uploads/2592448/ddd4246e-1dae-4302-8e33-7c51d0264d6b)

If your team spends real money or real time making explainer, training, or onboarding videos, talk to us: [founder@laminalabs.ai](mailto:founder@laminalabs.ai)

We would love intros to L&D leaders, to agencies making video at volume, and to founders who want video generation inside their own product through the API.

launches.body:
TL;DR: Kestrel turns natural-language prompts into deterministic, production-ready workflows that automate incident response, cloud provisioning, CI/CD, security, and developer requests. It supports 30+ integrations and is developer-first, with a CLI, Python SDK, and MCP server so you can manage workflows from where you (and your coding agents) already work. Build your first workflow in <5 mins with $1,000 in usage credits at [usekestrel.ai](http://usekestrel.ai).

<https://youtu.be/2y60CgQ-huM>

**The Problem**

Coding agents made every developer faster. But the platform team did not get faster with them.

Developers now ship with Cursor/Claude/Codex and generate infrastructure, deployments, and provisioning requests at a rate no platform team was staffed for.

At illumio I once waited more than three weeks just to get Kafka clusters provisioned for a new service I was building. And provisioning is only part of it. The platform team is also on the hook for incident response when production breaks, repairing the CI/CD glue that ties the deployment pipeline together, platform security, and every "can you just" developer request in Slack.

Most platform teams pick one of two bad options. They hand developers (and their agents) direct access to infra, CI/CD, and cloud accounts, and hope nothing breaks. Or they gatekeep and become the bottleneck every developer has to wait on.

Building a platform that developers actually like has been a luxury only the largest engineering orgs could staff, and an understaffed platform effort usually does more harm than good.

**The Solution**

See how it works: <https://youtu.be/g1dGUsuZgws>

Platform teams use Kestrel to automate incident response, cloud provisioning, CI/CD, security, developer requests, and more across their stack. You describe what you want to automate in plain English, and the Workflow Agent builds the whole thing. It draws from 140+ pre-built actions across 30+ integrations, plus custom HTTP APIs and webhooks for anything that isn't built in yet.

Once a workflow is configured it runs deterministically with no LLM deciding what to do at runtime.

You can define workflows that handle self-service developer requests without handing over the keys; scope who can trigger each workflow; fence it to specific clusters, cloud accounts, or repos; and require approval before anything touches production. Developers get a golden path without free rein, and the platform team keeps the guardrails without gatekeeping.

Kestrel analyzes your connected integrations and suggests ready-to-deploy workflows, and the Workflow Assistant turns your existing runbooks and scripts into production-ready automations, so you don't have to start from scratch: <https://youtu.be/IOoLb300rqE>

Every workflow you build in Kestrel is fully observable, with a dashboard that shows what's running, what's waiting on approval, and what failed; real-time step-level logs; and a failure diagnosis agent that fixes failed workflows for you: <https://youtu.be/SEInJ040ZVs>

The [Kestrel CLI](https://docs.usekestrel.ai/workflows/cli), [Python SDK](https://docs.usekestrel.ai/workflows/sdk), and [MCP server](https://docs.usekestrel.ai/workflows/mcp) let you and your coding agents build and manage workflows from the terminal and application code.

**How It Works**

First, connect your platform stack. Kestrel supports 30+ integrations across infrastructure, PaaS, AI compute, observability, on-call, networking, databases, CI/CD, and IaC:

Then, open the Workflow Agent and describe what you want to automate. Here are a few examples:

* “When a developer submits a cloud provisioning request in Slack, route it to the team lead for approval, provision the AWS resources with Terraform in the infra repo, and notify the developer once the pull request is merged.”

Everything you do in the dashboard is available via the CLI/SDK/MCP. E.g. you can generate a workflow, activate it, and clear an approval from the terminal:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104092&key=user_uploads/2950276/e5c068f1-98e7-4e35-9e83-407f2d4807a6)

**Ask**

If you're a platform engineer or eng leader tired of manually responding to developer requests, incidents, or CI/CD failures, you can try it yourself today with a 14-day free trial and $1,000 in usage credits. Use suggested workflows and the Workflow Assistant to build your first platform automations in minutes.

launches.tagline: AI-Native Procurement and Accounts Payable
launches.body:
### Hey everyone,

We’re [Jack Cameron](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jackmcameron/) and [Jacob Bland](https://linkedin.com/in/bland-jacob) at [Saldor](https://saldor.com/) .

**TL;DR:** Saldor helps businesses buy goods and services, and close their books faster.

**The Ask**: If you work in procurement or finance, or if you’re building a company with complex purchasing needs, email us at [team@saldor.com](mailto:team@saldor.com). We’d love to talk.

**The Offer**: We’re offering customers a white-glove pilot with no implementation fee.

After a brief onboarding call, we’ll do the work required to configure Saldor, connect your existing systems, and load real company data so your team can evaluate it in a live workflow for a short period at no cost.

<https://youtu.be/szTFpL0NWpg>

**The Problem**

Buying something at a company is rarely as simple as placing an order.

An employee submits a request. Procurement checks vendors, pricing, security, and lead times. Finance reviews the budget. Legal may review a contract. Someone creates a purchase order, follows up with the vendor, tracks delivery, and eventually matches the invoice against what was ordered and received.

Many companies still manage this through email and spreadsheets, or procurement systems that are expensive and cumbersome to operate.

The problem gets worse for companies building ambitious physical infrastructure. When data centers, factories, and robotics companies cannot get the right equipment on time, entire projects can be delayed.

We saw this firsthand at Crusoe, where we helped build GPU data centers. Existing procurement systems could cost hundreds of thousands of dollars to implement, required large teams to operate, and still slowed the business down.

**Our solution**

Saldor is an AI-native procurement and accounts payable tool.

Employees can request goods or services, and Saldor routes each request through the appropriate approval, security, legal, and finance workflows.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104430&key=user_uploads/1733940/50e219d2-f23a-4531-b6f6-1c4410b188d2)

Our AI agent communicates directly with vendors to collect documents, follow up on quotes and delivery dates, and keep records updated automatically.

Saldor can then generate purchase orders, track receipts, process invoices, and match bills against what was ordered and received.

Teams can also interact with Saldor through MCP and connect it to their ERP, accounting system, or other internal tools.

**The Team**

Jack and Jacob worked together as Crusoe building AI infrastructure before leaving to start Saldor. Jack (CTO) holds a B.S in Computer Science from Carnegie Mellon University. Jacob (CEO) holds a B.S in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from UC Berkeley.

launches.title: Bloomy: AI-powered mastery learning for K-12
launches.tagline: We use AI to help kids learn faster
launches.body:
**Hi everyone - I'm Alex, founder of Bloomy.**

**TL;DR: We help kids learn faster by using AI. In early pilots, students grew \~2x faster than the national average.**

[Bloomy](https://bloomylearning.com) is an AI-powered mastery learning platform for K-12 students. We diagnose students’ skill gaps, place students on a personalized learning path, and give them standards-aligned lessons and a Socratic AI tutor that helps without just giving away the answer.

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/8E5PhhWjtD4>

**Why I'm building this**

I started as a teacher. I taught 7th grade English and Writing with Teach For America, and every day I struggled to deliver differentiated instruction to 30 students with 30 different sets of needs.

Some students needed remediation, some needed acceleration, and many needed a tutor sitting next to them helping them reason through the next step. Benjamin Bloom's 2-sigma result always felt obviously true to me; the hard part was making that kind of tutoring affordable and available to every child.

Then AI changed the cost curve. 

When I saw innovative school concepts such as Alpha School, the model clicked: mastery-based learning, personalization, and high-agency students. But I kept thinking about the families and schools that already exist: homeschool families, microschools, hybrid schools, and regular classrooms where most kids are today.

**What Bloomy does**

Bloomy starts with a diagnostic (we integrate with third-party diagnostics and provide our own in-house one) and places each student onto a personalized learning path. Students work one skill at a time, get a short, standards-aligned lesson, practice, ask BloomyBot for Socratic help when they're stuck, and only move forward after showing 90%+ mastery. The skill path updates live based on the student’s performance and our own knowledge graph.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104376&key=user_uploads/3410278/aff91335-737d-4b76-bcc2-40414d3f3c08)

_Our knowledge graph informs skill progression to make learning more efficient._

Parents and teachers can see what the student has mastered, what's in progress, and where they need support.

**Where we are**

We're being adopted in many different contexts: districts with traditional schools, charter schools, hybrid schools, microschools, homeschools, and even families who just want some extra academic support for their kids.

Families can subscribe to Bloomy monthly or annually, and families using ESA/EFA funds may also qualify for direct pay or reimbursement depending on their state’s rules.

Before Bloomy, I taught with TFA, earned my Master’s in Education, designed GMAT and GRE curriculum for Manhattan Prep, led Lyft’s driver growth team for New England, earned an MBA from Stanford, and managed AI transformation engagements at McKinsey. Bloomy is the thing that combines all the aspects of my career: learning design, go-to-market, and AI.

If you want to reach out, you can email me at [alex@bloomylearning.com](mailto:alex@bloomylearning.com) or follow our updates on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/bloomy-yc-s26/).

launches.title: Osmaura - AI agents that identify legal needs
launches.tagline: We surface new matter opportunities for law firm partners.
launches.body:
**Tl;dr:** We’re building AI agents that surfaces new matter opportunities for law firm partners.

### **The problem:**

Partners at law firms spend at least 10 hours of every week trying to win new clients. 

However, they’re limited to corporate contacts within their network. Firms try to help by connecting them with prospects but it’s often unclear which ones are ready to become clients.

### **The solution:**

AI can give partners a deeper understanding of prospective clients and legal support they might need **at the right time**.

### **What we’re building:**

Our agents monitor companies and regulators across the web to surface early signals that a company may soon need counsel and ways to connect with them.

Here’s how it works:

1. **Understand the partner**: The agents build a profile of the partner using their practice group, previous deals, and their network.
2. **Find new matters**: Then, they continually find prospective clients and potential latent legal needs using external data sources (including disclosures, product launches, customer complaints, enforcement actions, rule changes).
3. **Orchestrate outreach**: Finally, they filter for potential clients the partner is well-positioned to land, and suggest tasteful ways to engage them.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hbBDbuNP-Mw>

### **Team:**

We’re Kali and Jity, two friends from MIT who talked to a lot of partners and saw just how much pressure they’re in when it comes to originating work, especially as the legal space gets more competitive.

_Kali_ → 2x AWS Intern and ML/NLP research at MIT focused on policy prediction and argument extraction. I’ve been interested in law and public institutions for years and I bring that context to building AI for the legal industry.

_Jity_ → Experience at Meta/Jane Street, and computational astrophysics research at MIT. I'm interested in building great technical products, and have spent months learning from law firm partners to understand how they win new matters.
