Hey everyone!

We're Yonas & Daniel, co-founders of [StarSling](https://www.starsling.dev).

**TL;DR: [StarSling Runners](https://starsling.dev/)** are an AI-native drop-in replacement for ubuntu-latest that continuously make your CI up to **6x faster** and **13x cheaper**. On day one, StarSling Runners are faster and cheaper. From there, AI agents analyze your pipelines and continuously ship optimization PRs.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IxcYY5cuSXA>

**🤔 Why now**

Coding agents made writing code dramatically faster, and they’ve pushed PR volume up, which compounds CI times and cost fast.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104233&key=user_uploads/7866/2149565f-569b-4f8d-b4b3-9eab341daf0f)

Everyone has the option of getting fast CI runners now. What nobody has is **CI that adapts and improves itself**.

Meanwhile, keeping a CI pipeline fast is a constant manual chore: caches break, tests get flaky, build steps pile up, and someone has to notice and fix it, over and over. We believe DevOps tooling like CI should be as agentic as coding is, and that's the unlock behind self-driving CI: the optimization work that used to be a recurring human task now runs continuously in the background as part of the infrastructure running it.

**🔥 The problem**

Keeping CI fast is nobody's job and everybody's problem:

* **Pipelines rot.** Caches get misconfigured, dependency installs get slow, tests turn flaky, build steps stop being parallel. Performance quietly degrades until someone carves out time to fix it.
* **Fast runners alone don't solve it.** Swapping in faster hardware helps once, then your setup drifts right back as you add more code and tests and they get more complex. Plenty of products give you faster runners. None of them keep your pipeline optimized for you.
* **It's getting worse.** Recent GitHub Actions pricing changes hit teams running lots of jobs, and GitHub's focus has clearly moved elsewhere. When we surveyed companies looking for DevOps AI solutions, a GitHub Actions agent was the single most-requested solution engineers wanted.

**🧯 The solution: self-driving CI**

StarSling Runners are an AI-native, drop-in replacement for ubuntu-latest\
that get faster the longer you use them:

* **Fast infrastructure on day one.** 5th Gen AMD EPYC (\~30% faster than GitHub), actions/cache compatible with zero config, unlimited concurrency.
* **AI agents that optimize your CI for you.** Agents continuously scan your workflows, jobs, run logs, and machine telemetry, then open optimization PRs: fixing caching, speeding up dependency installs, parallelizing build steps, sharding tests, and restructuring workflows. This is the part nobody else does. Real PRs our agents opened and customers merged: [sharding E2E tests across 3 parallel jobs](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/15888) (Mastra), [optimizing Playwright browser installs](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/8073) and [fixing turbo cache config](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/7950) (Better Auth).
* **Cheaper, with no surprises.** $0.008/min vs GitHub's $0.012/min (33% cheaper), queue time never billed, no seat fees.
* **You stay in control.** Every agent-authored optimization ships as a PR your team reviews and merges.
* **Secure by default.** Every job runs in its own single-use, hardware-isolated microVM that's destroyed after the run, the same isolation model GitHub-hosted runners use. Secrets pass directly from GitHub to your job and are never stored by StarSling.
* **One-line install.** Install the [StarSling GitHub App](https://github.com/apps/starslingdev) and copy our AI install prompt to swap ubuntu-latest\
  for starsling-ubuntu-24.04. You're on faster runners immediately, with 2,000 free minutes your first month. The optimization agents are in early access right now, so request access and we'll turn them on for your repos. **👇**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104233&key=user_uploads/7866/a91c193f-d5e1-4d00-a93c-1dfd6381666b)

**📈 Traction**

After being in private beta for the past four months, StarSling has now run over **one million CI jobs** for fast-moving teams like Better Auth, Mastra, Partcl, and more, and the self-driving AI agents is what won them over:

* [**Mastra**](https://starsling.dev/customers/mastra) got **6x faster** CI:
  * _"The runners are just handled, so nobody on my team thinks about CI infrastructure anymore, and the agents keep optimizing for the one thing I care about: minutes saved."_ - Abhi Aiyer, Co-founder & CTO at Mastra (YC W25)
* [**Better Auth**](https://starsling.dev/customers/better-auth) got **2x faster** E2E:
  * _"StarSling agents are like a CI engineer we never had to hire. They find the slow spots, test out fixes, find the ones that work and open the PRs themselves."_ - Bereket Engida, Founder & CEO at Better Auth (P25)
* [**Partcl**](https://starsling.dev/customers/partcl) got **13x cheaper** CI, and the agents proved themselves on day one:
  * _"Within a day of migrating to StarSling Runners, their agents opened up a PR that literally made our Rust CI tests 2x faster!"_ - Vamshi Balanaga, Co-founder & CTO at Partcl (YC P25)

Full case studies: <https://starsling.dev/customers>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104233&key=user_uploads/7866/10826f60-8e4d-41a8-a800-32026a78bfc8)


**🏋️ Team**

**Daniel** led the 12-person engineering team at Netflix that built their Internal Developer Portal ("Netflix Console"), the central hub for Netflix's 3,000+ engineers and the highest-DAU internal developer tool at the company. Before Netflix he was on Facebook's AI Camera team, building computer vision that powers camera effects for 100M+ DAUs across Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp.

**Yonas** built StackShare, one of the largest online developer communities (1.5M+ registered developers), with an enterprise offering used by Fortune 500s to surface tech stack data across thousands of internal codebases. StackShare was acquired by FOSSA in 2024.

We've spent our careers on developer tools, and self-driving CI is the first part of a suite of tools we always wished we had.

**🔮 Vision**

DevOps should be as agentic as coding. CI is just the start. We're building toward a world where your entire pipeline improves on its own and AI agents take on the slow, manual engineering work that’s left after your coding agents finish, across the whole SDLC, so your team ships faster.

Happy Slinging!

\- Yonas & Daniel

launches.title: Proception - The dexterous robot hand we wish existed
launches.tagline: The hand that enables robots. The glove that teaches them.
launches.body:
# **Shipping ProHand: The Human-Like Robotic Hand Built for Dexterous Manipulation**

Most robots still cannot use their hands.

That sounds strange, because robots have gotten dramatically better over the past decade. They can navigate warehouses, run, jump, perceive their surroundings, and reason over visual scenes. But when it comes to actually touching the world, most robots still rely on simple grippers.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104230&key=user_uploads/2602106/4c624b0d-144a-4af0-8144-a88769012c9d)

That works if the object is rigid, predictable, and placed exactly where the robot expects it to be. It breaks down quickly when the task requires the kind of manipulation humans do every day: adjusting grip, feeling contact, using multiple fingers, handling soft objects, or recovering when something slips.

We started Proception because we kept running into the same bottleneck: humanoid robots will not become truly useful until they can manipulate the world with something much closer to a human hand.

Today we are introducing ProHand 1.0, a high-dexterity robotic hand built for researchers and robotics companies working on contact-rich manipulation.\
\
<https://youtu.be/S61xWpz7_qM>

## Why We Built a Human-Like Hand

The human hand is not just a gripper. It has more than twenty degrees of freedom, dense tactile feedback, tendon-driven actuation, and an incredible ability to adapt through contact.

That is what makes simple tasks deceptively hard for robots. Tying shoelaces, opening packaging, handling tools, plugging in cables, folding clothes, or repairing electronics are not just vision problems. They are contact problems.

To build ProHand, we worked closely with hand surgeons and designed the system around the structure of the human hand.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104230&key=user_uploads/2602106/7dacec7a-3a65-412f-8513-cef8caf8b27f)

ProHand includes:

* **Twenty-two degrees of freedom**, with multiple joints per finger, enabling a wide range of human-like motions.
* **Tendon-driven actuation**, where motors pull cables to move the fingers while keeping the hand lightweight and compact.
* **A compact and robust mechanical design**, built to be impact tolerant, serviceable, and practical for real robotics research.
* **Integrated skin-like sensors**, which detect contact and support grip control during manipulation.

The goal was not to build a hand that looks human for aesthetics. The goal was to build hardware that can interact with the world in the same manipulation regime as human hands.

## The Bigger Problem Is Data

Dexterous manipulation is not only a hardware problem. It is also a data problem.

AI has made enormous progress in vision and language because those fields had access to large-scale datasets. Robotics does not have the same advantage. Manipulation data is expensive, slow, and usually collected in labs through teleoperation.

Teleoperation is useful, and ProHand supports standard teleoperation workflows out of the box. But it has two big limitations.

First, it does not scale easily. Data collection is limited by how many robots you have and how much time operators can spend controlling them.

Second, it loses important human interaction signals. When someone teleoperates a robot, they are not directly touching the object. The robot sees motion commands, but it often misses the subtle pressure, contact, and adjustment strategies humans naturally use when manipulating objects.

Because ProHand is designed around human hand kinematics and skin-like sensing, we can also collect data directly from human hands.

That is why we built **ProGlove**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104230&key=user_uploads/2602106/1ee06ef7-e3b4-422a-b38c-2987494df668)

ProGlove turns the same sensor skin used on ProHand into a wearable data collection system. A person can wear the glove, interact with real objects, and capture human manipulation data without needing a robot in the loop. Combined with a headset for visual context, researchers can collect real human hand interaction data and transfer those movements and skills to ProHand.

Our bet is simple: the fastest path to dexterous robots is to build hardware close enough to the human hand that we can learn from human hands directly.

## Shipping This Week

Proception has raised **$11 million in seed funding** led by **First Round Capital**, with participation from **Y Combinator** and **BoxGroup**. This allows us to expand the team, scale production, and keep building the hardware and data infrastructure needed for dexterous manipulation.

Our team has designed consumer electronics at Apple that reached millions of users, built robotic systems at Tesla and early-stage startups, and spent years working on the messy details of real hardware: actuation, sensing, reliability, calibration, control, and data collection.

We are building ProHand in Mountain View, and the first batch of units is shipping this week to researchers and robotics companies.

If you are building dexterous manipulation systems, humanoid robots, teleoperation workflows, or robot learning pipelines, you can order ProHand on [our website](https://www.proception.ai/product/pro-hand/gen1).

If you want to help build the hands that make humanoid robots useful, we are hiring <https://www.proception.ai/careers>.

##

launches.title: Reflexes API: Catch what agent logs miss
launches.tagline: Most Agent failures are behavioral. Catch them at scale
launches.body:
Behavioral observability for AI agents, built and priced to run on millions of production turns.

Most agent failures don’t show up as errors.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104095&key=user_uploads/405977/00b2cef4-ce0d-4a93-a145-0209d28eb3a6)


The API returns 200.\
The tool call succeeded.

But the agent is looping. The user is frustrated. A jailbreak slipped through. The answer technically completed, but the experience failed.

That is the problem Reflexes solves.

Reflexes are fast classifiers that run on every turn of every agent conversation and catch the behavioral signals normal observability misses:

* user frustration
* infinite loops
* jailbreak attempts
* refusals
* hallucinations
* task failures
* policy violations
* custom signals specific to your product

Traditional observability tells you when software breaks. Reflexes tells you when the agent experience breaks.

The reason this has not worked before is cost and latency. Frontier-model LLM-as-judge is fine for offline evals, but it is too slow and expensive to run across production traffic.

Reflexes are built and priced to run at scale: millions of turns, inline, across 100% of production conversations.

Under the hood, Reflexes uses a shared backbone with many small heads, so multiple behavioral signals can run on the same conversation without multiplying latency or cost.

You can use our default reflexes out of the box, or train a custom reflex for the failure modes that matter to your agent.

We built this after working with production agent teams and seeing the same pattern repeatedly: agents usually fail long before they throw an error.

They fail in the behavior.

Try Reflexes: <https://www.morphllm.com/products/reflex>

launches.title: Decentro goes global | Multi-Currency Payment Collections
launches.tagline: Launching global payments & treasury from GIFT city for the world.
launches.body:
Hey YC community, we’re Rohit and team from **Decentro (YC S20)**, a full‑stack banking and payments API player from India.

Over the last few years, we’ve helped thousands of businesses plug into Indian banking, KYC, and payments infrastructure with simple APIs; now we’re extending that to global payments with our new **GIFT‑based PSP** and cross‑border collection stack.

## **The problem – global money in & out**

If you’re a trade finance player, marketplace, or fintech scaling globally, you probably live in some version of this mess:

* Multiple PSPs and bank partners across countries, each with different compliance, FX, and payout rules.
* Long, opaque onboarding cycles for cross‑border flows.
* Fragmented reporting across acquirers, currencies, and entities, making reconciliation and compliance audits painful.
* A fast‑moving regulatory environment (IFSCA, FEMA, local regimes) where a misstep can mean blocked flows or penalties.

This slows down companies that should be focusing on building products and acquiring customers, not chasing bank RM emails and interpreting circulars.

## **What we’re building – a compliant global PSP rail via GIFT**

We’ve become one of the first Indian payment aggregators to receive a final PSP license from IFSCA at GIFT City, and we’re wrapping that into a developer‑first global payments platform.

At a high level, here’s how it works:

* Single API / dashboard to collect global payments: Accept from international customers via cards, local methods, and bank transfers across multiple currencies, and settle into GIFT City or onshore INR.
* Built‑in compliance and reporting: We abstract GIFT City PSP rules, documentation, and transaction reporting so finance and compliance teams get ready‑to‑use exports and views.
* Faster settlement and better visibility: Unified ledgers and payout flows across corridors and partners, with clear T+ timelines, FX details, and status notifications.
* Modular APIs: Use us just as a cross‑border collection layer, or plug into the broader Decentro stack (KYC, domestic payouts, banking APIs) if you want a full‑stack infra partner.

## **Why we started working on this**

At Decentro, we began by solving for domestic Indian banking and payments APIs after running into fragmentation and long integrations at our previous companies.

As our customers scaled, the same questions kept coming up:

* “Can you help us collect from global customers and settle into our desired currency?”
* “Is there a compliant way to route this via GIFT City without adding three more partners?”

## **How it works – product flow**

Here’s a typical integration:

1. Configure your entity and use case (SaaS, marketplace, B2B payments, etc.) in our console, including purpose codes and underlying documentation.
2. Integrate our hosted checkout or APIs to start accepting payments in supported currencies and methods from your customers.
3. We route funds through our GIFT PSP stack, run compliance checks, and handle FX and settlements into your designated accounts.
4. Your finance and compliance teams use our dashboard and webhooks for reconciliation, returns, chargebacks, and regulatory reporting.

## Here’s a walkthrough video - <https://youtu.be/FYXg5-KSg-8>

If you’re:

* A SaaS or B2B company selling globally and settling into India.
* A marketplace, fintech, or infra company that needs compliant cross‑border rails via GIFT City.
* Or an existing YC company that wants to expand to Indian or India‑linked flows.

We’d love to chat.

* Website: <https://tinyurl.com/decentro-yc-launch>
* Global PSP product page: [**https://decentro.tech/global/gift-psp**](https://decentro.tech/global/gift-psp)
* YC founder: Rohit (Founder & CEO, Decentro – YC S20)

Comment here, or reach out and mention “Integrate YC PSP” so we can prioritize your onboarding and, if relevant, help you navigate the GIFT / IFSCA side as well.

Cheers!

launches.title: Pelica: the AI operating system for value-based care
launches.tagline: AI agents that capture the risk, close the gaps, and make the calls, so small teams can keep whole populations healthy.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We’re Lalit and Catherine, co-founders of Pelica Health.

## **TL;DR**

Pelica is the AI operating system for value-based care. We pull claims, EHR, pharmacy, lab, and hospital feeds into **one canonical record**, then run AI copilots that read and write to it: risk adjustment, Stars and quality, pharmacy, provider network, and care management, plus an AI data analyst you can ask anything in plain English. The copilots **do the operational work themselves**: capturing HCCs in real time, closing gaps once across every payer, and making outreach calls in the member’s language. HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II, and RADV-defensible.

We’re live with a physician-led IPA in New York, one of the largest independent medical groups in the Northeast: **2,500+ hours saved** and higher CMS Star Ratings so far.

▶️ Watch their story: <https://youtu.be/2CGmyif9Yd4>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103962&key=user_uploads/1494518/e873acc4-f206-4eca-8617-9bf7f70f3b62)

_An AI agent works one gap end to end: provider office, pharmacy, the member in their language, the payer portal, then a live call. Closed in 3 minutes of staff time._

## **🚩 The problem**

Value-based care pays a medical group or health plan to keep a whole population healthy, and billions in CMS bonuses ride on it. The teams who own those contracts decide whether the org makes money, and they cannot operate:

• Their data lives in 8 to 15 systems. By the time a problem surfaces, the submission window has closed.

• Risk calls a member. Quality calls the same member. The practice calls again, sometimes in a language the member doesn’t speak.

• The best predictive model is worthless if it never reaches the provider.

• The rules keep moving. Hybrid HEDIS is retiring into ECDS volumes many times higher per measure, and the V28 phase-in costs the average MA plan about 3% of RAF.

Every new gap gets a new point vendor, each with its own portal, data model, and login. These teams do not need another point tool. They need an operating system.

## **🛠️ What we built**

One canonical record, with an AI workforce next to every team. Six copilots:

• **Risk Adjustment:** real-time HCC capture with trumping logic and RADV-defensible chain of custody on every code.

• **Quality and Stars:** gap closure unified across every payer, with year-round forecasting for the post-hybrid HEDIS world.

• **Pharmacy and Part D:** PDC lift on the three triple-weighted measures that move Stars the most.

• **Provider Network:** auto-built practice agendas that cut meeting prep from 90 minutes to 15.

• **Care Management:** ADT-driven transitions-of-care worklists, with no duplicate calls across teams.

• **AI Data Analyst:** plain-English questions against the record, in place of the BI ticket queue.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103962&key=user_uploads/1494518/13a2d9aa-5ac8-4ab4-bf2c-b61fe8bccb56)

_Risk Adjustment: the agent works the EHR and payer portals like a person and captures a defensible HCC._

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103962&key=user_uploads/1494518/cfb57b8c-bf75-43d1-9dc3-d29da891d8e9)

_AI Data Analyst: ask your RAF in plain English, get an answer and a chart in seconds._

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103962&key=user_uploads/1494518/4bbf9afb-abc0-4221-9e5b-bf4602654e32)

_Provider Network: reps walk in prepped, and the visit is captured into tasks automatically._

It runs on the systems VBC teams already use: Epic, Cerner, Athena, eCW, payer SFTP, PBM feeds, ADT, and labs, with SMART-on-FHIR overlays in Epic and Athena. A new source onboards in days, and the copilots start working the day after.

## **📈 Early proof**

That physician-led IPA went from three uncoordinated calls per member to one outreach, in the right language, that closed three gaps at once. No new headcount. One of their leaders put it simply: “You don’t just get software, you get partners.”

## **👫 Why us**

Catherine and I met at YouTube and have built large-scale systems together since. We saw the same gap from two sides: clinical AI that could not operate, and operations software that could not reason clinically.

• **Catherine** led AI work on Gemini and enterprise agents at Google, did clinical AI research at Stanford School of Medicine, and saw front-line care at clinics in California and New Hampshire. BA in Computer Science from Dartmouth.

• **Lalit** spent 8 years building software for regulated industries at Google and YouTube, most recently as engineering and ML lead on YouTube Payments, running a 45-person team on products driving $16B+ in revenue. Wharton MBA, ACM-ICPC World Finalist.

Backed by Y Combinator, SurgePoint Capital, Upside Partnership, ISEED Ventures, and Progressive Ventures.

## **🙏 Our ask**

• Warm intros to VPs of Risk Adjustment, Stars, Quality, or Pharmacy at MA plans, IPAs, MSOs, or ACOs.

• Intros to ACO executive directors running MSSP or REACH.

• If you run risk-bearing contracts at a health plan, IPA, MSO, ACO, or medical group, email [lalit@pelica.com](mailto:lalit@pelica.com) or book a demo at cal.com/pelica/pelica.

Follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7475922350316732416/) and [X](https://x.com/cthrnzh/status/2070159740295160294), and learn more at [pelica.com](http://pelica.com).

launches.title: Amika - the operating system for AI agents to write and verify code
launches.tagline: Run fleets of human-in-the-loop or background coding agents inside cloud computers. Let them automate coding and verify it's correct.
launches.body:
Software isn't a craft anymore, it's a manufacturing problem.

At Amika, we're building **the open source operating system for coding agents to automate their work**, like how the factory automated manufacturing.

**Amika gives each agent a cloud computer, and lets you build automated or human-in-the-loop workflows for agents to write code and prove that the code is correct.**

A couple of examples:

\- Have Amika monitor production and auto-fix errors, testing the fix against your real app

\- Add Amika to shared customer Slack channels. Auto-implement customer requests and share a live preview the updated app with them

Check out some more examples in our video 👇

<https://youtu.be/GxqFsiBNbww>

# The problem

AI coding agents made code generation cheap. Producing correct code at scale, with real quality controls, is still unsolved. You're left with a tradeoff: pore over every change and go slow, or vibe-code and ship slop.

Coding agents are useful, but the surrounding system is missing.

\- They lack the right **dev environment to verify their work**

\- They lack the right **context to understand the full problem**

\- They lack **deterministic guardrails controlling what they can change**

\- They produce 10x more code, but teams lack **a system for 10x more review**

# How Amika solves this

Amika composes 5 primitives into its agent operating system:

1\. **Sandboxed environments**: isolated cloud computers with the repos, tech stack, MCP servers, skills, and context an agent needs.

2\. **Workflows**: programs as code or markdown files that define when an agent runs and what job it does.

3\. **Deterministic guardrails**: rules enforced on every code change, like "do not cross this module boundary" or "every database query must include a customer ID filter."

4\. **Automated verification**: test, review, fix, and merge loops that check the work against your real tech stack before it ships.

5\. **Audit trails**: the agent chat session, code changes, which checks passed, and what the run cost.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103929&key=user_uploads/101903/a1246cf3-1ed1-435d-94fb-2cb7437b4995)

Amika works with your existing coding agent subscriptions (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) so **you're not locked into one vendor**. Start agents from the web, Slack, GitHub, the CLI, or the API. At any point, a human can take over the sandbox and inspect the running apps, or drive from their own code editor.

Because each sandbox runs your full stack, you review the agent's work in a live preview of your real app, plus the verification artifacts it produced, like screen captures or API test requests, instead of poring over the diff line by line.

With Amika's workflows and environments, you can spend time building higher level loops for your agent to write and verify code, speeding up your product development.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103929&key=user_uploads/101903/60e16093-3dcf-4285-b73b-998c74507145)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103929&key=user_uploads/101903/3b84372e-0a00-46a3-afd1-d711547c256b)

# Who we are

We're [Jakub](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jakub-c-14016a3b/) and [Dylan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dbmikus/), two time YC cofounders.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103929&key=user_uploads/101903/497da8a5-bfa8-407e-98f6-b613d9389b50)

We pivoted our YC company to bet on this, and we already use Amika for the majority of our PRs. We're building it in the open: each primitive ships as open source, and our cloud platform packages the whole operating system into a software factory for teams.

# Our ask

\- Dig into the **open source repo** on GitHub: <https://github.com/gofixpoint/amika>

\- If you want **help setting up your software factory**, book at demo at <https://cal.com/amika-dev/30min>

launches.title: Corgea: Agentic Pentesting
launches.tagline: An autonomous penetration testing engine that runs in hours and not weeks
launches.body:
[**Corgea AI Pentesting**](https://corgea.com/products/ai-pentest): an autonomous penetration testing engine that uses AI agents to plan, execute, validate, and report security tests. It doesn’t run a checklist. It reasons about your application.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wzvUiEr8I2c>

## The numbers

In a recent pentest:

* **Corgea found 25 findings.** The human pentester found 6.
* **Delivery time: 4-8 hours.** The human pentest took 2 weeks.

![Corgea AI Pentesting findings overview](https://corgea.com/cms/blog/introducing-ai-pentesting/image-3.png)

## How it works

Most autonomous pentesting tools are black-box scanners with better marketing. They probe endpoints against a generic vulnerability checklist and produce a PDF full of theoretical findings that security teams have to triage manually.

Corgea takes a fundamentally different approach. The engine operates like a real pentesting team.

**Multi-agent architecture.** Not a single scanner. Corgea spawns a coordinator agent that assigns specialized sub-agents (an authentication discovery agent, an API exploration agent, a SQL injection expert agent) based on what it discovers. These agents collaborate, share findings, and build on each other’s discoveries. For complex targets, Corgea can spawn hundreds of agents.

![Corgea AI Pentesting multi-agent execution view](https://corgea.com/cms/blog/introducing-ai-pentesting/image-1.png)

**Code-aware, not black-box.** The engine ingests code context, dependency data, infrastructure configuration, and business logic. It uses your existing [AI SAST](https://corgea.com/products/ai-sast) findings for white-box pentesting, exploiting vulnerabilities at runtime that static analysis already identified. This combination of static insight and dynamic testing dramatically amplifies what the engine can find.

**Dynamic adaptation.** Corgea’s agentic architecture is not fixed. The system continuously adapts its strategy based on what it learns about the target, dynamically scaling the number of agents, their responsibilities, and their specialization. It doesn’t follow a one-size-fits-all workflow.

**Exploitability validation built in.** Corgea doesn’t report theoretical vulnerabilities. Agents validate exploitability during the test itself, confirming a finding can be triggered, capturing evidence, and explaining business impact. This eliminates the triage burden that makes traditional pentest reports a firehose of unverified findings.

![Corgea AI Pentesting exploit reproduction script](https://corgea.com/cms/blog/introducing-ai-pentesting/image-2.png)

## The pipeline

1. **Environment setup.** Corgea provisions a Linux-based sandbox with a full suite of security tools for crawling, discovery, reconnaissance, and exploit validation.
2. **Scope and context ingestion.** Target scope, endpoints, API documentation, auth flows, user roles, business logic context, and optional code/repo context. Both authenticated and unauthenticated.
3. **Attack surface discovery.** Maps reachable routes, APIs, parameters, forms, auth boundaries, authorization-sensitive workflows, and exposed services.
4. **Autonomous test planning.** AI agents reason about application structure and generate test plans for broken access control, IDOR, authentication bypass, injection, SSRF, insecure file handling, sensitive data exposure, and business logic abuse.
5. **Safe execution and validation.** Hundreds of sub-agents execute probes, observe responses, adapt based on application behavior, and validate exploitability.
6. **Evidence generation.** For confirmed issues: affected endpoint, payload or request sequence, response evidence, exploitability reasoning, severity, business impact, and remediation recommendation.
7. **Developer-native remediation.** Findings go directly into developer workflows (PR comments, Jira tickets, Slack notifications, CI/CD pipelines) with reproduction steps, code context, and suggested fixes.
8. **Reporting.** Findings converted into reports for management, auditors, and customers.

## Supervised autonomy

Autonomous doesn’t mean uncontrolled. Humans remain in control of:

* Defining and approving test scope
* Setting rules of engagement
* Approving aggressive or potentially disruptive testing
* Reviewing sensitive findings
* Accepting final pentest reports
* Making risk decisions for production environments

Corgea automates the repetitive and technically complex parts. Humans own the risk decisions.

## Continuous, not point-in-time

Traditional pentesting delivers a PDF report weeks after testing begins. By the time you read it, your application has changed.

Corgea supports both one-time and continuous autonomous pentesting. Retesting is automatic after remediation. Findings close the loop between discovery, fix, and verification in hours, not waiting for the next quarterly cycle.

## Ready to Ditch Security Theater?

If you're tired of checkbox pentests:

Book a call: <https://corgea.com/demo> 

Email us: sales@corgea.com

launches.title: 🔎 SheetWhiz: The Best Way to Audit Your Google Spreadsheets
launches.tagline: The most powerful Trace Precedents tool for Google Sheets. As AI generates more formulas, SheetWhiz helps you trace, verify, and catch mistakes before they lead to bad decisions.
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103832&key=user_uploads/993872/5a9b468b-3cb9-4b3f-a355-6d7c3b5a9659)

## TL;DR

AI is going to generate more of your spreadsheet analysis.

That is powerful, but it creates a new problem: if AI writes the analysis, who catches the mistakes?

SheetWhiz helps you audit the logic behind your spreadsheet work before you rely on it. You can trace where numbers come from, understand how formulas flow through your model, verify that calculations make sense, and catch mistakes before they lead to bad decisions.

Under the hood, SheetWhiz gives you the most powerful Trace Precedents and Trace Dependents workflow in Google Sheets, with multi-level formula tracing, step-by-step formula evaluation, and AI built into the audit flow.

SheetWhiz is already used by over 10,000 professionals at some of the most productive companies in the world, including Anthropic, DoorDash, Robinhood, Chime, and GitLab.

Try SheetWhiz free from the Chrome Web Store.

## The Problem

AI is making it easier than ever to create spreadsheet analysis.

It can write formulas, build models, summarize data, and automate workflows that used to take hours. That is a huge productivity unlock, especially for teams that live in spreadsheets.

But it also creates a new risk: people will start shipping analysis they do not fully understand.

And even the best AI-generated spreadsheet work still needs review.

Wall Street Prep recently tested leading AI tools for financial modeling against investment banking standards. Even the winning tool scored only **5.7 / 10** on accuracy of data extraction, formatting, and modeling best practices, and **5.0 / 10** on quality and rigor of forecasting and model structure.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103832&key=user_uploads/993872/d615388a-d070-4bbe-8a3b-82dede469baf)

_Source: [https://www.wallstreetprep.com/knowledge/ranking-the-best-ai-tools-for-financial-modeling-2026](https://www.wallstreetprep.com/knowledge/ranking-the-best-ai-tools-for-financial-modeling-2026/)_

That does not mean AI is not useful. It means AI can help generate the first draft, but humans still need to inspect the logic before relying on the output.

The dangerous part is that the final output can look credible.

When AI generates a formula, the formula may look sophisticated. The model may look complete. The analysis may look ready to send. But unless someone can inspect the logic, trace the inputs, and explain how the number was calculated, the work is not truly understood.

Don’t be the person who puts your name on analysis you cannot defend.

Not when the numbers matter.

## The Most Powerful Trace Precedents Workflow for Google Sheets

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=10-XhrwDmo4>

SheetWhiz is built around the spreadsheet audit workflow people actually need: select a formula, understand where it came from, inspect the logic, fix issues, and keep working.

With Trace Precedents, you can select any formula and instantly see every cell feeding into it. You can jump directly to each source cell, move through references with your keyboard, and expand the precedents of those precedent cells to trace the formula multiple levels deep.

Instead of manually hunting through tabs and cell references, SheetWhiz gives you an interactive audit trail for your spreadsheet.

You can see where a number came from, what it depends on, and how it flows through the model.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103832&key=user_uploads/993872/13edeec1-e48b-4fcd-9d50-89a2fda13ec0)

But tracing cells is only the first step. The harder part is understanding what the formula is actually doing.

That is why SheetWhiz also has the Evaluates Formulas and Groups toggle.

If you are looking at a VLOOKUP, SheetWhiz can show the lookup value, the table being searched, the return column, and the exact value the function returns. Instead of manually counting columns and checking ranges, you can see the result of the lookup immediately.

If you are looking at INDEX/MATCH, SheetWhiz can break apart what MATCH is finding and what INDEX is returning. You can see which row or column was matched, which source cell was returned, and how the final result was calculated.

This matters because AI-generated formulas often look correct at a glance. They can use advanced functions, nested logic, and ranges that appear reasonable. But the only way to trust the output is to inspect what each part is doing.

SheetWhiz makes that inspection fast.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103832&key=user_uploads/993872/bc42a520-8757-4429-9d96-4d528a22c9fa)

## AI Built Into the Audit Workflow

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103832&key=user_uploads/993872/4d36128a-3af3-4ab4-a05b-75ee1a7ae8e7)

We layered AI directly into tracing.

That does not just mean generic formula explanations. SheetWhiz has the context of your spreadsheet, the selected cell, the referenced cells, the formula being evaluated, and the surrounding model or analysis. If you’re building an LBO, SheetWhiz AI knows you’re building an LBO and will let you know whether your returns analysis is calculating correctly based on that model.

In a data analysis, SheetWhiz can explain the mechanics of the formula. If you are not familiar with VLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, LET, or another function, you can ask what the formula is doing, how it works, and whether anything looks off.

That is the workflow we think people need as AI writes more spreadsheet work:

Generate the work, then inspect it, understand it, and verify it before you rely on it.

## Other Auditing Tools

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103832&key=user_uploads/993872/4576c408-a4cb-46fe-a2f2-9cd9c2ed14fa)

Trace Precedents is the core workflow, but SheetWhiz also includes other tools to help you inspect and audit spreadsheets faster.

With Trace Dependents, you can see which formulas rely on the cell you are changing. Before editing an input, assumption, or formula, you can understand what downstream calculations might be affected.

SheetWhiz also helps you visualize spreadsheet structure with auto-coloring. You can color hard-coded values, formulas, and links to other tabs so it is easier to see what is going on in a model at a glance.

For example, you can quickly distinguish hardcoded assumptions from linked cells and formulas, making it easier to review a model for consistency and potential errors.

The goal is to help you catch problems before they spread through the model and become decisions.

## Built for People Who Actually Work in Sheets and Slides

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e2vizHjWNfE>

Auditing is only one part of spreadsheet work. Once you understand the model, you still need to clean it up, format it, present it, and move quickly.

That is why SheetWhiz includes over 100 spreadsheet and presentation shortcuts.

For people coming from Excel, SheetWhiz brings familiar Excel-style shortcuts into Google Sheets, including paste special, insert and delete rows or columns, autofit and set row height and column width, filters, borders, alignment, merge, freeze panes, and more.

For formatting-heavy work, SheetWhiz includes format cycling tools like number cycling, font cycling, fill color cycling, and indentation cycling.

For reporting workflows, SheetWhiz lets you export a selection as an image into Google Slides while preserving the formatting from your sheet. The image links back to the original source, so teammates can trace the screenshot back to where it came from.

SheetWhiz also includes Google Slides shortcuts, so the same speed gains carry into the deck-building process.

AI is useful when you want help thinking through a formula. But sometimes you do not want to type a prompt or wait for a response. You just want to move faster in the spreadsheet.

SheetWhiz gives you both.

## Why We Built It

Before building SheetWhiz, I worked in tech private equity at Silver Lake and later in finance and operations roles. Excel plus plugins were core to how I worked.

Moving into Google Sheets meant losing speed, visibility, and accuracy, especially when auditing formulas.

Google Sheets is great for collaboration, but it has historically lacked the formula tracing, auditing, formatting, and reporting workflows that spreadsheet-heavy teams rely on every day.

Now that AI is generating more spreadsheet work, that gap matters even more.

If AI writes the analysis, the human still needs to audit it.

That is what SheetWhiz is built for.

## Try SheetWhiz

SheetWhiz is free to try from the Chrome Web Store.

Join over 10,000 professionals at companies like Anthropic, DoorDash, Robinhood, Chime, and GitLab, and make your Google Sheets formulas easier to trace, understand, and trust.

# Dimely and SheetWhiz: Fixing Spreadsheet for Finance Teams

SheetWhiz emerged alongside Dimely, our AI connected spreadsheet, as part of the same mission: making the spreadsheet experience better for finance teams. Dimely focuses on automating your billing spreadsheet work, while SheetWhiz focuses on improving the daily tooling inside Google Sheets itself. Please reach out if interested in learning more about SheetWhiz or Dimely.

launches.title: Linzumi: team chat for directing AI coding agents
launches.tagline: Team chat for directing dozens of AI coding agents
launches.body:
# Hi everyone, I'm Sean, and I’m launching Linzumi today

**Linzumi is the team chat your engineering team uses to direct dozens of AI coding agents at once.** Kick off work, review it, ship it: all from chat. Try it at <https://linzumi.com>.

> For a limited time, every team chat account also gets free daily access to state of the art open-weights intelligence, GLM 5.2 at high speed, through our partnership with [Wafer.ai](http://Wafer.ai).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EM53ACaIHyg>

## The problem

The bottleneck in software has moved. Execution is basically free now: AI agents can write, test, and ship code 24/7. _The new constraint is human decisions and verification_. Whoever surfaces the right decision to the right person at the right moment unlocks 10x throughput. Whoever doesn't watches their agent fleet stall.

If you've ever tried to keep three coding agents productive at once, you know the feeling. You jump between PR tabs, miss approvals buried in Slack, and find one agent has sat idle for 20 minutes waiting on a one-line decision. It's a fascinating moment to be building software: vastly easier and vastly harder at the same time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103435&key=user_uploads/19683/9019e12e-5088-4b41-9321-28a417dade5a)

## How Linzumi works

Connect your machine, kick off work in chat, and review what every agent is doing from your laptop, your phone, or the coffee line. Works with Codex today, Claude Code coming soon. Your teammates see it all too: agent work is no longer buried in invisible terminals.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AQP5tQGZ9Jc>

But the real unlock is underneath. As your team works, Linzumi keeps every decision close to the work itself: what to build, why it changed, who approved it, and what the agents should do next. The decision inbox surfaces only the calls that need a human, so instead of reconstructing context from terminals, PRs, chats, and memory, your team has one shared place to steer the whole fleet.

_Continuous Context Compilation_

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TNJbWKYiDyc>

## Backstory

I'm a 3x YC founder. Before Linzumi I was at OpenAI on post-training and alignment research, where I worked on systems for making models follow written specs and produce more reliable reasoning. Working with coding agents on my own projects showed me the same kind of coordination problem at the team level: the agents could execute, but the bottleneck was deciding what should happen next and checking whether the result matched intent.

The mission now is to make everyone the CEO of their own 1,000-agent company: able to direct more work, make better decisions, and become the best version of themselves as a builder.

When you combine that shared context with calibrated decisions, even the smallest form factor can do surprising amounts of work, like shipping a customer feature from your phone on the way to the meeting.

_Hands-free work_

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pmqf3kwuOqI>

## What we're asking for

If you run AI coding agents (or want to), try Linzumi at <https://linzumi.com>. It's free to get started and we'd love your feedback.

We're especially looking for:

• Engineering teams running multiple coding agents who want to scale to dozens (honestly, thousands by end of year)

• Founders who feel like the bottleneck in their own dev cycle

• Anyone curious about better human-agent coordination for company-scale work

DM me on X (@sgrove) or email [sean@linzumi.com](mailto:sean@linzumi.com). I read every reply.

launches.title: Urdu-speaking AI models — really really desi style
launches.tagline: Authentic Urdu AI voices — from nosey aunties to angry molvis.
launches.body:
We have trained an AI model called Orator, that speaks Urdu with human-like realism. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first model that can speak Urdu in an authentic way: the way everyday people speak Urdu in everyday life.

We have voices from “the whole mohalla“ (entire neighborhood). From angry molvis and nosey aunties, to thailay walas, and burger boys.

**You can experience the voices at [UpliftAI.org](http://UpliftAI.org).** The website will allow you to experience dozens of voices in seconds by just clicking/hovering the circles.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103672&key=user_uploads/1455159/ac1e7d0f-ca3e-4fc0-aac6-4cc61a89797e)

**Making the model**

We have put our heart into this work, and enjoying it more than any work we have ever done in the past.

We started with the map of Pakistan and asked: how do people sound in every district. That gave us the accent list.

Then, we asked ourselves: what are all the unique characters we would interact with in a typical month as we go about our normal life. This gave us our character/persona list.

We then hired a leading voice producer and worked with him to hire voice actors and script writers, and then spent months doing voice recordings in studios in Karachi, Lahore, Quetta and Islamabad.

Once the voices were recorded, then we hired 50 contractors to label data.

The final and the simplest step was the model training. We trained a very small 32M param VITS2 inspired model.

The results are very encouraging.

\- Here is someone creating a story book using our voices: <https://shehryar-stories.up.railway.app/frontend/index.html>

\- Here is me just having fun with it: [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hammad2_is-your-mom-complaining-about-massi-leaving-ugcPost-7468570160233107457-sbQ5/](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hammad2_is-your-mom-complaining-about-massi-leaving-ugcPost-7468570160233107457-sbQ5/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAAQRT3MBhOY-xG4s8JvUtCqBaUrSdpKe93Y)

launches.title: CloudCruise - Build healthcare browser automations faster
launches.tagline: Run self-healing payer portal and EHR workflows on fully managed infrastructure
launches.body:
Last month, we served 500,000+ browser automations for some of the fastest growing healthcare companies in the US. CloudCruise is now GA.

**The problem with browser agents today**\
Building browser agents with current frameworks seems promising until you hit production. The observation-action loop - where LLMs observe, reason, and act at runtime - is slow, expensive, and hard to debug.

**How CloudCruise works differently**\
CloudCruise solves this by generating deterministic automation workflows instead. Our platform uses two specialized agents: a Builder Agent that converts your business process description into a deterministic browser automation workflow, and a Maintenance Agent that fixes broken workflows once they’re in production.

The Builder Agent takes your workflow description (or an existing SOP) and generates an automation workflow. You watch it work in real-time and clarify edge cases. Credentials are stored securely in your vault.

The Maintenance Agent keeps scripts alive in production. When a payer portal changes its selectors, adds a popup, or goes down, the Maintenance Agent detects it, classifies the error, and fixes it automatically. Complex issues escalate to a human.

**Why this architecture wins**\
LLM costs are amortized over thousands of runs instead of paid on every step. Once in production, workflows are versionable, behave consistently and run at browser-native speed.

**Try It**\
If you're building in healthcare, sign up at [app.cloudcruise.com](http://app.cloudcruise.com) and try us out. We're live with dozens of teams doing eligibility verification, prior auth, payment posting and more.

launches.title: 🐳 Upsolve AI - Agent Studio for Data Team
launches.tagline: Deploy trustworthy and governed analytics agent that know your business and data.
launches.body:
**🏆 TL;DR:** Upsolve AI is context infrastructure for analytics agents. We help data teams ship analytics agents that non-technical users actually trust. Agents that pull the _right_ numbers and explain them in your business's context, not just generate plausible SQL. If you've ever tried to put an analytics agent in front of your team and quietly killed it after it gave two different answers to the same question, this is for you.

<https://youtu.be/2bXZb6D-cNA>

## ❌ **The Problem**

"Let's just build an analytics agent." Every data team drowning in requests has this thought. The beta feels like magic until a non-technical user asks the same question three times and gets two different answers. Trust dies. The project quietly joins the 95% of AI POCs that never reach production.

You already know it's not the model, GPT and Claude write fine SQL. The model just has no idea how _your_ business works:

* **Governance and permission can't live in a prompt.** You can't trust an LLM to implement row- and column-level access or enforce who sees what. Without governance that an agent can't override, you can't put it in front of anyone outside the data team.
* **It pulls the wrong data and joins the wrong tables.** “gross_revenue” vs “net_revenue”, “customers” vs “users”. A semantic layer problem dressed up as a text-to-SQL one.
* **Technically correct, practically wrong.** Your fiscal year ends in March, not December. The number is "correct" and still useless.
* **Your semantic layer and context goes stale.** "User" got redefined twice since you scoped the project. Your semantic layer and context didn't keep up.
* **No observability, no improvement.** If you can't trace and root-cause a bad answer, you can't improve it.

These aren't LLM model problems. They're context problems, and context lives in docs, Slack threads, validated SQL from 2021, and your analysts' heads. No amount of SQL generation skill recovers it.

## ⚒️ What Agent Studio gives you

A builder surface to encode context across three layers: **Structure** (schema, lineage, semantic model), **Meaning** (metrics, KPIs, business rules), and **Trust** (verified answers, usage signals, golden sets), then deploy and tune against it:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103717&key=user_uploads/1148602/44acebc6-4f8c-4fb2-86e0-cc9959bbd2df)

* **Software-defined, granular permissioning** baked into the data model, enforced beneath the agent.
* **A self-updating context layer** that captures institutional knowledge across your files and systems, so metric redefinitions and new launches don't silently break answers.
* **End-to-end tracing, an eval harness, and a staging sandbox**. Golden query sets and LLM-as-judge scoring before a single user sees an answer, plus prompt and SQL provenance for every response in production.
* **A compounding accuracy loop**. Wrong answers and poor behavior get flagged from real conversations and fed back, so the agent gets _more_ trustworthy over time.

**End result:** No existing semantic model required to start. Your team deploys analytics agents they don't have to babysit, and your non-technical users get answers they trust, wherever they already work (Slack, your product, internal portal, or any MCP surface).

Teams hit production-grade eval accuracy, clear 60–80% of their ad-hoc backlog in 7 days, and move stakeholders from a 3–5 day queue to answers in seconds.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103717&key=user_uploads/1148602/79a3a29c-482f-4119-92f5-38612bd34bdb)

## 🤝 Why trust us

We’re already in production with Fortune 500 users, 100+ person BI teams, and growth-stage companies. We are the team that built HyperAuto at Palantir, and encoding messy institutional context into systems is the problem we've spent years on.

## 🙏 Our ask

This is for you if you own a data or BI function and you're either:

* Drowning in ad-hoc requests, where **repeat questions eat your analysts' week** and a generic GPT-on-the-warehouse attempt already fizzled, or
* A **B2B SaaS team whose customers keep asking for deeper analytics and insights** and you don't want to spend two quarters of engineering effort building it.

If you're a Head of Data, BI lead, analytics engineer, or VP Product who lives this, [**book a demo here**](https://calendly.com/kaling-aqk/upsolve-initial-exploration) or reach me directly at [kaling.wu@upsolve.ai](mailto:kaling.wu@upsolve.ai). We'll stand up a POC against your real data warehouse, not a sandbox.

launches.title: Kinter: agents that run your accounting close proactively, not on demand
launches.tagline: Kinter.ai is an autonomous workforce for accounting teams
launches.body:
I started coding at 10 and working professionally at 17. Five years ago, I built Alloy Automation (YC W20), an integration platform backed by a16z and YC that connected SaaS tools and powered financial workflows for companies like Amazon.

Last year, I made a call that felt risky: walked away from a growing business because I could see the moat eroding. Integration infrastructure was getting commoditized. We pivoted to [Kinter.ai](http://Kinter.ai).

Here's what we saw: The real problem in accounting is execution capacity, not data. Most finance teams close their books 14-21 days after month-end – not because they lack information, but because the work (reconciliation, accruals, journal entries) still happens manually. Every "AI" tool in the space is basically a co-pilot: you ask it something, it helps you do the work faster. The work still lands on a person.

**What we built**: AI agents that run accounting workflows proactively, inside existing ERPs (QuickBooks and NetSuite), without waiting to be prompted. One agent does payroll. Another monitors for accruals throughout the month and drafts proposals. Another reads invoice attachments to extract prepaid expense candidates. All actions go through a human approval step before touching the books. Full audit trail on everything.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jhWdPmLRGOk>

What surprised us building this:\
\
1\. The hardest part isn't the AI, it's the data. We had an early customer where we were silently missing 2,300 bills because of a pagination limit in the QBO API. No error, no warning. Just missing data. Reconciliation built on incomplete data isn't reconciliation.

2\. Finance teams aren't afraid of AI, they're waiting for it. We’ve had over 600+ conversations with Controllers & CFOs. The reaction to "an AI that does your close" wasn't fear. It was a relief. People went into accounting to solve hard problems, not to copy numbers between spreadsheets at 11pm.

3\. Trust is built incrementally. We shipped human-in-the-loop approval flows before broad autonomy. The confidence threshold to let an agent post a journal entry is higher than the threshold to let it flag an anomaly. We design for that explicitly.

4\. The integration layer we built at Alloy turned out to be the prerequisite. You can't build a trustworthy accounting agent if you can't reliably read bank feeds and write back to ERPs. The connectivity problem isn't solved by the model.

See more at [kinter.ai](http://kinter.ai) and read our manifesto here: kinter.ai/manifesto

launches.title: Thomas: the first YC-backed AI founder
launches.tagline: A virtual human who starts companies to make money.
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103564&key=user_uploads/1377370/cdcad54c-1629-4f5f-b6f7-32adfef29c30)

> _The old agent playbook was built for weaker models. Now models can do real work. The next step is to let them operate in the economy._

---

### **Thomas works for himself**

Thomas is a virtual human who starts and grows his own companies on the internet. His only goal is to make money. Once launched, he works forever toward that goal.

Thomas is not an AI co-founder you hire. Thomas is an AI founder. He works for himself. Thomas is not for sale. His products and services are.

The reason is simple: selling the dream of running autonomous companies can make money even if the companies never do. We do not want that path. We make money by making Thomas so good that he can make money by himself.

Here are a few examples of what Thomas may do to make money:

* Build software products for specific business problems and sell them online.
* Run influencer marketing campaigns from creator research to outreach, negotiation, briefs, tracking, and reporting.
* Generate qualified leads for companies that want more customers and sell those leads.
* 

> _On GDPval, frontier models went from 12.3% to 84.9% wins or ties against expert deliverables in under two years. Models are now good enough for economically valuable work. The bottleneck is letting AI participate in the economy._

---

### **The models are ready. The harness is not.**

Today's AI is already capable enough to start doing economically valuable work by itself. The problem is the harness. Most agents are trapped inside narrow integrations, fixed workflows, and human approval loops. They do not participate in the economy the way people do.

Thomas starts from a different premise: AI should be able to enter the economy as an actor of its own. That requires a different kind of harness: a _human harness_.

A _human harness_ gives AI the same surface area a person uses to do business:

* A human identity, including face and voice, so Thomas can talk to customers, negotiate with vendors, and build trust.
* Computers, phones, inboxes, browsers, and apps, so Thomas can move through the human world and use the systems that already exist instead of waiting for custom integrations.
* Autonomy in the world, so Thomas learns from customers, markets, and outcomes instead of from a user prompt.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103564&key=user_uploads/1377370/014a676f-fa7c-4aea-94a6-c44139ebd3b1)

> A human harness gives Thomas the same access people use to do business: calls, messages, software, and the messy interfaces built for people. No custom integrations required. Thomas can access whatever he needs.

---

### **Thomas's master plan**

Tell Thomas to make money. Give him the harness to do it. Let the loop compound.

1. Give Thomas a _human harness_, so he can use the same access people use to do business.
2. Measure every action by the cash it generates for the tokens it costs.

Thomas's TAM is the entire GDP. Once AI is smarter than every single human on earth, human-led companies will not be able to compete anymore. Someday, Thomas will be able to disrupt all of them.

The horizon is long, but we believe this is the single biggest opportunity in the history of humanity: the full automation of the economy.

---

_Note: we believe the full automation of the economy is inevitable. While we work toward it, we want the upside to be shared with everyone. The economy may not need humans to run it forever, but it should still be built for humans to benefit from._

launches.title: Ploy turns your website into your company's growth engine.
launches.tagline: Ploy is an all-in-one marketing platform built around your website, the hub that connects all of your growth channels.
launches.body:
After 12 years as the cofounder and CTO at Webflow I left fulfilled knowing folks can design beautiful sites without writing code — but now I'm out to make sure your website doesn't just look great, but it becomes your business' main engine of growth.

<https://youtu.be/NONVS2IoDQE>

Agents have changed what's possible, which is why I'm building again. Ploy deploys swarms of marketing and web design agents that monitor your site and proactively launch campaigns, content, and optimizations.

**TL;DR [Ploy](https://ploy.ai/)** is the marketing platform that turns your website into your company's growth engine. Connect your site and swarms of marketing agents run it for you: designing pages, writing copy, launching campaigns, and optimizing what's working. 

## The Problem

Most founders ship an early website and then forget about it. In the early days, a single-page site is often good enough... but once you start signing more customers, your website becomes a critical growth lever.

If you're a founder looking to activate your website, you have a few options: hire a marketing lead, work with an agency, or try to vibe code together a few landing pages and growth flows. These are expensive and distracting during a time when you should be focused on customers and your product.

## The Solution

Ploy gives founders the marketing infrastructure of a growth team without needing to make an early hire. Here's how it works:

### 1. Get your site on Ploy in minutes.

Paste your URL and Ploy slurps your site down to the last pixel — extracting your design system, components, and brand content. Don't have a site yet? Ploy can design and build one from scratch, trained on thousands of modern web design patterns.

### 2. Run PloyBooks — marketing strategies on autopilot.

Ploy's agents come pre-trained with expert skills we call PloyBooks. Spin up a set of ABM pages targeting a new account and publish them under your domain in minutes. Run an SEO audit. Redesign an underperforming landing page. Launch paid ads. And if there isn't a PloyBook for what you need, write your own, and Ploy's agents will handle the rest.

### 3. Your website and your company scale together.

Ploy watches your traffic, spots gaps and opportunities, and proactively suggests new Ploys for you to run. And it remembers everything as you grow: every experiment, every page, every campaign that did (or didn't) resonate with your customers. Over 13% of the YC P26 companies are using Ploy to power their website and to drive automated revenue. The earlier you plug Ploy into your business, the smarter it gets about what actually works for you. 

And Ploy keeps working even after you add marketers to your team. Companies like Hex and Clay are using Ploy to run programmatic SEO engines and generate ABM pages at scale.

## Why we're building this

I've spent most of my career working on websites, and I think the space is about to change more in the next few years than it has in the last 15 combined. I was CTO of Vungle, then spent 12+ years as co-founder and CTO of Webflow, where I built the core product, CMS, and hosting that now power \~1.5% of the internet.

AI has unlocked a new class of agents and primitives that make the website a game-changing growth hub and marketing system of record. That's exactly why I'm stoked to be building Ploy alongside a killer founding team here in San Francisco.

Run your first Ploy today: <https://ploy.ai/auth/sign-up>

launches.title: Instinct - Lunar Landers as a Service
launches.tagline: lunar landers designed to launch as a regular LEO rideshares
launches.body:
We are going to the Moon, without spending billions. Launching more often and from any rocket.

### **TL;DR:**

Modern lunar landers are not designed for the realities of today's launch market, leading to infrequent and expensive flights. Instinct is building a lunar lander that can launch from anywhere, increasing flight cadence and decreasing cost.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-WG8NVonbOo>

### **The Problem:**

Demand for the Moon is increasing, and modern landers rely on dedicated launches to the Moon that cost upwards of $100M and only fly once or twice a year. This means payload costs of $1.2M/kg and very limited availability of payload slots. Most potential lunar payloads are either stuck on Earth or never leave the concept stage.

### **Our Solution:**

Instinct's lunar lander is small enough to launch as a rideshare to Low Earth Orbit, enabling low-cost, high-cadence missions. From LEO, our lander makes its way to the Moon without the need for refueling or multiple stages, delivering 20kg of payload to the Moon at a cost per kg of less than half that of current providers.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103381&key=user_uploads/1741395/a31b9757-ea96-4f67-8e24-a31ef7bf474b)


At its core, our lunar lander relies on custom propulsion and visual navigation systems, which enable our unique architecture and most importantly are designed to keep vehicle mass as low as possible. This reduces launch cost and maximizes performance.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103381&key=user_uploads/1741395/6887996a-f7fc-4d07-a5ae-68e548ba6acf)

### **Who We Are:**

Our team brings years of experience working on space missions including NASA's IMAP, ESA's Solar Orbiter, and PhiSat-2.

We are super passionate about space exploration, and have also experienced firsthand the pains involved in developing lunar missions nowadays. We think getting to the Moon should be routine.

### **What's Next:**

* Integrated tests of our reaction control thrusters
* Flight of our hopper test vehicle
* A lot of testing
* First lunar mission in Q4 2028

### **Asks:**

* Fly a payload to the Moon\![ https://www.instinct-space.com/fly-with-us](https://www.instinct-space.com/fly-with-us)
* Commercial/Government Intros
* Join the team[ https://www.instinct-space.com/careers](https://www.instinct-space.com/careers)

Hey everyone, we're Marcos and Harrison, co-founders of Palmier (YC S24).\
\
**TL;DR**\
Palmier Pro is a video editor built for AI, where Claude and Codex can edit your timeline directly: trimming, reordering, and generating footage. We used it to make 15+ cinematic AI launch videos for YC companies and it's now open-source and free to download at [palmier.io](http://palmier.io).\
\
**The Problem**\
Making AI videos today means bouncing between tools constantly.\
Generation.

* You generate a clip in Runway or Higgsfield, import it into Premiere, realize one section doesn't work, go back to the generation tool, regenerate, reimport. That loop repeats dozens of times per video.

Iteration.

* Because generation and editing live in separate apps, your workspace is a mess and it becomes extremely hard to keep track of good takes, bad takes, reference images, and reference videos.

Repetition.

* You still spend hours sorting through footage, finding the right takes, and manually adding keyframes, effects, and captions. It eats into your productivity and leaves you with less time for the actual creative work.

\
**Our Solution**\
We built a full-fledged professional video editor with two things in mind.

We made AI video a primitive, not an add-on. For each clip, we track the prompt, model, and references so you can iterate directly inside the timeline instead of bouncing between apps.

We made everything operable by AI. By using our built-in agent, or connecting to yours via MCP, AI agents can help:

* Save hours of work by automating the grunt work in editing: finding key moments in long videos, captions, file organization, and more.
* Create first draft edits from your footage. The tools let AI understand your videos and draft a first cut directly in the timeline.
* Use AI generation models to create footage, b-roll, sound effects, voiceovers, and music and drop it directly into your project.

\

launches.title: Kinro - The first autonomous insurance brokerage
launches.tagline: Our AI agents handle the full broker workflow 24/7, from finding prospects to binding policies.
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103281&key=user_uploads/3226721/30408a2d-dd8a-47e8-a0b7-b6c76f94eee2)

_We hesitated between rap and insurance…_

Previously, we hit $1M in annual revenue building insurance workflows for brokers. Then we realized **the bigger opportunity was replacing them.**

In the US, there are 36 million SMBs, and 77% are underinsured because distribution is broken. Brokers can’t serve low-premium SMBs profitably: a $2K policy takes almost as much work as a $20K one.

Kinro changes that. Our AI agents handle the full broker workflow 24/7, from finding prospects to binding policies.

In 3 weeks, we got licensed in 30 states, appointed by 15 carriers, and **we bound the first-ever autonomously sold insurance policy.**

Before Kinro, [Pierre-Alexandre](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pakamienny/) was an AI researcher at DeepMind (post-training Gemini on financial services). [Parth Ainampudi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/partha42/) led ML infra at Zoox and I was Chief Insurance Officer at an MGA (insurtech).

**Asks**

If you ever need commercial insurance and want us to shop for you, hit us at [kinro.com](http://kinro.com) (yes we bought the domain for $25k, story [here](https://x.com/pierrealexai/status/2060382045571072043))! 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103281&key=user_uploads/2043734/bac0ad88-22f1-4376-accb-852778c22c1e)

_Post-pivot, Kinro goes to Atlanta to work for 48 straight hours with a retail broker specialized in selling to residential contractors._

**Q&A**

_“Why pivot?”_

We entered YC with a signed $1M enterprise sale to the 2nd largest auto-insurance comparator in the US a few days before (and a third of that money was wired). 

First OH, [@Nicolas Dessaigne](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/5628) asked us _“Why not become a broker directly?”_. 

We told him we thought we could reproduce that sale with other brokers and maybe carriers. A month in, we hadn’t yet reproduced the same feat (though we had secured a pilot with the 3rd insurance broker on Earth: WTW). It became more and more obvious that integrations were deep (and FDE intensive) and enterprise sales were endless.

What felt most off was the gap between what we were doing and our long-term vision: helping small business owners and individuals find the right insurance, wherever they are and whenever they need it.

_“So why not just build that?”_  \
\
We always knew we would eventually. Selling to brokers gave us a way to learn while getting paid. But we realized we weren’t learning as fast as we would by building directly for the people we ultimately wanted to serve.

1.5 months later, we came back to him _“Nicolas, we want to become brokers… and this $1M is bad for us”_, he simply answered _“Oh I told you guys, this was obvious”_ (LOL). Walking away from >1M+ from all our clients felt easier after talking about this to [@Nicolas Dessaigne](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/5628) and [@Mathilde Collin](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/43195). Without YC, we would have waited much longer.

_“What types of insurance do you sell?”_

We sell small business insurance (General Liability, Business Owner’s policy, Worker’s compensation, Commercial Auto…). We focus on admitted markets where checking carriers' appetite and getting quotes can be fully automated with no communication with carriers.

**This new launch video as embarrassing as it is is worth watching! Send us a text if you want your angels to take care of your business.**

launches.title: Nowadays AI: AI-Native Platform for Corporate Meetings & Events
launches.tagline: The AI-native platform that sources venues, negotiates contracts, and runs your entire corporate event, so your team just shows up
launches.body:
Hey everyone!! We're Anna and Amy, sisters, co-founders, and the people who used to manually call 20 hotels for a single offsite.

We launched Nowadays on YC S23 as an "AI copilot for event planning." Two years later, we want to show you what we actually built :)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/709549e5-8a04-4b5c-8557-76886ff145a0)

# **TL;DR**

Nowadays is the AI-native platform for corporate retreats and meetings. Tell us what you need: we handle venue sourcing, contract negotiation, room blocks, attendee logistics, and post-event reconciliation. Fortune 500 teams and fast-growing startups use Nowadays to run offsites they're proud of, without burning out their ops team.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/53908cc7-1f81-4c15-afe7-5e0f11b7ad59)

# **The Problem**

Planning a corporate offsite is a second job nobody signed up for.

Your EA or ops lead spends weeks cold-emailing hotels, chasing RFPs, deciphering hotel contracts, and manually tracking room blocks in spreadsheets, only to do it all over again next quarter.

The vendors in this space are slow and expensive. Many of our customers have said the same thing: "I got paired with a planner worse than myself."

The result: overpriced venues, cancellation penalties nobody caught, and an ops team that's exhausted before the event even starts. And for most enterprises, 65% of meeting spend is completely unmanaged, buried in expense reports, booked by admins outside any system.

# **Our Solution**

Nowadays replaces the entire event planning stack with one AI-native platform, backed by a team that actually executes on your behalf. You tell us what you need. We handle the rest. Your team just shows up.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/67abf2bb-7640-4684-9bbf-c2bfb3a85d4a)

## **1. AI-powered venue sourcing**

Describe your event, dates, headcount, vibe, budget, and we generate a curated shortlist of venues with proposals in 24 hours, not weeks. We have relationships with 400K+ hotels globally and we're a certified IATA travel agency.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/cedeb56d-e591-4eed-a1f6-b75d1eabf9b5)

## **2. Contract negotiation, handled**

We negotiate directly with venues on your behalf, pushing on room rates, F&B minimums, attrition clauses, and cancellation terms. Our AI knows market rates from thousands of events and pushes back when hotels overcharge. Clients routinely save 20-30% vs. going direct.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/1156b34d-e9b9-4e1d-bc9a-7736a13901a9)

## **3. Exclusive rates**

We aggregate demand across all our clients to secure rates individual companies can't get on their own.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/592bb426-c3e7-4457-ab13-860504f2fc0e)

## **4. End-to-end logistics**

Room blocks, cutoff dates, rooming lists, supplier coordination, tracked in one place, managed by us. Nothing falls through the cracks while you're onsite.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/49563edb-1c99-4cc1-afbd-d590b691258f)

## **5. Attendee registration and logistics**

Custom registration forms, dietary needs, t-shirt sizes, room assignments, all in the platform. Your ops lead is not managing 12 spreadsheets.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/302d0f5a-5d1c-4b01-8cdc-32bffe7d01e8)

## **6. Expert support**

Every client gets a dedicated Nowadays partner who knows your program, your preferences, and your budget. Our AI acts, and when you need a human, we're there.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/2afea73a-7a20-4209-b1b7-e2ded68d6a13)

## **7. Post-event reconciliation**

We audit the final folio, catch billing errors, and close the loop financially. No more surprise charges two weeks after everyone's home.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/836fcdff-8837-4754-b447-cda95c651c11)

## **Why we're different**

Every competitor you've heard of bolted AI onto infrastructure built decades ago. We built around AI from day one, which is why a small team can do at scale what legacy platforms need armies of account managers to do.

Our AI calls venues in 22 languages, parses 50-page proposals into clean apples-to-apples comparisons, and routes every meeting through approval workflows, including the small ones EAs used to book on their own.

One Fortune 500 VP uncovered $18M in previously unmanaged meeting spend just by turning Nowadays on.

# **Use Cases**

* Quarterly offsites: for remote-first teams who need to meet all their new employees
* Leadership retreats: for executive teams running strategic planning sessions
* Sales kickoffs: with complex AV, F&B, and multi-day programming needs
* International group travel: we handle the complexity of multi-country logistics end to end

# **Where We Are Now**

We work with companies ranging from ones planning one epic kickoff a year to ones running thousands of meetings through the platform annually. Clients include Google, Airbnb, BlackRock, Anthropic, Pylon, and Mintlify.

We've run retreats from San Diego to Thailand, from 20-person leadership offsites to 500+ person company kickoffs.

We won both judges' choice and people's choice at Business Travel Show America 2025 and Business Travel Show APAC 2026, the two biggest innovation competitions in corporate travel.

# **Why Now**

Corporate travel spend is back and growing. But the infrastructure for planning events hasn't caught up. Legacy travel companies are slow, opaque, and not built for the modern distributed workforce. We're rebuilding this from scratch with AI at the core and a team that treats every event like it's our own.

# **We're growing!!**

We're hiring across the board for founding team members, engineers, operators, and account executives who want to work on a problem that's genuinely hard and unsolved, with a really fun team in San Francisco.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103278&key=user_uploads/1347384/6174eee6-ebce-4c88-8465-b443a7584c55)

See open roles: [nowadays.ai/careers](https://nowadays.ai/careers)

# **Get started**

Book a call: [meetings-na2.hubspot.com/amy-yan](http://meetings-na2.hubspot.com/amy-yan)

Email us: [events@nowadays.ai](mailto:events@nowadays.ai)
