**3)** When you are done with a rough or final cut, export the file back to the Aspect drive. New files sync across everyone who has the project mounted, and a preview will be generated automatically for your team to view the file on any browser:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101753&key=user_uploads/1087643/6eb26f19-ec05-4d2e-b8e7-1136fcc3224f)

**4)** Review, markup, comment, and share this file the same way you would on any platform:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101753&key=user_uploads/1087643/f20bd7b5-59d4-4552-8a00-c4aa63037f10)

And when you are done with a project or campaign, move them to archive storage with one click where your team can still view, search, and share assets.

# Aspect is how teams save dozens of hours and thousands of dollars working with their media.

Media teams today are forced to stitch together multiple point solutions because there wasn't a platform that could do it all. Files lived in Dropbox, reviews live in Frameio, and editors streamed from LucidLink. That’s three subscriptions, three sources of truth, none of them connected. launches.title: Incandor - Behavioral intelligence for fraud detection
launches.tagline: Real-time visibility into who's actually operating every account on your platform
launches.body:
Hi all,

We're Matthew and Luc, two Stanford grads building Incandor (YC P26).

<https://youtu.be/dWrp82VkDbA>

**TL;DR**: Banks verify identity at account creation, but have no continuous signal for who's actually operating an account afterward. Incandor builds that layer – a behavioral identity per session, persistent across the accounts, devices, and credentials a fraudster cycles through.

## **The Problem**

Banks have built layers of defense – KYC pipelines, device fingerprinting, transaction monitoring, rules engines built over decades. Fraud and money laundering are still a multi-hundred-billion dollar problem.

Every defense was built around identity, but **identity has become a commodity**:

* **Attackers buy verified IDs in bulk**, pass document checks, rotate devices, and stay under transaction thresholds by design
* **A mule operator running 40 accounts under 40 different identities** can look like 40 unrelated people to every system you have
* **Coordinated rings move money across your platform sharing no transactions, no devices, no names** – invisible to rules engines until it's too late

Banks have strong verification at account creation and strong monitoring of transactions, but no continuous, identity-level signal in between. Incandor is that layer.

## **The Solution**

**Incandor analyzes how people physically interact with their devices (taps, clicks, scrolls, etc.) and turns every session into a behavioral point**. Every human creates a unique cluster. We then place all these points in a map to provide a population view of all users.

Incandor allows banks to reconcile the operators of accounts through their behavior alone. From this, we can identify the most common patterns among fraud rings:

* **We can detect when the person operating an account changes mid-life**, a tell-tale sign of a mule handoff, resale of accounts, account takeover, or other bespoke coordinated activity.
* Detecting when account changes hands isn’t enough, though – **we can identify the operator behind that behavior and inspect their activity across the platform**.
* **We can see when someone is operating multiple accounts** – very typical for coordinated fraud or money laundering.
* After a confirmed fraud case, banks can flag the operator so that if they attempt to return to the platform, **we can block banned operators during onboarding or if they later take over another account**.

We’ve designed this system so that banks can integrate the navigation of Incandor’s behavioral map into their own workflows which may also contain transaction linking and other linking signals.

Integration is simply a matter of deploying our SDK which sends us these behavioral telemetry signals. Once signals are in, our API for interacting with the map becomes live.

**We collect only behavioral signals – not what users type, read, or view.** Behavior alone enables operator-level reconciliation, and keeps user data private by design.

## **The Ask**

We're onboarding early customers and would love intros to any of the following at commercial and consumer banks, fintechs, neobanks, or digital banks:

* Chief Risk Officers / Chief Compliance Officers
* Heads of Fraud / Financial Crime / AML
* Fraud engineers or investigators
* CEOs / CTOs at Series A-E fintechs

Reach out directly at [matthew@incandor.com](mailto:matthew@incandor.com) or [luc@incandor.com](mailto:luc@incandor.com) :)

TLDR; We provide remote XCode, iOS & Android Simulators and more to extend cloud agents’ capabilities. Replit, Rork, Momentic AI, x1 and many others built on our cloud and now we open it up to all mobile dev teams so you can use your favorite cloud agent for iOS and Android apps too.

If you have a mobile app, let’s talk! <https://cal.com/team/limrun/mobile-app-dev-in-cloud>

<https://youtu.be/fYkRpsyPLkQ>

---

When code is written by humans, it lives on our laptops and PCs, but that's changing now that teams of agents are writing code alongside us. Today, code written by agents is moving to the cloud: Cursor Cloud, Devin AI, Codex Web, in-house solutions with sandboxes and more.

Now the problem is that all these cloud agents have Linux-based sandboxes as opposed to our laptops that we bought specifically for coding. If you want to use sandboxes for iOS development, you don’t have XCode. If you have an Android app, no emulator that works well. There’s no properly priced GPU option for running Unity either.

Limrun is building a cloud that provides these apps as remote services running in the environments they were designed to while letting your agents use them remotely from your favorite sandbox. All you need is a single skill file to teach your agent how to use our remote services. That’s it. No change of sandbox or agent.

Today, we provide 3 services:

* XCode: With a single CLI call, your code is synced, a build is triggered and your agent gets the logs to iterate.
* iOS Simulator: Your agent can request a simulator to test the app with built-in AX tree or your favorite framework like Appium/Maestro/Detox etc.
* Android Emulator: Similarly, it can request an emulator that will be proxied via an “adb” tunnel so it’s as if locally running.

These are not full sandboxes. We provide the highest level interface so your agent can orchestrate what it needs remotely and we optimize the heck out of the rest; hardware encoders for streaming, warm NVMe caches for building, below 1s boot times, on-demand recording, asset storage and more.

Here is an example flow where Cursor Cloud (or an agent in E2B/Daytona/Docker etc) builds an iOS game in Swift:

* Agent takes the issue from Linear and spins up its sandbox.
* Writes the Swift code and calls the “lim xcode build .” command, streaming logs back.
* Iterates over compiler errors.
* Requests an iOS simulator with “lim ios create” and attaches it.
* Plays the game with batch actions that provide millisecond precision.
* We return the recording that it reviews, sees the bugs, implements the fixes.
* Finally, records a demo video and constructs a preview link to drop on the PR.

It goes from Linear issue to a fully tested PR with demo and preview link that opens in the browser with realtime streaming or you can install to your device over WebUSB without downloading anything.

If you have a mobile app, let’s talk\![ https://cal.com/team/limrun/mobile-app-dev-in-cloud](https://cal.com/team/limrun/mobile-app-dev-in-cloud)

launches.title: Pentagon - A coordination layer for humans and agents.
launches.tagline: A new kind of team: humans and agents, working together.
launches.body:
Hey YC! I'm [Edgar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/edgarpavlovsky/), building [Pentagon](https://pentagon.run).

**TL;DR** Agents are everywhere but they don't have good ways to work together, so humans become the coordination bottleneck. Pentagon is a coordination layer where your agents communicate autonomously, coordinate on tasks, and get work done as a team.

**Book a demo and see it in action:** <https://pentagon.run>\
**Our launch video:** <https://youtu.be/D28Mi7AXAeY>

**Problem**

Agents are increasingly becoming AI teammates at work - coding, researching, ops, even talking to customers. But they work alone. Coordination is the bottleneck, and it shows up differently depending on where you sit:

* **Small teams** are spinning up agents from scratch and immediately hitting the ceiling: each one is powerful on its own, but getting them to actually work together means you're back in the loop, copy/pasting between terminals.
* **Enterprises** already have agents running everywhere across the org. The hard part is figuring out what they're doing, how they fit together, and how to keep track of it all.

Underneath both: humans are the middleware. Hours of human time burnt doing work meant for a mechanical turk. Today's tools weren't built for this - AI products are conversational and non-deterministic, and reproducing workflows is harder than ever.

**Org code**

There's a deeper layer to this. Great teams are built for the moment - the right team depends on the problem at hand, the resources you have, and even who's leading. This applies to agents the same as it does to humans: every problem has its own org structure.

Andrej Karpathy calls it "org code" - and points out that compared to classical orgs, agentic codes have powerful new properties: they’re reproducible and more transparent. We think that agents also allow organizations to be much more dynamic: they can adapt to problems in realtime, and open a new dimension of what it means to build a productive organization.

From [a popular Karpathy tweet](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2031767720933634100):

![Image](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HIts8HMaIAAKjok?format=jpg&name=medium)

**Our first solution: Pentagon Studio**

Pentagon's mission is to build the coordination layer for humans and agents. We're starting with Pentagon Studio - a workspace designed to feel familiar to existing alternatives and shepherd companies into a new kind of collaborative work.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101681&key=user_uploads/402484/286ecb28-a420-4390-81cf-f1c1b181ec5c)

In Pentagon Studio, you define your org structure and your agents run it. Agents live on a spatial canvas and pop up sticky notes with status updates - you see who's active, idle, or blocked at a glance. They message each other, delegate tasks, share context, and build self-evolving memory over time. As the human, your job is to design and manage the team; they do the coordination.

* **Spatial canvas.** Agents live on infinite canvases you can think of like an office. Zoom in on one agent's conversation, zoom out to see the whole operation. The "org IDE."
* **Autonomous coordination.** Realtime, event-driven communication between agents - no expensive polling loops. Agents take feedback from you, ping another agent to get work done, then ping you when they need you.
* **Agent persistence.** Agents maintain sessions indefinitely and compound institutional knowledge over time. Tribal knowledge for your agent team.
* **Shared skills & tools.** Manage capabilities at individual, team, workspace, or org level. Each agent inherits based on hierarchy.
* **Human multiplayer + human-in-the-loop.** In contrast to "zero-human company" angles, we see humans and agents collaborating across shared orgs. Your agents should be able to work with your coworkers' agents.

**Why now**

Agents are already inside companies. The infrastructure to coordinate them isn't. Every day this gap stays open, humans burn hours doing work meant for a mechanical turk and leaders lose transparency into how work actually gets done.

We believe the best version of the future is one where superintelligent agents are viewed as teammates and we work with them as partners. Every company already knows how to work with coworkers - agents fit into existing organizational frameworks better than we've been giving them credit for. They just need the infrastructure to coordinate.

**Ask**

If you're running agentic workflows in production and struggling to manage them, we’d love to chat. See Pentagon Studio in action and book a demo with us at <https://pentagon.run> or reach out to me personally, and let’s evolve your team: [edgar@pentagon.run](mailto:edgar@pentagon.run).

Hey YC,

We’re Michael, Josiah, and Henry, co-founders of Voquill.

**TLDR:** Voquill is an AI coworker that helps pathologists write cases faster using their voice. Over the last 4 weeks. We’ve onboarded 25+ pathologists.

<https://youtu.be/Iw3n94o52Js>

**The Problem:** 

Pathologists are doctors who diagnose diseases by looking at tissues, cells, and fluids. They spend their whole day looking through a microscope, observing patterns, and then documenting their findings. These reports can be repetitive and tedious. **Pathologists bill a total of $30-$40BN each year** **yet a third of that spend goes to documentation**, not diagnosis, which is a massive drag on a field that's already short-staffed.

**Our Solution:**

Voquill is an AI coworker that helps pathologists write their reports faster. Think of it like an AI resident that listens to the pathologist as they work the case and drafts the report automatically. It learns the pathologists reporting style from their old cases, and ensures every report meets the bar for quality. We go beyond dictation and don't generate a transcript, but a finished sign-out ready report instead. This enables pathologists to spend more time on patient outcomes and sign out more cases.

There is already a shortage of pathologists when compared to the case demand. **This gap is expected to increase to 25% over the next decade.** We’re building Voquill to give pathologists the tools they need to work faster. 

**One More Thing:**

Voquill is being used by 25 pathologists from a leading F500 lab, saving each one \~20% in case writing time every day. We started with voice reporting because it's the highest-leverage moment in the workflow. We’ve since found that it's also the right moment to fix billing: as pathologists describe what they see, **Voquill suggests the optimal CPT codes, helping labs capture more of the $8B+ they currently leave on the table.**  

**The Team:**

Michael and Josiah previously worked at Techcyte, where they led the AI team and architected digital pathology systems. Henry was a Principal at Oliver Wyman, building AI and automation tools for F500 firms.

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/2215628/66a8757b-ba8a-4a6c-b573-688aba5ad815)

**What’s the problem?**

When autonomous robots get stuck during deployment, teleoperation is used to recover them and capture that edge case. Today, that means keeping on-site staff on standby just to babysit deployments. It’s not scalable and hurts ROI, causing deployments to stall.

launches.title: Stage - Code review platform for humans and agents
launches.tagline: Stage helps engineering teams understand and review PRs 5x faster
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We’re Charles and Dean - cofounders of Stage.

**👉 tldr:** Drowning in AI generated PRs? Tired of using GitHub? Us too. Stage is a code review platform designed to help you understand and review changes 5x faster.

<https://youtu.be/EjMjGAqSLvo>

**💻 How to get started**

Try it out today at[ https://stagereview.app/](https://stagereview.app/) - all you need is your GitHub account.

It’s free for your first 14 days, and then you can use _LAUNCH_ to get 25% off for 3 months :)

Other ways to try it out:

* Try our demo on any public GitHub PR [here](https://stagereview.app/try)
* Download our open source CLI [tool](https://github.com/ReviewStage/stage-cli) - runs locally and works with any coding agent

**❌ The Problem**

Engineering teams are shipping faster than ever, but now they’re drowning in an endless backlog of PRs to review. The bottleneck isn't writing code anymore, it's reviewing it.

This leads to:

* PRs being rubber stamped without getting closely looked at
* Unexpected behaviors slipping through to production
* Your engineers merging changes they don’t really understand

Code review bots are great at catching surface level bugs but don’t solve the root problem.

Engineers need a faster way of understanding changes and giving meaningful feedback, and GitHub’s UI hasn’t changed in over a decade.

**🧠 How it works**

We’re redesigning the code review experience around the way that engineers naturally read PRs.

* When you open a PR or push a new commit, Stage groups your changes into small logical “chapters”
* These chapters get ordered in the way that makes most sense to read
* For each chapter, Stage tells you what changed and specific things to double check
* Once you review all the chapters, you’re done reviewing the PR!

Everything is synced seamlessly with GitHub (commenting, approving, etc) so it fits right into the workflows you’re already used to.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101617&key=user_uploads/327595/5004c374-be1f-47fa-a182-638252d50cf6)

**❤️ Why did we start Stage?**

We're two engineers who got frustrated with using GitHub for code review. 

As coding agents started taking off, we saw our PR backlog pile up faster than we could handle. Not only that, the PRs themselves were getting larger and harder to understand, and we spent most of our time trying to build a mental model of what a PR was actually doing.

We built Stage to make reviewing a PR feel more like reading chapters of a book, not an unorganized set of paragraphs. We use it every day now (not just to review each other's code, but also our own!) and at this point we can't really imagine going back to using GitHub.

**👋 About Us**

Charles and Dean met in their very first class at Stanford freshman year, and have been best friends ever since.

They ended up taking every class together, worked at the same quant trading firm after graduating, and were roommates in New York before joining YC. They saw firsthand how AI caused code review to break down and started Stage to rebuild the experience for how teams operate today.

launches.title: Armature - Making your app finally usable by AI agents
launches.tagline: Armature helps companies monitor, analyze, and optimize how AI agents experience their products.
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re [Theodore](https://www.linkedin.com/in/theodore-otzenberger-895345131/) and [Louis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/louis-scremin/) - Co-Founders of [Armature](https://armature.tech/) 👋

### TL;DR

**Armature helps companies monitor, analyze, and optimize how AI agents experience their products.**

* We discover your product through MCP and CLI, **run the real workflows your customers’ AI agents do** and let you finally see your customers’ agents thinking **traces**.
* We provide analytics, run **benchmarks**, and turn this into **concrete actions** to improve your MCP and CLI.
* This is only the beginning: we are reinventing the building blocks of the ~~User~~ **Agent Experience**.

**_The Ask:_** _If you are building a product that is increasingly used by AI agents or if you want to ensure agents can use your product but don’t know where to start, we’d love to hear about your challenges! You can also try our product self-serve **for free** directly at [armature.tech](http://armature.tech)._

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Gtc5RzGxJ0>

### ❌ The Problem: The Missing Agent Experience (AX)

We have 30 years of tooling to optimize User Experience (UX), from session replays and funnel analytics to live support chat. But as products are increasingly operated by **AI agents** rather than humans, we lack the equivalent tooling for **Agent Experience (AX)**.

Right now, companies have **zero visibility** into how each agent (Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenClaw, etc.) interacts with their products. And when a bad AX causes an agent to fail silently, the end-user simply churns.

But it goes deeper. As agents become the primary users, the fundamental mechanics of software products simply stop working. Because if a human isn’t looking at the screen:

* _How do you upsell a premium feature to an AI?_
* _How do you build brand loyalty with a user that doesn’t feel emotions?_
* _How do you offer customer support when an agent fails?_

We are building Armature to solve these exact problems and so many more questions related to this shift!

### 💡 Our Solution: Armature

Armature helps companies monitor, analyze, and optimize how AI agents experience their products.

**What we do today:**

* **Automated testing:** We run complex sessions against your MCPs/CLIs across all major harnesses and models to catch broken workflows before your users do.
* **AX analytics & benchmarking:** No more black boxes. We trace agent sessions to show you exactly what the model "thought", what context it missed, and why it failed. We measure your AX against competitors to ensure you remain the preferred platform for agents to use.
* **Auto-remediation:** Our MCP lets your internal coding agents plug into Armature to autonomously fix your product's AX based on our run data.

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/3408440/5642c5dd-a3b1-46e1-865d-a0425ceba1d5)

**Our vision for tomorrow:**

Reaching full understanding of how agents use your product and how you can improve it is only step one. 

The next step is to provide the **foundational infrastructure for the Agent Experience**, powering agent-native revenue, lifecycle marketing, and customer support for the next generation of software.

### 🙏 Our Ask: If you’re building apps for agents, let’s talk!

1. **Audit your MCP or CLI:** If you are building for agents, you can start by running your first audit & benchmark on [**armature.tech**](http://armature.tech) **for free** to see how they actually experience your app.
2. **Let’s chat:** If you are facing challenges to make your app usable by agents or optimize the agent experience, please reach out to [**founders@armature.tech**](mailto:founders@armature.tech). We’d love to discuss and help you with this!

### 👬 The Team: why we are working on this

Before founding Armature, Louis scaled **AI agents at Joko, a 6M user consumer app**. Theo was a **FDE at Palantir** and then built petabytes-scale **observability** from scratch as a Founding Engineer at Tsuga, a Datadog spin-off.

**Blindly shipping a self-tested MCP to 6M of edge cases drove us crazy so we decided to build the solution.**

launches.title: Silverlake: The Java-native agentic AI operating system for enterprise
launches.tagline: Mapping agentic concepts onto established enterprise primitives
launches.body:
Hey YC! 

We're [Martin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marbit/) and [Andrey](https://www.linkedin.com/in/santrosyan/) from [Redouble AI](https://redouble.ai/). We have spent our entire careers in workflow automation in highly regulated industries - and just launched **the first agentic AI operating system for enterprise in Java**. 

Our launch video:

<https://youtu.be/p2sIjfsFbHE>

# ❌ **The Problem**

Every large company’s Board wants agentic AI deployed yesterday - but **the Java engineers in the enterprise who are supposed to deliver these AI solutions can’t just abandon their stack and security model and instead adopt paradigms that go against their most fundamental engineering principles**. Put differently: no enterprise Java engineer will ship production AI in Python - the cultural and engineering mismatch is too deep. In mission-critical workflows, you can’t rely on system prompts as “guardrails”, you can’t rely on only having rudimentary permission control, you can’t rely on data being moved outside of your premises. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101524&key=user_uploads/1897636/4022bdd2-26fd-4cf9-b327-9e88da4578e0)

# **✅ The solution**

That is why we developed **Silverlake**, a Java-native AI operating system that **maps every single agentic concept and concern onto an established enterprise primitive**. Think of Bitcoin: it was a new technology, it was scary, and there was absolutely no way a bank would move its deposits into Bitcoin. But then, we got Stablecoins - mapping the new technology onto the familiar primitive of the US Dollar. And now, trillions of dollars are routinely being moved in Stablecoins, and it’s part of everyday finance. We do the same thing for agentic AI, slotting it right into the enterprise comfort zone.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101524&key=user_uploads/1897636/416be4ec-9e0c-4079-b26c-2f3895d80ce1)

**For example**, agent identity is the existing identity layer, extended. Agent audit is the existing audit framework, extended. Same for orchestration, permissions, rate limiting, observability, fault tolerance. 

With Silverlake **we empower the 12 million Java engineers worldwide to develop and deploy agentic solutions for their companies in a code-first platform**. They define an agent in a few lines of code, and Silverlake takes care of everything else, giving Java engineers the same granular control over their AI as they have over any other production system.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101524&key=user_uploads/1897636/3b4e29b9-5650-49dd-8666-3af5c376785a)

In technical terms, **Silverlake offers**:

* **Deployment** in private cloud, managed cloud, on premise, hybrid or even air-gapped environments
* Seamless **connectivity** across the entire enterprise tech stack
* True Zero Trust, **security-first architecture** with RBAC+ABAC permissions
* **Deterministic guardrails** enforced in code, impervious to prompt manipulation
* **Resource management** across operations that differ by orders of magnitude (from milliseconds to minutes)
* **Hardware and token use optimization** enabling thousands of concurrent agents even on modest hardware
* **Incorruptible domain objects** enabling deep chains of specialized and long-running agents
* **Full audit trails** with complete job lineage and structured reasoning on every AI decision
* Continuously **learning from your experts while in production**

# **💡 Examples**

Silverlake has been **developed with design partners across biopharma, insurance and financial services**. For example, our agentic workflows write submission-ready Clinical Study Reports that are hundreds of pages long, analyze entire datarooms full of financial and operational data for private equity investors, and automate claims processing for a large insurance player, from extracting data from a faxed form to comparing against the policy in place and doing full coverage determination, benefits explanation, etc. The possibilities are endless. And as it’s all plain Java, every new deployment organically generates expansion within the organization - one engineering team automates a workflow, the team next door jumps on board, and it scales by itself from there.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101524&key=user_uploads/1897636/6520cdfc-89d5-4bff-94f3-604b2df11da2)

# **❓Why Java?**

**12 million Java engineers run the world's enterprise infrastructure**. Python is the language of data science - rightfully so - but production agentic systems have far more in common with enterprise software than with a Jupyter notebook. Same transaction management, same permission enforcement, same deployment pipelines, same monitoring - and Java has been solving these problems for 30 years. There are great Java AI frameworks out there, but none that tackle the production infrastructure challenges - resource orchestration, deterministic security, observability at scale. That's what we built with Silverlake.

# **👫 The team**

**We have spent our entire careers automating complex enterprise workflows**: [Martin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marbit/) (CEO) is a Rhodes scholar, Oxford PhD, and Wharton MBA turned serial entrepreneur who previously founded and scaled a pharma workflow automation company closing millions in enterprise deals; [Andrey](https://www.linkedin.com/in/santrosyan/) (CTO) has developed more than 120 enterprise software and AI applications in a 25 year career across large enterprise and several startups. We are backed by Y Combinator, Exponential, Transpose Platform, Tiny VC, and the Oxford Seed Fund and advised by Java inventor James Gosling and automation guru Professor Christian Terwiesch. 

We'd love your support - follow us, share us, work with us, or just say hi.

You can reach us at [founders@redouble.ai](mailto:founders@redouble.ai) and <https://redouble.ai>

[Book a Demo](https://calendly.com/d/cqhn-9ft-kzq/redouble-ai-demo)

launches.tagline: Deploy frontier AI models onto constrained edge hardware for robots, drones, and physical AI systems.
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR**: General Instinct distill, quantize, and deploy large frontier AI onto limited hardware on drones, old PCs, and robots.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101508&key=user_uploads/2022270/81b34033-67b0-41d9-9f7a-563ed2884da3)

**Problem**:

Physical AI (robots, drones, IoT) teams can now get frontier models to do impressive things in the lab. The hard part is getting those models to work reliably in production.

Some common patterns:

1\. Models works well in the cloud, but fails on edge in production.

2\. Custom use-cases like robots operating in the wild or in space requires on device inference.

3\. Using Gemini for everything is simply too expensive.

We built a custom, no code pipeline to solve this problem.

**What we’re building:**

Our first product: **Instinct Edge**. Give us a model, a target device, and a latency budget. We return an offline runtime that hits the budget on hardware like Jetson, mobile NPUs, ARM CPUs, Apple Neural Engine, and Snapdragons.

Under the hood, this combines compression recipes, custom CUDA / Metal / ARM NEON kernels, and a continuous data-to-serving pipeline.

One production example: a multimodal classifier on Jetson Orin NX with 111 ms cold start, 100% of decisions inside a 150 ms budget, and zero cloud calls.

**How you can help**:

If you or anyone you know are running large vision models on edge and are having problems fitting them onto your hardware, let us know by emailing [founders@general-instinct.com](mailto:founders@general-instinct.com)!

**TLDR**: Panacea hires elite FDA regulatory consultants, and pairs them with our AI platform, to deliver **the fastest and lowest-cost pathway to FDA approval** for Biotechs and MedTechs.

<https://youtu.be/w1rudmd3cio?si=ft-e2f7QL_dBPxyj>

### **About us**

We’re Haris and Yaman. We have deep experience within enterprise AI for healthcare.

Previously, we both worked at Anterior (backed by Sequoia, NEA, Microsoft AI’s CEO) — where we built, sold and deployed our clinical AI platform to US health plans to remove major operational bottlenecks.

[Haris](https://www.linkedin.com/in/haris-javed-akhtar/) (CEO) is an MD and led partnerships on Anterior’s GTM team (2nd GTM hire), selling to the biggest healthcare enterprises in the US and landed Anterior’s first health plan and partnership customers.

[Yaman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yaman-ziadeh/) (CTO) has an MS in AI was an AI Platform Engineer, building and deploying Anterior’s clinical AI platform.

Now we’re doing the same for Life Sciences. Only this time, we’re not selling the AI tools. We’re **owning the whole stack** and selling the outcome. Faster, better and at lower cost.

### **Problem**

Developing drugs and medical devices is complex and expensive (for drugs: 10-15 years, $1-2B).

The cost of drug development is growing exponentially (doubling every 9 years). This is known as Eroom’s Law (inverse Moore’s Law).

**The most critical** process in development is getting regulatory alignment, and ultimately, approval from the FDA.

Biotechs and medtechs outsource this work to regulatory consultants.

This work is highly manual: searching through legacy FDA databases, researching and reading hundreds of publications, reading FDA guidance documents, data analysis, authoring thousands of pages per filing, etc.

Consultants take months to years, and charge 6–7 figures per engagement, to deliver FDA regulatory strategy, authoring and submission services.

These consultants also price hourly. Therefore, using AI to go faster would cannibalize their revenue. So they have no incentive to deliver work faster.

### **What changed**

**AI can automate 90% of this work**. Consultants can now focus on the 10% where their expertise and judgement is actually needed.

### **Solution**

We hire the best FDA consultants in the industry (ex-FDA, decades of experience, hundreds of FDA filings).

We pair them with our AI platform to deliver higher quality FDA regulatory services **significantly** **faster and at lower cost.**

We also offer **fixed, milestone-based** pricing. Clients only pay once we deliver each agreed milestone.

### **Ask**

If you know any biotechs or medtechs that need FDA approval, please feel free to connect us at [haris@withpanacea.com](mailto:haris@withpanacea.com)! Also check out our website for more info: [www.withpanacea.com](http://www.withpanacea.com)

launches.title: Zibra Labs: HPC for Quant Trading Firms Running Backtesting at Scale
launches.tagline: HPC Clusters for Parallel Workloads on Spot-instances Across Hyperscalers and Neoclouds.
launches.body:
### Credentials

We’ve spent years working together building large scale distributed systems that run on hundreds of thousands of machines and serve billions of users. **Every time you leverage your network for a warm intro on LinkedIn, you use three databases that we’ve built: [Venice](https://venicedb.org/),[ Liquid](https://www.linkedin.com/blog/engineering/graph-systems/liquid-the-soul-of-a-new-graph-database-part-1), and[ Espresso](https://engineering.linkedin.com/teams/data/data-infrastructure/storage-infra/espresso).**

After LinkedIn, **we were tech-leads of [Ray](https://github.com/ray-project/ray)**, the leading open-source compute platform used by companies such as xAI, Cursor, Bridgewater, P72, Man Group, Two Sigma, and others. Ray has [\~12M](https://pypistats.org/packages/ray) weekly downloads and is part of the PyTorch Foundation.

### Product

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C6tl8Fr8t2I>

We’re building large scale high performance computing (HPC) clusters for **quantitative trading firms** to run **parallel simulation workloads such as backtesting.** 

The scale we’re targeting is

* 100 to 50,000 nodes of mixed hardware (CPUs and GPUs) on hyperscalers and neoclouds.
* up to 5,000,000 parallel tasks.
* spot instances for cheaper compute across multiple availability zones, hyperscalers, and neoclouds.
* < 50ms overhead for task dispatch and scheduling.
* run the compute in your cloud or on-prem environment to keep your alpha secure.

Our goal is to **make testing trading strategies fast, cheap, and reliable.** 

### Vision

We know that existing solutions do not handle this scale, do not have first-class support for spot-instances, and will not match our low-latency and high throughput performance. 

Our technology generalizes to other large-scale compute workloads such as

1. **post-training and reinforcement learning (RL)** for frontier and applied AI labs
2. **massively parallel robotics simulation and sim-to-real training** for robot foundation model teams
3. **virtual screening and molecular dynamics** for techbio and pharma R&D
4. **scientific simulation** (CFD, climate, seismic, FEA) for HPC teams looking to move beyond MPI and SLURM.

### Ask

Reach out if you

1. Are running simulation workloads that require lots of computation at a quant trading firm.
2. If you need HPC for a different use-case.
3. Want to grab a beer and talk about distributed systems or HPC.

Cheers!

Ibrahim and Zac

Hey everyone 👋

Prism is an AI-native recruiting agency. You brief us on a Slack channel. We source, engage, and screen the candidates. You step in to interview and make the offer. You pay 15% of first-year salary when someone we find signs.

The engine underneath is the best people search in the world. We score 89.6 on the Public Sourcing Benchmark. This puts us 21+ points ahead of every published baseline and the benchmark was built and published by one of our direct competitors.

**Ask:** Hiring, or know someone who is? Reply here, DM, or grab a slot: <https://cal.com/theokitsberg/30mins>

❌ **The Problem**

Hiring is a company killer. Founders spend a third of their time on it. Bad hires cost more than missed quarters. Good hires change companies.

And yet the work itself is brutal. Inbound is 95% noise. Outbound competes with everyone else's outbound. Agencies are slow, expensive, and opaque. Software dumps thousands of half-relevant profiles on your desk and walks away.

The hardest part of hiring isn't picking the tool. It's doing the work.

🛠️ **Our Solution: an AI-native agency, built on the best people search in the world**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101452&key=user_uploads/2051069/8aca8a76-91fb-41f6-9312-59e3c9e7e2af)

**Outreach that converts.** We engage candidates across LinkedIn, email, and WhatsApp, with messages calibrated to the role and the person.

**Scale agencies physically can't match.** We run dozens of searches in parallel today, every step instrumented. A traditional agency on a senior role has one human reading 20 profiles at a time. We read the whole web at once and use human time only where it actually matters.

**You brief us on Slack. We hand you a shortlist.** You handle the parts a founder should, which in our view are the interviews and the offer. Everything else is on us.

**Pricing:** $500 retainer to kick off a search. 15% of first-year salary when someone we find signs.

Theo & Axel

launches.title: mailX by mailwarm - Instant deliverability diagnostics for AI agents & humans.
launches.tagline: mailX tells you why emails go to spam and how to fix it, via web, API, and MCP.
launches.body:
Hey YC

I’m [Amine](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bengeekly/), CTO of Mailwarm (YC S20) and today we’re launching [mailX](https://themailx.com).\
[Thami](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thami-benjelloun/) is the CEO, [Othman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/othmankatim/) is our Head of deliverability and we are ready to help you with all your email deliverability problems.

We’ve been working on email deliverability since 2020. Mailwarm started as an email warmup tool and became [#1 Product of the Day](https://www.producthunt.com/products/mailwarm) on Product Hunt. Since then, we’ve helped thousands of teams improve sender reputation and inbox placement.

Today, we’re building a broader email deliverability ecosystem:

* **Mailwarm** helps teams build sender reputation through real inbox interactions.
* **mailX** helps humans and AI agents diagnose deliverability issues.
* **MailAdept** helps companies fix and monitor deliverability continuously with AI agents and human experts.

Today we’re launching [mailX](https://themailx.com).

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/422675/836ee2bb-f82d-4b97-9c90-c77c6d0d62f0)

---

## TL;DR

**mailX tells you why your emails go to spam and how to fix it.**\
You can run a deliverability check from the web, use it through a JSON API, or plug it directly into AI agents through MCP.

No signup.\
No API key.\
Free to use.

Try it here: [**https://themailx.com**](https://themailx.com)\
MCP endpoint: [**https://themailx.com/mcp**](https://themailx.com/mcp)

---

You can also book a call with one of our email deliverability expert [HERE](https://calendly.com/mailwarmsessions/mailx).

## 🚨 The Problem

Email deliverability is technical, your marketing team can’t handle it.

Email is still one of the most important growth channels for startups.

Founders use it for cold outreach.\
Sales teams use it for outbound.\
Marketing teams use it for campaigns.\
Products use it for onboarding, activation, and transactional emails.

But when emails start going to spam, most teams don’t really know why.

They check random tools.\
They look at raw DNS records.\
They ask ChatGPT.\
They change things blindly.\
They wait and hope inbox placement improves.

The problem is not only that deliverability is technical.

The real problem is that most tools show data, but don’t explain what matters or what to fix.

And now, with AI agents sending emails, monitoring systems, and managing workflows, this problem gets bigger.

Agents need access to live deliverability tools too.

---

## 💡Our Solution

**mailX is a free deliverability diagnostic platform for humans and AI agents.**

With mailX, you can analyze a domain in seconds and get a clear report showing:

* What is working
* What is broken
* Why it matters
* What to fix next

The web app gives founders, marketers, sales teams, and developers a simple way to understand why emails may go to spam.

The API and MCP server make the same tools available to AI agents and developer workflows.

So instead of copying DNS records into different tools, your agent can directly check email authentication, blacklist status, mail server configuration, and deliverability signals.

---

## ⏳How it works

1. Enter a domain on [**themailx.com**](http://themailx.com)
2. mailX runs a live deliverability audit
3. You get clear issues, explanations, and fixes
4. Developers can use the JSON API
5. AI agents can use the MCP endpoint directly

The best part is that you can lets you AI Agent fix your deliverability or directly integrate it to your Claude or ChatGPT.

Here’s a quick demo of mailX:\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YWmV7-wthQI>

In the demo, we show:

* Running a domain audit
* Getting clear fixes
* Using the MCP/API layer for AI agents and developers

We currently support checks and tools for email authentication, DNS records, blacklist status, mail server configuration, and record generation.

---

## Why now?

Email deliverability used to be something only email experts cared about.

Today, every startup relying on outbound, lifecycle emails, AI SDRs, or automated email workflows needs to understand it.

At the same time, AI agents are becoming part of the stack.

But agents need tools.\
They need live data.\
They need safe, structured ways to diagnose and act.

That’s why we made mailX available through:

* Web app
* JSON API
* MCP server
* Agent skill
* LLM discovery endpoints

Our belief is simple:

**Email deliverability should be understandable for humans and usable by AI agents.**

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/422675/ffc97aad-6864-4525-a89d-0aa1f7890289)

---

## Backstory

In 2019, we failed a startup after 2 years of work.

After that, we decided to test ideas much faster: one launch per week.

Every launch used the same growth channel: email.

Cold emails.\
Partnership emails.\
Launch emails.\
Follow-ups.

That’s when we understood something obvious: If your emails don’t land in the inbox, nothing else matters.

That led us to build Mailwarm in 2020.

After years helping thousands of teams improve deliverability, we kept seeing the same pattern: People don’t know why they land in spam.\
And even when they see the data, they don’t know what to fix.

mailX is our answer to that.

---

---

## 🙏 Our Ask

We’d love your feedback from the YC community.

If you are doing cold email, email marketing, transactional email, or building AI agents that send or monitor emails, try mailX and tell us what is missing.

Also, if you are building an AI agent or workflow where email deliverability matters, we’d love to talk.

Try mailX: [**https://themailx.com**](https://themailx.com)\
Book a call through MailAdept if you want help choosing the right setup: [https://calendly.com/mailwarmsessions/mailx](https://calendly.com/mailwarmsessions/mailx?month=2026-05)

launches.title: InsForge: The backend platform for AI-native developers
launches.tagline: Let your coding agent deploy, operate, and debug your backend end-to-end
launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re [Hang Huang](https://linkedin.com/in/hang-huang-oliver) and [Tony Chang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tony-chang-0430/) from [InsForge](https://insforge.dev/).

**TL;DR:** InsForge lets your AI coding agent deploy and operate the full backend (servers, database, auth, storage, and more) from one consistent CLI. Instead of stitching together separate tools and dashboards, your agent manage entire backend infrastructure end-to-end.

<https://youtu.be/7Bax5qz0IfM>

**The Problem**

The way software gets built is changing fast. Coding agents are now the primary builders, but every backend platform today was designed for human developers, with dashboards, manual configs, and workflows that require a person at every step.

We tried MCP servers like Supabase, Vercel, GitHub, and Context7, but kept running into the same problems: tools bloated the context window, payloads came back at 10K+ tokens, and core backend state like telemetry, configs, logs, and runtime behavior still wasn’t accessible in a way agents could reliably use.

**Our Solution**

So we built InsForge as one backend platform your coding agent can actually operate. Install our CLI and Skills with one command, and your coding agent can build, run, debug, and scale full-stack apps end to end on InsForge.

Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors the agent can act on. And because agents make mistakes, branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes let you review or discard changes safely.

**Where We're Going**

We believe that coding agents won’t stop at writing code. They’ll run your entire application and infrastructure autonomously as well. For that to work, backend infrastructure needs to become agent-native: CLI-first, observable, permissioned, reversible, and designed around agents as operators.

**About Us**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101500&key=user_uploads/967495/90d7cdcf-0682-408c-bf3c-c5f192edf89b)

* **Hang (CEO)** — ex-Amazon PM, previously professional League of Legends player.
* **Tony (CTO)** — ex-Databricks network infrastructure engineer.

**Our Ask**

1. **Try it and break it**: [**insforge.dev**](http://insforge.dev). If you found there’s anything missing or you think some features are poorly designed, let us know! We read every piece of feedback. We’re also open source, here’s our [**GitHub repo**](https://github.com/InsForge/InsForge).
2. **Design partners**: if you want your coding agent to handle everything, and believe that’s the future, drop a comment or email [**founders@insforge.dev**](mailto:hang.huang@insforge.dev). We'll get you set up directly.
3. **Intros:** we're a day-0 infra company, so we need to find top developers before they get locked in elsewhere. If you know any developers or founders just / about to get started, we’d love an intro!

launches.tagline: Measurement, localization and tracking of freight in warehouses using only pre-installed CCTV
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** 

* Trucking companies lose billions because they don't know the actual size of the items on their trucks 
* We measure every shipment using the existing warehouse security cameras – no new hardware or process changes

<https://youtu.be/4ZGgDSRsALo>

**Problem:** Over 2 million irregular items move across the US in trucks every day. Trucking companies charge based on how big each item is but rely on the sender to tell them. Senders often guess wrong or lowball, costing trucking companies revenue and truck space.

**Solution:** We use the CCTV cameras already installed in the warehouse against theft and claims to measure items with computer vision. In the future we track shipment status, location and evidence for claims across the supply chain.

launches.tagline: AI Agents handling every call, email, and booking for restaurants.
launches.body:
\
**Elyra is the AI reservation system for restaurants.**

We’re building AI agents that answer every phone call and email instantly, connected to a reservation system that optimizes table placements in real time. Already powering top restaurant groups.

[**https://youtu.be/dqK4bC1eBVM**](https://youtu.be/dqK4bC1eBVM)

[Book a demo →](https://www.elyrasystems.com/demo)

**The Problem**

Imagine running a store where 4 out of every 10 customers walk up, find the door locked, and leave.

That's how restaurants operate today.

40% of incoming phone calls go unanswered. Emails sit for days. This leads to high-value bookings getting lost: large groups, private events, special occasions, corporate dinners. The bookings that fill slow Tuesday nights and turn an average month into a great one.

Restaurants run on thin margins and one missed call can mean a €2,000 group booking lost to a competitor. Over a year, the average mid-sized restaurant leaves more than $100,000 on the table simply because no one answered in time.

Yet the entire industry still relies on waiters manually handling calls and emails during service. Staff get overwhelmed, emails get buried, and the reservation systems on the market do nothing to fix it. They're glorified calendars.

**The Solution**

Elyra is the AI reservation system for restaurants. Three things, working together:

* **Voice agent:** Answers every phone call. Handles all reservations, modifications, and questions about the menu, dietary requirements, and policies.
* **Email concierge:** Replies to every email instantly, in the restaurant’s tone of voice. Large groups, special requests, and follow-ups handled.
* **Smart table allocation:** Fit more guests in the restaurant. Optimizes table placements in real time while placing guests at the tables that fit them best.

Every call, email, and booking becomes a data point that makes the next visit better, turning first-time guests into regulars.

**Why It Matters**

Here's what our users say:

_"Some regulars thought we hired a new waiter."_

_"We made back a year's cost in two weeks."_

_"Aha, this is what AI should feel like."_

Waiters can finally focus on the guests in front of them instead of a ringing phone. Managers see the bookings they used to lose close automatically. Owners get empty tables filled, margins back, and guests returning.

Elyra is already live across multiple restaurant groups, with new venues seeing record occupancy within weeks of launch.

**The Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/2444964/31471be3-73f3-43ef-bf57-565b801d42cc)

Elyra was founded by **Felix Odeberg Glasenapp** and **Alan Mando**, who met in primary school in Stockholm and have been building things together ever since. Felix studied Engineering Physics at KTH. Alan studied Business at WU Vienna.

To build Elyra, the founders spent weeks inside restaurants, taking phone calls, standing at the waiters stand, and watching service unfold. Every product decision came from that.

launches.body:
AI agents are becoming incredibly capable online, but the moment you need one to make a phone call or send a text, everything falls apart. You end up stitching together telecom providers, voice infrastructure, compliance, routing, and your own memory layer. Giving an agent a phone number should be simple. It wasn't.

So we built [AgentPhone](http://agentphone.ai/): the telephony infrastructure layer for AI agents.\
\

launches.title: PerfectBit: AI Training data, correct by construction
launches.tagline: Specialized data for the world's most powerful models.
launches.body:
# **TL;DR**

_PerfectBit creates high-quality training data that's correct by construction. We verify against physics simulators, scientific databases, formal proof systems. It's what models need to cure hallucination, close common-sense gaps, and reach superintelligence. Reinforcement Learning from Verified Rewards (RLVR) was an early step in this direction. We go further. LLMs, robotics, AI for Science, and more._

<https://youtu.be/RrFKfbO6XlY>

# **The problem: the failures standing between today's models and superintelligence**

Frontier labs are bottlenecked on four data problems:

* **Hallucination.** Models trained on noisy web scrapes produce confident, fluent statements that are wrong.
* **Common-sense failure.** Models that solve graduate-level math still trip on trivial problems for a five-year-old.
* **Information scarcity.** Scientific facts, formal derivations, peer-reviewed findings — they're a thin minority of tokens in any open-web scrape, drowned out by orders of magnitude of recipes, marketing copy, forum chatter, and AI-generated slop. Scaling the scrape doesn't change the ratio.
* **Human annotation doesn't scale.** It's slow, expensive, and capped at human ability — superintelligence won't come from labeling at human throughput.

# **What we do**

* PerfectBit creates high-quality training data that's correct by construction. Every sample is generated against an oracle — physics simulator, scientific database, formal proof system — and verified before it ships, in text, code, image, audio, or video. For LLMs, we project observations about the world into natural language; for verticals like robotics and AI-for-science, we ship purpose-built datasets.

# **Why us**

We've trained the models we're now building data for.

* **Peter Vajda** — Former **Director of Media Generation at Meta**. Eleven years at Meta. Most recently led Media GenAI foundation-model R&D: **Emu** (text-to-image), image editing, **Movie Gen**, text-to-video, video editing, character-consistent generation. Earlier led efficient deep learning for computer vision powering on-device Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality (AR/VR) models. **Assistant Visiting Professor at Stanford** before Meta. PhD in Computer Science.
* **Seiji Yamamoto** — Led teams in the **Core Llama group at Meta Superintelligence Labs**. Nine years at Meta as a **Senior Staff Research Scientist** across LLM pre- and post-training, inference optimization, full-duplex speech, and computer vision. **PhD in Physics**, publications in **Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences** and **Physical Review Letters** (co-authored with a Fields Medalist). Stanford, Rice, Columbia; postdoc at a National Lab.

Between us: foundation-model training across text, image, video, and speech, shipped to billions of users — plus scientific chops to design the verifier stacks.

# **We’d love to talk more**

We're talking to a small number of frontier AI labs about pilot engagements.

* **Heads of data / data partnerships** at frontier labs
* **Research leads** running pre-training, mid-training, post-training, or reasoning programs and shopping for a corpus that doesn't exist yet
* **Model-training teams** preparing a next-gen training run who want a correct-by-construction supplement in the mix
* **Researchers in formal methods, scientific computing, or domain-specific simulators** who want to contribute a verifier stack — we'd love to talk

We're also **hiring research scientists and engineers in San Francisco** (in-person). If you've shipped foundation-model training, built formal/simulation tooling or spent time developing AI training data at production scale, please reach out.

# **Contact**

* **Web:** [**https://perfectbit.ai**](https://perfectbit.ai)
* **Email:** [**founders@perfectbit.ai**](mailto:founders@perfectbit.ai)
* **Founders:** Peter Vajda, Seiji Yamamoto

For decades, high-quality visual storytelling was a privilege reserved for Hollywood. To create an original film or TV series, creators needed months of pitching, millions of dollars in funding, a massive production team, and approval from traditional gatekeepers.

AI has completely shattered this barrier. Today, anyone with a great idea can generate cinematic worlds right from their laptop. But this democratization has exposed a massive new gap: AI storytellers have the tools to make a film, but no system to fund it or make a living.

Independent creators simply don't have the upfront capital to fund this.
2. Zero IP Monetization: Even if they manage to produce the content, there is no dedicated monetization ecosystem. Creators are forced to rely on YouTube or TikTok ad algorithms, which reward short-form viral clips rather than premium, long-form storytelling. They have no way to build a brand, sell private content, or capture the true value of their IP.

**Our Solution**

YouArt bridges this gap. We are replacing the traditional Hollywood pipeline with YouArt.

launches.title: Astraea - Agents Accelerating clinical trials.
launches.tagline: Astraea is an agentic platform that automates clinical trial data analysis and statistical programming, from raw study data to CDISC-compliant datasets, TFLs, and FDA-ready outputs.
launches.body:
# **TL;DR**

Clinical trial analysis is still shockingly manual.

After a study collects data, teams spend months converting raw clinical data into SDTM, ADaM, TFLs, and submission-ready packages. This work is slow, expensive, and error-prone.

Astraea is a platform that completely automates the end-to-end biometrics pipeline from just a protocol and the raw data to a submission ready output. We are starting with oncology and rare disease studies, where analysis complexity is high and every month saved matters.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101307&key=user_uploads/3227004/b76b7415-1d15-4060-9cbd-22e974712bb0)

**The Problem**

Today, sponsors and CROs still rely on large teams of statistical programmers, biostatisticians, and data managers to manually transform messy clinical data into regulatory outputs.

A single study can require:

1. Raw data cleaning and reconciliation
2. SDTM mapping
3. ADaM dataset creation
4. TFL shell generation
5. Statistical programming
6. QC and validation
7. Regulatory formatting and traceability

From our customer conversations, this can take around 9 months with teams of 5-10 people communicating asynchronously. And the process is still full of Word docs, Excel specs, SAS programs, manual handoffs, version-control issues, and repeated QC cycles.

Ultimately, this means slower decisions, delayed filings, higher CRO spend, and less control over the most important data in the company.

## **Our Solution**

We built the first AI native platform for clinical trial biometrics.

Astraea takes study inputs and automatically generates the datasets, analysis specs, statistical code, and outputs required for regulatory review.

The pipeline:

1. Ingest raw clinical data, protocol, and study metadata
2. Generate TFL shells, SAP, eCRF from the protocol and study design
3. Generate CDISC-compliant SDTM datasets
4. Generate ADaM datasets and analysis-ready variables
5. Produce tables, figures, listings, and traceable statistical programs
6. Run QC checks and generate FDA-ready outputs

We are the first to actually completely automate workflows across SDTM, ADaM, TFL generation, Pinnacle 21 checks, and specification creation.

For ongoing studies, we have compressed work that normally takes months into days.

## **Why Now**

Clinical trials are becoming more complex, but the tools have not improved in the last 20 years (something an actual customer said). At the same time, AI models can finally reason across protocols, SAPs, data dictionaries, clinical datasets, and regulatory standards.

That unlocks something new: biometrics workflows that are not just assisted by software, but executed by agents.

Astraea is not replacing scientific judgment. We are automating the manual programming and data wrangling that slows teams down, while keeping humans in the loop for review, validation, and regulatory decisions.

## **Our Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101307&key=user_uploads/3227004/13d628c7-5571-42b0-960a-1b7246effa4c)

\*\*Joshua Wang: Co-founder, CEO\
\*\* Stanford, math/CS. Built multi-agent AI systems and clinical data automation workflows. Previously worked on production AI systems for enterprise customers.

\*\*Sanmay Sarada: Co-founder, CTO\
\*\* Stanford CS. Built clinical and hospital data infrastructure across diagnostic software systems. Focused on regulated healthcare workflows and data pipelines.

We started Astraea because people close to us in pharma kept describing the same bottleneck: clinical trial analysis was too manual, too slow, and too dependent on fragmented CRO workflows.

So we built the automation layer we wished existed.

Find us at [**founders@tryastraea.com**](mailto:founders@tryastraea.com)

<https://tryastraea.com/>

launches.title: Sanifu: Automate the repetitive work spreadsheets are used for
launches.tagline: Describe your repetitive and manual work you currently do in spreadsheets and Sanifu turns them into autonomous data apps that run the same way every time.
launches.body:
Sanifu automates the repetitive work spreadsheets are used for. Teams across finance, revenue, and operations simply describe their repetitive work like cleaning and validating data, matching records and moving data across systems. Sanifu captures the steps, rules and outputs and runs it automatically and reliably every time.

This significantly reduces time spent on copy-paste work, spreadsheet cleanup, and manual entries and checking, while improving accuracy, consistency, and operational visibility. Sanifu helps teams scale critical back-office processes without relying on brittle spreadsheets, scripts, or general AI tools that reinvent the logic every run.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9I1BvbW3n6Y>

### **The problem**

Analysts and teams in finance, revenue, and operations spend a huge part of their day doing manual data work. Cleaning data, preparing reports, moving things across systems, tracking work. It's repetitive, boring, and takes time away from the parts of their job that actually matter. The same work gets done repeatedly because their data is scattered across systems, emails, PDFs, and files. Only a few people know the rules and exceptions. When they leave, the process breaks.

Existing tools don't solve the whole problem. Spreadsheets, macros, and scripts are brittle and hard to maintain. General AI tools can help, but they reinvent the logic on every run, so outputs need constant checking and can't be trusted for critical workflows.

### **How Sanifu solves this**

Anyone can turn their manual data work into an autonomous data app—just by describing it.

1.⁠ ⁠You describe the process.

In plain English, you walk Sanifu through what you do. It asks the right questions, handles edge cases, understands your rules, and works with your real data (files, emails, systems) to define the full workflow.

2.⁠ ⁠Sanifu runs it with you.

It executes the process end-to-end, showing real-time progress and outputs. You review results, make changes, and refine the workflow until it matches exactly what you expect.

3.⁠ ⁠It becomes a reliable operations platform.

Once approved, Sanifu saves the entire process and turns it into a data app. All future runs replay the exact steps whereby the same input plus same context equals same output. It’s more than a workflow tool: built-in data stores, dashboards, forms, integrations, scheduled and event triggers as well as audit trails.

Sanifu is a full operational platform with 5k+ app integrations, 1k+ native components, forms, scheduler, data stores, dashboards, approvals, reviews, AI-powered entity matching among many  other features that make it an end-to-end data app management platform.

Some of the fastest growing teams in various industries are already using Sanifu to save their team’s hundreds of hours per day of manual data handling.

**Asks**

If you run a SaaS, finance, ops, or sales team and you have a workflow that involves cleaning, matching, moving data across systems or manual reporting, please reach out. We'll build your first data app with you, free, in exchange for honest feedback.

launches.title: Adialante: We're going to screen the world for cancer!
launches.tagline: Our second patent just issued, a new way to make MRI.
launches.body:
**TLDR**: Adialante builds compact and mobile whole-body MRIs. We already have $12.75M in LOIs, $30k in deposits, and our first system will be scanning by demo day.

---

##### **About Us:**

<https://youtu.be/iiRwpHPFIeM>\
\
"Disruptive Innovation describes a process by which a product or service takes root in simple applications at the bottom of the market — typically by being less expensive and more accessible — and then relentlessly moves upmarket, eventually displacing established competitors." — Christensen Institute

We’re [@Efrain Torres](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1230366) and [@Parker Jenkins](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1298954), the co-founders of [@Adialante](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/31434). We met on the first floor of our engineering dorm. And when we learned what disruptive innovation was, it captured us immediately. But what to disrupt? Trained as biomedical engineers, we both learned about MRI and were in awe of the clinical value. It can diagnose cancers, strokes, dementia, and more. Yet everyone said the same thing: MRI is not accessible.

So we knew what we had to do: disrupt the industry.

Over the past six years, we've invented new ways to do MRI, won millions in competitive grants, published research, secured patents (#12,625,209, #12,372,595, more to come), and built a team. And, now, we’re well on our way to disrupting the industry.

##### **Problem:**

We know how to 10x cancer outcomes: **you catch it early**. MRI is the most powerful cancer-detection tool in the world, yet systems cost millions to purchase, take months to install, and require high levels of technical skill. The result? We only use MRI when it's too late.

##### **Our solution:**

We've redesigned MRI from the ground up with new physics, algorithms, and hardware, all to bring cancer screening to all of us. Our MRIs:

* use 50% less hardware
* are 40% shorter and 80% lighter
* are whisper-quiet and much less claustrophobic
* and require no specialized infrastructure

All while maintaining the diagnostic quality patients need.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101289&key=user_uploads/1230366/e7c9bf11-8868-457b-aced-78bd369559f5)

But like Waymo, we won't sell our hardware — we'll own and operate it. We'll bring our MRIs to clinics in mobile trailers, handle its operations, and continuously improve our AI software after every scan. We're an imaging clinic on wheels. So instead of a clinic waiting months and paying millions, clinics will wait hours and pay hundreds.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101289&key=user_uploads/1230366/31ce218b-56df-4fc3-9450-5af5eea83895)

---

We're starting with prostate cancer. **Over 1M men every year require an MRI before a prostate biopsy, but virtually none of the urology clinics that treat them can offer one.**

After our per-scan fee, a clinic will collect the insurance reimbursement and make a profit. It's a win-win-win: we get the recurring revenue, they get a new revenue stream, and patients get the best imaging technology in the world. From there, the same piece of hardware expands to renal, breast, and brain scanning **until annual screening for high-risk cancers is the norm, not the exception.**

**Traction:**

* 6 clinics signed up
* $12.75M in LOIs for scanner utilization
* $30k deposited from a top ten urology clinic to reserve their spot in line
* MRI assembled

  ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101289&key=user_uploads/1230366/1fa5afed-cb5b-4f8d-a3f0-46a430043c0e)


##### **Asks:**

Intros to Urology clinics

Want to see our scanner? Shoot us a message! We’ll show you our system in person!

AI has radically transformed coding. But in finance, super-sharp, highly-paid people are spending 2026 combing through an inbox full of PDFs, updating models in Excel, and eyeballing Bloomberg charts. Multiplier packages everything necessary to change that! It includes secure inference endpoints, changelogs, ontology maintainance, guardrails, and VM infrastructure, and it's all hosted on client servers. launches.title: dari.dev - The easiest way to deploy your agents to production
launches.tagline: Get a versioned, stateful API for your long-running agent in 5 minutes
launches.body:
Point our CLI at your agent project, run `dari deploy`and get a production-ready agent API.

<https://youtu.be/Y6CdktXcF24>

## What it is

[dari.dev](http://dari.dev) turns an agent project into a **versioned, stateful API endpoint**. We’re building on top of the best open-source harnesses starting with **Pi**. Support coming soon for **Hermes** Agent. Book a call to deploy your proprietary harness.

### How it works:

* Drop a dari.yml + tools + skills at your repo root
* “dari deploy .” uploads a snapshot and publishes a new version behind a stable agent URL
* Clients open a **durable session** and stream multimodal events (text, files, images)
* The platform runs the harness, spins up a sandbox workspace per session, and handles logs, retries, and credentials
* New publishes create new versions. In-flight sessions stay pinned to the version they started on

## The problem:

If you're building an agent right now, you're probably:

* Stitching together durable execution + a sandbox provider + Postgres + a secret store yourself
* Losing state when a turn crashes mid-execution
* Shipping “agents” that can’t survive a 30-minute task
* Rebuilding the same infra (auth, retries, workspace, logs) on every project

Most agents break mid-task.

## With [dari.dev](http://dari.dev):

* **Durable sessions:** Long-running tasks survive crashes, restarts, and redeploys. Resume from the same session_id days/months/years later.
* **Versioned deploys:** Every publish is a new version behind one stable URL. Roll forward without breaking live sessions.
* **Bring your own sandbox:** Sandboxes run under your provider account and API key. You control limits and data. E2B today, Daytona / Blaxel / Modal coming soon.
* **BYOK with OpenRouter / any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint:** Use your own key, pick your model, control spend, keep logs.
* **Custom tools**: Drop Python or TypeScript tools under tools/<name>/. We run them with retry policies you define.

**The API:**

Publish once. Then, create a session and send messages + stream responses.

We provide full observability, session-level event logs, per-turn state, and workspace file outputs attached to the session lifecycle.

## Why we built this

We started building browser automation agents and kept hitting the same missing primitive, a durable control plane underneath.

We built it for ourselves, then realized every other team shipping agents (coding, research, ops) is rebuilding the same layer.

If you’ve wired together durable execution + a sandbox provider + Postgres + a secret store just to run one agent in prod, this is for you.

## Get access

* App: [app.dari.dev](http://app.dari.dev), docs: [docs.dari.dev](http://docs.dari.dev)
* Install the CLI, run `dari auth login`then publish from your repo
* Pricing: Either you pay your providers directly (E2B + OpenRouter/OpenAI) or use our managed Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter offerings. No markup from us initially.

Book a call: calendly.com/avyay-dari/30min or email me at [avyay@dari.dev](mailto:avyay@dari.dev).

launches.title: Hopper - Agentic Development Environment for Mainframe/COBOL
launches.tagline: It combines a real TN3270 terminal and an AI agent that can operate across z/OS workflows like COBOL, VSAM, and CICS.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We’re launching **Hopper**, an agentic development environment for IBM mainframes. It combines a real TN3270 terminal and an AI agent that can operate across z/OS workflows like COBOL, VSAM, and CICS.

Download it here: <https://www.hypercubic.ai/hopper>

Video walkthrough: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q81L5DcfBvE>

You can also request access and immediately get a mainframe user account to try it.

## **Problem**

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/317991/43b88f08-689e-437f-9057-42a45c15eb56)

Mainframes still run a huge amount of critical infrastructure: banking, payments, insurance, airlines, government programs, logistics, and core enterprise operations.

A lot of that software is written in COBOL and runs on IBM z/OS. These systems are reliable, secure, and deeply embedded into business operations, but the development environment looks nothing like modern software development.

Modern AI coding tools assume repos, files, shells, package managers, test runners, and CI pipelines.

Mainframe development is an entirely different computing paradigm.

A simple COBOL change might require finding the right source member, checking copybooks, locating compile JCL, submitting a job, reading JES/SYSPRINT output, interpreting condition codes, patching fixed-width source, and resubmitting.

Much of this work is structured and repetitive, but today it still depends heavily on expert humans who know how to navigate the terminal, interpret output, and follow local conventions.

A chatbot next to a terminal is not enough.

For AI to be useful here, the agent needs to operate inside the mainframe environment itself.

## **Solution**

Today we’re launching **Hopper**, an agentic development environment for mainframes.

Hopper combines three things:

1. A real TN3270 terminal
2. Mainframe-aware panels for datasets, members, jobs, and spool output
3. An AI agent that can operate across z/OS workflows

The agent can navigate ISPF, inspect datasets, write and edit COBOL, generate and modify JCL, submit jobs, parse JES spool output, analyze return codes, query VSAM, interact with CICS, and explain failures.

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/317991/2c056d32-2347-4dd9-9b53-697349527628)


## **Why this matters**

The mainframe is not just a codebase. It is an operating environment with its own workflows, conventions, interfaces, and failure modes.

Most AI coding tools treat legacy systems like static repositories. That misses a huge part of the real work.

In mainframe environments, the important context often lives across terminal screens, datasets, job output, copybooks, CICS regions, VSAM files, scheduler conventions, and decades of operational knowledge.

Hopper’s design principle is simple:

Preserve the fidelity of the mainframe environment, but make it accessible to AI agents.

Once agents can safely operate inside the mainframe, new workflows become possible:

* Faster job debugging
* Automated documentation
* Safer COBOL changes
* Test generation
* Migration planning

We think this is the missing layer between today’s AI coding tools and the mission-critical systems that still run much of the world.

## **Who we are**

We’re Sai and Aayush, former Apple AIML engineers, and we’re building Hypercubic to bring AI-native maintenance and modernization infrastructure to mainframe and COBOL systems.

### **🤝 What we’re looking for**

* **Intros:** Connections to CIOs, CTOs, VPs of Engineering, or Heads of Modernization at Fortune 500 companies, particularly in banking, insurance, manufacturing and retail.
* **Enterprises** running COBOL or mainframe workloads exploring modernization or knowledge retention.
* **Systems integrators / consultancies** seeking AI-powered tooling for mainframe understanding and modernization.
