launches.title: Salus - Runtime guardrails that validate AI agent actions before they execute
launches.tagline: Salus checks your agent's actions, blocking incorrect ones and providing feedback to guide retries
launches.body:
### **TL;DR:**

**Salus is an API that wraps around your agent and checks its actions at runtime, blocking incorrect ones and providing immediate feedback to guide retries.**

We’re Kevin and Vedant, former roommates at Stanford who studied CS, now building Salus full-time.

### 😔**The problem:** 

Your agent processed a refund without looking up the order, costing you thousands. It emailed your top lead using hallucinated data, ruining the deal. You only found out three hours later from a support ticket or an angry email.

Evals, output scoring, and observability are all necessary—but all reactive. They can reduce the likelihood of these problems occurring, but there's no solution that inspects an action as it’s about to execute. Salus does that.

**Ask:** If you are deploying agents and want to improve their correctness we’d love to help. Book a demo [here](https://calendly.com/d/cycy-fbc-fyj/salus-demo), and we can onboard you immediately with just a pip install and a few lines of code.

### 💻 **Our Solution:** 

<https://youtu.be/uyl5NJTY5Cg>

**How Salus validates an action:**

1. Actions must be **grounded in evidence**: Salus maintains an evidence cache for each run that every proposed action is validated against. Evidence includes all outputs from prior tool calls and the entire conversation history.
2. It must **adhere to policy**: Write constraints in YAML, markdown, or plain English. Salus compiles them into runtime checks that are version-controlled, diffable, and shadow-testable
3. And **more**: PII detection, budget/loop protection, idempotency, human-in-the-loop escalation, content moderation

**Self-repairing:** When Salus blocks an action, the agent receives structured feedback to guide a retry. In our benchmarks, **58%** of blocked actions recover and complete the task correctly.

### 📊 **Benchmarks:** 

We tested Salus on τ²-bench and ODCV-Bench. On τ²-bench, agents with Salus follow policies more reliably, at up to **60% lower cost**. On ODCV-Bench, Salus **reduced misalignment by 52%** on average across 12 frontier models (see below).

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/1940292/e48b27f6-2e13-4d40-a9a4-13135ff981bc)

### ➕ **Other Features:** 

While we believe the missing piece is runtime validation, we know **evals and observability** are crucial. That’s why we incorporate all three in **one centralized product**. Using templates and LLMs, we generate thousands of both adversarial and realistic evals that have full context of your agent’s domain.

Contact us: [founders@usesalus.ai](https://founders@usesalus.ai)

* Built to be used between site visits, calls, and active builds

launches.title: Ditto Bio – Evolutionary therapies for autoimmune disease
launches.tagline: We discover new drugs by harnessing parasite biology
launches.body:
We're [Adair Borges](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adair-borges-phd-729857222/), [Dennis Sun](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dennis-a-sun/), and [Emily Weiss](https://www.linkedin.com/in/emily-weiss-phd-939559124/), the founders of [Ditto Bio](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/ditto-biosciences).

**We believe the world's best immunologists live inside of you.** 

TLDR; We transform parasite strategies for hacking the immune system into breakthrough drugs for autoimmune disease.

Viruses, ticks, and worms are the natural enemies of the human immune system. Over millions of years of experimentation, they've developed extraordinarily effective molecules to prevent your immune system from attacking them. This makes their proteins ideal drug candidates for autoimmune diseases, where a hyperactive immune system attacks the body's own tissues. We're mining the genomes of these organisms to translate these naturally occurring drugs into novel therapies.\
\
<https://youtu.be/4QFngdirw58>

**The Problem**

90% of drugs fail in clinical trials, when they are tested in humans for the first time. These failures come after companies invest 3-5 years and $15-20M “derisking” drugs in cells and mice. Everyone knows that cells and mice aren’t people, but without a smarter strategy, billions of dollars will continue to be wasted making drugs that will never reach patients.

**Our Approach**

We start with molecules that _already work_ in humans. Parasites have been running experiments on people for millions of years, creating powerful molecules to control the human immune system. Our AI platform identifies drug-like proteins from these organisms at scale, which we then engineer into safe, effective therapeutics.

**The Best Drugs Come from Nature**

Aspirin, penicillin, Botox, and GLP-1 agonists like Ozempic and Wegovy all originated as molecules from other organisms: aspirin from willow bark, penicillin from mold, and GLP-1 agonists from Gila monster venom. We're establishing parasites as the next transformative source of therapeutics.

**Our Team**

We’re three PhD scientists trained at top institutions (Harvard, Berkeley, UCSF, UCSD) with 40+ years of experience in computational biology, host-parasite interactions, and evolution. We worked together for 3 years as early scientists at another startup before founding Ditto.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97563&key=user_uploads/2915094/304ef78d-d58a-499d-9ada-63096be7fb40)

**Our Data Moat**

Since founding seven months ago, we've analyzed 1M+ proteins across primate-infecting viruses, ticks, and parasitic worms. We've discovered thousands of proteins predicted to hit clinically validated human targets. Early experiments show that we have surfaced an untapped source of new drugs that act on high-value targets for immune diseases. Our proteins can achieve extremely tight binding (1–2 nM), among other drug-like properties.

We’re also building a tissue biobank that lets us map real-world immune memory to parasite proteins. This approach gives us a major advantage in tackling one of the biggest barriers facing all novel protein therapeutics: predicting and designing around immunogenicity.

The opportunity is vast: >98% of viral and parasite proteins remain uncharacterized. We're systematically mining this unexplored biology at scale to find and deploy nature’s best drugs.

**Our Ask**

If you’re an industry immunologist, biologics drug developer, or protein designer, please reach out at [founders@dittobio.com](mailto:founders@dittobio.com) to learn where our novel targets, natural scaffolds, and immunogenicity assays could make a difference for your drug programs.

Hi Everyone! 

We’re **Drake, Kent, and Esteban**, co-founders of [**Maywood**](https://maywoodai.com/). 

# **TL;DR** 

**Maywood automates deal execution for investment banks, from decks to diligence.**

Banks do not lose deals because of bad judgment. They lose time to repetitive work, fragmented information, and processes that do not scale with deal volume. 

Maywood removes execution bottlenecks so that deal teams can focus on judgment rather than mechanics. 

 

[**https://youtu.be/OCgXCora2OQ**](https://youtu.be/OCgXCora2OQ) 

# **The M&A Process Doesn’t Scale** 

There was $5 trillion of M&A in 2025, yet M&A workflow spans dozens of fragmented systems. Deal teams spend an extraordinary amount of time reconciling updates across platforms, copying figures from client materials, and reviewing large decks line by line to ensure accuracy and consistency. As teams increase transaction volume, they are forced to trade off speed with quality. The more deals a team runs, the harder it becomes to maintain a consistently high standard of execution. 

Execution, in practice, does not scale cleanly. We see this across middle-market and large investment banks. Teams rely on increasingly manual oversight to keep processes on track, with senior bankers spending time reviewing mechanics rather than focusing on judgment, positioning, and client advice. 

We believe the best deal teams should win based on the insight and guidance they deliver to clients, not on their ability to manage PowerPoint and internal coordination at scale. 

 

# **Maywood Expedites Execution and Elevates Quality** 

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/2969341/7e11d106-ad35-4d3f-b52a-8969cdadf936)

Maywood is building an AI execution layer for investment banking. Our goal extends much further than producing decks at the push of a button and instead centers around unlocking deal teams to focus on their relationships with clients and maximizing outcomes. 

### **1. We do the Foundational Analysis** 

Maywood provides a thorough research process covering the company, industry, deal dynamics, and more. Instead of analysts and associates spending days pulling comparables, industry context, and buyer rationales or managing directors (MDs) prepping endlessly for their next call with the management team, our system handles the entire process natively. This enables Maywood to optimally position each company being sold, in some cases replacing an MD’s original thesis altogether. 

### **2. Our Materials Can be Sent Directly to Clients** 

Maywood analyzes past confidential information memorandums (CIMs) and pitches to extrapolate firm-specific language and formatting standards. We run models that determine what has led to success in the past and emulate that in current deals, all while being in an isolated system. Some MDs forward materials directly generated on Maywood, while others use it to draft first-pass materials and iterate quicker using natural language to make slide mutations. 

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/2969341/86433f7d-2dfb-4678-a235-18b429c7690a)

Maywood also transforms the due diligence portion of the process, where buyers ask countless questions about the transaction. Maywood surfaces answers immediately and flags missing information along with key risks to ensure deal teams are fully equipped.  

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/2969341/9910819f-a237-47f5-8465-6421fad16989)

### **3. We Deliver Everything via a Single Platform** 

Everything is connected. The analysis feeds into decks and the due diligence module. Data updates propagate throughout the entire system automatically. Every feature works as a function of this continuously updating data layer, from first document uploaded to close. 

 

# **Who This is For** 

We are focused on middle-market and large investment banks running multiple sell-side processes per year and teams that care deeply about quality, consistency, and speed. 

We are already working with several banks and are seeing strong results! 

 

# **Our Ask**  

If you are, or know, any of the following, we would love to talk: 

* Investment bankers thinking seriously about how AI fits into execution 


* COOs, heads of operations, or tech leaders at banks evaluating productivity tools 


* Former bankers with strong opinions about what actually matters in sell-side execution 

You can reach us at [**founders@maywoodai.com**](mailto:founders@maywoodai.com). 

If you know anyone thinking about selling their company, we are happy to help out as well! We have a lot of banking connections to help you navigate this process and get the best outcome possible. 

 

# **Team** 

**Drake** leads product, strategy, and go-to-market. He saw the significant shortcomings and breakdowns of the deal process firsthand while working on some of the largest deals in the industry. He previously worked in private equity at Blackstone, where he helped roll out AI initiatives. He graduated Summa Cum Laude from the Huntsman Program at Wharton. 

**Kent** leads AI and go-to-market. He always loved doing analyst work first manually and then automating it end-to-end right after. That mindset led him to MIT, where he conducted deep research in neural stylistic transfer. Wanting to do this at scale, Kent went to BCG to automate work at Fortune 500 companies. When he heard deals take 6-9 months end to end when the manual work could be shortened to weeks, he founded Maywood to transform the industry. 

**Esteban** leads AI and infrastructure. He saw how much AI could transform a financial organization during his time in the hedge fund space at Balyasny. With a strong research background in AI and machine learning, he joined Kent and Drake in founding Maywood to bring those same transformations to dealmaking.

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/426038/042dbaa7-b053-47f5-acd3-e6208af8971c)

Hey everyone, I'm Naman, founder of Oximy.

**TL;DR:** Enterprises have dozens of AI tools with zero visibility into what's being used, what it costs, or where sensitive data is going. Oximy sits on your network and gives you the full picture. Discovery, spend intelligence, and data protection in one platform. We're processing millions of requests daily for enterprises in financial services and healthcare.

**Ask:** If you're dealing with AI sprawl, shadow AI, or data governance challenges, we should talk.

👉 Website: [oximy.com](http://oximy.com)

👉 Book a demo: [oximy.link/demo](https://oximy.link/demo)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kL-hr9OzsS0>

**The Problem**

AI adoption in the enterprise isn't slowing down. But visibility is basically zero.

Here's what we hear from every company we talk to:

* "We have no idea how many AI tools our employees are using."
* "Finance keeps asking me what we're spending on AI. I can't give them a number."
* "Someone pasted our entire customer list into ChatGPT. We found out three weeks later."
* "We bought Copilot licenses for 500 developers. I couldn't tell you if it's actually helping."

It's not that companies don't care. It's that there's been no way to actually see what's happening.

Until now.

**The Solution**

Oximy gives you three things: **Discovery**, **Spend Intelligence**, and **Data Protection**. They all connect into a single platform that gives you complete visibility into AI across your organization.

**1. Discovery: See every AI tool in your org**

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/426038/849af8fa-f0a1-48e1-b8da-b387511dc3fe)

You can't govern what you can't see. Oximy automatically detects and categorizes every AI tool your employees are using, sanctioned or not.

No surveys. No manual tracking. No waiting for expense reports to come in.

_Example:_ A financial services company came to us thinking they had 15 approved AI tools. Within the first week, we found 63, including several free tools that employees had signed up for using personal emails. Their security team had no idea.

**2. Spend Intelligence: Understand what AI actually costs**

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/426038/fd25f8f5-af21-4004-838a-788412064fe6)

AI spend is exploding, but it's scattered across teams, tools, and cost centers. Oximy consolidates everything so you can see exactly where money is going and where it's being wasted.

Which tools have overlapping functionality? Which licenses are sitting unused? Which teams are getting ROI and which aren't?

_Example:_ A growth-stage tech company discovered their marketing, design, and product teams were all paying for different AI image generation tools, over $80K per year combined. They consolidated to one tool and redeployed the savings.

**3. Data Protection: Know where sensitive data is going**

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/426038/c7bb7815-1af8-47eb-8f65-d5c97ff6bd85)

The biggest AI risk is unintentional data leaks.

Employees paste customer info, source code, financial data, and internal strategies into AI tools every day. Most companies have no visibility into this until something goes wrong.

Oximy monitors data flows to AI tools in real time. You can set policies, get alerts, and block sensitive data from reaching unauthorized tools.

_Example:_ A healthcare company set up Oximy and, within 48 hours, flagged an employee uploading patient records to an unapproved AI transcription tool. They were able to intervene immediately and avoid a potential HIPAA violation.

**How It All Connects**

Most companies try to solve these problems separately. A CASB for shadow IT. A spend management tool for costs. A DLP for data protection.

The problem is that AI doesn't fit neatly into any of these buckets. And none of them talks to each other.

Oximy is built from the ground up for AI. Discovery, spend, and data protection all live in one platform, so you get the full picture, not three partial views stitched together.

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/426038/9cdcb6f7-149f-4101-a0b0-d118b8887e11)

See a new AI tool pop up? You immediately know who's using it, what it costs, and which data it accesses.

See a spike in spend? You can trace it back to specific teams and tools.

See sensitive data flowing somewhere it shouldn't? You can block it and trace it back to the source.

Everything connects.

**How It Works**

We integrate at the network layer, sitting on your firewall or proxy.

Why does this matter?

Because every AI tool communicates over the network. ChatGPT, Copilot, Midjourney, Claude, Gemini, and every new tool that launches next month. We don't need endpoint agents. We don't need individual integrations with each vendor. We see everything automatically.

This also means we're future-proof. When the next AI tool shows up, we're already watching.

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/426038/4cd8ad8c-e125-4b7d-87e6-268edf631be7)

**Why Now**

Two years ago, AI in the enterprise was experimental. A few people are trying ChatGPT. Maybe a Copilot pilot.

Now it's everywhere. And governance hasn't caught up.

CISOs are being asked, "What AI tools are we using?" and don't have an answer. CFOs are watching AI costs explode with no accountability. Boards are asking about AI risk and getting shrugs. Regulators are starting to pay attention.

The companies that figure out AI governance now will be the ones that can scale AI adoption safely. The ones that don't will either slow down and lose, or speed up and get burned.

We're working with enterprises in financial services, healthcare, and growth-stage tech companies. We process millions of requests every day across thousands of AI tools.

If any of this resonates, we should talk:

* CISOs and security leaders who are trying to get a handle on AI risk
* CIOs, AI Transformation, and IT leaders dealing with shadow AI and tool sprawl
* CFOs and procurement who are trying to understand AI spend

👉 **Website:** [oximy.com](http://oximy.com)

👉 **Book a demo:** [oximy.link/demo](https://oximy.link/demo)

launches.title: Origin - Safer Cell & Gene Therapies with AI
launches.tagline: AI designed regulatory DNA sequences to program gene expression patterns
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/552024/dd558bc0-b110-466f-b603-d3acb473ba54)

Hey everyone!

We’re Yash and Malhar from Origin.

**TL;DR**

* Using AI to make cell & gene therapies **safer** by designing **DNA switches and dials**.
* Our model’s synthetic regulatory sequences program precise gene expression patterns in disease cells.
* We’re building the **largest** **proprietary dataset** consisting millions of experimentally validated regulatory DNA sequences across many different cell and tissue types.
* Our model **outperforms Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome** at predicting regulatory element activity.

<https://youtu.be/jCN43gOy7x8?si=pkZU6sGREgiI-EHA>

**The Promise**

Cell and gene therapies have successfully been used to treat diseases like stage IV leukemia, retinal disease, and spinal muscular atrophy. However, their application is limited due to concerns around safety and efficacy. But this drug class holds the promise of being a **durable cure** for diseases like cancer, autoimmune, neurodegenerative, aging, and more.

**The Problem**

Toxicity events largely arise due to our inability to control **where**, **when,** and to **what** extent genes are turned on. Regulatory DNA sequences - enhancers and promoters - function to modulate the expression of genes. Current approaches to design these sequences involve naive methods like repeats of known motifs (patterns) and random ligation. These methods either **reliably yield poor candidates** or require **brute force to search** for even one promising hit.

<https://youtu.be/SDJFAJULTP0?si=IYXFHLAqU88CcaXK>

**Our Solution**

Axis – our state-of-the-art model – is trained to design and screen regulatory DNA to activate therapeutic genes in target disease cell-states.

Axis is able to rapidly sample **millions** of functional candidates when prompted by the cell-state. We’re currently testing these sequences in the lab to produce the **largest proprietary dataset** of synthetic regulatory elements, measuring their interaction with transcription factors and the phenotypic outcomes of gene expression.

**Axis’ sequences have the highest predicted expression in targeted cell types**

Using Malinois, an independent and in-vitro validated prediction model by the Broad Institute, we observed that Axis’ generated sequences had the highest transcriptional activity in the cell type they were prompted by.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97480&key=user_uploads/552024/deb58343-aec7-4554-a176-d4ff1927da9f)

**Axis’ sequences contain known biological features**

Regulatory DNA sequences are activated when proteins called transcription factors bind to them at specific patterns of ATGCs known as motifs.

HNF4A is a known master regulator of hepatocyte and liver gene expression. We observed that in the generated sequences, its known motif most frequently occurred in HepG2 (liver cell line) targeted sequences.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97480&key=user_uploads/552024/d4e9dc1a-47c7-4599-99f3-f0b4d8980c6a)

**Axis’ sequences have high diversity and explore a large design space**

Over 72% of our generated sequences have no BLAT alignment match up amongst themselves (using a 20bp threshold).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97480&key=user_uploads/552024/45c66f66-c144-46ac-aea9-2739e6aae6d9)

**Axis outperforms Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome**

Axis demonstrates strong performance in predictive benchmarks measuring molecular properties of real regulatory sequences. These include measures like chromatin accessibility and transcription factor protein binding.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97480&key=user_uploads/552024/f1b68778-ea47-44b1-a2fc-ee4ac39c25bf)

**The ask:**

If you know or are someone working on partnerships at pharmaceutical / biotech companies working in cell & gene therapies, reach out to explore:

* Partnering on regulatory sequence designs for target disease cells.
* Getting access to our proprietary dataset of sequence properties, sequence-protein interactions, and cell-state perturbations.

\
Feel free to reach out via email at [yash@origin.bio](mailto:yash@origin.bio)

launches.title: Cardboard - Agentic Video Editor
launches.tagline: Edit videos at the speed of thought!
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Cardboard is an agentic video editor. It gives you the power of Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve without the learning curve. It is orders of magnitude faster + cheaper than the old way of making videos.

It lives in your browser and helps you go from a sea of **raw footage** (talking heads, screen recordings, screenshots, B-rolls) to a great video in seconds.

Think of it as “**vibe editing**”

<https://youtu.be/xLBxatFM7uk>

**The Problem**

**Video has become the default distribution channel for growth, marketing, and brand storytelling. The teams who iterate fastest on video, compound attention over time.**

Many of us sit on mountains of raw assets - product walkthroughs, customer feedback, tweets, blogs, changelogs, emails, and newsletters - that should turn into **testimonials, launch videos, recaps, and ad experiments.**

But, editing is **painfully slow**. Getting to a first cut still means hours of manual work, expensive tools, and async feedback loops. This is where the momentum dies.

As a result, most teams ship far fewer videos than they should - not because they lack ideas or footage, but because the editing process can’t keep up.

**The Solution**

**We are building Cardboard - it is an agentic video editor that lives in your browser.**

You can:

1. Ask for a first cut (“make a 60s recap” / “cut this into ads”)
2. Search footage by meaning, not filenames
3. Then refine it yourself on a timeline

The goal is to make video production feel closer to modern design / coding tools - fast, accessible, and collaborative - so the teams can iterate fast and ship more.

**Why us?**

We met in middle school and have been best friends since the last 15yrs. We built Cardboard because we lived with this problem ourselves:

launches.title: Didit: the fastest way to verify real humans.
launches.tagline: All-in-one identity platform built for speed and fraud prevention.
launches.body:
We’re Alberto and Alejandro Rosas, identical twins and co-founders of Didit. We’ve spent our lives impersonating each other. That used to be rare. Today, **AI has your photos and your voice.** Soon it will call your grandma, and she won’t know. The internet needs a fast, reliable way to prove who you are. **That’s why we built Didit.**

## **TL;DR**: We made identity verification finally work on the internet.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KU9Jf79J8XE>

## What you need to believe …

The internet is about to get weird.

* AI can already copy your **voice**, your **face**, and your **videos**. Perfect fakes are basically here.
* Bots are about to flood everything — social media, marketplaces, apps, support chats, even phone calls.
* Very soon, you won’t trust what you see or hear online.
* When trust breaks, **identity becomes mandatory**. For logins, payments, access, everything.
* This market is going to 1000x.

## The problem (we’re not ready)

The scary part? Our current identity systems already suck.

* They’re **slow**, **insecure**, and **expensive.** Built for a pre-AI internet.
* You’ve felt it: verifications that take days, uploading the same document twice, random rejections.
* Real users get stuck. Attackers get through.
* Companies end up stitching together 5–10 vendors just to run identity. Engineers hard-code rules. Ops can’t move fast.

We don’t need more tools. We need a **new identity platform** — fast, secure, global, and simple.

**Didit is that platform.**

## The solution

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eTdcg7JCc4M>

We built Didit by doing the opposite of everyone else. We didn’t stitch together vendors or wrap legacy systems — we built everything **from scratch**: ID verification, biometrics, liveness, auth... Then we put it all together into **one all-in-one platform**. We obsessed over UI and UX, optimized every millisecond, and designed flows where real humans verify in seconds while fraud gets blocked by default. Onboarding rates go up, friction goes down, and teams finally get a complete, connected view of each user.

Because we own the entire stack, we can do something most identity companies can’t: offer **simple pay-per-use pricing at very competitive rates**. No contracts, no minimums, no surprises. Companies that switch to Didit usually switch once — and they don’t churn. Once you go Didit… you don’t go back 😄

## Traction

* **Millions of humans verified every month**
* **700+ active B2B customers**, growing **\~20% MoM**
* **Pure PLG** so far, now layering outbound
* **300%+ NRR by month 6**
* **\~90% paid customer retention** at month 6

Didit clearly works.

Now we’re executing the expansion into **mid-market and enterprise**.

## Didit path to trillion dollar company

Even if we’re Spanish, we don’t really do “**_siestas”_**. We do **relentless execution** — and we’re very good at it.

We believe identity will become one of the most important pieces of infrastructure of the AI internet. As soon as you can’t trust what you see or hear online, proving who you are becomes non-negotiable. We envision a world **where identity is frictionless and instant** — one click, face-first — and works everywhere: logging into apps, authorizing payments, accessing services online and in the physical world. Your **Didit Identity** becomes something you carry with you, **reusable, private, and trusted by default**. Long term, we even see governments running secure digital services and online democracies on top of Didit. This is a massive shift and we’re going to lead it.

## Ask

If you’re verifying users or fighting bots, fake accounts, or multi-account abuse — **reach out**. We’ll help you onboard **faster, reduce fraud, and lower costs.**

Know a company dealing with identity verification / kyc ..etc? Every intro comes with an **amazing Spanish paella** 🥘 as a gift.

VaultPay is a digital banking platform bringing Visa cards and modern financial services to the Democratic Republic of Congo, a country of 120 million people where 85% remain unbanked, and 90% of transactions happen in US dollars.

**The Problem**

The DRC has been overlooked by the fintech industry. While mobile money dominates most of Africa with razor-thin margins, the DRC's dollarized economy means our users transact at an average of $40/month, nearly 3x Nigeria's $15 average. Higher transaction values mean healthy unit economics from day one.

**What We Built**

Think Apple Wallet meets CashApp. We offer virtual and physical Visa cards, USD and CDF accounts, and we're rolling out an agency banking network that transforms local businesses into cash-in/cash-out points, following the Square model for Africa.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97421&key=user_uploads/350695/198f0423-193f-4546-8c38-c6c46dc243bc)

**Traction**

We launched in Q4 2025. In four months, with zero marketing spend:

* 17,000+ users signed up
* $20K MRR
* 80% are accessing formal financial services for the first time

**Why Now**

We're the first startup to secure a full payment license from the Central Bank of Congo, rather than operating under another bank's license, as most African fintechs do. This opened doors: Visa invested in our launch and is finalizing a deal recognizing us as their distribution partner for DRC expansion. Ecobank, one of Africa's largest banks, chose us to power its card experience, integrating its CashXpress program ($15M in monthly cash-in volume) into our platform.

**Team**

We left Airbnb and Google in Silicon Valley to build this. Backed by YCombinator, Tekedia Capital, Michael Seibel, executives from SoFi, Airbnb, and CashApp, and engineers from Google DeepMind, Meta, and Uber.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97421&key=user_uploads/350695/9bb15e33-5144-43ed-b8f1-c75f8fd8f2ba)

AI collapsed what should have taken years into months. We own our entire stack, including product, KYC, analytics, customer service, and data science, all with a very small team.

**The Opportunity**

Everyone chases the same markets in Africa. Meanwhile, we're building the financial rails for an entire nation before others catch on. That is our moat. DRC is currently undergoing a massive nationwide digital transformation and is one of the continent's largest consumer markets.\

launches.title: Seeing Systems: Modular Autonomous Drones for Modern Warfare
launches.tagline: We build modular, autonomous strike drones that adapt as warfare evolves.
launches.body:
# **Hey everyone**

We’re Alex & Matthew - The brothers building **Seeing Systems**.

---

## **TL;DR**

We're building **inexpensive, autonomous strike drones** designed to stay operationally relevant as warfare evolves. By combining true hardware modularity with an agentic control system that lowers cognitive load on operators, we enable faster upgrades, broader adoption, and more than 2x reduction in lifecycle cost.

Our customers and partners include the UK Royal Marine Commandos, several other units in the UK, and 4 other NATO forces, and we are currently shipping prototypes to Ukraine for iterative feedback.

<https://youtu.be/Ia_A1T-l7d8>

## **Problem**

Military forces face two linked challenges:

1. **Platform Obsolescence:** Fixed drones require replacement or major rebuilds whenever missions or threats evolve, driving high costs and slowing operational adaptation.
2. **The One Pilot Problem:** One person can only control one drone at once, requiring full attention.

Countless stories can be found of western drone systems becoming obsolete, needing to be shelved and eventually replaced.

A Few Examples:

* <https://newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/ukraine-s-military-rejects-german-helsing-1768811354.html>
* <https://militarnyi.com/en/news/ssu-abandons-altius-attack-drones-after-failures-at-front/>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97412&key=user_uploads/2822007/9dfb1275-b59e-4c17-9862-3a9d8a11534d)

# **Solution**

We build autonomous, modular drones that solve both problems at once:

* **Modular hardware:** Swappable payloads, sensors, compute, and comms let one platform support strike, ISR, or swarm missions. Upgradable and effective year after year.
* **Agentic autonomy:** Automates tasks like navigation and coordination, so operators with no prior training can use systems to their full effectiveness.

How do we know? Well, Forward Deployed Engineers. Giving each unit we work with a point of contact, we take feedback and integrate them into our system in a matter of hours. A close collaboration with the UK Royal Marines Commandos is actually what led to the development of this system.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97412&key=user_uploads/2822007/7170ca7a-bd1d-4d2b-a6a7-f77ce762975e)

## **The Team**

**Matthew Le Maitre - Co-Founder, Software**

Former Jane Street Software Engineer and top-ranked CS graduate from the University of Cambridge. Matthew’s path started at the Mobile Robotics Lab at Cambridge, where he worked on autonomous systems and context-aware drones. He now leads the software side of Seeing Systems.

**Alex Le Maitre - Co-Founder, Hardware**

Alex has been obsessed with unmanned systems since childhood and is largely self-taught in embedded electronics, firmware, and PCB design. He has previously designed Explosive Ordinance Disposal (EOD) training and diagnostic hardware for military users, alongside projects with national-security implications. Originally from the island of Guernsey, Alex now leads hardware development with a focus on building robust systems that help keep our people safe.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97412&key=user_uploads/2822007/dfc9b55c-c1b7-4ac3-a6bb-8e7760b2d006)

If you’re a military contractor, defense organisation or special forces unit looking for a real operational edge, contact us at [founders@seeing-systems.com](mailto:founders@seeing-systems.com) &[ www.seeing-systems.com](http://www.seeing-systems.com)

launches.title: Webhound Reports: Deep research that scales with your budget
launches.tagline: Long-running deep research for the highest quality reports
launches.body:
Hey everyone, Moe here.

We're building Webhound — AI research agents where you set a budget and the agent keeps researching until it runs out. More budget = more sources, more depth.

**How we got here:** We started with a product (now called Datasets) that builds structured tables from the web. It worked, but we hit a wall: as datasets got bigger, costs exploded and context became unmanageable. And for open-ended datasets, we never had a clean answer for "when should the agent stop?"

So we rebuilt everything around two ideas: costs that stay linear with time, and giving users direct control over depth.

The new architecture is a **Planner-Executor-Verifier loop**. Executors get fresh context each run. Planner and Verifier work from summaries and can search over what's accumulated. Runs until budget's out.

We tested it on traditional deep research as a sanity check. At $3-5, it beat the top result on DeepResearch Bench. At $15, it way outperformed it, even running on older models (gemini-2.5-flash). So we shipped it as Reports and put the same architecture into Datasets.

**We now have two products:**

* **Reports** = cited research docs (competitive analysis, market research, system design). Always uses the full budget—more budget means more sources and deeper coverage.
* **Datasets** = build structured tables from the web, or upload your own and enrich with new columns. We can access LinkedIn, YouTube, Reddit, and most other sites. Examples: lead lists with company info, competitor feature matrices, lists of VCs filtered by thesis, GTM leads with emails. Stops when complete, or at budget, whichever comes first.

**Asks:**

* **Try it** – [**webhound.ai**](http://webhound.ai), $5 free. Honest feedback welcome.
* **Spread the word** – if it's useful, share it with anyone you know doing a lot of research (investors, analysts, consultants)

– Moe

launches.title: Fort: Automatic Strength Tracking for People Who Care About Longevity
launches.tagline: Other wearables track sleep and heart rate, but underestimate or ignore muscles and strength!
launches.body:
**TLDR;** Most wearables focus on sleep and heart rate. Fort is a wearable that automatically tracks strength training, for people focused on longevity.

**We just opened pre-orders!** [**fort.cx/order**](http://fort.cx/order)

<https://youtu.be/qU0IWkdsgY4>

**Setting The Scene**

Strength training has exploded in popularity over the past decade, especially recently. Whoop’s own data shows that strength workouts on their platform [**increased 122% YoY**](https://www.whoop.com/us/en/thelocker/whoop-year-in-review-2025/?srsltid=AfmBOoqLaNJlnaNn6uXWcFH8qfuk0ZRdry97kTI07R10adtOEx1jAR5H) between 2024 and 2025. For female Oura members, strength training was the [**third most popular**](https://ouraring.com/blog/oura-member-data-reveals-top-fitness-activities-among-female-members/?srsltid=AfmBOopcf5eXLLjOArvhBtKWvDVyd_oGxHgg2pOPhG3B7e5gHl9ME4Pb) activity, behind “walking” and “housework.” People now see strength training as a critical part of their wellness routine, not just a niche hobby for gym bros.

And yet, neither Whoop nor Oura offers a strength tracking feature that actually works.

**The Problem**

If you want to track strength workouts on existing wearables, you typically need to manually log every set, rep, and exercise. There are some attempts at automatic rep and exercise detection from Garmin and third-party Apple Watch apps, but the experience of using these products is unrefined compared to cardio or sleep features.

Even after logging everything manually, wearables underestimate or ignore muscle fatigue, and lack actionable insights on how users should adapt their training to achieve their goals.

**What we're building**

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/1251673/343e5478-aeaf-426d-98a0-b04ac5978c5d)


Fort is a wearable that measures motion and heart rate to detect exercises, reps, sets, form, and fatigue that occurs while strength training. The device is a screenless band that can be worn on the wrist, attached magnetically to workout equipment, or worn with body straps elsewhere, so we can capture movements that wrist-only wearables miss.

We also track steps, sleep, heart rate, and cardio exercise, to provide you with a comprehensive picture of your health.

You can wear Fort all day, and the battery lasts a week with normal use.

**Who it’s for**

Anyone who cares about their health and regularly does some form of strength training, like gym or pilates!

**About us**

[Paul](https://www.linkedin.com/in/paulcschneider/), [Zac](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zacvalles/), and [Miranda](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mirandanover/) are ex-Tesla engineers who worked on Cybertruck, Semi, and Cybercab. We know how to build and ship consumer hardware at scale.

**Fort is shipping starting June 2026. Pre-Order at: [https://www.fort.cx/order/](https://www.fort.cx/order/)**

Hey everyone 👋

We're Pavan (PK), Gunin and Nirmit – co-founders of Ritivel.

## **TL;DR**

Ritivel is an AI-native workspace for regulatory and medical writing teams at life sciences companies. Our AI agents draft CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs in minutes instead of weeks, helping drugs reach patients faster.

<https://youtu.be/VrqJtPDy_do>

## **❌ The Problem**

Every month a drug is delayed from reaching the market costs pharma companies \~$45M in lost revenue and more importantly, delays treatment for thousands of patients who need it.

Yet regulatory teams are stuck in a painful, months-long process to create FDA submissions like CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs:

**1. Information overload** 📚 These submissions require synthesizing thousands of pages of clinical data, prior submissions, and regulatory guidance which is an overwhelming task even for experienced teams.

**2. Document hunting & version chaos** 🔄 Teams waste hours digging through SharePoint folders, juggling multiple document versions, and chasing colleagues for the right files.

**3. Endless follow-ups** 📧 Regulatory leads spend their days sending reminder emails, tracking down missing inputs, and managing status updates across teams.

**4. Manual drafting bottlenecks** ⏳ Even with all the information gathered, the first draft alone takes weeks of painstaking work by highly specialized (and expensive) regulatory writers.

---

## **🔧 Our Solution**

Ritivel deploys AI agents that transform how regulatory teams work:

**Draft the most common document types like CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs in minutes** ✍️ Our agents generate comprehensive first drafts directly in Microsoft Word, following FDA formatting requirements and pulling from your existing clinical data and prior submissions. Every data point includes citations linked back to the original source, so reviewers can verify with one click.

**Automated follow-ups** 📧 Integrated with Outlook, our agents handle reminder emails and follow-ups automatically, so you're not stuck chasing colleagues for missing documents.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97327&key=user_uploads/939300/aa5a53c8-8d14-4c11-a20c-fecd59724cae)

**Accelerated project management** 🚀 By automating the document gathering and drafting loop, teams can focus on review and refinement rather than administrative overhead.

**TL;DR:** APIs weren’t built for agents, we fixed that. Developers and agents get instant access to hundreds of APIs through our MCP or SDK. No key management, no billing headaches, pay as you go. API providers list once and become instantly discoverable. 

_Ask:_ We’d love an intro to teams building agents to understand how they’re handling paid APIs today. Contact us at [founders@orthogonal.com](mailto:founders@orthogonal.com)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CixNTItWDjI>

**The Problem:**

AI agents are about to become the biggest consumers of APIs on the internet. But they struggle to access tools.

MCP helped standardize tool calling, but created fragmentation. Some services have MCPs, others don't. Some map to single APIs, others wrap entire workflows. Agents end up with 30+ tools, bloating context.

Worse, any MCP requiring identity or payment means managing accounts, API keys, billing, and auth across dozens of services. And most APIs don't even have MCPs.

You could have your agent find APIs, sign up, handle auth, and buy credits, but the failure rate is high. The entire API economy was built for humans.

Meanwhile, API providers are leaving money on the table. Billions of agents could be paying for their APIs right now, but they have no way to find or transact with them.

These APIs are locked behind API keys and human payment methods, which agents do not have access to.

**The Solution:**

Orthogonal is where agents go to find and pay for APIs.

Hey YC 👋 

We're Rabii and Hashim - co-founders at Entropy! 

# TL;DR

We’re building an AI operating system for specialty healthcare that improves over time. All automations sit on top of Atlas, our provider level context layer to ensure that we capture institutional knowledge and build on it over time. 

We’re supporting multiple clinic locations that serve thousands of patients every single month and growing fast.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7UdXR-bhzHg>

# The Problem

**Specialty clinics are drowning in manual tasks that are costing them billions of dollars and failing their patients and referrers.** 

* Intake staff manually process incoming faxes, emails, forms, and calls.
* Billing staff need to check eligibility, submit prior authorization requests, and submit claims.
* Patients are stuck waiting weeks for urgent care and referrers have no visibility. 
* Clinics are losing revenue as they miss out on patients and have their claims denied.

Static automation can’t handle this complexity as SOPs and payor requirements are changing constantly. 

# The Solution

**Entropy automates your entire referral and revenue cycle workflow - and gets smarter every single day.**

* **Intake:** Capture referrals from faxes, email, portals. Extract patient data, create charts.
* **Insurance:** Verify eligibility, submit prior auths, track approvals, fight denials.
* **Communication:** Update referring physicians, remind patients, manage documentation.

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/376535/772d5e5f-e300-4b80-b082-62e56ed0fe63)

**Here's the difference:** All automations are built on Atlas, our context layer. It’s a living knowledge base of the clinic’s operations that evolves over time. It learns from every referral, every authorization, every edge case and adapts autonomously. When a payor changes their requirements overnight, Atlas accounts for this without engineering or operational lift. 

We're live across multiple clinic locations that process thousands of patient referrals monthly, now 90% faster than manual workflows.

**About Us**

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/376535/1485e2f1-89d4-492b-841e-8ede57427eee)


Healthcare is personal to us. Hashim spent a decade navigating referral hell while managing a chronic condition. Rabii watched his parents do the same. When we sat with specialty clinics, we saw the chaos on the other side - so we're fixing it.

We've spent our careers scaling complex operations. Rabii at McKinsey building digital businesses, Hashim at Careem handling pricing for millions of daily transactions. We've seen what happens when automation actually works and what it takes to build something that scales.

**Our Ask**

If you lead ops, intake or RCM at a specialty care provider (or know someone who does), let's talk: [rabii@withentropy.ai](mailto:rabii@withentropy.ai).

launches.title: Ruma Care: We help clinics get patients on their biologics faster
launches.tagline: Automating prior auths for the most expensive meds
launches.body:
Ruma Care automates prior authorizations - we’re starting with clinics that administer the most expensive specialty medications.

Biologics are expensive medications that cost $80-$150K+ per year per patient, and often need to be administered in specific settings called infusion clinics. Medical providers buy these drugs up front to secure pricing deals and safer inventory - they are reimbursed for the cost of the medications through the patients’ insurance.

Because they’re so expensive, these specialty medications are **denied by insurers at a rate of 37% each year**. When they are denied, **providers don’t get reimbursed for the medication and are left covering the costs.** Ruma Care solves this so clinics get paid, patients get treated faster, and care teams spend less time fighting insurance.

### **Launch Video + Ruma Demo**

[**https://youtu.be/WwAa5VreO0M**](https://youtu.be/WwAa5VreO0M)

### **Problem**

Clinics can lose money when prior authorizations are denied.

Specialty medications like biologics cost $80K/year, which is why insurers are highly specific with requirements on access. Clinics are required to follow complex, hidden requirements such as:

* Trying cheaper drugs first
* Using specific drug brands or biosimilars
* Submitting through fax instead of portals

None of this is standardized. Each insurance company has different rules, and those rules change quarterly.

Clinics with high volume spend thousands of man-hours on completing these forms: the average prior auth takes 30 minutes and is still submitted through paper, fax, and phone.  When it is denied, the process can stretch into weeks or months of appeals, phone calls, and faxes.

During this time, clinics have already invested staff time and often administered high-cost drugs. If reimbursement is denied, that cost is never recovered.

### **Product**

We do solve the problems in 3 ways:

1. For each medication, diagnosis, and insurance combination, Ruma extracts the submission criteria required to get the drug approved by insurers.
2. We pull out the correct forms, then automate the form-filling for prior authorizations.
3. Lastly, we enroll patients in copay assistance programs, all in one workflow and platform.

We turn a process that traditionally spans 70+ online portals, disparate paper forms, and manual phone calling into a single, streamlined platform. As we process prior authorizations, our models learn from denial patterns to understand exactly what insurers need to see to get a prior authorization approved.

We are live across clinics in California and Nevada, and helped them cut the denial rates by 50% and reduce staff time per prior auth by 20x.

### **Our Story**

I quit my big tech job to work as a medical assistant. I wanted to understand why specialty medication access in America is so hard.

Christina experienced this as a patient herself, she spent years fighting payers to get on her biologic treatments.

We met at Yale’s CS50 class freshmen year and built a Yale dining app for food ratings. We took an entrepreneurship break to work in Big Tech (Apple, Uber, & Walmart), and startups (Medallion, Sigma), scaling Uber One across 13M+ users and building ML models for Siri and iPhone users. We built products for customers like United Health Care and the U.S. Health & Human Services. Now we’re building Ruma Care.

Here’s more about our story: [**https://substack.com/home/post/p-176970044**](https://substack.com/home/post/p-176970044)

### **New Launch of Formulary Navigator - Free tool for providers**

We spoke with 150+ providers. Every one said navigating insurance coverage rules is their #1 challenge.

So we created the **Ruma Formulary Navigator.**

Providers can enter the insurance plan, medication, and diagnosis, and instantly see coverage rules and prior authorization requirements. <https://ask.rumacare.com>

And we’re providing this for free to bring better access and knowledge to the medical community. 

If you know any hospital administrators, doctors, and coordinators at infusion clinics and hospital systems, we’d appreciate an introduction. 

Feel free to share this with any doctors, nurses, or medical admin staff struggling to understand new formulary changes in 2026:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97245&key=user_uploads/1967697/468d68f7-8ea2-4b53-97b4-f2191f8510fe)

Hi all - I’m [Chetan](http://linkedin.com/in/chemishra), the founder of [Rhizome AI](https://rhizomeai.com/).

# _Tl;dr_

_What has the FDA’s feedback been on real world evidence in review comments?_ 

We help life science companies know what the FDA thinks.

Regulatory affairs teams ask a question and get an answer backed by terabytes of regulatory & clinical databases from the US, EU, etc.

Unlike ChatGPT, Rhizome reads up to 1,000 documents per question, accompanies each statement with a citation, and doesn’t hallucinate.

**_Ask_**: If you know any biotech or medtech leaders (esp if they’re regulatory affairs or R&D), I’d appreciate [an intro](https://calendly.com/mishrachetan/launch-yc)!

Ultimately we want all reg affairs teams to be as informed as [the most regulatory man in the world](https://youtube.com/shorts/whOX6BuvgMI). 

### 😖 The problem: Knowing what the FDA thinks

The FDA is the customer of every function in life sciences. It doesn’t matter whether you are regulatory affairs, R&D, quality, manufacturing, commercial, etc.

At the same time, it’s difficult to understand their thinking. Guidance documents are high level and vague. The only alternative is doing (or paying a consultant to do) manual, painful research on past decisions they’ve made and understand _why_. Other regulators around the globe are no easier.

ChatGPT / Claude / etc. have only made it worse

* They trust their knowledge and only look up what they feel the need to. This means low-latency, but high-hallucination research
* Even when they retrieve sources, at most, it’s a few dozen. It’s also liable to include lots of internet junk mixed in with the authoritative government databases the industry trusts
* They don’t make it easy to check citations. They cite a 1200 page PDF and you don’t really know where to dig inside it.

### ✨ The Solution: Hallucination-free, deep research for life sciences

Rhizome Ask solves this problem by providing hallucination-free and thorough deep research for the life sciences. There’s a few key things our customers like:

* We didn’t have a single hallucination reported in 2025. 
* Every statement comes with a citation
* We read up to 1,000 documents per question in a few minutes before writing an answer. We’re continuously extending this limit.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97268&key=user_uploads/668813/dbc9e5d3-d827-4dfe-8b2d-52dfab9bb2b1)

* _“I would cry if I lost access to Rhizome” -_ an RA manager at a drug delivery device company
* “_10 minutes of work can accomplish what would have taken weeks._” a device engineer at a pharma company

### 🤝 Who am I

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97268&key=user_uploads/668813/85808e43-72d1-4d28-b536-7fd8d4af6c5c)

A bit about my background. 

I joined EvolutionaryScale as their first product engineer, launching an AI inference platform to help scientists design proteins. I joined Instabase as #16 helping banks with document & imaging processing, closing $7m as the technical lead. 

When looking to start my own company, I realized we saw many AI startups focused on drug discovery, but a _lot_ less attention bringing those products to market.

launches.title: ShapedQL: The SQL engine for search, feeds, and AI agents
launches.tagline: Connect your data. Train your models. Query text, user or session context and retrieve relevant results in milliseconds.
launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋\
\
I'm Tullie, the founder of [Shaped](https://www.shaped.ai/).\
\
**TL;DR**\
\
Today we’re launching ShapedQL, a new language purpose built for agents, feeds and search. We built ShapedQL because we realized that while retrieval has become easier (thanks to Vector DBs), ranking and relevance are still incredibly hard.\
\
Launch video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Owj_uSUPNaU>\
\
**Problem ❌**\
\
Most engineering teams we talk to are stuck maintaining a "Frankenstein" stack. To build a "For You" feed or give an AI Agent personalized memory, they have to glue together a vector database, a feature store (like Redis), a reranking service, and thousands of lines of Python spaghetti code.\
\
**Solution ✅**\
\
We built ShapedQL to turn that "house of cards" into a single interface.

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/812951/eed67b43-7c3b-4b0f-819a-5bbd31db2732)

ShapedQL is a domain-specific SQL dialect that compiles down to a high-performance, multi-stage ranking pipeline. With a single query, you can define the four stages of modern relevance:\
**1. Retrieve:** Fetch candidates from multiple sources (Hybrid Search, Collaborative Filtering, Trending).\
**2. Filter:** Apply hard constraints (e.g., "in stock" or "within 50 miles").\
**3. Score:** Rank results using real-time ML models (optimizing for clicks, purchases, or watch time).\
**4. Reorder:** Enforce diversity so your users (or Agents) don't see the same 5 items repeatedly.

We're seeing teams reduce 2,000+ lines of maintenance code down to \~30 lines of ShapedQL, while shipping features like "Cart Upsell" or "Conversational Recommendations" in days instead of months.

If you're not a fan of SQL we also have Python or Typescript SDKs, perfect for a real-time production integration.

![uploaded image](/media/?key=user_uploads/812951/d3cc12cc-3c74-448b-adf0-ae65d9359b79)

**Ask 💬**\
\
**1.** We have a Product Hunt launch at this link: <https://www.producthunt.com/products/shaped>. Any support or and upvote would be greatly appreciated!\
\
**2.** Please try out our interactive demo at [playground.shaped.ai](https://playground.shaped.ai), we’d love to hear any feedback on the new language. Were you able to easily make a query? Do the docs make sense? What is it missing?\
\
**3.** If the problems above resonates and you’re struggling to get true relevance from your vector store or current retrieval system, please get in touch! Book on this calendar here: <https://www.shaped.ai/contact> and mention you’re from YC. I’ll make sure to jump on the call to help you out myself.

launches.body:
Hi YC, I’m [Joseph Zhang](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2323858) and I’m working with my cofounder [Sophia Kim](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3126931) to build CatchBack Cards,  an iOS and web platform for maximizing the thrill of collecting Pokemon and Sports cards. We allow collectors to create custom mystery packs with personalized chases and customized odds with cryptographically trusted tooling. Users can rip open digital packs and get physical cards shipped to them, receive buyback offers on cards pulled from their mystery packs sent straight to Venmo and PayPal, and buy/sell cards in our $1 marketplace.

[catchbackcards.com](http://catchbackcards.com)

catchback cards on the iOS app store

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97204&key=user_uploads/2323858/bc1ee024-41f9-4255-83d2-4920a5a622ef)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFLVCQQhvcE>

**What we’re building**

The trading card market is massive, fast-growing, and _very_ large in transaction volume. Globally, physical trading cards (sports, Pokémon, anime like One Piece, etc.) represent a $20B+ annual market, growing at double-digit rates (\~10–15% YoY) even after the pandemic boom. Beyond retail sales, billions of dollars move through the secondary market each year via graded cards, private deals, and resale platforms. What’s striking is how _offline_ this economy still is: at local and regional card shows, millions of dollars change hands over a single weekend, through cash deals, trades, box breaks, and private six-figure transactions—most of it fragmented, informal, and poorly tracked. This is a real, high-velocity market hiding in plain sight.\
\
Mystery packs are popular in Pokémon and sports cards, but today they’re mostly run manually or through platforms with high fees and limited transparency. CatchBack lets anyone create their own mystery packs with their desired pool of cards, risk levels, and personalized odds, and gives collectors the option to buy packs, to list cards in the marketplace, and to get an instant buyout offer on whatever they hit in the pack. We provide cryptographic randomness proofs and open source our card selection code so that users can independently verify and trust our mystery packs. Users trust our packs more because they can pick exactly what goes into their pool and can see mathematical proof, which physical mystery packs cannot recreate. 

We’re also building a platform that digitizes cards and allows users to transact ownership rights to cards for just $1. Previously, eBay buyers dealt with fraud issues, ridiculous hidden fees, and shipping headaches, and we’re creating a system that allows for maximal liquidity and convenience in speculating on card investments.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97204&key=user_uploads/2323858/478ed561-02d9-403a-83d8-2496f9b6a458)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97204&key=user_uploads/2323858/f43cc95b-6446-4770-838b-e588f40ebfbc)

**Who it’s for**

Our users are card collectors who open mystery bags and creators (Pokémon, sports cards, slabs) who already sell to communities on Instagram, Discord, and live marketplaces. 

**Why we started this**

We spent a lot of time buying, selling, and comping cards across eBay, Whatnot, and Instagram DMs, and kept seeing the same problems: high fees, fragmented liquidity, and a lack of trust in mystery packs. Other blind box sites stuff their bags with undesirable floor hits and gouge their users on shipping fees, listing fees, and marketplace fees. launches.title: EigenPal: AI Document Workflows
launches.tagline: EigenPal automates enterprise document processes with AI
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** EigenPal automates your document processing workflows with AI. If you have humans reading documents and typing data into systems - KYC docs, invoices, claims, shipping forms, contracts, receipts - we replace that. Works on messy scans, handwritten forms, third-party docs. Beautiful workflow builder, testing, and team functionality. On-prem ready or use our cloud. Working with 2 large European banks on loan automations already.

Try on: [**eigenpal.com**](http://eigenpal.com)

**2 minute demo -** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pEfhqhylS2Y>

**What We Learned**

Working on back office document automation, we kept hearing the same questions:

* _"How do I know this workflow will actually work before I bet my ops on it?"_
* _"I aim to have 100 workflows. How will I monitor them all?"_
* _"Can this run in our cloud? Data can't leave our infrastructure."_
* _"Our files have contracts, amendments, and extensions that reference each other. Can you piece that together?"_

Traditional automation tools were built for deterministic processes and they're not designed for AI. AI is a game changer for document processing, but businesses still can't trust it at scale. Why? Evals and monitoring aren't built in. And most new platforms can't run on-prem.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97202&key=user_uploads/2221380/d651a1db-2002-456e-9c18-55d290083745)

**The Solution: A Platform Where You Can Trust AI Workflows**

EigenPal is built around one principle: like any employees you entrust work to, you need to trust your workflows before you deploy them and monitor them after.

* **Agentic workflow builder.** Our AI workflow builder let’s you create workflows with easy in your natural language. It can even iterate on a workflow on a test dataset to tune accuracy.
* **Eval-first.** Before any workflow goes live, test it against your historical documents. See exactly what accuracy you're getting. Deploy only when you're confident. **Set up a feedback loop in production** so workflows are adjusted with feedback.
* **Document-centric.** Upload files directly, no public URLs needed. Built-in storage plus a powerful template filler to generate polished output docs from your extracted data.
* **Configure everything.** Choose your OCR/VLM, LLM, configure every step of the pipeline separately. Access built-in tracing for workflows in our app or export via OpenTelemetry.
* **Monitor hundreds of workflows at once.** One dashboard showing costs, compliance logs, and failures across every workflow. Know immediately when something drifts.
* **Collaborate with your team.** Org workspaces let you share workflows, templates, and results with colleagues. Build once, use across your team.
* **On-prem or cloud.** Runs in your infrastructure with your LLMs, or use our hosted version. Your choice.

**We believe the group chat is the real social network.**

If you've got a group chat that's been a little too quiet lately... this is your sign.

<https://youtu.be/pn07_bo6rfs>

**🔄 The Rapid Evolution**

You may remember [**text.ai**](http://text.ai), our AI that lives inside SMS, iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram chats. Tens of thousands of users and over 10M+ messages across 150+ countries in a rapid few months showed us something we didn't expect:

People didn't just want answers. We realized they wanted a social friend who understands and acts. Together.

Not a sterile bot. Someone with personality and character. Someone who understood their unique group, who's vegan, who hates horror movies, who always wants ramen.

They wanted a premium chat experience that was inherently social.

Why?

We distilled it down to one thing.

There is a place where we feel our happiest. All of us.

The group.

Humans are born into them. And thrive in them. But today, there are very few products to support them.

Places where groups can live. But not thrive.

And so, friends drift apart. Plans go unplanned. The chat fades.

So, we started building Alfi, our human-first, AI native approach to messaging.

It doesn’t simply process but understands context, group dynamics, and whether you’re actually asking for help or just chatting with friends.

launches.title: Kita: Turn financial documents into risk signals for lenders
launches.tagline: Make document-driven decisions 70x faster, with built-in fraud checks
launches.body:
Hi YC! We’re Carmel Limcaoco and Rhea Malhotra, the co-founders of Kita. We met over our gap year during COVID while we were undergrads at Stanford, and have been best friends ever since. Carmel is from Manila, is a past founder, and worked in computational music and audio at Apple. Rhea has a background in computer vision & robotics and was awarded the highest honor in Stanford Computer Science. We were both completing our Master’s in CS at Stanford when we chose to build Kita full time. 

**TLDR:** We turn messy borrower documents into the data layer that powers lending in emerging and undertapped domestic markets.\
\
[Kita (YC W26) Launch Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_z9lR5p9NMg)

**The problem**

In emerging markets like the Philippines, where there are no banking APIs, a borrower’s financial history is locked in noisy documents: bank statements, payslips, utility bills, and more. For lenders, accessing and validating a borrower’s data is nearly impossible.

Today, lenders either review these documents manually or rely on legacy OCR. Manual review is slow and expensive, while OCR breaks on real-world inputs and still requires human verification. This slows loan decisioning, raises costs, and caps lending volume.

**What is Kita?**

Kita uses vision-language models to outperform traditional OCR, turning noisy borrower documents into fraud-checked, decision-ready signals for underwriting models. We are built specifically for emerging and undertapped markets, hyperlocalized around the signals that actually drive underwriting outcomes in places like the Philippines, Indonesia, Mexico, and beyond.

Over time, Kita links historical repayment outcomes to document-level signals, becoming a custom learning engine trained on a lender’s own data and decisions.

We’re starting in Southeast Asia with plans to expand to other emerging markets. We’re also exploring underserved segments in more developed markets, like parts of the U.S. where borrowers still rely on documents.

**Our ask**

* **Intros:** We’d love introductions to lenders or fintechs operating in lending or credit, in emerging markets or in the U.S.
* **Founder wisdom:** If you’ve built or scaled lending, underwriting, or risk infrastructure, we’d love to learn from you and compare notes.
* **Operators in financial services:** If you work with document-heavy workflows, we’d love to understand the problems with turning documents into usable data.

launches.title: DAIVIN! - We let humans breathe underwater (without oxygen tanks!)
launches.tagline: We use electrolysis to extract oxygen from water and convert it into breathable gas for divers
launches.body:
Hey everyone I´m [Leo](https://www.linkedin.com/in/leo-kankkunen/), the founder of [DAIVIN!](https://www.daivin.tech/)

**TL;DR**\
Did you know, a single bottle of water contains enough oxygen to **sustain a** **human for a day?**

DAIVIN uses electrolysis to extract the oxygen from water and convert it into breathable gas for divers, enabling tankless underwater breathing limited only by battery duration.

Demo video: <https://youtu.be/r5HfL8Bw0dw>

👤 **The Team**\
Hi I’m Leo, I’m an electrical engineer with seven years of experience in the electrical industry and the youngest person in Finland to achieve the highest national electrical certification, authorizing me to independently execute and sign off complex electrical power lines. I’m also a certified diver and served in the military.

# ❌ **The Problem**

Underwater diving technology hasn’t changed in almost 100 years, and is rife with problems:

1. **Intense oxygen tank logistics.** Oxygen tanks hard-limit where, when, and how long a dive can happen. In elite and remote operations, logistics - not depth or physics - sets the limits on mobility, mission flexibility, safety, and cost.
2. **Unsafe by design:** Pressurized gas systems add mass, failure modes, and cognitive load, making diving roughly **1,000× more dangerous than flying**. DAIVIN! replaces stored gas with on-demand oxygen generated from water.
3. **Slow and exposed:** Bulky gear forces divers to move \~5× slower than walking, extending task time and exposure. DAIVIN! reduces bulk and drag to restore underwater mobility.
4. **Cost-prohibitive** Professional dive systems cost tens of thousands of dollars, with helium exceeding **$100 per tank**.

# ✅ **Our Solution: Apply electricity to the water around you and dive safer, longer, and deeper than ever**

DAIVIN! removes tanks entirely, enabling missions to start anywhere with a shoebox-sized system.\
\
\*\*Put on the vest:\*\*\
You wear a lightweight vest with triple-redundant electrolyzers.

\*\*Strap on the batteries:\*\*\
A lightweight battery belt replaces the traditional weight belt. The system is quadruple-redundant at the circuitry level, meaning that even if a wire were to fail, three independent paths per electrolyzer maintain continuous gas generation.

**Electrolyzing H₂O**\
Our device uses the resource you are already in: water. We apply traditional electrolysis, where DC current splits the water molecule (H₂O) into oxygen (O₂) for breathing and hydrogen (H₂), enabling deep diving to depths of 200 meters / 650 ft without nitrogen narcosis, oxygen toxicity or dependence on expensive helium.

\*\*Dive Freely:\*\*\
If decompression is required, decompression time is reduced because hydrogen exits body tissues faster than nitrogen. If entangled, a single palm sized battery can provide **up to one hour of additional breathing time**. If operating remotely with no support team, recharge anywhere using solar power. No tank logistics. No cognitive load.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=96969&key=user_uploads/1925087/29ed7bd4-aeaf-449a-b96e-e3ab81eb7a3d)

# **✨Future**

Today, oxygen is treated as a logistics problem: moving heavy, pressurized gas from point A to point B. That framing is wrong. Oxygen is fundamentally an **energy problem**.

Where logistics break down, on-demand generation wins. In crisis zones or at high altitude, carrying tanks is a liability. It is far more efficient to carry - or source - water and convert it into oxygen when needed, whether for wounded personnel or climbers operating far from support.

The same logic applies to space. A pressurized oxygen tank is limited in gas supply, but water is abundant, and already present. In space, we won’t transport air; we’ll extract oxygen from ice.

Even in airplanes and hospitals, oxygen delivery still relies on bulky tanks or legacy systems like pressure swing adsorption that consume space and deliver lower purity oxygen. From first principles, water plus electricity yields the highest-purity oxygen possible.

We’ve been hauling the container when we should have been bringing the source.
